review:
Tactical Breach Wizards is a game whose Steam rating is misleading because it benefits highly from the ‘thumbs up’ or ‘thumbs down’ binary. It’s a solid, competent game, whose trailers and description clearly showcase what the game is about, both mechanically (grid-based puzzle game) and tonally (quippy). So I would say it’s a rock solid 7/10, which can be tough to give a thumbs-down to.

The problem, then, is that rock solid 7/10 leads to a 97% thumbs-up that gets interpreted as a 9.7/10. This game ain’t that. Even if you decide to buy this game, you should not go into it expecting something at that level. It doesn’t have the spectacle or the depth or the aesthetics or the ingenious design or anything else you would associate with a 9/10 or a 10/10 video game.

Instead let me offer a simple decision path for whether you should purchase this game:

Have you played Into the Breach? If not, go play that one first.

If so, next question: Do you want to play more of Into the Breach? If not, do not play this game. If so, then consider playing this game, as the mechanics and aesthetic do offer some fresh aspects to this type of game.

That’s it. I wish I had realized the similarity before I played this game past its refund window.

Because I wasn’t a huge fan of Into the Breach for much the same reason I’m not a fan of Tactical Breach Wizards. I find the gameplay superficial and unengaging.

The problem is that when you have a completely deterministic puzzle game, highly constrained to a handful of actions within a grid-based gaming board, with essentially unlimited and friction-less rewinds, then the gameplay has no stakes, no surprise, no shocking moments, no real sense of discovery and wonder. It just feels like work to me: I’m doing something I already know I’ve mastered and have no real chance of failure but the work’s still gotta get done.

Pretty much the opposite of what I’m looking for in a game. You may be different.

review:
This has got to be one of the most disappointing games I have ever played.
The premise is fantastic: a turn-based urban fantasy story sounds like an easy shot, and there's a lot of potential complexity in the way you address each combat encounter. Accessibility options are better than average and the vision for the game seems to be well-executed.
Now, how do they fuck it up?
The dialogue is god-awful, let's get that out of the way immediately. For every chuckle I got there were nine weary sighs in between, and the only inherent comedy of the gameplay seems to be pushing people out of windows and making the "defenestration is a funny word" joke incessantly. The comedy is toothless, just a handful of Marvel-style quips in between each combat encounter, and the dialogue choices seem to affect nothing. Way too much of this game's plot is just a shitty James Bond film with random MacGuffins replaced with magical counterparts.
And as for the gameplay, you realize fairly quickly that every room is structured in such a way that you can win no matter what set of tools you have available. This seems like a good design decision, but you quickly realize why better turn-based strategy games like Into the Breach and XCOM don't do this: these aren't combat encounters anymore, they're sliding block puzzles with extra steps. The ability to rewind and try again endlessly, the perfect accuracy and predictability of enemy movements, the lack of consequences for failure (doing extra objectives just unlocks outfits) makes the game a collection of lukewarm puzzles rather than a series of intense shootouts, and this is a problem the developers should have noticed EARLY. There are no stakes, no failures to learn from or triumphs over adversity, just the slow, methodical march towards the solution with errors just wasting your time.
The bland story, obnoxious dialogue, boring gameplay, and timid design overall suggests this game was made by a fairly young studio. I don't hold things against indie games that they can't help, which is why I didn't complain about the graphics here, but an indie dev team needs to have the spark. What does this game say about the player and the characters? What does it make you feel to experience it? What makes this game stand out against its influences, against its contemporaries?
Nothing.

Sadly this was a major letdown for me.

The game is not xcom with cool mages, is not a top down tactical strategy rainbow six - is just a boring and irritating puzzle game where you have to do [b]EXACTLY[/b] what the game wants you to do on every single level or you will not succeed at all.

The game made me feel like the only way to try to enjoy it was by reading a guide - however if the player needs step-by-step instructions to play your game, then the player is not experimenting, the player is not making mistakes and learning, the player is not playing a game, the player is not having fun - the player is just a robot pressing the right buttons at the right time.

In a very appropriate analogy: the game made me feel like the hostage, tied, blindfolded and suffering while trying to understand whats going on - instead of the smart, professional and capable hero that rescue those in need.

Its a fun idea but ultimately just a bit boring.

Damage feels basically irrelevant, with more emphasis put on moving enemies or defenestrating them, while this does make you think creatively about positioning it ultimately makes every level just a pre setup puzzle simulation, and you just find yourself looking for the fastest way to complete each section. I think it would be more fun if there was more customisation, like more abilities for characters that can be equipped to create varying playstyles and creative builds that can be strengthened by your companions. Every level can basically be completed without taking a single hit or worrying much about your own positioning. 

Story/writing

The story is a bit uninteresting so far for me personally and is largely communicated in text bubbles popping up between characters in motionless scenes. This would be fine if the writing was good, however it feels relatively juvenile. The writers are constantly just looking to make jokes in dialogue at every moment and for my taste theyre mostly not funny, it would be nice to have some variation in characters instead of them all just being cynical unfunny jokers. 

overall i would give the game a 5/10, giving points mainly for the fun art style and some interesting puzzle situations.

It's a tossup whether or not to recommend this.

The story is satisfying and cool. The psychoanalytical dream sequences honestly could've been done without entirely though. Nobody ever likes dream sequences in anything, especially not when they are used to break the "show don't tell" rule of storytelling. Overall though I'm glad I experienced the story.

It's frustrating that there aren't often any ways to check the dialogue history (because the dialogue isn't interesting enough on a moment to moment level for me to remember it).

The gameplay is addictive, but that doesn't make it fun. It compelled me to buy the game after the demo, and kept me docile through the story, but I barely enjoyed the gameplay itself. If I were to change it, I'd remove the skill tree and design all the levels with those skills in mind, to provide something that's outside the "uncanny valley of difficulty" where it's numbing but addictive.

Overall the story carries this enough that I'm torn on recommending it. I decided not to just because it's not on a DRM-free storefront like GOG and Itch, and all else being equal I decide on my purchases based on that.

review:
Tavern Manager Simulator is part of a flood of games on Steam. This sort of Business Manager Sim game is extraordinarily common, and lots of them have major issues, but this one has a lot of promise, and seemingly-attentive devs, so I am leaving this review specifically for them:
I really like the basic skeleton of this game. I sank over a day's time into the gameplay, and I can easily see myself spending more time on this, and recommending it to others with similar tastes, but not in its current state, and there are several reasons why:

1. Most importantly: Upgraded Fairies are indistinguishable from unleveled fairies. I have some fairy waiters at level 9 who are exactly as efficient at their jobs as level 1 fairies. This makes me feel like all my effort automating my tavern was pointless, as the fairies will only ever be kinda bad at their jobs. Their speed does not seem to increase, their carrying capacity is forever at 1, and their speed seems fixed. These problems combine into an incompetency when it comes to processing customers. Even taking advantage of their flight to mostly cater to tables on the second floor, they are simply worse at their jobs than me. And this is especially noticeable with the Cleaner, who is instantly overwhelmed by a single dirty customer, much less a group of five.
2. Constant Negative Reinforcement Sorceress: The Sorceress, I want to say, isn't really much of a threat, but she IS profoundly annoying. Constantly demanding highest quality stuff wouldn't be such a problem if the above was resolved, but as a consequence of her implementation, she takes time out of the rest of my tasks in order to berate the quality of my fairies' work. This is not fun gameplay, it's being complained at for something I have no control over. I kept expecting my fae army to start doing better jobs, and for these complaints to cease, but they have lasted deep into the upgrade tree, and I'm nearly at the end at this point, (with tremendous grinding involved).
3. Hay, Water, and Firewood: Hay and Water are extremely annoying to interact with. Other players have pointed this out too, but these are easily the least-engaging parts of gameplay, and should absolutely have been automated much earlier. Additionally, the Stables are a great idea with mediocre implementation. Leading the Horse into the stall is clunky and I frequently get displaced by the Horse in the process.
4. Decorations: Decorations are Pointless. In a lot of games like this, Decorations improve the rate you receive customers, justify higher prices, or improve the perceived conditions of your establishment. In this game, they cost money. That's it. They just eat your money. There's literally no benefit to buying them. In fact, they're all downsides. They make your inventory harder to navigate, take up space in your tavern that could be handling customers, they can obstruct your fairies or your customers, and most of them are ugly, and there's a distinct lack of variety. A lot of the decorations are just variations on one another. I do not need a selection of 12 houseplants that cost hundreds of gold for some reason.

Overall, this game is a gem buried inside a lot of frustration and tedium. I can't recommend it until some things change.

1. It would be nice if the fairy levelups actually mattered. If Waiters could carry additional items, move much faster, and perform tasks more quickly, it would make them feel better to use, and facilitate busier taverns. Likewise, cooks and bartenders should be more capable of perfect pours and perfect dishes, becoming much more reliable into the higher levels. Additionally, job roles for Woodcutter, Waterfey, and Stablehand would be extremely nice, especially if Woodcutter and Waterfey were available early. Lastly, I think a general boost to the Cleaner would be a massive deal. As it stands, the Cleaner feels almost useless besides keeping a resting neutral state. Enabling them to tackle bigger messes (either by having their cleaning action be an aoe that can more easily handle footprints, or giving them a much faster item interaction time as they level) would really make this game feel less like a drag to play in the endgame.
2. Sorceress's standards should be lowered just a little bit. It would also be nice if her language was a bit more responsive to the actual state of your tavern. She'll call my tavern a "Disgusting hole" regardless of how clean it is and how fast my service was, if her steak didn't sparkle. This is misleading. She should maybe have a few more lines and some if-then statements to give you ideas for how to improve the tavern, rather than just being a rude customer you HAVE to interact with.
3. As mentioned above, more fairy jobs specifically related to Hay, Firewood, and Water would be huge benefits to the playability of this game. But additionally, Hay could use some re-examination as well. Feeding Horses feels extremely pointless a lot of the time, and giving us something like the water pump for the Hay would be quite nice. Let me feed all the horses at once and save some time. Feeders exist.
4. Decorations should have some kind of impact. It could be a bonus to customer arrival speed or patience, it could be a boost to gold tips, it could be a boost to cleanliness, you could even go case-by-case, but decorations cannot just be a hole you throw gold into that makes the game worse. The decos that mess with pathing should be fixed (this might also be an issue with the noble tables, too, by the way, and the decos should either be way cheaper, or should have real gameplay value.

Bonus: I really wish there was a way to get rid of the beggar that wasn't just braining them with a pan. I get that it's a joke, but it does make me feel bad every time. I'd be fine giving them a room at the hotel to get rid of them for 24 hours. I think that'd be kinda cool actually.

FINALLY: A note about the "Security" system. It's basically just a notification system, but at 2k gold, it'd be a lot more valuable to gameplay if it actually interacted with the thief. I would love it if you got a sensor at like 300gold somewhere in the early game, and then later a security system that actually kept them out, or potentially attacked them for you, that could be placed in the Warehouse.

A lot of these critiques and suggestions have to do with a general lack of conveyance in this game. A lot of mechanics and interactions are pretty unclear until you watch them actually unfold, and it would be nice to have more direct information about what things do, how long things take, and how fast things move, especially the fairies, which do not feel like they actually get anything from leveling up.

Anyway, I hope to see some improvements in this game, since I have enjoyed my time with it so far, and am curious about the Bard.

review:
If there was a way to review a game as neutral, I would here.

The good: 
-I like being able to go out and find little odds and ends, like finding the gnomes on the roof or the random events beyond that.
-The decor is fun, though I don't like how some of it has a hitbox and can be moved by guests.
-The game itself is fine, although repetitive, that might not be some people's thing.

The bad:
-It gets super grindy later, like I'm only two trophies away from being 100% done and its just a slog. There's no need for level 12 to take *that* long. I get padding a game out but man that's literally all it is. All I do is start the day, glance around in case any timed orders come in then quite literally sit on my phone because it takes too long. Rinse and repeat.
-The stuff you can do outside is a one time thing, like once you do everything out there, that's it. It would be nice if there were some events or themed days that could happen. It feels kinda like a nothing burger after a bit?
-The upgrades are fine but few and far between for new/interesting things imo. It took forever to unlock the freezer and now that I have it, its more of a 'use once or twice' kinda item. You just freeze ice, a few drinks and that's it. Semi boring. 
-Needs more variety, more diverse furniture. It gets to look very same-y all the time even with lots of items spruced around.
-Beyond that I have a handful of gripes. Why can't the fairies make perfect food/drink? Why even employ them if they can't? Why is the VIP 'rich' section so big? I don't even have that many of them going in, it's never full and the room is a bit awkward in size and shape.
-The food critic is annoying. If I passed once I don't see why you have to multiple times. All she's there for is to tank your creditability when you can't be bothered to make perfect soup etc.

~27 hours in, day 200+th

This game made me think, maybe it would be a nice feature if our goblin could lobotomize itself with the chisel.

Honestly, there is no thought put in the game loop. It is absolutely horrendous.
Its like the devs making you eat dirt and then laugh in your face and then push a 100 DLCs in your face and tell you you will like it.

review:
"Trash Goblin" is part bubble-wrap popping mobile app type puzzle-lite and part "Power Wash" style cleaning game and part business tycoon... this is an unusual mix but it could work if done right.  The idea is that you're a little goblin that lives downstairs and you chip away at blocks to reveal trinkets, clean and polish them and then sell them for gold to upgrade your cleaning stuff and sleeping environment.  Okay.

The game is modestly well polished and appears well, despite the somewhat simplistic mobile tier graphics. 

There's a lot of clicking through text dialogues that was incredibly annoying, and then once you get into the two minigames that form the backbone of this, you get bored immediately.  This is the kind of game that probably would have done well on mobile, but the developers seem to have missed their target audience.  Why make thousands of dollars when you could make hundreds?

The biggest insult, however, is the truly offensive pricing... more on that later.

From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

The game features simple, cartoony 2D graphics, of the type you normally expect to see in low effort mobile apps.  3D graphics programming does require a degree of skill and competence and unfortunately not all developers have the budget or talent to deliver this, despite 3D graphics cards hitting the mainstream in the 1990's.  Considering this is being evaluated as a PC game, having the graphics phoned in like this isn't going to result in a high quality, visually impressive game that PC gamers are used to seeing.

The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just point and click stuff like a browser/Flash game.  The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction.  You'll get none of that here.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

Next is pricing and value.  Is this game worth buying from among the 175,000+ games on Steam?

Trash Goblin has the pathetically optimistic price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  But worse, there's an additional $40 of DLC including content unlocks... so to fully own this game, you're up for a full AAA price... SIXTY UNITED STATES DOLLARS... for something that right now is only in a position to compete with free mobile apps.  

For comparison, the initial $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Detroit: Become Human", "Yakuza 0" or "Factorio"... the full price they're asking would get you any AAA game.  Just unacceptable.

Play Viscera Cleanup Detail or Power Wash simulator instead of being robbed.  $60.  Just who do they think we are?

Overall it's a good game. I will not knock it down for it's ability to keep my attention. But as of posting this, the performance of the game itself along with bugs makes it extremely frustrating to continue.

For a game of this graphical caliber, with a limited amount of active animations, I would expect minimal performance issues. I have gone through quite a few moments where it will freeze for a minute, play for a second, freeze for a minute, play for a second, etc. on loop. This is made more frustrating as my computer is still working, everything else is fine, other applications accessible, etc. It most recently took me a solid 3 minutes to exit the game as it was not responding. Wouldn't even let me switch screens until it decided I had had enough.

The bugs I've experienced are minor, but infuriating. Occasionally patrons of your shop will give you gifts for doing quests for them, and I like to keep these on my shelves not in the working area. Bad idea, most of those shelves have some level of "false wall" behind them. Items will magically slip between the atoms of the universe and fall into the endless void! There also seems to be an issue where if you are holding an item and are attempting to switch locations in your shop (i.e. workplace to sleeping area), the item will get caught on the corner and fall onto the floor, unreachable. 
I guess this might not be necessarily a bug, but rather someone not testing the play space itself. In my opinion, that would be kinda crazy though considering 95% of the game takes place in only one location.

review:
I like this in theory, but this is so buggy I assumed it was early access for a moment. I've had - in the three times I've opened this game - two game-breaking bugs (like literally, the second time I opened the game and the graphics appeared so dark as to be nearly black and I just had to randomly click until the regular visuals reappeared. The second time it just opened and then crashed completely and needed to be reopened again). 

Objects regularly warp and stretch fully across the screen. I've had items duplicate (that came in handy but isn't really meant to be happening), and a couple of times disappear. 

Today's new bug is my cleaning station suddenly becoming several levels darker for no apparent reason, with no way to change the light values back, so it's very dingy just on that one screen. I can't actually see the items on the labels in the bath, it's so dark. I'm sure the next in-game day will bring an entirely new and exciting bug, lol. 

It also feels very strangely paced. I don't know if this is because of updates adding more elements that it affects early game dynamics, but in the end to feel like it's even worth using the caravan, I am sometimes closing my shop for two weeks at a time just to focus on building up items. There's no point, after all, just selling mostly valueless items via the caravan if you can upcycle, but upcycling takes a long time to do. In addition, just about every "stranger" character I meet wants something I don't have, either because I've upcycled it, or because I literally don't have it. I'm lucky if I make a sale with a stranger character once every 3 days, even if I find 5 items per day and see multiple strangers per day. The RNG around customer requests feels extremely broken / not aligned with what I actually have/possess to sell (it's a miracle whenever I get a stranger who doesn't *only* want some low value item that isn't upcycled). This combined with merchants on caravan days only asking for your lowest priced items and ignoring the highest value / upcycled items disincentivises travelling via caravan at all. 

I have never once, despite being on day 34-35 in-game (ETA: day 100 now, and still never gotten close to filling my stash/running out of space), gotten close to filling my stash/running out of storage room, which makes all the bag/stash-increasing items (of which there are many) kind of useless for me. I imagine they're extremely useful for those who are late-game, but this is where I do think the balance of the game is a bit strange. It's obvious that stash increasing is meant to be affordable in the early  and mid-game, but I don't need it. Meanwhile the later game items that cost 1,500g are the ones I'm needing now to frantically increase my item pool in general. 

I enjoy enough of this game to keep playing, but at its current level of "polish" I can't recommend it to others. Maybe it needs to go through a clean in the Goblin's sink. It feels a little that in racing out a lot of different elements and moving parts etc. there's some core issues in the game's structure that need some time and attention. I bought this a while back and only started playing in the last three days, and am kind of shocked at how janky it is. I've played item cleaning/collecting/upcycling-style games before, and this is definitely the most buggy, though it's also trying to achieve the most. Hopefully getting back to basics will just help a bit. Until then, maybe wait before buying (or playing) this one!

ETA: I'm sticking on not recommended due to additional Paywalled achievements (behind DLC), which also implies future Paywalled achievements even if you pay for current DLC.

review:
This was interesting for maybe 3 or 4 hours, but started getting pretty boring and frustrating from that point forward. I'm probably 90% through, but I feel I'm really just punishing myself for pushing rurther. I woud very much recommend Wyrmhall: Brush and Banter instead, and I'll explain why.

The main problem with this game is the lack of clear direction or a focus on making the core machanics fun and engaging. It feels like content was thrown at the game without really trying to make it balanced, cohesive or streamlined.

Let's assume cleaning is the part you're supposed to have fun with. It's basically the same after the first hour, and then it gets boring quick. The game knows this and offers upgrades that let you do less of it, and do the rest faster.

There are time slots to spend and an option to pay to get more of them, but there is no fail state, no deadlines, no running costs to worry about.

If earning money was the point, you'd have more of a goal to go for. As such, the game encourages you to take less money to boost your reputation that would in theory get you more money. But really it's just to grind an achievement faster. Most upgrades are kinda useless. You can buy a ton of extra sheves that make it harder to find the thing you're looking for. I guess it's to let you decorate the place maybe? Oh yeah, forgot you can also spend money to docorate the place.

The story itself progresses kinda randomly. Character pops in, request a thing, gets a thing. Banter ensues. It's ok, but nothing special.

If you got an impression that finding peices and assembling specific things is something, you're playing it wrong. It's far better to just attach all sorts of things to other random things with no rhyme or reason. Better for inventory management and profits. The end game is about getting access to more items you can pull out of a sack at random, at which point there are no other goals to go for.

edit: i still stand firm with my review and even firmer with the added achievements for the DLC which COSTS MORE THAN THE BASE GAME.

Trash Goblin is as advertised which is a cozy shopkeeping game of chipping trinkets, cleaning them and upcycling them for requests then selling them. 

a nice tip for players: while chipping, look at the shadow casted below and you'll see the item you're about to discover.

now why did i give it a negative review? here are some of my reasons which i feel would have been addressed before leaving early access:

[list]
[*] why is the tub upgrade only limited to 3 items at its last stage of upgrading? could've been a mechanism where we can just dump dirty trinkets and maybe use up 2 'energies' instead of a whole day.

[*] the ability to travel to more than one place when you reach endgame. no point of me hoarding items when all i want to do is sell more instead of waiting for (at the most) 2 customers per day at my shop.

[*] the space after you upgrade your tools is basically empty and useless. this space could have been combined with the bed space or front of the shop instead of just one space where nothing really happens.

[*] a better chipping tool where i can just simply chip every dirt at once instead of figuring out the logic especially for the purple ones. it would've been a big help for endgame when we're chipping away for random trinket spawns.

[*] the trinketpedia. OH MY GOD FOR ME THE LAST ITEM IS THE BEAR PLUSHIE RIGHT ARM. the amount of chipping i did... imagine your max chipped items are 6 PER DAY and i've reached 305 IN GAME DAYS plus ALL THE OTHER ITEMS IN THE TRINKETPEDIA SPAWNED AT MOST 3 TIMES. why can't we just call our auntie to get us a missing trinket? i don't mind waiting 7 in-game days instead of chipping randomly. and you can't just order the missing item since it has not been discovered yet so yes, end game is basically pointless once you've obtained 39 out of 40 achievements. i understand RNG is implemented but god, this is ridiculous... maybe learn about it from Gemporium's artifact finding mechanism?

[*] abrupt ending. like what do you mean... that's all? that they come back and that's all? no in-game trophy or something to congratulate you or like a much better upgrade of tools? it's just not satisfying after helping out with the various 'main' characters.

[*] please stop spawning nimble jack items. I AM SICK OF THEM!
[/list]

that's my review right now, i feel like i was caught in between as i started playing at the end of the early access stage and while playing it, the completed game released its 'final' update so yes, i would love for more patches to address the 'Seen It All' achievement.

review:
I want to like this game, but I cannot recommend it. I feel like it had so much it could of done if they fixed the problems, but the developers have shown that they have moved onto there next game, and left the mess I will describe. There is a lot of bugs, jagginess in terms of gameplay and story. So let me run you through it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Lets start with the main story, if you can call it a story.
--The main story has no driving factor. The only driving factor is your own desire to sell to the area and other areas. There is no major conflict, despite the war going on in the background which causes you no problems, until they realized how flat the story was and tried to cram some in at the end, but it wasn't satisfying. 

The ending that was so rushed. It requires you to steal supplies, some which you can only get in certain places every 2 days, which causes your reputation you built to go in the trash.

As for the people you interact with, the main influencers don't feel like they have any personality, and could very easily be replaced with a blank wall with a note attached and I wouldn't notice a difference. Honestly, if you told me about your day at work, that would have more thought put into it, than this main story. Most of these characters are not voiced at every part, so prepare to read.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Robbery, Reputation, and Wanted System
--So you can rob warehouses, chests, crates, cars, and medical tents. Warehouses contain chests and crates with chemicals, crafting supplies, and sometimes weapons, clothes, and recipes. 

A little of a neat system. Robbing these lower your reputation in that area, and doing it enough will cause you to gain a wanted level. The wanted system has 3 levels, person of interest, which last ~24 minutes irl, suspect for ~25 minutes, and wanted for ~30 minutes. Plus when Wanted runs out, it goes to the lower level one, then the level below that. If you plan on robbing, get used to seeing these at the top of your screen. Even if you rob a warehouse in the middle of the jungle with no one around, you will lose rep and gain wanted levels. 

The police have some good sight, don't need to stop to gain stamina, and love to beat you down. But guess what, that is not the end of your wanted level. One of two things will happen, either you will go to a jail cell and can walk out, but you still have a wanted level, or you go to prison with a wanted level. 

Prison is fun, you have to do laundry or bake bread to earn 50 cards to get out of prison, or pay 75k and get smuggled out, or just jump the wall. But it gets better, the police will treat you as a threat in the prison and beat you down and where do you respawn? Outside of prison in the town next to it, while still being marked in prison. So either you climb back in or say goodbye to whatever you had when you were arrested.  For more law enforcement stuff, see the raids section.

In terms of reputation, it is very easy to get, but if you have negative reputation, you cannot park your car in a town/area. Don't you love spending 12 mill on a mansion and you cannot park there because you lost reputation in that area?

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Employees and clients
--First note is that you cannot turn off sales on the first island. Why does this matter? Well if you have a dealer there, they will ping you that they are out of product every time someone tries to buy from them. So you must always produce weed and Amp to shut them up, otherwise you'll hear the buzzer a lot.

You can have lab assistants who produce drugs with cash, which is helpful, but a bit too easy.

The dealers are simple and useful, but run out of product and the buzzing starts.

Distributers give product to the dealers so you don't have to give everyone stuff, just them, but if they run out, prepare your ears to hear 4 dealers tell them that they need stuff, and they will buzz in your ear nonstop.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Production of product.
-- There is never a point where this doesn't feel grindy. Best example is making Amp. Well getting one of the basic materials for it is can be taken from a chocolate bar. How fun does it sound to hit 6 stores across multiple islands to get ~150 candy bars? What about stealing the supplies? Well check the robbery, reputation, and wanted system section for the problems of that. 

But back to the production, the production feels too grindy, and once you manage to get past the set up and producing a lot, there isn't enough demand of product for your massive operation. Mixing feels like a joke compared to DDS1. Like why did they even include it. Raids may hurt at the start, but eventually, you can have kilos taken in a raid, and it wont feel like a problem. Which brings me to the raids section.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Raids on your homes.
--So raids can happen when you're not wanted, but have a higher chance when your at the place. They will take all the drugs, which make sense. But what if I have items stored in the safe room? Those are gone as well. The safe room is for you to stand in. After the raid is done, how fun is it that the guards and still standing on your front lawn ready to beat you down? Not very fun, but it has happened a lot. Saving and loading is the only way to fix this bug, but hey, when you load back in, you get to see the raid happen again.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Map
-- I kind of like the map to a degree. Broken up into small islands that get large and large. The downside is that traveling feels like garbage and it feeds you false information. 

Are you running? Enjoy sliding down hills to escape cops, but also enjoy finding pits and areas where you must use the emergency teleport to get out of. 

Are you driving? Well I hope you weren't hoping that you could actually drive instead of teleporting, but at least you are going places, unless your reputation fell too low, then you better start running to that mansion. 

Are you boating? Well the boats are the only good part, well some are. Most boats you can actually drive around and dock on any part of the shore that is reasonable. Which is helpful because for me, most docks didn't work on my 2nd playthrough, but the beaches worked as my dock. But what about spending 12 million on a yacht? Well back to teleporting for you. Plus I its a gamble if the storage space is what is listed. 30 slots? Na, this baby takes 5 slots.

You know what is even better? When the map shows a road where there is no road or path. Sounds like a simple thing to fix, yet the devs do nothing about it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Character stats
--Your character has a couple stats that are very obvious, but sometimes it is not.

You may decide to test your product on yourself to see what it can do. Well it gives you a stat boost. Lets take Amp for an example, all the game tells you is that you have the amp effect. The game give no other info, so you are force to look up online and find a spreadsheet by some people who dug through the game code.

_____________________________________________________________________
Home decoration
--Simple, there isn't enough furniture in the game to make your home feel properly put together. There is some stuff, but I am willing to bet to you that the mansion you buy, won't feel like a home.

review:
I went into DDS2 with the excitement of a kid on Christmas morning. I’d been waiting for this game to drop for ages because DDS1 absolutely nailed the simulation side of things. The handling, the growing, the feeling that you were actually running the whole operation - it was immersive and addictive.

Fast forward 7 hours into DDS2 and my excitement has been completely drop-kicked out the window.

What happened?

In DDS1, you felt like you were part of the process. You were in it. You were the boss, the worker, the guy doing everything. In DDS2, apparently I’ve been promoted to Professional Bench Clicker. Everything revolves around crafting benches.

Instead of feeling like I’m running a gritty underground empire, I feel like I’ve bought a The Sims: Backyard Chemistry DLC.

Half the time I’m staring at crafting menus wondering if my character is a drug dealer or just really passionate about woodworking.

I genuinely tried to give it a fair chance — 7 hours is a solid trial run — but the magic from DDS1 just isn’t there. The immersion that made the first game great has been replaced with “walk to bench - click button - wait - repeat.”

I didn’t expect DDS2 to reinvent gaming… but I also didn’t expect it to turn me into a bench-based lifeform either.

review:
Killing Floor is one of my favourite franchises, so much so I have 100% Killing Floor 2, Killing Floor 1 was one of the first games added to my library nearly 15 years ago, and I also like the VR game. So it hurts my soul to not recommend KF3. As I over all don't mind it, but it is a far cry from the others, and not in a good way. 

I've seen a lot of people complain about normal stuff about microtransacitons, general lack of content compared to others in the series, and the major differences in general. But my biggest problem comes from the gameplay on a deeper level. Notably the movement and netcode feel way worse. I absolutely HATE the dodging mechanic where you can hit your sprint key and strafe to avoid heavy attacks. This inturn though, makes the game not fun at all; Previous games were all about positioning, get caught off your guard and it could be the end. Not in this one. Spam your sprint key and slide your way out of most situations assuming the netcode doesn't fuck you over and cause you to take damage when you otherwise wouldn't and vice versa.
Ontop of that is the design of enemies, every enemy now has a noticable wind up to tie in to the dodging, and I hate it. 

Weapons just do not feel as satisfying or diverse enough to warrant tons of games to experience it. Couple of games in and you'll get the feeling of everything and head towards repetitive. Not to mention the quality of animations from KF2 (Mo-capped and extremely fluent and downright beautiful) are straightup not present. I thought sequels were to improve on its predecessors, not move in the other direction.

So much potential as the enemy design, general gameplay loop, and other differences compared to the other titles are excellent ideas and have much potential. But its execution is not at a similiarly thoughtful level that the other games are.

Killing Floor 2 is an over all, much higher quality game. In content (maps and classes and match variety), graphics (clean and easy to identify threats, and thoughtful animation work), and gameplay fluidity.

review:
I played the game and as someone who has put alot of hours on Killing Floor 1 and Killing Floor 2, I'm severely disappointed and I am easy to be amused too unlike most picky players out there.

So to start off, Killing Floor 3 is NOT like the previous installments. They chose to do things their way rather than listen to the community. I'll list down the pros and cons.

Pros:

Despite being too different, as a CASUAL game its actually alright. Fun if you want to play with friends and you dont want any intense challenges. Just a game where you go by and have a little fun. Plot seems pretty interesting too, and its own objective mode is somewhat good too (better than Killing Floor 2 objective mode if I'm honest, though Killing Floor 1 is still superior on that area).

Upgrades, very interesting concept. You dont need a gun thats built in the attachment. You can use different guns and use different attachments on them. Reliable for creativity if theres any gun you prefer and stick the attachment there.

Level up system, looks actually fun and some interesting upgrades.

Honestly with all that, it really felt like the game is in place and could have been potentially good. But then theres cons....

Cons:

Limited healing. All of them. Your syringe is not rechargeable and any healing darted weapons as medic are not rechargeable either. Tripwire is forcing us to not get hit so much. I get its meant for players to "git gud" and not get hit so much. But removing it just adds more stress on all players. Which means our safety net is extremely limited. This makes our survival far less assuring comparing to other games where its possible if you simply dont get hit so much and utilize syringe more when fully charged, giving you hope to survive. In this? No hope, you just have to kill all and not get hit at all.

No Steam workshop. The WORST decision of all gaming which I held hope for so long that this game will turn around. I held my tongue for YEARS because I wanted to believe this game will make a comeback with this update. If they had reconsider, I am VERY positive this game would turnaround real quick because modders knows how to make the magic work. But because Tripwire said "NO" and decided to make their own "workshop" version (which btw, not the same and pretty much a watered down version of it). Which means we are not expecting like Killing Floor 1 or 2. Because of their decision, all the hopes I have for this game was pretty much wiped and I was holding faith it'll get better up until now I am convinced it will not.

Low player count. The outcome of everything that happened. Theres not alot of games. Thats probably why Tripwire had to use cross platform on all consoles because they knew without Steam workshop the player count would plummet and its likely used to keep the player count alive. But alas, Killing Floor 2 still achieves it.

Overall, as mentioned its a good game but better as casual game. I didnt bother to play Hell on Earth anymore nor interested (which I LOVE playing it on matches btw) because I know its not gonna be the same. Some would say skill issue and sure, maybe it is because I do get hit alot and saved by my own syringe and medic. But thats the magic into being better at the game vs forcing you heavily to do better in the game. But honestly, I'm willing to get by IF they decided to change their mind about Steam Workshop (which I doubt, and honestly saying no was the last straw for me).

So until they reconsider their thoughts on Steam workshop and announce its return, I'm not changing my review. Even if I'm told thats impossible to bring back. Thats fine, my review stays thumbs down and I move on to other games to play. I held my tongue long enough and forgive them for too long as well through the years. They'll have to accept the consequences of their own actions.

review:
This is a mixed bag... I withheld buying this game for so long because the devs made so many poor decisions and the reviews were bad, but I got a good deal and decided to give it a try.

In essence, it's a pretty good wave shooter. It looks good and plays well for the most part. But what ultimately made me leave a negative review is that I feel this game has lost its core identity.

This game is faster and more action-packed compared to the older games. As a Sharpshooter main, I feel this class has been completely ruined in the third game. The Zeds are simply too fast. No more running around with dual pistols, popping headshots, and switching to a rifle for the bigger ones. Instead, it's a constant cycle of running, dodging, and bashing. They're constantly in your face, and the cramped maps only make things worse, ruining the fun of playing the Sharpshooter class.

Besides that, it's obvious they went for the hero-class system, which is a garbage move. Now, classes are locked to their weapon types, destroying flexibility. On the other hand, they added better weapon customization, so it's a mixed bag once again.

I'm also not a fan of the more futuristic approach to weapons. I liked it better in the earlier games, when you had real-world weapons and more variety.

TL;DR: It's a good shooter, but it has lost its identity as a horror shooter & dont feel like a KF game.

review:
This is not killing floor. This is Call of Duty zombies.

EDITED AFTER MAXING ONE CLASS:

This game is awful. I wanted to max one class and get all others to level five before I revised by my review, but I simply cannot be bothered to play any more of this garbage.

Since day one of KF 1, I have always mained Support Specialist.

It's gone. No support specialist.

Instead, you have "Engineer". This is the poor imitation of what was the Support Specialist class

Even worse? They also removed demolitionist. They are both now squished together into engineer.

The class starts with a mag fed pump shotgun, followed by the double barrel. Next is an auto shotgun. After that? A grenade launcher. Lastly, a laser beam that lights enemies on fire.

Yes, the traditional shotgun class has a firebug weapon for the final tier. No equivalent option for a shotgun or an explosive. The engi has various penetration skills that explicitly state they do not work with beam weapons.

These are the only weapons available to the class. Every class has 5 weapons to choose from.

Every class has a unique secondary weapon. Gone is the old reliable, consistent pistol. You know what the shotgun class starts with as a secondary? An SMG. The firebug? Well naturally, they have a magnum with a machine gun primary. Both starting weapons for firebug do their damage up front, rendering the fire irrelevant. You also only have 2 options for your secondary on every class. Your starting secondary, or you can buy a dual wield to have 2 of your secondary.

This game has completely removed the specialization of classes. Any gun in the game can have incendiary rounds.  Every class gets a machine gun. Every class gets a precision rifle.

You know what else they removed? THE WELDING GUN!

That's right, gone are the days of "Oiym weldin' this doah!". Not like that was a hallmark.

Healing syringe is no longer a cooldown item. It is a consumable that must be purchased and refilled. Ammo, health and armor pickups? Nah, those are gone. Need to purchase all of that now. Can't see where the trading pod is going to be ahead of the wave ending anymore. Weight system is gone, now it's 2 primary slots and a secondary.

The weapon pool is miniscule. Staples like the Husk Fireball Launcher are dust in the wind.

They changed all of the predictable behavior of the zeds. Scrakes now have more health than a fleshpound. They also have a Mortal Combat Scorpion hook to pull you in from downtown. Flesh pounds have flails they can swing out to hit you from further away. Clots can spit acid globs at you. Sirens stop when they scream and kill you almost immediately when they do.

You can now combat slide. You have a dodge. You can mantle terrain. There's next to no fall damage. You can jump like an Olympic pole vaulter.

There are now activatable traps. Activatable sentry guns. Activatable escape zip lines. Ammo refill points mid wave at the cost of money.  Armor crates that will have a permanent spot to refill your armor. You can spend 5 battlepass tokens to get an hour of double XP. You have premium currency to buy store packs, like the classic outfit for DJ Scully. You have special gadgets, like a monkey bomb, a shock trap, and then you have the multi tool...

You can't activate any of the traps, turrets, or any other map interactable without the multi tool. Why the hell isn't this a baked in loadout item?

Class progression is now a skill tree. No longer does your class have a set of innate bonuses that become better the more you play your class, which ensured your understanding of your role on the team increased with your level. Now, your teammates can't inherently understand what you can do based on the level of your class, you do whatever you decided to build for. Again, class and role don't matter anymore since everyone can do everything.

You know what every KF fan was asking for? Your class to have an ultimate. Yes, every class gets a recharging ult like it's a hero shooter. The engineer has a goofy giant speaker system that comes out of their back and blasts sound waves at the enemy... You can't make this crap up. They also added resource gathering and crafting. Outstanding.

You can now craft weapon mods, level up these weapon mods with more resources, and equip them so your custom loadout will be available in the shop. Adding weapon mods make the gun more expensive, unless you're playing Gunslinger which has a skill that makes modded weapons cheaper for every mod they have equipped (The discount applies to the base cost of the weapon with modifications, but still makes them stupidly cheap). You can change the ammo type so you can make every weapon in the game an incendiary for the firebug. Gunslinger benefits from every class's secondary, so you can take the Engi's SMGs. Now Gunslinger is horde clear and a mid range hard target DPS. If you want a tier 4 shotgun for Engi, you need to mod the shotgun from Firebug's tier 4 weapon so it shoots regular shotgun shells. Using a different class's weapon no longer builds experience for that class and instead levels whatever you have equipped, so there's no reason not to do this. Weapon mods are essential for surviving anything over normal difficulty, so you must do this.

Now in all fairness, there are times that this is a good system. The double barrel can be turned into the classic boomstick, or you can choose to turn it into the quad barrel Doomstick. Too bad that firing both barrels into a Scrake's face doesn't kill anymore

All the maps are soulless and completely suck. KF 1 Bedlam is infinitely more inspired than anything on display here. They compensate for this by NOT HAVING CUSTOM MAPS! Yet again, a STAPLE OF THIS FRANCHISE

Even when in solo, you require an online connection at all times. The servers suck, so you will see "Network Connection Error 4", which is apparently a server authentication error, all the time. When this happens, you lose all of the resources and XP from your current run. Also, you don't get your double XP time back.

This is obviously to try and stop cheaters who want to sidestep their resource grinding mechanics they stuffed in, but there is an easy solution to this non issue. Set max possible rewards one could get from a match, add 10% to that number, and ban anyone who gets above that threshold at match end. I cannot sympathize with this as I couldn't care less if someone wants to skip this grind because I want to skip it too.

Double XP only counts time while you are actively in a match. Now I do not have proof of this, however I am positive that they make the game more difficult when you are running double XP. I ran 5 matches on a single map running Hard difficulty, cleared all of them. I popped double XP and did not clear a single one in that hour. Completed the run I did after double XP ended.

There are 3 possible bosses. These things are a joke. Never once have I died to the boss because of how laughable their move sets are. They barely do any damage, telegraph their attacks way too obviously, and barely do any damage.  And no, none of these bosses are Hans or The Patriarch.

But don't worry, there are 4 paid battle passes for cosmetics with a 5th Halloween one running right now. All of the cosmetics are terrible and the Halloween one is just a ton of recolors of Commando Chicken. The game is a content desert, every class that isn't Gunslinger needs reworked because they are all terrible to play, there should be way more maps and guns, but we're only doing paid cosmetics.

This is awful. Why did they make this. None of this is Killing Floor, this is a slopified imitation of a classic title and I am elated to see it fail. I hope Tripwire shutters because this is an insult to this franchise. Nobody has any use for a studio that really thought they could monetize before they made a good game.

TL,DR: If you're a killing floor fan, this game is not made for you. If you are a modern CoD Zombies fan, you are the target audience

review:
I don't recommend it at full price, but at 50% or better deals, treat this review as recommend.

While it's a pretty average shooter in terms of gunplay and feeling of combat, in terms of Killing Floor atmosphere, it's worse than KF2, feels more generic. Although I have to give credit to the devs in that it's in much better state than on release (both in terms of atmosphere and other mechanics / bugs, especially QoL). If you're a massive Killing Floor fan, then you will probably have fun in this game, but if you're just a fan of horde / coop shooters in general, then there are better games than this (even the good old Left 4 Dead series).

In terms of performance, it is very hit or miss depending on current update. While I have a beefy rig and the framerate was fine in general, the shader compilation has been a problem for a lot of people (mildly annoying for me), as for some people it often times made them unable to join a match, because the compilation took to long. After it, you need to load an actual level, which loads for an eternity.
And after you spend all your game time loading stuff, you get a message that the connection to server was lost.

Does this sound fun to anyone?
It might be just on my end because of the specs, but I believe there was a better way to deal with all this loading.
I will give it another chance from time to time and update my review accordingly, but for this moment, this will be my only negative KF review, as I truly believe in this game.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Why does this game have a "dodge" mechanic if it's not used to "dodge" things but just to run away faster or move from a point to the other?

The game is STILL, very BADLY optimized. VERY VERY BADLY.

The passes lack content and good looking skins... The animations of this game are still worse and more janky than KF2....
When you kill zeds you don't feel like a "killing machine" or like it's fun, it feels like a chore that you're forced to do...

There are literally more things in the in-game store, than gamemode in the game (we only have the "weekly" and the standard "survival" (5 or 10 waves).

The ziplines in-game are pretty much useless... Almost no-one uses them, and even if you do, they have cooldowns. Really useless.. The turrets not so much, they kind of "do something".
The multitool traps are useless too, yes player use them, but they're not really that useful most of the times..

Fleshpounders have the most broken hitboxes so far with their "reach extendable arms" attack, they still hit you from 100 meters, and they can turn at the last millisecond to hit you either way (and you can't really dodge, sooo)

The invisible bitc-es apparently have more health than all of the other "light" zeds (yes even the blade arm zeds, you can 1 tap them instantly)

The bosses feel more like a Piece of giant meat that eats bullets, with a flashy 2nd phase that it's there just for show.

Going down just to stand there waiting for someone until you bleed out, for an enemy to come close and insta-lock you into a mortal kombat fatality is the most anger inducing feeling i've ever had playing this kind of genre.. Not only you get killed by BS, but you have to stand there looking at the bot doing a 1 minute fatality on your body.

It feels like they intended the gameplay to be "you will go down a LOT, and part of the gameplay goes around this mechanic"
That way, if someone dies, they cannot only blame themselves, but now they can blame you for not saving / reviving them. (even the fact that if you kill the last zed on the map, all the downed players will get instantly helped up)

Literally the Whole gameplay is: Play / farm for broken DMG or Stun builds / and shift + slide all the time.
God forbid i want to go alone around the map, it's a suicide apparently.

(I will not mention the limited stims, because they're not so bad, since you can sort of "bypass" them) even tho it really doesn't make sense that they made them "limited" but you can spam stim bags on the ground and bring 7-8 stims in your class. You'll still die before running out of them..

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Y'all might say "skill issue" or smth, and it might be true... But playing HOE on KF2 or Havoc 30 on darktide is more reasonable, more fun and rewarding that this bullcrap.

I've had literally no fun playing this game since the Beta (i bought it because i wanted to give it a second chance)
But damn this feels like i'm wasting my time playing this game... No rewards / no good skins / no fun / no interesting gameplay.

review:
I had to look past a lot of bad leading up to this point in order to enjoy the game. I had mixed feelings most of the way, but I still had a lot of fun. I loved the predecessors and was willing to give the game a shot.

A lot of poor design decisions went into the game:
 - The "headquarters" reminds me of the windows xp 3d desktop (a not very functional thing that nobody wanted)
 - The shaders issues....
 - No weapon, armor, or ammo drops on the maps
 - The support items (grenades, syringes, and tools) are priced so high that if you actually use them you can't afford armor, ammo, or weapons
 - All of the zeds have additional abilities that are leading to some serious balancing issues in which any attempts to fix seem to make the game worse.
 - The zed teleportation system seems unfair (getting hit from behind by a gorefast that wasn't there literally half a second earlier)
 - Rather than fixing current balance issues and bugs, more content is being added which makes further balancing more of an issue.

The game lost a lot of the 'killing floor' feel, mostly due to the pacing; feels a lot more like CoD with the amount of sprinting and sliding you need to do. The characters are very bland outside of the classics (foster & skully). Honestly the only real positive thing that I can say is that I think they did a good job with map design.

The most recent balancing update straight up broke the game. All difficulties seem to have changed significantly. Some are much harder on solo but much easier in multiplayer than they were prior to the update. I have a hard time seeing any meaningful balancing changes that will scale to all modes, difficulties, and player counts.

I have to say that I am hopeful for the future of the game; the developers are putting in the time, attention, and work to roll out improvements, content, and balancing updates. An example of this is the weapon attachment system improvements that allow you to pick the modifier, which used to be random and take 50+ craft and recycles to get what you actually want. The perks themselves are fun and the skill tree perk upgrades are a welcome addition.

At this point, I feel that I have given the game a fair shake and did have some fun and feel like I maybe got my money's worth but I wouldn't do it again, especially after so many updates consisting of one step forward and two back. I can't recommend that anyone else purchase the game at this time. That being said, I will continue to play occasionally and revisit from time to time in hopes that some of the balancing issues are resolved.

Original review: It's early and it's a lot of fun. I recently bought the game after the completion of the first 4 seasons. I'm enjoying unlocking everything from those seasons with daily and weekly challenges. Shaders take a while to load the first time around and after driver updates, as expected. This month there will be a big Halloween update that I'm really excited about. I bought KF a year after its release so I started it at a similar time as I've started KF3. TripWire has laid off 20% of its employees which has raised some concerns, but the game is definitely not abandoned. Will it receive as much support as the first two games though? Only time will tell. For now, it's a lot of fun though.

Update: I've been a customer of Killing Floor since year 1 and was part of its modding community. I regretfully made a purchase in the in-game store for 1,500 credits yesterday (10/7/26). Today (10/8/26) the Ronin Bundle went on sale for 750 credits. I asked for a refund of 750 credits today within 24 hours of my purchase.

Their response:

"Thank you for contacting us at the Killing Floor 3 Support.

Unfortunately we are unable to provide a partial refund for store items. Killing Floor 3, like Killing Floor 2, will occasionally make items in the in-game store available at a discount. Our promotional pricing is strictly limited to orders placed within the sales promotion.

We apologize that this was not the answer you were looking for, but we hope for your understanding."

If you're okay with supporting a company who doesn't care about their customers then do your thing, but be prepared for a response like this if you ever buy something that goes on sale immediately afterwards. They offered no resolution at all. Tripwire Interactive clearly doesn't care about its customers anymore.

review:
Update: So I have followed the guides on how to fix things(on the comment and Reddit). There is nothing wrong with my GPU. It works fine with other titles. Upgrading is unfortunately not an option for me. I have also done the trouble shooting mentioned with the settings as well as the AMD Adrenalin program. Somehow it went smoothly. But there are times that it still crashes. The crashing decreased. But it is frustrating to crash on a Long game and lose all the material and experience points. After maxing and fully upgrading two perks (Medic and Firebug), yeah the gameplay is a bit better than KF2. I still miss the old KF2 servers and the ease of finding a lobby with a lot of people. The recent discount with the in-game store content helps. 


It is a decent game, but I feel that it has lost the feel of Killing Floor 1 and Killing Floor 2. Maybe it is because the setting takes place 50+ years in the future. I cannot quite point out what is missing at the moment, but if you removed the Killing Floor title, the game could easily feel like a generic shooter. That said, it works at a bare minimum.

I have experienced crashes here and there, although I am not sure if they have anything to do with AMD hardware.

The thing I hate most about the game is the “Premium” Supply Pass. Coming from someone who played Helldivers 2, I feel that at least players could grind the game and eventually unlock everything in the Warbonds. In Killing Floor 3, unlocking the Premium Supply Pass feels quite pointless. There are some neat free cosmetic items you can get, and you can also earn some premium Dosh or currency while progressing through the Supply Pass, but I still don't think it is worth it.

Another thing I dislike is the lack of players. Although there is crossplay between PC, PS5, and Xbox, it usually takes a while to find a lobby with other players. There is also no browser-style, searchable lobby system, which is frustrating because it would make it much easier to find and join games with other people. I do hope they fix this and that the player count increases in the future.

That said, there are also some “upgrades” and “improvements” compared to its predecessors.

I like the gadgets, which make each class and perk feel more unique. The upgradeable and moddable weapons are also welcome additions to the game. The environment can also be used against the Zeds, such as the lasers in Onslaught map and the other environmental traps. There are also turrets and armor crates.

However, I do miss the ammo boxes, weapons, and armor pickups from the previous two games.

The movement also feels really nice and is quite helpful during combat. However, another negative thing I noticed is the lack of “character” among the enemies and bosses. I don't get the same sense of fear from fighting intelligent or sentient enemies like the Patriarch and Hans Volter, who would taunt you in the previous games. In Killing Floor 3, it feels like you are mostly just fighting beasts such as the Impaler, Crawler Queen, and others(Dr. Moorcroft's character is a bit unforgettable).

Overall, this game is a tough sell at this point.

I am admittedly addicted to grinding weapon and perk levels, but I highly advise against getting the game right now. A friend of mine was supposedly going to buy it, but I told him to get other games such as Helldivers 2, Space Marine 2, or Darktide instead.

By the way, this game was a gift from my nephew because he knows I love the first two games. I appreciate the gift, but I wouldn't buy Killing Floor 3 for myself in its current state, especially given the current player count.

Maybe after a few more patches and if there is a huge sale, I would consider recommending it.

For now, it is a pass for me.

review: If you're expecting another KF1/KF2, you're in for a major disappointment. It feels like an early access game, and I mean that in a bad way considering how long it's been since it was released (the odds don't look so good). KF2 had a rough start but they ironed out its flaws in a timely manner. But this one has a lot of bugs and technical issues. Many things just don't feel complete and/or thoroughly tested. The UI is poorly laid out, convoluted yet uninformative, and just an overall eyesore (and don't get me started on navigating "The Stronghold" to set up matches; sure you can get around this by pressing Tab but that's counter-intuitive). I have no problem with grinding perks, but the game forces you to grind for materials to craft/upgrade equipment (making even Normal difficulty seem like Suicidal or Hell On Earth difficulties in previous entries). Oh and lots of micro-transactions, making the game almost feel like "pay to win".

review:
As of September 11

Shader compilation takes enormous amount of time, in the meantime you could have done 5 different shader compilations in 5 different games but here it probably wouldnt go past 50%

Graphics is generic UE5 crap, most of the animations are bad, models (especially rifles/long weapons) are "futuristically" ugly.

Guns are practically non-existent. For each class there are literally only 3 weapons to choose from (excluding a starting one) and there are two primary slots, meaning if you even want to use a different weapon, you cant. While gun modifications seem cool on paper, in reality it does nothing to solve this issue. KF2 had a large weapon pool along with universal guns. Not only that, in KF2 there was a huge gun variety as well. A lightsaber, a sledgehammer that shoots bullets, a railgun, different types of semi/full auto weapons. You can forget about it in KF3. Here it looks as if every single weapon came out of the same assembly line.

Maps suffer from the same issue as weapons. There are practically non-existent, and whats even worse, their art style literally look the same as if the action happens in the same exact place in the same exact time. If you would join all these maps altogether I bet you couldnt tell if these are separate locations (maybe except for the snowy one). Not even gonna talk about KF2 maps. Each from 20+ maps is completely different and offer different visual style.

The only good things about this game: 
- enemy/boss design. They look better, have variety of attacks, and are no longer braindead.
- skill progression is subjectively better, you can actually choose your playstyle and not have a five basic predefined skills

In the current state, i cant recommend this game. KF2 is just way better in almost every aspect, and has better replayability as well because of the map, gun and achievement variety, which this series and genre IS ALL ABOUT. I dont care KF2 is longer on the market. You have just released an unfinished product.

review:
Been playing this series for over 15 years and there are a lot of gripes I have with the game, but first on the list is my HATE of the move to the carpal tunnel inducing call of duty/apex legends style movement system. 

Personal playstyle gripe aside, there's so much more they've managed to mangle with this entry in the series. 

*Performance - THE elephant in the room. The game doesn't run all that great even on powerful hardware and despite the shader compiler changes in this most recent update (summer 2026), it still takes FAR too long to load into matches. On top of that, even minor graphics changes still require ~5 minutes to recompile, though that's down by nearly half compared to before. It's brought with it a lot of instability though and I have a couple friends that can't even play a full match without crashing anymore. 

*Gunplay - very arcadey and enemy models can be shot into a million pieces, but it's lacking the visceral punch of weapons in prior games. Some guns feel decent, others are underbaked and basically unusable past normal (even when upgraded with tier 3 mods), and then there are the clearly overperforming weapons everyone runs. Perhaps another personal gripe, but the iron sights ADS on a lot of weapons is absolute trash and obscures a significant portion of your view.

*Aiming - it's stiff and feels wrong, plus there's something weird with their in-built mouse acceleration that I still haven't totally ironed out. 

*Melee - hit feedback isn't punchy enough and (at least in my experience with it so far) the weapon range/length doesn't feel like it matches the hitbox of your swing. The bash is fine, it's mouse-click attacks that seem off.

*Progression - faster paced than other entries and has a more comprehensive skill tree, though they've bogged down the game with resource collection which feels more like an attempt to diversify the progression gates than a "fun" weapon customization system.

While it's clear Tripwire has made some decent progress addressing the community's issues over the past year, the game just suffers from a case of being underbaked when they released it. I'm sure the next year will bring even more changes and by the end of 2027 it might even be the game it should have been at launch, but for now there's more I'm annoyed with than enjoying.

review:
Modern Live-Service Bloat Kills a Classic IP — A Franchise Blueprint for Recovery

Not Recommended

I’ve been a fan of the Killing Floor series for years, but Killing Floor 3 completely misses the mark on what made this franchise special. While the post-launch patches have stabilized frame rates, fixed initial crashes, and smoothed out gunplay mechanics, the core identity of the game has been replaced by a generic, predatory live-service framework.

The Good
Gunplay & Movement: Weapon feel, recoil, and sliding mechanics feel tight and responsive.

Performance: Stability and netcode are in a much better place now than they were at launch.

The Bad (Why I Can't Recommend It)
CoD-Style Monetization: The game relies heavily on time-gated Battle Passes, high-priced bundle store rotations ($10–$15 per pack), and filler cosmetics.

Character-Locked Cosmetics: Armor pieces and skins are locked to individual Specialists instead of being globally customizable across classes, stripping away player value.

Loss of Class Identity: Shifting from classic Perks (Commando, Support, Berserker) to hero-shooter "Specialists" with button-cooldown ultimate abilities makes this feel like an arcade hero shooter rather than a grounded, brutal horde survival game.

Atmosphere: The dark, gritty horror aesthetic, dynamic lighting destruction, and heavy metal identity have been sanitized for a high-contrast, sci-fi hero shooter feel.

How to Fix This Game & Bring Players Back
If Tripwire wants to rebuild trust and recover the player base from KF2, here is the blueprint:

Scrap the Live-Service Monetization: Remove time-gated Battle Passes. Replace them with an earnable, permanent Perk Mastery System where skins, weapon variants, and outfits are unlocked through gameplay milestones (e.g., Hell on Earth completions).

Decouple Cosmetics: Allow earned or purchased outfits to be equipped across any character class, rather than locking them to single Specialists.

Return to Classic Perks: Convert Specialists back into distinct Perks with deep passive skill trees. Remove button-cooldown abilities and let players buy/build any weapon synergy they choose.

Restore the Horror Aesthetic & SDK Tools: Darken map lighting, restore dynamic light destruction, upgrade the gore engine, and release full Steam Workshop SDK tools on PC.

Right now, KF3 prioritizes monetization models over gameplay depth. Until the developers pivot toward player retention and series identity over microtransactions, stick to Killing Floor 2.

review:
Tried to give this a fair shot, but man... I REALLY dislike it.

Negatives:
Movement feels awful in this game. It feels like every time you try to dodge or vault something or use a zipline you're fighting your character to lock into the animation. When it does work, particularly for ziplines, it feels very jarring. And then half the time it just doesn't work at all (mostly for dodges). Running feels slow compared to the other games in the series.

It's a lot harder to see zeds in this game than in the previous two... they blend a lot more with the environment. It also feels like more than half of zeds lunge at you really quickly and/or have long-range attacks now, which isn't necessarily a problem on its own, but when combined with not really being able to see or outrun zeds as easily, it makes the entire game way more irritating. Also, husks feel even more broken in this one, which is saying something because they were already the worst in the other two games.

Audio cues are confusing... sometimes it sounds like a zed is right in your ear when they're actually ten or more feet away.

Please give us back server browsing. Even if you make it accessible only from the hub, GIVE US SERVER BROWSING. I want to be able to see what round a server is on before joining, and what my ping is going to be, etc.

This is just a cosmetic gripe but I also dislike that they made it so every character only has 2 cosmetic slots... a helmet and an outfit. BORING! And while KF2 was littered with microtransactions just as much if not more so than this game, at least a lot of the the items and characters you could buy LOOKED good. Where is Mrs. Foster, you swines?

Voice lines are less frequent and less whimsical, from what I experienced... which, if you disliked the frequency of voice lines previously, could be a positive I suppose... but it's a negative for me.

Neutral:
The new maps aren't bad, but it's sometimes unclear which areas are traversable until you're right up on them... which becomes problematic if they're not. That said, you can traverse a lot more places than in the previous games. Being able to jump on top of some things and go up some ledges is really nice, despite my gripes about how inconsistent it can be.

I could see people disliking the hub area but it doesn't really bother me since you can just go into the menu and don't have to run around to the different stations unless you just wanna explore. Not sure if that was an option from launch but regardless, it's a nice QOL option that makes the hub area ok for me, though honestly just being able to do everything from the title screen would've also been ok.

Pros:
The weapons/gunplay feels good from what I experienced, bullets and explosions and zed attacks feel appropriately impactful. And while the lack of weapon variety is disappointing, the customization options do add an interesting twist. I like that you collect materials as you play that you can then spend on customizations.... that feels like it could be a fun gameplay loop for a long time, especially if they added more weapons and mods as time went on.

The perk trees having more options and the ability to upgrade your perks is pretty intriguing. I didn't look through all the different perk trees, but the ones I looked through had some fun options. I clearly didn't unlock much given my playtime, but just based on gut feeling it seems like an improvement over the previous games.

The new bosses were fun (and a lot less BS than some of the KF2 bosses...), though I feel like I didn't experience them in the way you should be able to because I fought them all solo. If I were to play again I'd hope they would add the patriarch back into the rotation at some point, though, just cuz it feels strange without him.

The music still slaps from what I noticed, and the weapon and zed sound effects are good.

Conclusion:
Honestly, even though I really disliked it, I believe the game is salvageable. There are some good bones here. But until at LEAST the movement and visibility are improved, I don't see this being a game I could realistically enjoy. It doesn't matter how good your gameplay loop is if the gameplay itself is not fun.
