My friend had mentioned the game has a bunch. I was ready for that. What I wasn't ready for was the fact that this game takes so long to load. Every single time and I had to restart it several times, because it would not connect to my friends. I had to listen to my friend tell me repeatedly that this was a good game, they had been playing it single player for a handful of hours and liked previous iterations. I however can't agree, because I have spent 46 minutes attempting to play this game with them, we never even made it to a lobby together. We tried join game, we tried invites, switching who was hosting, double checking our networks, connecting inside the game. The connection would fail. The loading screens would take forever. The game would freeze on the loading screens. I have never had my interest for a game drop so quickly. I am sorry to the people who clearly worked very hard on the game, on the graphics. The network, the drm, whatever is preventing three people who are highly motivated to play the game from being able to to do so, whatever it is ruined the creative teams work utterly. I cannot recommend this game because the only reason I was interested in it was to play multiplayer. This wasn't cross play, we all have decent machines. We play all sorts of other games together all the time. But something about how Killing Floor 3 has been implemented is just broken. No game should take that long to load, no game with multiplayer should take that long to fail to establish a connection.

review:
[b]The game is in a better spot from launch however the Devs still [u]NEED TO FIX THESE MAJOR THINGS[/u] to bring back the core audience:[/b]

[b][u]The Bad:[/u][/b]
 (The worst thing)
[b][u]*Lack of Cross-progression:[/u][/b]  You can mix and match weapons from different perk classes but you don't get any XP or you used to but they unlocked all the attachments in a previous patch. So all the XP goes nowhere now instead of just sending it to the perk of the non-class weapon you are using(like in KF2) the XP when using that non-class specific weapon just vanishes into thin air. Cause your progression is very attachment material loot grind dependent and attachment bonus affix reroll dependent. You're going to rely on other classes weapons sometimes especially when starting a character from level 0 just to keep your XP/mats and beat the Final Boss wave. Because the Base weapons are all so dirt cheap weak damage and have rarities like COD zombies you either buy that purple weapon or use the upgraded attachment weapon from a different class when level 0, but also it punishes experimentation because some of the most fun is using a gun on a class it doesn't belong like Ninja. On a boss and seeing what happens but you get no XP because it doesn't belong to the class. Which really defeats the purpose of mix of matching because their is no progression at all.

[b][u]*UI:[/u][/b]  There's no way to turn off the UI task/challenge thing in the top left you can only lower the opacity, it's just cluttering my vision and getting in the way. Also the cross hair reticle, I wish there was more customization to change the color or lower the opacity.

[b][u]*Graphics:[/u][/b]  The game only offers DLSS, FSR, Xess, there's no option for custom Anti Aliasing if you want to turn it off. And raise the sharpness in game because sometimes it's really hard to Spot the Zeds. All these fancy graphics options make it harder to visualize the enemy. You can turn off bloom, depth of field, Chromatic blah blah blah all these goofy graphical things that make the game harder to play but impress the video game journalists.

[b][u]*Economy:[/u][/b] The game actively punishes you for upgrading your weapons/attachments by raising the base price so high that if a starter weapon like the Gunslingers revolvers is upgraded too much it outweighs the price of just buying a tier 4/late stage weapon like the AF2081. Also it got rid of the free ammo drops around the map and the free weapons drops in the environment you could sell for Dosh in KF2 which limited/reduced the impact of missing your dosh kill targets by giving you a lil extra pocket change. Making the econ strictly kill dependent. Also it's worse because now you need to upgrade armor, buy syringes and buy the other gadget equipment it gives you even less dosh to work with making the economy much more strict and painful to play.

[b][u]*Movement:[/u][/b] The Dash action and Running problem. you can't dash forward while running, Dash is dual-mapped to run with dash button by default. It creates weird choppy inputs where you seemingly can't dash when a Scrake grabs you with their grapple hook, or flesh pounds are pummeling you in and a screecher comes in to finish the job. So you need to diagonally input a forward right or forward left input to bypass it. Then the crouch slide is the opposite where it only works when moving forward. And the movement is slower in this game FOR YOU,(than KF2) the zeds move faster than you. So you need to zigzag your dash while being chased by 3 flesh pounds and a scrake that can literally grapple hook you across the map at any time. Then if you get grabbed and try to crouch slide out you need to make sure it's a forward input or you will crouch or die. They changed the movement system added all this bloat, but didn't add any auto-run features or nothing to make all these things more seamless and intuitive instead it just makes everything more clunky and difficult for the player. 


[b][u]The Good:[/u][/b] 
-I like the bosses/boss design is better and more varied and creative than KF2 (they don't simply just run at you} some shoot spikes out the ground, have cool abilities. These are some of the strongest boss designs in the series.
-Outdoor maps like Radar, feel pretty good and have enough sightlines and routes to train zombies
-Special perk/class abilities add a brief break in the gameplay loop Gunslingers Focus guns, Ninjas grapple shock swing, Commandos drone.
-The turrets make sense the environmental interaction, though some may see it as a ripoff of other things.
Ninja can be really fun if they fix the movement, and add the cross progression so I can still get XP using any weapon on him. Devs only want you to play the game as they intended then do things that stop experimentation for the sake of balance but just alienate everyone from their game because they can't have fun playing the way they want.
I see the devs are trying to make amends with what they've done, but I'd like to see them go the full mile and overhaul the entire movement system and allow cross progression on the weapons so people starting out can experiment with whatever combo they want and aren't gridlocked to one style.

review:
[h1][b]Killing Floor 3: A Technical Mess Holding Back a Fun Shooter[/b][/h1]

Killing Floor 3 has the foundations of a genuinely enjoyable co-op shooter. The gunplay is fun, there is a decent variety of enemies and classes, and playing alongside friends can be a great time. Unfortunately, those positives are buried beneath a mountain of technical problems that make simply playing the game an unnecessarily frustrating experience.

[b]The Highlights[/b]

✅ Fun gunplay
The shooting itself feels satisfying and impactful, which is exactly what you want from a game built around fighting hordes of enemies. There is a solid variety of weapons and classes to experiment with, making combat enjoyable when everything is working properly.

✅ Good variety of enemies and classes
There is enough variety in the enemies and playable classes to keep encounters interesting and encourage different approaches to combat.

✅ Decent level design
The maps are reasonably well designed and provide some good spaces for fighting through hordes. While they are not particularly groundbreaking, they work well for the gameplay.

✅ Music is fine
The soundtrack does its job and fits the action without being particularly memorable.

✅ Decent graphics
Visually, the game can look good when performance issues are not getting in the way. The environments and enemy designs have plenty of detail.

✅ Fun with friends
When you can actually get into a game together, Killing Floor 3 can be a lot of fun with friends. Unfortunately, the technical problems surrounding multiplayer can make getting to that point unnecessarily difficult.

[b]The Downsides[/b]

❌ Constant shader compilation
One of the biggest frustrations is the sheer amount of shader compilation. It happens frequently, including when changing many graphical settings, and the process can take an incredibly long time.

❌ Abysmal performance
Performance is simply not where it should be. Even with hardware capable of running the game, the experience can be plagued by poor performance and inconsistent frame rates.

❌ No anti-aliasing
The lack of proper anti-aliasing results in constant shimmering and distracting visual noise, particularly on objects in the distance.

❌ Shader compilation when changing settings
Having to wait through shader compilation simply because you changed certain graphical settings is an especially frustrating design choice. It makes experimenting with settings a chore rather than something you can quickly adjust.

❌ Loading screens can cause intense flickering
The flickering during loading screens is particularly unpleasant and can be genuinely uncomfortable to look at, especially for players who are sensitive to flashing imagery.

❌ Unbalanced audio
The audio mix can be inconsistent, with some enemies being dramatically louder than others. This can make encounters unnecessarily chaotic and make it difficult to judge what is happening around you.

❌ Multiplayer connection issues
Trying to play with friends can be frustrating. There are occasions where you can be kicked while loading into a game and end up being placed with random players instead, making co-op sessions unnecessarily difficult to organise.

❌ No toggle to sprint
The lack of a sprint toggle for keyboard users is a surprisingly irritating omission and makes movement feel less convenient than it should.

[b]Final Verdict[/b]

Killing Floor 3 is a frustrating example of a game where the underlying gameplay is actually pretty good, but the technical state gets in the way of enjoying it. The gunplay is fun, the enemy and class variety is solid, and playing with friends can provide some genuinely enjoyable moments. Unfortunately, those positives are overshadowed by persistent performance problems, excessive shader compilation, visual issues, audio inconsistencies and multiplayer problems.

For a game that has been out for this long, these issues are particularly disappointing. The experience should not feel like you are fighting the game's technical problems almost as much as you are fighting its enemies.

⭐ A fun shooter buried underneath a painful technical experience. With the number and severity of issues still present, Killing Floor 3 is not worth buying in its current state, and personally, I won't be returning to it.

review:
[h1]Edit[/h1]
Their big September update seems to've fixed up some of my previous technical pain points (key word [i]some[/i]) — but honestly... the more I play, the sadder I get. The first game's grindhouse vibes, charming indie metal, and the incredible levity its ‘00s Brit humor dialogue sensibilities provided, with all of its bizarrely horny and hilariously stupid energy... this franchise just keeps drifting further and further away from all of that. After all of these years, I've yet to understand why Tripwire seemingly haven't looked back at KF1, or clearly taken note of any of what made that game such an enduring classic. 'Cause from what I can tell, the general consensus among their "fans" — and the internet at large, really — is that KF1 was easily the most cohesively-directed and broadly appealing entry in this whole series, and none of their efforts since have come remotely close

For context on my and many others' feelings on KF2: I think its vibes were horrifically dragged down by half of its soundtrack being comprised of remarkably awful Christian metal, its dialogue being noticeably far less vulgar and fittingly adult than the first game’s (it’s got too much of that 2010s Marvel-type quippiness, imo), and Tripwire's environment art direction dropping the first game's dirty and oppressive atmosphere for one that was generally a lot more colorful and flashy. This game, though... this game just takes every aesthetically-displeasing misstep that KF2 made, and absolutely [i][b]runs[/b][/i] with them. To the point that this almost feels like a caricature of the second game, made by the most vocally displeased fans of the first game. A soundtrack with virtually nothing going for it, and goofy "futuristic" tech base-y environments that are just [i]swimming[/i] in unpleasant neon lights

Putting it simply, this game has none of KF1's atmosphere — that ubiquitous grunge and grime, the devastated environments that feel like nightmarish reflections of places you've actually found yourself in before, the classic survival horror-influenced flow, etc — and none of KF2's saving graces, either. Remember the industry-upending level of detail that all of that game's weapons' animations had? Or the grotesquely satisfying sound effects that you got from every popped head and severed limb? Yeah... this game is remarkably lacking in those regards, somehow. Even the much-touted improvements to their gore systems in this game just aren't [i]felt[/i], as a result of the flow of the gameplay being sped up so much

So, yeah... with all that said, this whole package clearly just [i]really[/i] ain't for me. And, y'know, while that's certainly disappointing: I still sincerely wish the best for the whole Tripwire crew. Heck — maybe after Maneater 2 is out, their director(s) will tap back into the kind of unrestrained grittiness that defined the games of Tripwire’s golden years. Or, if they go against the industry's current norms, and jump straight into developing another new IP — maybe they'll find a new niche, and a refreshed identity for the whole studio alongside it! I truly have no clue as to what this team's future looks like, beyond the success that I hope their second ShAR(k)PG will bring them; but I'mma just keep hoping that the Tripwire name will eventually be elevated back to [b]Top Dawg AA[/b] status among fans of every genre they work within

[h1]Original Review[/h1]
Killing Floor 3 is the only game I've played almost twenty years that's genuinely given me a headache, and I'm honestly struggling to figure out how it's accomplished that. Just turning around makes me feel like I’m being stabbed in the eyes — and no matter how much I've fiddled with the settings, it still manages to give me this horrifically nauseating sensation. Killing Floor 1 and 2 never made me feel this way, nor any other Unreal 5 game I've played... so I'm really at a loss in trying to figure out what, exactly, is so fundamentally [i]off[/i] about this game's visuals that it’s making me feel sick

Note: none of the footage I’ve gone ahead and watched on YouTube has captured what actually playing the game is making me feel, either. My only guess is that there's something about my frame pacing in-game, or perhaps the way lights strobe, that's just an absolute assault on the senses (in the bad sense)

If anyone who reads this happens to have any idea as to what the source of my woes may be, [i]please[/i] let me know what your guesses are, ‘cause I truly want to give this game an honest shot

review:
2025 AAA Unreal 5 installment of underappreciated franchise turns out to be out of touch and shit!!! EVERYONE IS SURPRISED

+ weapon customisation/crafting and larger skill trees in theory allow for more replayability/progression, and feels like one of few genuine improvements on the Killing Floor formula brought on by this title. While I have yet to explore most of it yet (considering 45 of my 90 minute playtime has been spent compiling shaders), conceptually it makes plenty of sense for this game to have, since (outside of perk levelling) Killing Floor 2 felt particularly lacking in long-term progression.
- bad voice acting (horrific in some cases)
- bad dialogue/writing
- bad weapon design
- post-mw2019 style overly animated/shaky weapons
- few perks 
- uninspired perks
- few weapons
- extremely limited weapon variety per perk
- ugly maps
- bad maps
- poor map variety 
- horrific aesthetic, doubling down on many of the controversial decisions made in Killing Floor 2
- poorly optimised
- ugly vfx (fire, blood, muzzle flash etc.)
- bad modern-era seasonal models
- lackluster content updates (and content in general)
- unreal 5 
- poor enemy animation
- poor enemy pathing
- Feels incredibly out of touch and I'm honestly unsure who this game was made to appeal to. Especially with how first impressions focused the gaming market has been for the past 10 or so years, it doesn't really make much effort to draw attention to itself or invite in new players. It lacks any of the wit or charm of previous titles, and has restylised itself to look like literally every other late 2010's generic sci-fi shooter, 10 years late. 


It sucks because despite the many many warnings since its release last year, I found myself actually wanting to play this game. I feel as though there is a genuine gap in the market for this style of game, and the Killing Floor formula had plenty of room to grow into it. Especially as someone that has enjoyed my time with Killing Floor 2 and actually felt as though a third game could bring some significant improvements to the table, I was pretty disappointed to hear that Killing Floor 3 was so poorly received on its release. Despite having received over a year of live service updates, I can now see why. Though I still genuinely hope that the game is improved on over the years, I find myself somewhat doubtful after now seeing how deep rooted many of its issues are. It's not the sort of thing that gets fixed with a couple of superficial seasonal "content" updates. Particularly when it's completely blown any and all reputation with a relatively small community, I have little faith that the game will even have enough staying-power to make it to its Destiny 2: Forsaken if ykwim. 

I will continue to play this game for a bit, even though I'm lowkey embarrassed to. I largely believe that Killing Floor 1 and 2 are far superior in almost every way, and they also don't make me feel like a fat pig eating from a fat pig trough when I play them.

I have a different problem than most existing Killing Floor fans that leave a negative review. Mechanically, I [i]would[/i] love this game, but the audio and visuals are fucked.
You are practically forced to use supersampling for the game to run at a reasonable FPS.
High quality supersampling = low fps.
High performance supersampling = higher fps, but blurry enemies as they move.
That combined with bad (sometimes nonexistent) audio design, it feels like you're playing the [i]suggestion[/i] of a game, or having a bad dream of playing a game. The largest enemies can completely sneak up on you. They actually muffled and quieted some of the most impactful audio events since the previous 2 games, so it's even quieter. Teammate shooting their grenade launcher? Silent beyond 10 feet away. Fleshpound sprinting at you, smashing everything in its path with its chain spike grinders? Sounds like a child gently scraping a fork and knife together. Footsteps? What are those?
I recommend Killing Floor 2 over this, although that is probably hard to get into unless you've played DOOM. Might try this game again if it gets a good modding community or custom map support.

review:
I really want to recommend the game. The bosses are cool and a nice update from KF2's bosses. If you enjoyed KF2, this game really just feels smoother with a few minor gameplay changes like limited syringes but a nice dash baked into movement for a more engaging combat, weapon mods to allow for weapons to be customizable, and mantling. 

There of course are way fewer maps as the game is much newer, but the maps that are there feel nearly as good as the majority of KF2's, though a few of KF2's best maps a clearly superior to KF3's pool so far. The weapons and classes feel the same as well. They're limited, but the mods you can craft do add something to the pool at the very least.

Now the really bad parts are the load times, the lobby connection, and the random hiccups. It makes everything incredibly frustrating to even try to play. I'll load into three games just fine, and then out of nowhere stuck on the loading screen for two waves until I give up and alt F4. 

I initially had the game on ultra and was running without any hiccups until suddenly wave 2 I was crawling at 10 fps. I put on a frame limiter and down to high graphics and that brought me back to a steady 90 fps that I limited at. That is for 2 more waves until it suddenly dropped upon the wave loading again. I tried dropping settings down to medium, but it decided it needed to load shaders but just froze at ~2900 shaders and never moved.

I really enjoy the higher depth of weekly challenges provided and the story that is baked into the game, but it really feels like they just tried their best at making a shitty battle pass as every other sellout company has and forgot there has to be a game to back it. 

I really don't recommend buying it in this state unless it's <$5 dollars. The hassle to play just isn't worth it. Go play KF2

review:
Possibly the least optimised game I have EVER played.
I tried KF3 on the free weekend after being a big fan of the first 2 but being hesitant to purchase KF3 due to poor reviews.
First Thing players are greeted with is the longest shader compile of their life. My friend with a somewhat lesser PC couldn't finish compiling after hours of waiting patiently and ended up giving up on the game altogether.
Once I finally finished the shaders, I hopped in and realised how sluggish the game feels due to the low FPS.
After tinkering around in the settings, I ended up settling on low and off for most settings just to get a decent and smooth FPS. This is especially surprising given how optimised the first 2 games felt on max settings.
Given that my PC has pretty much the best AMD GPU and CPU to offer, I was shocked that it ran so badly. 
I can only compare performance to cyperpunk on phycho raytracing settings without looking even remotely within a universe of the graphical fidelity as Cyberpunk.
The weapons are pretty cool and there is a lot of customisation of the attachments and class loadouts which I kind of like. 
Unfortunately there are not very many weapons like KF2 and also there are fewer classes to choose from.
There are loads of microtransactions everywhere and the game feels like a massive leap down compared to the prior KF's.
I feel as though Tripwire Studio no longer cares about making a good game and just want to maximise profits without considering the player base.
I will probably revisit this game in the comming years but for now I will leave it alone till another free weekend or feel deep discount.
Let's hope the Devs are reading reviews and make positive changes to bring this game into a good state,

review:
**Not Recommended**

Killing Floor 3 is a masterclass in how to squander a beloved franchise.

**What you get:**

* Endless shader compilation because apparently playing the game is optional.
* Crashes that remind you this feels more like a paid beta than a finished product.
* Hardware compatibility so bad that whether the game runs seems to be decided by a coin flip instead of your PC specs.
* Performance that ranges from mediocre to downright embarrassing, with stuttering, frame drops, and optimization that feels completely absent.
* A cast of painfully bland, obnoxious characters that somehow managed to replace the personality and charm of Killing Floor 2 with nonstop cringe.

The technical state is unacceptable. It doesn't matter how good the gunplay is if the game can't stay stable or deliver consistent performance. When it isn't compiling shaders or crashing, it's reminding you how lifeless the new cast is.

This isn't a worthy successor to Killing Floor 2. It's an overpriced technical disaster wrapped around some of the worst characters the series has ever seen.

Wait for deep discounts. Better yet, just reinstall Killing Floor 2.

review:
Where do I even start? It is so sad to see a franchise that I have dedicated many hours to fall this miserably. Everything that made KF1 and KF2 unique has been thrown away recklessly... This is not even a Killing Floor game for me. This is just a failed attempt that was tried by developers just to stay "meta". KF3 does NOT know what it is trying to be. Battlepass? HUB system? Paid Cosmetics and Gun skins? What the hell are you guys trying to be? Is this supposed to be a sequal or just a live service game like COD or Destiny 2? I get it, you need to address as many people as you can, but KF Franchise NEVER had that popularity as those live service games. And don't even get me started on how those AAA companies behaved towards their core community. People still pay for that poor service, but it is not a devotion or commitment to the game itself, it's just... habit. And none of the KF games are able to mimic them, let alone impose them to their players. Before the release, I had so much expectations. And because I've spent almost 2k hours on KF2, it was such a let down to see how unrecognizable KF3 was... 

If TripWire's intentions were clear when KF1 was first released, then I wouldn't even bother writing this. That being said, I do not hate this game. It has ups and downs of course, like other KF games but my anger is based upon my personal disappointment and developers' delusionalness. People BEGGED them not to go along with this. They (including me) have warned them about the outcome. This game could have been delayed, postponed. Of course it'd damage the initial hype but at least we would have had a solid KF game. Only if they'd listened to one thing that made KF games phenomenal; their audience. 

All things aside, even the graphics, the movement, and even the ZEDs look like they belong to a different franchise. Nothing makes this game a KF game in my eyes. Shooting is bland, maps are barely tolerable, the server browser is replaced by a DRG style matchmaking, which is somehow implemented poorly. All the weapons feel the same, hell, even the classes feel the same to be honest... There is no unique, fun, or a fundamental feature left... I know it is still being updated, but I am 95% sure that it'll never feel like KF game, for me at least.

review:
This game has a massive, fundamental issue that stops it from being a good co-op game, let alone a Killing Floor game.

In KF1 and KF2, each match had progression: You and your team started with pea-shooters and worked your way up to wonder weapons by the end, which should sound familiar since this is the formula that made COD Zombies a top tier cooperative experience. (past tense, they also f'd it up)

In KF3, power scaling happens outside the match. You spend resources at the out-of-match Armory to upgrade your guns, which then lets you take on harder difficulties.

They took the "play" out of the gameplay. The only reason you would even engage with the actual shooting is to do one thing: Farm resources, which you then use to upgrade your kit outside the match.

This kills progression [i]within[/i] the match since you're now hard-capped by your loadout. The only thing that matters in the end is how you specced your weapons, not what actions you and your team performed during the match to upgrade yourselves and then win.

Sure, older KF games had perks you needed to level, but that was the "floor" (pun intended). Level 1 or max level, you started the match with essentially nothing and had to work your way up to the best equipment the game had to offer. More importantly, you and your team worked together to do it, everyone wasn't on their own separate progression path. The KF equivalent of defending your teammates until they roll a raygun is gone.

For this reason, there's nothing that can save KF3. They took away progression from the actual moment-to-moment gameplay and gutted cooperation in the process. They can't fix this without throwing away the whole game and making KF4.

I wish steam and an option between positive and negative because thats just where this game sits. Its not the worst game but maaaaaaan does it feel incomplete. now im not as burned given that i got this on a pretty deep discount but having played KF 1 and 2, this games got some issues.

While the Devs continue to work on this game an yes ik its been out for a little while it feels too little too late. 
everything from the maps, the guns, the perks it all just feels off. the ebb and flow just are not here. ill start with the guns and how they feel. The game has nowhere NEAR the amount of guns KF2 has, and the shooting just feels floaty an they dont have that kind of weighty and meaty feel to them. This and the reload animations feel Painfully fucking slow, i feel like im reloading longer than im shooting and yes some skills have reload speed buffs but still.

The maps are fine for what they are but they just don't really stand out and you don't have as many ways to control the flow of combat on them. The welder isn't in the game at all so making chokepoints or having the players decide "lets hold them here" is only kind of a thing. one of the perks DOES have a tool to block a door but there's not of lot doors that you can block off with that to begin with so. 

Another thing missing is the rechargeable healing syringe. players can no longer just heal one another outside of using one of the medic's guns, and to heal yourself you instead use a finite syringe that you rebuy at the trader which also has a painfully slow animation, buy the time its finished youve already lost the health you would have recovered on account of being shanked 9 times while using it. 

The classes, yes theres less of them. the Swat with his riot shield isnt here nor is the demolitionist with his rocket launcher to let the flesh pound know hes in the wrong fkin neighborhood and the berserker is now just the ninja which is still fun but has only a few melee weapons.
 
Matchmaking works, kind of.  Theres no server browser and so far more than half the time im ending games with only  3 or 4 people(out of the 6) when the lobby does manage to fill up half  the match is already done with. 



These are just a few of the big things that stand out to me and the Devs have a loooong way to go on this one.
Give us back our welders, our rechargeable healing syringe, add way more guns and let them feel good and fun to use and for fucks sake speed up some of the animations. for 10 bucks games fun even if it is a huge downgrade from KF2. Is this worth full price to a fan of KF 1 and 2? fuck no. get this on a steep discount

review:
I want to enjoy this game, and at first it was enjoyable, I prefer to play hard mode in KF3 as it WAS challenging, fun, and rewarding. However Tripwire did an update where the zeds got to deal more damage but their health pools were lowered. I honestly have to say that the only difference I seen was the Zed damage, I have maxed out about 2 of the perk classes, and I am always struggling just to make it through a match. Hard mode in this game feels like what Suicidal mode is in KF2. The "lowered health pool" for zeds does not feel different than it did pre-zed boost.

the Weapons in the game are lack luster for the most part, some guns are good, some are alright. I upgrade all the weapons to the best of their abilities, but sadly even when putting them to Tier 3 upgrades, the weapons STILL struggle to kill most zeds. it genuinely feels like boosting damage of the guns doesn't work, especially when striking Zed weak-spots or going for the head.

another thing I want to point out, the updates for this game are VERY lacking. It takes forever to get anything new. Like we got stuck with some alright weapons, then finally we get the winter update operation, and we got two new weapons, an operator, and the dumbest cosmetics. Why are cosmetics so important in this game? instead of the every now and then new weapon and map, we instead have to wait half a year for the next gear haul, which like said before, lack luster.

Now there is the case with the zeds, not only were they unnecessary buffed with damage, but some of them are just ridiculous to go against, the fodder zeds are minor, only complaint I have is when they SOMEHOW can stop you in your tracks and you get annihilated by the medium-big zeds. Gorefasts become annoying when their arm blade can hit you from 10ft away. Stalkers for some reason are nearly impossible to hit, it sometimes feels like my projectile curves around them just enough that the stalker can ALWAYS get a hit on you. Bloaters do not bother me. Sirens and Husks on the other hand, they ALWAYS appear right behind you, can be in an empty hallway or room, and then somehow a husk or siren is right behind you and now your armor is shredded by the husk or your health is drained by the siren. the heavy zeds like the Scrake and Fleshpound, this is where issues really come in, these dudes will tank ANY damage, no exaggeration at all. Scrakes are vulnerable to ballistic and another damage type, but holy shit they still refuse to die no matter HOW much bullets hit their skull or weak spot. Same thing with the fleshpound, I have a few guns that deal force damage as that is what they are vulnerable to, but still takes forever to kill one

review:
As a Killing Floor 1 and 2 player, I figure I can leave a short, honest review of Killing Floor 3.

Some context: I pre-ordered it back at launch to give it the benefit of the doubt, then refunded it. The game came out very, VERY badly optimized. Content was thin and it wasn't even fun to play.

Positives from my recent run with it:

1. Gunplay: feels satisfying, the weapons work, and online clearly runs better now. Something these games have always nailed is the feel of the recoil — every gun kicks differently, and KF3 keeps that. There's still stuff to polish, but you can actually start to feel the core of the game.

2. Enemy design: pretty well done. Giving each one different weak points (something that started showing up in KF2) is a big win and makes gameplay more dynamic. On top of that, they reworked every enemy so they feel fresh again instead of a rehash of KF2.

3. Bosses: from what I've seen, another win. Challenging, with interesting mechanics. It needs more of them, but it's on the right track.

4. Perks and classes: with caveats I'll get into below. It's a good call that the devs realized the hero system doesn't fit this game. Letting players pick their skins and classes freely, in whatever combination suits them, is a big plus.

5. Map design: another win. Maps have room to run instead of you constantly getting stuck, and there are different ways out of different situations — snagging on a pillar isn't the end of the run anymore.

6. Damage types: great addition. Adds a ton of dynamism and chaos, both to the weapons and the enemies.

Unfortunately, that's where the positives end.

Cons:

1. Weapon upgrades: I don't have the words for how badly the upgrade system works. You have to farm materials all over the place, which is fine on its own, but the sheer number of upgrades per weapon is absurd. For a moment I even liked the idea of having a progression system — I was thinking about unlocking every upgrade on every weapon. But if you want, say, all ammo types and their upgrades + all attachments with all their upgrades, that comes to a total of 405 UPGRADES PER WEAPON. That's farming 400 upgrades for a single gun, in a game that currently has 1,200 active players. If you ask me, identical ammo and attachments should be shared across weapons. That way farming actually feels rewarding and you're steadily unlocking things.

Worth stressing: attachments, ammo and so on have a huge impact in-game. Unlocking them shouldn't be this much of a chore.

Now, someone's going to say "just unlock what you need, it's quick." And what if I want to unlock everything? What if I want to keep unlocking stuff and trying out combinations? I have to grind 400 upgrades? I don't see the point.

2. Weapon aesthetics: a lot of them really miss the mark. No personality at all. So much energy spent on the design and I honestly can't make sense of how strange they are. They don't convey anything, and they've got parts on them where you can't tell what they're even for.

3. Design/UI: not bad, but odd. I don't want to be running around the base to do basic things, and I think they know that, because you can reach upgrades, maps, etc. from any station. The way perks and skills are handled is also strange: skills can only be viewed from the menu (I couldn't find a way to check them mid-match), but to see another class's skills you have to swap class, which kicks you out of the menu, so you have to go back in and navigate to skills all over again. Very clunky.

On top of that, the scoreboard — scores, damage, etc. — isn't an in-game overlay: your character stops moving while it's open, so you basically never get a chance to look at it.

4. As far as I can tell, there's no way to set up quick access to your primaries the way you want. If I have a primary and a secondary, I get to them with 1 or 2. If I have two primaries, I have to press 1, then 1 again — it doesn't let me quickly pick which primary I need, and that's a big downside.

5. The "ultimate" system: inherited straight from hero shooters. Personally, I don't enjoy pressing a button and watching every enemy in front of me just vanish. Sadly the game is probably balanced around using them, but I'd like there to be some way to lock these abilities out. Let it be a shooter, not a hero shooter.

6. Perks: I haven't tried them all, but Sharpshooter feels off. The idea is to combine freeze damage with static damage and reposition. Unfortunately this is a game where you can't stand still, so it's very hard to actually get value out of it.

That's what I've seen so far. To be clear, I don't think it's a bad game right now, but I humbly feel there's stuff to improve, and the most critical parts wouldn't require changes that big. If I run into more, I'll add it.

review:
UPDATED 09/09/26:
I am completely sick of being put into matches that are nearly finished and getting stuck on loading screens so I am not able to use the shop before a wave. This is basic stuff devs. Put a server browser into the game. Fix the bloody loading freeze when joining an in-progress game. Until these are fixed I don't care how good or bad the gameplay is because the QoL is so bad at this point this is just trash. I'll update this back to recommended only once this is fixed.

ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW:
I played both KF1 and KF2 and I have to say I actually really like KF3. In my opinion this game changes some of the parts of the game that make the previous games a bit grindy. I know some veterans of the particularly KF1 love the old kite and heal strategies but KF3 for the most part removes this by putting a limit on how many self heals you can do in a round! The movement is much fast and more dynamic with emphasis on dodging and positioning.

The part that is the real selling point for me is the weapon modification system. When you first start the game if you've played previous KF games you might be disappointed by the lack of variety of weapons with each class having a measly 5 weapons to choose from - but this is deceptive because the weapon customisation can completely change the way a weapon plays and feels. Changing the ammo type of a gun can entirely change the role of a gun. There is strategy and build-crafting elements to this system where you have to weigh up not only what are the best combinations of add-ons but also take into consideration the overall cost of the parts because you need to buy these weapons in round. Do you want to attach everything to have a super expensive late game monster of a gun or just attach a couple of key components to be able to buy a decent custom gun much earlier in a round. 

Now this is not to say the game doesn't have issues. The elephant in the room is the amount of content compared to previous titles is very low. Much fewer maps, fewer enemies, fewer weapons (but made up for with mods as mentioned previously), fewer perks... but despite this I am still having a lot of fun and this is something that can be added to with future updates which I hope continue to be rolled out. It is also promising to see that the paid battlepasses only contain cosmetics, not playable items so there isn't a FOMO to keep you paying unless you want cosmetic rewards.

The other elephant in the room is performance and shader compilation. My personal experience is the first shader compilation took a very long time but after that the game has been running very smoothly for me with only one instance so far in my playtime of performance ruining the experience (against a particular boss on a particular map my frame rate tanked). YMMV on this, I know others have had issues but attaching my specs to this so you can compare.

Sooo... I did bloody waffle on a bit here didn't I... I guess the long and the short of it is I'm having a lot of fun in this and for me personally I really like the changes they made to the core gameplay but also understand why some veterans are upset. Overall this is a recommend from me but veterans be aware that the core gameplay does feel very different.

(F2P ran out before I used the system extensively but I don't see a world where it's not stupid) And the weapons. Phew... what the hell happened? I heard Killing Floor 2 launched with a small amount of but it's been a year and the weapon selection is just pathetic. And the weapons that there are not the least bit memorable. The ninja weapons (while I never used them) seemed at least like a good attempt at trying to do something new and cool, but does that mean Commando gets no love? starting with class identity, its dead, every class is just survivalist with the only unique aspects being the gadget and the grenade, the passive tree on the left side of -most- classes is completely class agnostic, coupled with the barren weapon selection it'll start to dawn on you that this is by -choice- 

Where you start to pull apart the million mobile game adjacent systems, you've spent a good few hours shooting glowing red cameras and LED displays (but only the right kind of glowing red displays!) and have collected enough of the items that drop exclusively from enemies to make sure there is a hard throttle on how much you can get out of the retention nightmare machine - You've now got the privilege of engaging with the attachment and armoury system full of most modern sins, imperceptible sub 5% bonuses to random recoil stats the game doesn't explain? why not - stats that you can only interpret by name and a vague idea, yeah fuck it man I love my stumblesome red dot sight.

Dot effects that are functionally IMPOSSIBLE to parse because figuring out the breakpoint for a bleed with the limited tools you have, and your inability to intuit just -what- affliction power even is, +20 fire affliction? that's great man what is that? 20% of my damage is fire related, 20% chance to inflict incendiary damage based on a damage formula? no? hoping the community just datamines and does the legwork for you? fair.

And then the actual issue alluded to with class identity, the weapons aren't tailored for the classes anymore, you're not the support with shotguns who was the teams backbone against specific zeds, you're not your teams sharpshooter with the M14 handling ranged pressure and mid to high threat zeds, you know who is? everyone.

That M14 that was supposed to be your niche and maybe, maybe a unique off class option for someone with the knowledge to apply it (think taking the 500 magnum as a last option as a low weight, cost effective damage option on sharpshooter) 

The ninja is using it, he's taken talents in his tree with minimal design direction only having a splattering of melee specific perks, being one of the 2 only classes next to gunslinger that has an actual identity associated to it's weapons, no engineers single shotgun talent does not count - and even then you're looking at maybe 2-3 options usability not withstanding but I digress 

The ninja has taken all cut damage related damage boosts, he's put special ammo on his gun so it's now exclusively cut damage and now that M14 is his weapon, fuck it he probably has a weapon in every category in cut damage variants because having 10 of the same shotguns is #content

And then to really compound the lack of class identity, the halfway hero shooter design, we've got a halfassed movement system there to make sure to erode any sense of positioning, and you know what? It's a net positive in KL3 because having to do something that was a genuine highpoint in KF2, which was playing as a team of friends, is fucking -miserable- in KF3 as the most disgusting blood and viscera textures explode in the most unsatisfying way from enemies in your face that your teammate shot, as your performance tanks, and your PC that blows the needs of the game out of the water turns into a personal furnace as the gunslingers give you a minor seizure with their grenades and the firebug actually took a flamethrower and all of a sudden you realize why most of the videos on youtube are solo runs.

So run, sprint faster than the enemies, do your dodges, slide everywhere, loop the enemies that can't interact with the ziplines the enemies can't interact with them, grind that 100+ wave of enemies down slowly, they'll never catch you.

Also the enemies are a step back, not fidelity wise despise the models looking like something shat out by a nu-doom developer, but what made the old ones charming despite flaws like bouncing around on geometry like tables was the insanely high quality animation work, not overexaggerated telegraphs as the pound gets it's stupid arms out and takes 4 seconds to do the "please use a new dodge system we worked hard on his god please" move.

I could go on forever, there is next to nothing this game does that I would want backported to KF2.

Give. Up.

review:
However, If you were hoping for Killing Floor 1 with KF2's bells and whistles, or just a better KF2, you may be disappointed. It lacks many core elements that gave Killing Floor its identity. Instead KF3 is a trend-chasing title that feels designed by committee, borrowing from many live-service games, while forgetting what made KF a unique experience.

While not necessarily negatives, lets dig into what specifically makes this feel so different, shall we?

Gameplay & Mechanics Changes
The Healing Syringe: One of KF's most identifiable and unique gameplay mechanics, the recharging healing syringe to heal yourself or a teammate is now limited to a max of 3 uses and only works on yourself. You can buy refills from the trader pod during/between waves, but Dosh is more scarce already. You can buy and deploy Med Bags for 1 or 2 more, but takes up the same slot as other items in your loadout, which is smaller since weight is gone. Before, you could use the few seconds of downtime during a wave to top off your/a teammate's health, rewarding players that paid more attention to downtime, kite enemies/dodge to heal yourself during waves or the boss all day. You were rewarded for healing others, as it would heal them much more & earn Dosh. Now players are incentivized to hoard their syringes until near death. Using them during downtime to top yourself off is a massive waste rather than a boon. If you want to heal others, you have to buy a Medic weapon or play as one. This fundamentally changes the core gameplay loop, completely shakes up the way the game is played. Who asked for this?

The Welder: Gone. Pressing the 'use' button next to doors closes/locks them, requiring Zeds to destroy them as if welded. Doors cannot be repaired. You can also equip/buy optional explosive locks, but these take up the same slot as other items you'd want on your loadout.

Respawning Ammo Crates and Weapons: Gone. No more respawning weapons to use/sell, ammo crates, or body armor lying around, compounding the issue of Dosh scarcity. Each map has a tiny amount of single-use lockers containing armor, but can only be opened if you equip/buy (if off-perk) the new 'Multi-Tool,' which as above takes up the same slot as other items you'd want on your loadout. You cannot manually drop weapons for others to use.

Crafting: While an odd change, it is one I rather like. You can grind for materials to craft mods for your weapons to customize damage types, status effects, etc., each with a random bonus effect. Each mod can be upgraded individually. However, doing so makes them expensive at low level, unable to afford them until nearly the last wave/boss. On Hard/HoE, they are even more difficult to afford. You can carry 2 primaries, but buying two fully modded/upgraded is rare. This compounds the Dosh/Healing Syringe issue since having to buy Syringes, bags, or a Medic Pistol also drains your little Dosh, moreso if it is modded/upgraded.

Perks: Specific characters are locked to specific perks. Sure, they promised to fix it down the road after significant backlash, but who thought this was a good idea to begin with? And to launch the game without this? The management at Tripwire clearly had no intention of making anything resembling Killing Floor from the start until fans forced them to. How is this not listed as Early Access?

Zeds: Stalkers? Gone. The formerly black Crawlers are now the same fleshy grey as most of the Zeds, harder to make out different types of them in a crowd. When in a full lobby, its hard to see anything with the various effects going on. Where's the victory screen post-boss fight where I can throw grenades/dosh at my teammates?

Trend-Chasing, Audio & Missing System Features
Trend-Chasing: Characters locked to Perks with abilities on cooldown like a Hero Shooter. Ziplines. Apex Legends style sliding. Vaulting and bleedouts like CoD Zombies. It has a hub/Battle Pass ripped straight from Helldivers 2. A crafting system for weapon mods. Upgrading your armor between waves or weapon mods uses the same rarity scale found in MMOs (White > Green > Blue > Purple). Zeds have been redesigned like they came from Doom 2016 with Glory Kills. Again, not necessarily negatives. Merely noting KF3 chasing industry trends and a departure from KF 1&2.

Audio: Most of the music is actually pretty good, a few callbacks to KF1 tracks. The audio mixing is a complete mess though. It's difficult to make out the audio cues for when Crawlers, Scrakes, or Fleshpounds are coming. Character dialogue is full of cringey one-liners that make me miss KF2's banter-at least those had charm. It has moved even farther away from the peak British goofiness we loved from KF1. In fact, there's barely anything British left in the game. The Firebug has the worst lines by far. Awful, corporate safe edgy writing.

Server Browser: Gone. No longer can you browse a server list & join. Instead, you have to enter the hub, walk to a kiosk > select difficulty/map > walk to a VTOL waiting for you. Then after a delay you get a loading screen and it just drops you into whatever it can find, regardless of what wave the server is on.

Text Chat: Gone. But the Cash Shop & Battle Pass are up and running for launch.

Steam Workshop: No mod support. But anti-cheat is enabled, so corporate at Tripwire can ensure people can't wriggle their way out of paying extra for skins, attachments, etc. in the cash shop. KF 1 & 2 had a healthy modding community with hundreds of maps that extended the life of the game.

Game Length: Only 5 waves + Boss Wave. The Medium (7) and Long (10) wave game lengths are absent at launch. The game feels like it was rushed out the door.

Monetization, Bugs & Performance
Now onto the negatives:

Monetization: Three editions ($40-$80) of the game, Season Pass, Battle Pass, plus a separate Cash Shop requiring premium currency that you have to (mostly) buy. The amount of premium currency given from the Battle Pass even after 25 hours of gameplay isn't enough to get a single skin if you bought only the base game.

Bugs: Multiple crashes or game freezing when trying to craft or upgrade weapon mods. Matchmaking freezes ~15% of the time, requiring I go back to title screen > enter Hub > terminal > VTOL again. Switching to secondary mode on melee weapons often will not 'reload' it, requiring me to switch modes 3/4 times. Bosses teleporting around when around certain terrain, glitching through platforms or the floor sometimes when jumping. Husks often teleport around when grappled, rubber banding to their original location unharmed afterwards, wasting your grappling hook.

Performance: Unoptimized. Crash, lost connecting 10x .... Drop fps... Mi pc is rtx 5070 r5 5600

Final Verdict
All of this, yet somehow it isn't listed as 'Early Access.' This game is a perfect example of why chasing trends kills identity. This is a soulless husk of a game wearing the Killing Floor IP as a skin suit and has been monetized to hell by TWI corporate. While I think it is fun, this isn't Killing Floor, but a live-service Frankenstein.

If TWI addressed my issues with the Healing Syringe, spawning weapons/ammo/armor, and the Dosh economy, I would overlook many of the changes mentioned here.

someone at trip wire made a conscious decision that it is more important to have day one functional paid battle pass than a text chat....let that sink in

They sold an Early Access game as a full release. And don't even want to fix critical bugs. But they didn't forget to add microtransactions.

review:
(Free Weekend Impressions)

(This would be marked as Mixed if I could)

Coming from the perspective of someone who really enjoyed KF2, and someone who's way more of the arcade, faster-paced PvE shooter vibe than the more grounded or realistic, I like this game for reasons that some of the KF1 fans I know hate it, and hate it for reasons they also hate it.
I am of firm belief that Tripwire absolutely fucks when they animate and deal with weapon handling and design, these weapons feel godly, look godly, and play godly. The problem is there's so.. little of them? Loading up and seeing, like, there's no Demo, and explosives are basically just the M32 on one class is. Kind of lame? There's not really any oddball weapons, ones I liked using like the Hemogoblin, Seeker Six, it's a very painfully basic array of weapons that - yes feel VERY good to use, but there's just not a whole lot of variety.

The attachment system is actually maybe the worst thing I have ever experienced, maybe even worse than Ubisoft's Division 1 attachment system. Crafting individual single use attachments for individual guns, having to deal with the clunky loadout screen, then the individual attachments have a special tier 3 thing, and you UPGRADE them, and- It's kind of just, overbloated? When it could be so much simpler? Take Division 1 -> Division 2, Ubisoft must've figured out it sucked because you just craft the attachment once and you own it, and can play with it however you want. Even if that meant increasing resource requirements for anything, just allowing you to permanently unlock and swap T3 mods whenever you wanted would be so much better for QoL and simplify a process that doesn't need to be THAT complicated. It also already balances itself out by increasing the base cost of the weapon so, there's, probably no harm?? It's a nice alternative to KF2's flat upgrades, it's just executed, weirdly.

Limiting syringes is kind of weird too? It seems almost counter-intuitive to a game that leans MORE into KF2's arcade-like aspect to also strip away your cooldown-based healing? You have cooldown based gadgets but cooldown based healing is like, too much now? It makes solo-play much more difficult because the game DEFINITELY wants you to be teaming up in co-op to cover that base, but it's just such an unnecessary change that doesn't feel like it bundles well with the rest of the mechanics. It's not like cooldown heal makes it inherently easier - you can't spam it, so your decision matters differently.

I do think the addition of perk gadgets is pretty neat, controversial take but, it doesn't hurt anything and just adds more decisions and flair to the explosive aspect, just, again, limited grenades is fine, limited ammo is fine, but limited syringes is such a weird decision!

The movement is a cool addition, I TOTALLY get why classic KF players hate it because it is absolutely NOT KF but it's a personal preference thing, I like arcadey, blah. Skill tree depth is awesome, love that, skill trees are always a nice place to have complexity. It's very Borderlands-y almost and that's pretty cool. Build diversity is nice like this where it isn't a weird mess of menus and material crafting junk.

Initial shader loading is ass, I'm assuming that's normal with every modern game though.

Some of the voice acting is a little.. flat? New trader person is such a downgrade to the old one (nitpick).

Overall it feels like a game with a lot of potential that's just bogging itself down with wanting to be a live-service so bad so it ships void of content and full of clunky junk. I don't care about the cosmetic stuff or marketing, just the game, so that doesn't factor in for me, but, lack of weapons, the attachment system, and a weaker solo experience makes it kind of iffy. I would say to any prospective buyers to wait for another free weekend to try yourself, or just keep waiting for them to iterate on it more. It's NOT unsalvageable and it's honestly pretty decent as it stands, just needs some more work cleaning things up and padding out content.

Also my computer is not that good and it could still run it so thumbs up there??

review:
The first impression could not be worse.  With a 10 minute shader precompile, followed by a miserable "wait to be told to press W to walk" tutorial, which is interrupted by a pop-up advertisement for a battle pass, and then said tutorial fails to introduce any actual game mechanics -- while assaulting you with 8 consecutive text-only popups about the most advanced mechanics (8 different kinds of damage and 4 different kinds of enemy health)  you're not set up for excitement.

Once you start playing,  you first notice that you're getting popups for 12 different resource-currencies for shooting collectibles and enemies, ala some mobile game.   Once you get past that, you start to see there's a great framework and MOST of the killing floor DNA is here. Zeds are very readable and the models are fun to see, and things FEEL polished on the surface...

Fans will be frustrated by the way this game has the polished BONES of a good killing floor game,  while cutting much of what made killing floor unique in order to streamline towards a more modern 'key binds and cooldowns' shooter style. (weapon weight replaced with less flexible weapon slots, door welding is gone, heal-stims are consumable charges rather than recharge over time) -- and the weapon diversity is gutted in favor of a grindy 'weapon mod' meta-progression

New players will enjoy that the game has a healthy foundation, but be confused by the unexplained intricacies & off-put by the rain of different resources and XP bars that give it a very "mobile free to play" energy.

review:
Tl;Dr:
Inventory system isn't fun to engage with, with attachments that make guns too expensive and punishes experimentation while offering little back to the player for said experimenting. 

Movement feels awkward and clunky with a weak dodge that feels like it dose not work, with enemies having too aggressive of tracking with attacks, and bosses like the Alpha Scavenger not being fun to fight due to movement.

Perks have lost alot of their unique identity.
--------
The largest issue is the new inventory system. Guns can be customised with various modifications, ammo types changing the damage type of weapons, sights, magazines, extras like laser sights and under-barrel attachments and on the surface, this is cool. The amount of time in KF2 where I've thought, "Man, I'd like this weapon more if it did or didn't have a scope or sight" is a decent amount. However, all these fancy bits make guns more expensive and forces you to pick Power vs. Economy. This isn't bad, but the stats on these attachments ruin the system. The economy in most cases FAR outweighs the power gained, with sights at base adding a nothing burger of +2% accuracy when aiming down sights, and sights aren't the only issue adding to this. Ammo types, like making your shotgun a Slug or Flechette shell, can range from adding 300+ to 500+ to the total cost, making economy a nightmare for something as simple as changing ammo to play around with the weapon. The sandbox of KF3 is centralised around balancing the player's economy per kill/wave with guns, that are held back by modifications that add little to the gameplay loop.

Mods can also be upgraded, making the stats not as bad, but still adding little to the gun. At T3 upgrades, they unlock a bonus stat. After sinking a bit too much time into upgrading a single attachment, such as a drum mag for an AR you like, your choices are narrowed down to a table where only 3 of the 10+ options that are worth picking, for example: Buckshot shells for the starting Engineer class gun, get to pick one bonus stat such as 1% bonus damage for every 1 player within 10m of you, or adding 15 Toxic Power, what is Toxic Power? They don't tell you, so who knows, or gain +5 bonus damage when surrounded by 3 enemies. That's right, a whole 5 damage to a gun with 550 base! There are a few good bonus stats, but honestly, stats like this bloated the RNG system, forcing the change to allow players to select what they want, making the whole thing feel less awful to interact with. However, crafting materials are expensive and take far too long to accumulate. The fix for this is pretty easy. Scrap the system or make improvements, such as lowering the cost per attachment/modification and amping up how good these can be, make players want to craft wacky guns rather than punishing someone for experimenting, give more materials and scrap the upgraded attachments or again get rid of the nothing stats.

Secondly, movement, the movement feels clunky. Dodging is the new mechanic to the series and is very DOOM Eternal inspired. However, I still feel like enemy hit boxes just ignore the very brief Iframes you get. A prime example is the tracking of enemy projectiles. Bosses will spray projectiles at you, making you feel like you're never out playing these enemies, but it often feels like you get hit more because of the mechanic, Husk cannons, Bloat vomit and a lot of the melee attacks from Skrakes, Fleshpounds, and bosses, still feel like they connect, skill issue or not. The fix for this would be to lower how aggressive tracking is, especially since so many enemies apply damage over time effects that eat your armour, once again ruining the economy of the game, along with upgradable armour tiers, it just feels off, another item to use money on, fighting over weapon upgrades, ammo resupply or the new dreaded tool system.

In addition to movement, the bosses, while cool in design, and make no mistake, I do like the art direction of 3. The bosses move far too fast. The new Scavenger boss is the worst offender, as not only does its melee track aggressively but the effect it applies that amps up its own damage vs. players and feels awful to play against as it gets so many free hits. Additionally, it's healing mechanic, where it consumes the gore left behind from killing its adds. Even after destroying the gore pile to interrupt it's healing mechanic, it will receive a huge heal and gain a buff. I assume it's a bug, but it adds to how awful the boss feels to fight with odd hitboxes on its melee attacks similar to the Chimaera boss.

Third and last of the glaring issues, I want to talk about the perks. Class identity was KF2's peak. I loved the fact that I had a favourite perk and I could list reasons for it. KF2's Firebug is my example, with a lot of Beam weapons or sprays that made enough fire to bathe the hoards, with some fun additions such as the Dragon's Breath trench gun or the Microwave gun that popped zeds like balloons. Commando was great in KF2 with the team passive to let them and your team see Stalkers. While added back to KF3's Commando, it's only the Commando player's vision that is affected, not the team. Support not being in the game but is now relegated to being a hybrid of Support/Demo from 2, except you missed the fun part where players could interact with the perks with Support giving ammo once per round and Demo giving grenades. This mechanic is relegated to a once-per-use ammo bag "tool". The Perks are missing so much of the utility and personality of 2's perks. They're all now Gun guy but with different bland flavours, Engineer gets one Grenade Launcher, and a laser gun that deals fire damage instead of it going to Firebug, and Firebug has a Plasma Launcher that looks like it was meant for Engineer.

Additionally, and the last issue with the perks is the perk Gadget/Ultimate/Super? These gadgets are just not fun. Some range from get out of jail free cards to just no fun to use. Commando just gets a drone that deals acid damage and follows you around. It's plain and deals acid damage? The drone feels like it should be just bullets or micro missiles or something that fits the class theme and fantasy of Commando. Acid damage feels like chemical warfare, perfect for Medic or Firebug. Firebug just explodes in an AoE around them, and that's it, it's an emergency "Oh no" button. Engineer becomes a mobile sound system that feels fun against small enemies but useless against anything larger than a clot, it's clunky and way too low damage for what it is. Sharpshooter is the first signature where it feels appropriate and is fun. Although it would be more fun as a crossbow, Ninja follows suit with a pretty fun gadget getting you into a fight with a grapple hook for enemies only. I just wish Ninja was just Berserker as I miss the really silly weapons they had such as blunt melee weapons and the nail gun. Medics just got a bubble heal that poisons zeds walking into it. It's fine and serves the "Healer class". Gunslinger is the newest and I don't have much to add other than, gravity grenades should be a globally purchasable weapon rather than their unique grenade.

All in all, these are my biggest issues with KF3, and what holds me back from recommending hoard/survival game enjoyers. I know my fixes aren't what the wider community may agree with, but I wanted to offer criticism and workarounds rather than blindly hate the game, because I don't hate KF3, I want it to do better, because I like Killing Floor.

review:
I do not recommend this game for several reasons, and here’s why:

The first and main reason is shader compilation. For two hours after launching the game, all I did was update shaders. I launch the game — shaders, press “play” — shaders, press “start tutorial” — shaders, finish the tutorial — shaders, press “play online” — shaders, open graphics settings — shaders, apply medium settings — shaders. Everywhere, even in the graphics settings, there are shaders. Even when switching from low to medium settings or back, shader compilation appears and takes about 5 minutes after applying the settings!!! This is horrible!!!

The second reason is optimization. On medium graphics settings with DLSS set to Quality, I only get 50 FPS, while both the GPU and CPU are loaded as if they’re “taking hot baths” at around 85 degrees. In the end, both GPU and CPU usage are almost maxed out.

To achieve stable 60+ FPS and keep the GPU and CPU cooler, you have to set DLSS to Performance with low graphics settings.

The third and final reason is the gameplay. It’s so “good” that, besides shader compilation, I didn’t see anything else in the game.

Final verdict: This game deserves 120 shader compilations out of 10.



Не рекомендую эту игру по нескольким причинам и вот почему:

Первая и главная причина, это - компиляция шейдеров. На протяжении двух часов после запуска, я только и делал, что обновлял шейдеры. Запустил игру - шейдеры, нажимаю играть - шейдеры, нажимаю "начать обучение " - шейдеры, заканчиваю "обучение в игре" - шейдеры, нажимаю "играть в онлайне" - шейдеры, нажимаю "настойки графики" - шейдеры, нажимаю "применить средние настройки графики" - шейдеры. Везде, даже в настройках графики эти шейдеры. Даже, чтоб поменять с низких настроек графики на средне или обратно, появляется эта Комплиляция шейдеров, которые применяются на протяжении 5 минут, после выбора настроек графики!!! Это ужасно!!!

Вторая причина - это оптимизация. На средних настройках графики с DLSS на качество всего 50 FPS, а видеокарта и процессор нагружаеются так, как будто принимают "горячие источники" под 85 градусов. В итоге загруженность видеокарты и процессора болбяться под сотку.

Чтоб достичь стабильные 60+ FPS и холодную видеокарту с процессором, надо ставить DLSS на производительность с низким качеством графики.

Третья и последняя причина - геймплей. Он настолько хорош, что кроме компиляции шейдеров в игре, я ничего кроме них не увидел

Итог: Игра заслуживает 120 компиляции шейдеров из 10



Я не рекомендую цю гру з кількох причин, і ось чому:

Перша і головна причина — це компіляція шейдерів. Протягом двох годин після запуску я тільки й робив, що оновлював шейдери. Запускаю гру — шейдери, натискаю «грати» — шейдери, натискаю «почати навчання» — шейдери, закінчую навчання — шейдери, натискаю «грати онлайн» — шейдери, відкриваю налаштування графіки — шейдери, застосовую середні налаштування — шейдери. Усюди, навіть у налаштуваннях графіки, ці шейдери. Навіть якщо змінити низькі налаштування на середні або навпаки, знову з’являється компіляція шейдерів, яка триває близько 5 хвилин після вибору налаштувань!!! Це жахливо!!!

Друга причина — оптимізація. На середніх налаштуваннях графіки з DLSS у режимі «якість» я отримую лише 50 FPS, а відеокарта і процесор навантажуються так, ніби «приймають гарячі ванни» під 85 градусів. У підсумку завантаження GPU і CPU майже під 100%.

Щоб отримати стабільні 60+ FPS і холодніші комплектуючі, потрібно ставити DLSS на «продуктивність» із низькими налаштуваннями графіки.

Третя і остання причина — геймплей. Він настільки «хороший», що окрім компіляції шейдерів я в грі нічого іншого не побачив.

Підсумок: Гра заслуговує на 120 компіляцій шейдерів із 10.

So Ive just played this game for 1 Hour. So Take that in mind, if you read my recommendation.
First it took like 20 minutes for the game to compile the shaders, till I could finally get into the main Menu.
Than I wanted to go into the Mission–Hub, which for any reason is now a Room in which you can also shoot at some targtes or watch your inventory/guns.
What is wrong about having a menu? And it ALSO had to load compilers for that lobby-room or whatever you wanna call it too.
So Game starts, compilers load, I want to start a Mission, Compilers Load.
Before I can start the first I have to do some sort of small tutorial.
Why? Why cant I just directly spring into action? What is all that useless crap?!
So after finally starting the first mission, it just felt so off. The Weapons dont feel as heavy and impactfull as before, overall the graphics, while being a bit better, just look more plastic than in KF2 and the splatter effects also seem to be a downgrade. The blood doesnt stick like it used to.

I mean they defenetly did a good job in taking everything out of the killing floor formular that made the game special and turned it into some frankenstein-game with modern gaming aspects that no one asked for or needs.

review:
A Disastrous Sequel – Worse Graphics, Terrible Performance, and Lost IdentityReview:

As a long-time fan of the franchise, Killing Floor 3 is a massive disappointment. Honestly, Killing Floor 2 might have come out in 2015, but it still looks significantly better and plays way smoother than this sequel.The graphics in this game are outright awful, and the performance is completely unacceptable. The shader compilation issues are a total nightmare. The game stutters so badly and causes such erratic hardware behavior that even my PC's RGB LED lights start acting completely crazy whenever the shaders load. I do not have a weak PC by any means, yet this game runs horribly. On top of that, the gunplay feels incredibly weird and clunky compared to the tight, satisfying mechanics of KF2.Ultimately, the game feels like it has completely lost its identity. Binding specific perks to locked characters makes it feel too much like a generic hero shooter rather than a true Killing Floor game. Additionally, the launch content is quite limited, the performance is plagued by frequent frame drops during full matches, and the cash shop was fully working on day one while the actual game still desperately needs polish. Save your money and stick to Killing Floor 2.
They need to call it shaders floor 3.
Rating: 3/10

review:
Don't wanna upset any of my friends who like this game, but its still ROUGH.

Shaders took 30 minutes to compile on an NVME and a AMD Ryzen 7, game runs at 30 - 40 FPS, movement feels float-y, there isn't much variety in how the A.I interacts with the players, (They kinda just run in a straight line towards them much like KF2)
the voice acting on the zeds, players, and trader are all very under played, (The scrake kinda just sounds like a regular dude now as opposed to a mental freak), and I can't understand what the story is or what's even happening anymore with the locations or characters, (Something from the Sabre Interactive days of KF2)... Also, completely subjective, but the Rocky Gray soundtrack is SUPER generic compared to zYnthetic's work in KF1 and KF2. I know he did a few tracks for this game, but...

Comparisons aside, this just isn't a good game (Yet) even outside of the pre conceived notions that it needs to be just like the other two and that it's just a bad Killing Floor game. I'd argue that it's just a bad game in general. Strip away the KF stuff, and you just got a DOOM bootleg.

To put it this way: If it wasn't Killing Floor, I would've gotten bored and uninstalled at the 4th compiling shaders screen.

Also, more importantly... Where's Kevin? And I ain't talking about the memorials.

review:
I don't like it. 

Guns guns guns :/ (I like guns but not these ones)
-the scale of the weapons are off
-the futuristic variants of conventional firearms and their attachments look horrendous and nonsensical
-some guns sound fine but the new deagle, for example, sounds like a cap gun fired through a paper towel roll (in another room)
-they give you too many attachments so there's this dumb back and forth where you have so many options but they're restrictive, conflict with one another, provide negligible benefits, or make you overthink the process entirely. Have fun reading 6 different ammo types each with 6+ different characteristics and trying to figure out what they do.
- Test out your weapons at the range? Nah. Here are flat inorganic targets that only provide one type of feedback: they fall down and get back up :^) 
-"weapon inspections" and reloads look like they were animated by hand one afternoon before lunch so they're awkward and stiff aka no kf2 mocap (no hate towards the animation team I'm sure they're swell people)
-also, what are we doing out here gathering scrap metal and chips lmao I'm out here fighting for my life but they need me to keep tabs on my pcpartpicker list

Visual clutter and awful feedback. 
Stylistically, environments look flat and lack depth. Similarly, it's hard to tell what's going on when the screen is filled with enemies, plumes of blood, gore, and explosions. I can't really explain it in detail but it makes me appreciate how well KF2 was handled. In addition, there are times when I know I'm getting hit but it doesn't even register in my mind as damage and now my armor's gone and I'm almost dead? I don't get it, man. A kf3 fleshpound waving its arms around and charging into me doesn't incite the same level of urgency that a kf2 fp would

Resource Management (it's a stupid loop that they can't even figure out)
It's like they added all of these special gadgets just to differentiate themselves from kf2 but realized too late that they needed to be balanced apparently??
For example, no more ammo crate spawns scattered across the map like in kf2 so anyone can drop an ammo bag. *BUT* you can only do that a finite amount of times per wave and per match for balancing purposes! What if none of your teammates dropped ammo bags or they wipe early and you're on your own? Uhhh, you can go to the one trader pod that's available and autofill everything in the middle of a wave if you have the money. [?????????????]

Movement
They had some trailer explaining how mantling and sliding was innovative. There's no momentum. You slide and then stop. You mantle/climb constantly but it's buggy, slow, and breaks the frantic pacing. Even the AI has trouble figuring out where to go.  If you're getting overwhelmed use a zipline I guess. KF2 had you staying mobile but it didn't need these gimmicks or have you pocket watching your teammate's multitools. If anything, adding all of this verticality just creates more problems and balancing issues

The Grind
On paper, you level up the same as Kf2. In fact, I kind of like the skill tree rework. Adding more skills and leveling them up more regularly adds some variation. The problem? You have to keep playing this game. 

Overall, I put the most time into commando during the free trial. Whose idea was it to make the only AK a high RPM bullet spray weapon that they personally recommend for close quarters? "Uh oh!! It'd be redundant to have a stopping power AK with a heavy Scar. If only there were other ways we could differentiate the two like in Kf2!" Btw, we added little pistons or w/e tf to the scar because it's da future :^) 

I never write reviews but you really forced my hand kf3 lmao I have so many thoughts on my short time with this game but I'm running out of steam. Apologies if there are any errors in this review but I also don't care. This is not a Killing Floor game. It would be fine/mediocre if it didn't have the killing floor name. Give it another 5 years and they'll figure it out, I'm sure.

So, basically, Kf2 is still a masterpiece.

And I still don't want it :\

Please, OG tripwire crew, make a new Murdering Ground or something
