review:
After playing the free weekend, I can say this game has potential but in its current state is mediocre at best. I have played a lot of killing floor 2 and can say this feels quite detached from it. Lets go over some things I like:

-Enemy animations can be pretty neat, with enemies from killing floor two getting new animation sets that are honestly very cool. Like the Siren's neck extending before attacking.
-Weapon animations and inspect animations are also pretty decent, a good chunk of guns feel good to shoot but some do feel slightly lackluster like the support's grenade launcher as its explosion feels quite meh. Could be due to my graphical settings however.


Now, what did I not like?:
This game doesn't really feel like killing floor. Sure you have a shop and open maps with hordes of "recognizable" enemies but the healing, multitool, damage systems, and other core aspects in previous games are completely different. I'll give some examples of what I am talking about:

-Your healing utility is no longer infinite. This makes medics a lot more necessary, even more so than they were in killing floor 2. I ran into a round modifier where enemies exploded on death and it tanked my health to the point I died due to a war of attrition to my healing. Additionally, when a player is reduced to 0 hit points they can still crawl and shoot slowly dying while waiting for a revive similarly to CoD zombies. I don't necessarily hate this, but it just feels off in a killing floor game. There was a cool execution animation on me from a boss though when I was down.

-Additionally the welding tool (aka multi-tool) now takes up a gadget slot. It doesn't weld doors but instead activates traps around the map like turrets. This is ok at best, I personally would prefer it to be available to everyone but its not terrible.

-The damage type system I honestly just don't like. Weapons have different damage types and you can modify them to change them with upgrades but there are so many it feels like I am playing an RPG. I can understand basic ones like chunking through armor or freezing and enemy then shattering them but damn there are just too many for my taste (9 to be exact that are all strong, neutral, and weak against something). This also makes boss fights annoying since every boss will have damage types they are weak to and damage types they are strong to meaning you are selecting damage types to fight a boss rather than just the weapon.

-The above statement ties into weapon customization and the selection of weapons available. Firstly, there is a pitiful amount of weapons (~5 different primaries and 1-2 secondaries per class). This is likely due to the vast weapon customization where you can create customization loadouts for each weapon. Attachments allow the changing of its damage, handling, damage type, etc. There is so much that it is just overwhelming and again feels less like killing floor and more like a shooter RPG. I went to craft an ammo type for a gun, and it even prompted me to select, from a list of ~20 options, a 3rd level bonus to the thing. That was for one out of 8 customization slots on 1 weapon. 

-The over complexity of the weapons ties into what I think is the biggest departure from the previous titles. In killing floor 2 the difficulty and progression came from leveling up and selecting a small amount of perks, learning what to buy when, how to effectively use different weapons, and the weaknesses of each enemy and different weapons may interact with them. These are all things you do by simply playing the game. Killing floor 3 feels like the difficulty comes from how well you can optimize your loadout outside of the game. Sure, learning when to buy what can be important but the fact that customization can drastically change and improve a gun and having it be so complex means that a decent chunk of your time is going to be looking at stats for upgrades to improve your gear. Kind of like an RPG. Add the new much larger perk tree onto that and you I hope can see where I am coming from.

-Bosses all look quite similar. I think its this new "mire" stuff they got. Its not bad and there is a surprising number of them but they lack the character and stand out looks of the first and second games.

-There is a battle pass. I am not a fan of paid battle passes in an already paid game. It could be worse, like with killing floor 2's loot boxes, but it does feel like battle passes are becoming modern loot boxes with how many paid games have them now.

-I also ran into a bug where the tutorial popup to use a trade terminal never completed even after buying from the terminal several times so all my games had that annoying popup just sitting in the top left corner of my screen.

I personally don't like RPG shooters very much. I want to play the game and learn it by playing the game, not staring at stats in an inventory screen. That's why I think this game ultimately is a departure from killing floor. The base simplicity of the original games where you focus on shooting the enemy and dealing with their antics has been replaced with complex RPG mechanics. Its an RPG horde shooter with the killing floor ascetic painted over it.
 
If you like RPG shooters where there is heavy customization and want to try a horde game out then you might like this game. If you are looking for an updated killing floor then I'm not sure if its the game for you. Maybe check back in a year.

People keep saying this is just the natural progression of Killing Floor.  Personally I disagree, after playing 1 and 2, this seems like they looked at CoD and said we need to do that.  Everything about CoD is why i"m playing KF for my zombie shooting needs.  The guns aren't real, they're just weirdly real shaped with tons of junk bolted on, and the movement is so ridiculous I feel like I should be wall running like I'm in titan fall again.  But I'm not.  
Now let's be clear, I checked the box for free receipt, I already bought this once and refunded,  I just wanted to see how it was during the free weekend of July 25th 2026.  And I came away lacking gunplay wise.  
Now, the Zeds, they were fun, the extended behaviors even at low level was a delight, the flesh pounds getting extendo arms, the scrakes pulling you in, the sirens getting more range on them.
That said they seem less human than they were before, and I know that sounds odd coming from this game where genetic modification is a big thing, but another big thing to the story is they pull people down into factories that change them, and they don't look like it anymore.  They look super clean too given all the mechanical stuff grafted onto them.
So overall, I will not buy this again. Maybe if they make a KF4 they go back to the roots, welding doors, slower movement, more methodical gunplay.  Also keep the wall climbing crawlers, that's been something I've wanted to see since KF1 and has been a blast.

I will buy this game eventually, when mayor updates are added and the gun repertoire expands, but as of now, this game needs to be put back in the oven for a good year or two so the devs can properly give an identity to this game and decide wether or not this game is part of the Killing Floor franchise.

review:
All right, I've played it. Based on what I (and many other fans of the previous games) saw from the reveals, the NDAs during the beta test, and the Specialists system, we didn't want this game at launch. Now that there's been a Free Weekend, I wanted to see if it's improved in any way.

THE GOOD

The game is slowly recovering its visual and audio identity. The Gunslinger perk was added and a few of the perks now have some of their iconic weapons such as the double-barrel shotgun, trenchgun, Desert Eagles, etc. DJ Scully and a descendent of Masterson joined the roster, adding MUCH-needed visual identity to a game full of random new characters. At launch, Mr. Foster was the only thing even identifying this as a Killing Floor game.

THE BAD

The game still lacks any sort of server browser. You can't find games in progress if you specifically want to squad up as opposed to being at the mercy of matchmaking. Normal had plenty of players due to the Free Weekend, but Hard was completely dead. The game lacks many pop-culture firearms and the visual identity of perks from the previous games. Where is the AA-12? Where is a traditional SCAR-H? Where is the M99 AMR? Why doesn't the Firebug get a traditional flamethrower? We don't even have a normal Fire Axe. Even if weapons function similarly, players want to play with weapons they recognize.

Decoupling the Perks from the characters (like they should have been from the beginning) was a good move, but I wouldn't recommend this game to any of my KF2 friends or new players.

review:
I mean its nothing like KF2 or KF3 it just shares the name. Actually kind of fun, for the first hour. Things to get rid of/add to the game to actually make it good:

1.) Get rid of the KF3 trash dialogue, go back to the basics, get creative and look back at what made KF1 so great.
2.) Trash the weapons,  they're soulless, get rid of the rarity system for weapons (this isn't Fortnite), bring back actual weapons or slightly build upon what is already available, KF2 did an excellent job with making guns sound amazing and addictive to use well, sound design is lacking in KF3, every gun just feels and sounds generic.

6.) Fire the DEI hires and get the original devs that made KF1 & KF2, keeping the current employees will kill this game further & sink your company to bankruptcy. (if you need help just look at the original founding employee pictures and find them and hire them).
7.) Add a community workshop system, this will add a ton of fresh ideas for which you can get with the modders and ask them if you can implement those systems into your game, maybe like a bounty, if it's good then they get x amount of dollars. 
8.) idk search for Killing Floor 3 on YouTube and just press enter and follow what the negative videos say, this isn't a hard thing to fix, you literally printed the winning blueprint from making KF1 & KF2
9.) Optimize this to run on actual user hardware not Nasa's computer systems, this should be priority BEFORE the game launched, it isn't our hardware, it is more your implementation on how you have structured the game.

review:
This is kind of bad,

Let's start with the good aspects:

> The game looks good, because of course it does, it's Unreal 5. 
> The new damage types In my opinion is a new layer of depth which can be used to learn to more effectively deal with enemies, because each enemy has weaknesses and resistances to different things.
> The gun customisation system, although insanely limited, is a good step forward for "upgrading" guns from the previous games' upgrade systems, which didn't change attachments or anything.
> The new bosses look good and I like the direction they took them. Especially because of how crazy they went with their size. In KF1 and 2 we only had humanoid bosses, but in this, it's beyond humanoid.
> Hot take but I do like the ultimates, I think they can help in a pinch and are pretty cool.
> The sliding, dashing and vaulting is welcome, even if movement still feels very clunky (like previous games)
> Cross-platform is genuinely goated and should be in every co-op game In my opinion, so the fact that they got it is very good.
> Code-based invite system is good, especially for a streamer that likes to play with viewers and doesn't want to bloat their friends list.
> Getting kills feels satisfying because of the crunching sounds and gore, which I can't glaze too much because it's a defining feature of the series, and is expected.
> The crawlers' crawling on walls is a genuinely good evolution of the enemy.
> The trader is far less annoying this time around. (I genuinely hated the french trader from kf2)
> Zed time happens WAY less often (in the previous games I would actually get kind of sick of zed time because it happened sooooo often, and I would very often get caught reloading for 48 real life minutes because zed time triggered)
> The battle pass system seems to be entirely acquirable for free, which is very based in this day and age.
> There are WAY more perks, which all can be upgraded. It definitely is an upgrade from the limited perk selection of the previous games.
> There is a solo offline mode (WOW). Another feature that used to be standard but now gets praised.

I wish I had more good to say about this game but that's it, really. Now for the bad aspects:

> Firstly, the game runs like * * *. It needs to compile shaders CONSTANTLY and takes FOREVER to do so. The game even crashed when I changed my settings at one point. My PC is aging, it's true, but I get dips to under 50 FPS on lowest settings during busy gameplay, which is unnacceptable. If your game can't run well, in this day and age of extremely expensive PC parts, then no one will play it, simple as.
> The enemies are a big thing to talk about. Their animations are janky, jittery and they move irregularly with no smoothness, which is such a downgrade from both previous games. Furthermore, their silhouette and color palette is incredibly similar, which makes them very very hard to distinguish quickly in the heat of gameplay. Most of the time I'm not even sure what I'm shooting at. Also, they gave ranged attacks to cysts, fleshpounds, scrakes, and more annoying rapid fire attacks to husks. I get that the player has better movement but this just become annoying incredibly fast. Another thing to talk about is the bloat and the siren, which became a complete joke in this game. They have such long windups for their big attacks that they never really end up doing them at all. I can count on my fingers the number of times I've seen a siren scream.
> I think the sound design is serviceable, what really really sucks is the voice lines (again). For the enemies voicelines (The very few zeds that talk, like the bosses, fleshpounds, scrakes and stalkers), they sounds absolutely terrible and are just complete cringe. Please hire a writer. And let's not talk about the character voicelines, oh my god. The character voicelines have gotta be some of the most uninspired, cringe, bad writing, marvel one liner sounding *** voicelines I've ever heard in my life. Please hire a writer. Atleast the trader isn't as annoying this time.
> The menus could be better. I think the menus are just "ok", for example I'm not sure why the trader offers multiple variants of weapons??? Why can't it be just >base weapon or custom weapon, this would avoid so much confusion.
> And talking about weapons, oh my god. The weapons don't feels grounded at all. I do not feel attached to any weapon I've used so far. And there is also so very few of them it's kind of crazy.
> No infinite, cooldown based healing? This completely prevents you from clutching as the last survivor unless you're lucky or play medic.
> The bosses are mostly just bullets sponges (Way more HP than previous games) and have no interesting gameplay mechanics tied to them. In KF2, bosses had different mechanics that differentiated them, like the patriach running away, matriach's beam and electricity, volter's gas, abomination's armor, etc. But in this game, there's not really any of that, or just a watered down version of what we had (Mooncroft) 
> The stronghold, although cool, is, in my opinion, completely unnecessary, and just adds more loading screens, more compiling shaders and less convenience. Everything in the stronghold should just be accessible from the main menu, so you can check the BP, armory, mission selection, perks, etc. and jump in the game right away.

This game needs a No Man's Sky level comeback, which will not happen. Makers of this game seems to only have a surface level idea of what a Killing Floor game needs to be and what the problems were with the series in the first place.

I say skip this and play the other 2 games.

review:
Even coming back to the game after it had some time to build itself back up from the disappointing beta via a free weekend, I still feel this game is a complete disappointment. The gunplay feels hollow with rather mediocre gun sounds, amateurish animations, confusing stats that are not intuitive in the slightest, and a, while admittedly thorough, ultimately half assed weapon upgrade system. With the visual settings, every environment looks very same-y, zeds blend in to the background due to poor lighting and character design rather than meaningfully implemented camouflage, combined with just, horrendous art style.

Every step forward, with perks coming with unique sidearms that you can trade out, deployable gadgets, a more in-depth skill system, and the aforementioned attachment system, comes with at least three steps back. Medical syringes are not rechargeable, like they were for every prior entry, instead being weirdly limited and not even healing you enough to be worth a limited supply. Random ammo drops are completely missing, instead requiring you to either bring a Supply Bag gadget, or visit a trader pod and dump cash into it to fully resupply, and even then this only works with bullets, not grenades like it did in prior entries. Melee feels slower and sluggish, with the directional combo system from KF2 returning in a much clunkier, less smooth feeling title, resulting in melee feeling more like you're desperately mashing buttons. It is nearly impossible to tell what direction Zeds are approaching you from, as not only do they make very little footstep noises, but they have a tendency to spawn merely 4 feet behind you when you turn around, making it feel less like you're being punished for not paying attention and more being given free damage as an excuse to make you panic, waste healing, or just cause frustration.

Overall, it is a miserable experience. I wouldn't even recommend getting on sale, just dont bother.

review:
KF3 is fairly fun and there's a lot of interesting redesigns/reworks of zeds, but it needs a lot of work to overshadow the staying power of KF2.
 
My gripes:
- Too much time on loading screens (+ the game can load in your character before your ability to control the character, so you can gain control after you're already swarmed)
- The base is a less functional, zero fun, dogshit ripoff of the Deep Rock ship, and you know it.
- Commando weapons lacks 'umph', making it feel like the KF2 Swat class with lack of high damage options, bullets noticeably weak even on the lowest difficulty.
- The lack of Demolition class is felt due to the lack of explosive weapon options, and the low-impact (umphn't, if you will) of explosives and weapons in general.
- My questline got bugged on the oil rig mission, and there's no way to remove the task icon burned into my screen on every map including those where progression is impossible.
- Pretty regular crashes, exacerbated by the extremely long initial loading screen, and 2 additional loading screens before you can actually play (to ship, and into a match).
- Party system broke twice for literally "unknown reasons". Brilliant.
- Generally poor optimization leading to regular frame hitches and dropped frames (I've got a 2070 Super, 6-core i5, running on an m.2 with plenty of RAM, and I'm running it on about the lowest settings)

Overall, KF3 remains pretty disappointing one year after release. There's plenty of little things I like about KF3, but I can't justify buying or recommending it in its current state.

review:
TLDR; Physical disk size is smaller compared to KF2 and other newer titles because they make you compile shaders every match/loading screen. Its KF2 but CoD'ified, more shops, stupid menus and other complicated methods of achieving the same goal. In any form or shape, if you want KF - Play KF1 or KF2. 

Not gonna rant about graphics, its just not that important compared to gameplay.

Played for 10 minutes ish... Compiled shaders for 30+ minutes - That includes after you've loaded the initial starting menu screen. You have to compile shaders every match/load that you do - I'd rather have a 100+GB game installed instead of increased loading times.

Honestly, its just like playing KF2 - But with alot of needless stuff added to the game. Things like a physical ship or something other (just like HellDivers 2, and you have to load matches - just like on HellDivers 2)

Everything happening in the game is essentially the same as the old recipe, waves, shop/trader, dosh, grenades, classes/perks and so on. The useless stuff added in my opinion is weapon loadouts? I dont get it, its not CoD, the only thing I do like about that is the fact you can change the actual "ammo" that you wish to use. It should just have been a KF2 remaster of some kind with these tiny functions added, maybe some other shooter stuff like which sights you like, ammo type, mag sizes, but not all of this skin shop extra shop, shop within the shop stuff. 

Sry for rant, I was just really looking forward to the next KF since I've played alot of KF1 and KF2.

review:
It's kf2 with better textures. Not much new, also it has an in-game shop. Full price game with in-game shop, LOL. Nope. Not worth the money.
1) Balance is "meh", just like in kf2. You can be blocked between enemies hitboxes and textures, even new dash mechanic won't save you to escape. Also dash is useless, you still will get hit, it has like 0.1% chance that you can escape, or only if you are chased by the most ordinary enemies.
2) Weapons. Quite interesting feature that you can craft your own weapons now and then buy it between rounds. But you will make 1-2 OP guns, and that's all. For bosses you may make guns that will have dmg type for their weaknesses, but it is not that important, because it doesn't do much sh!t.
3) With that amount of maps, this game is more like in alpha stage.
4) Bosses are better than in KF2, except for Moorcroft, because the dev team thought not to do a new boss, but to combine Patriarch and Hans Volter from kf2 in one boss in kf3. Lame. Good thing at least they make it heal from zeds and not players. But ffs, after you drop this b!tch's hp below 50%, he will try to run away every few seconds to heal, and he exactly like Patriarch has some jet engine up on his ass that will make him run fast asf. Your only hope in that moment is that "Adrenaline" will activate and in slowmotion you will kill him.
5) Anything you will do can interupt reloading, also sometimes the guns switch between themselves without you doing anything.
6) IDK if it was one time lag or the servers are made out of sh!t, but yep, it was once that I've got disconnected from the server at the end of the game.
7) Missions that "reveal" the lore, are boring asf. Because there are so few maps, you will run between them to do these tasks. And the lady will tell everytime "hmm, we are back here again". No sh!t sherlock, really? Also wtf is that new "mire" sh!t, the game doesn't explain while you do campaign, so go check the internet for answers, and tell me if you will find something.

Does this game costs money? If every cosmetic would be achievable through gameplay, yeah, but with in-game shop, ffs no, this is some f2p sh!t stuff with no actual in-game lore, why would someone want to buy it? Well, except the most fanatical fans, or someone who doesn't know where to spend it's money. I've spent that free weekend to achieve max lvl with 1 class, and still didn't, lol. And with that amount of maps, it is kinda boring, ngl. I have no desire to play that game for a while.

review:
I finally get to try out the game due to the FREE WEEKEND trials and I have a few things I wanna say:

-The game is badly optimised, even with my new laptop I've bought, where I can run games like BG3 and Ghost Recon Breakpoint on Higher graphics saddens me.

-The battlepass while not neccessary does make me realise what corporate companies does to beloved video games with this type of monetisation.

- At the start (First time launching the game) it took me nearly 45 mins of Compiling shaders before i could even play, meaning if I wanted to refund the game before I even got the chance to play I wouldn't...

- Walking around the "main lobby" while is interesting it does seem abit dull? Like theres nothing much to do in the base while it being so BIG.

- The amount of characters we have this game is even less than the first 2 games, I was excepting at least Dar or the Punk lady the be here, but alas. At least we get Foster and Bill's grandson and Skully?

- Not gonna lie, I kinda wished there were more bosses or call backs to the older bosses. Dunno if it's lore related but I miss the Patriarch and his stupid banter.

- The med stims now costing money to use and only having 3 charges feels cheap, Dunno why they made this change when the first 2 games handled it pretty fine. Since you can get overwhelmed by enemies and having no stims is an instant death,

+ Tho I will miss the French merchant, bringing back a british merchant is nice

+ The interactions for vaulting, climbing, sliding, side dashing and Ziplines make mobility much better so thats a plus!

+ The new gears we get are much cooler as well and add more diversity to tools which is nice I guess?

+ I'm loving the new character designs, even tho the Cyst look like uncircumcised weenies, most of the designs seem like an upgrade, ESPECIALLY the Stalker. . . I'll head out now

Overal the game is pretty mid, I hope the devs see that and try to fix their mistakes before KF3 just gets shutdown or something. It has potential, just not in the state it's currently in. . .

review:
Man, I tried, I really wanted to give this game a fair chance, but it just wouldn't let me. I made at least a dozen attempts to play and every single time, this thing would either crash or give me a "Connection lost" error. This is not an issue on my end as literally everything else works perfectly. I even went the extra distance and did some troubleshooting to try and make this work. But it didn't and I never even got to start a match. 

So, sorry! I wanted to give this game an honest chance and write a fair and constructive review afterwards, but I wasn't given the opportunity to. All the """"playtime"""" you see was spent on loading screens and compiling shaders. So many damn shaders. Takes over 20 actual real life minutes to start the first time. And after all that, the game still loads in with missing textures and assets still not loaded in. Absolutely horrendous.

And since the only thing I managed to reach is the stronghold, let me talk about that I guess. There's nothing wrong with having a diegetic menu where you interact with the game via an actual location in it with all the menus being terminals and devices you go to and use directly. Warframe, Deep Rock Galactic and Helldivers 2 all do this wonderfully. But all of those games do this thing where once you boot up the game, you load directly into that location so you can start doing stuff right away. Why is it that here you go loading screen -> compiling shaders -> loading screen -> main menu -> click play -> loading screen -> compiling shaders -> stronghold -> go to terminal to start mission -> loading screen -> compiling shaders -> connecting to host. Why??? And then the main menu has an "Exit to title" button. What title? Literally nothing exists before this. You want me to go back to the image of the Fleshpound? I got to stare at it enough while compiling shaders, thank you. So many failures of basic game design. I guess going off of this, I don't know if I can expect anything good from here on out.

Oh, but I do know that the pop-up advertising the battle pass popped instantly and it had no issues taking me to the screens where I can spend some real dosh. Of course that would work perfectly.

And by the way, do you want to know what the error in the crash log states the issue was? Failed to load shaders. It spent over 20 minutes just on the first instance and then several more minutes later loading shaders, but I guess that just wasn't enough. There was still more shaders it couldn't load so no game for me. You can't make this sh!t up, I swear.

So is the game good? How's the gunplay? The progression? The characters? The gameplay loop? Are all the veteran players saying that it sucks correct? I guess I'll never know for myself. But going off of this unfathomably terrible experience and the fact that text chat had to be added months later and treated as a major update, I think I have a pretty good idea of what to expect and it seems I'm not missing much.

They say first impressions are the most important and this has been one of the most abysmal experiences I've ever had with a game. I've had better luck running shareware Unity asset flips made by some drunk Russian in his spare time than I did with this. I wanted it to be good, I really did and the state of affairs makes me sad, but I can't deny reality. And the reality is that this experience has been inexcusable.

I paid no money to give this a try and I still feel ripped off.

F#ck this game.

I'm going back to Killing Floor 2, I need to wash this bad taste out of my mouth with copious amounts of Zed blood. I suggest you follow me there.

review:
Played the game on a free weekend to give it a swing after hearing nothing but bad things since launch.

It doesn't feel like a sequel in any capacity. Compared to previous entries, there's only flaws. Lack of weapon variety, no endless mode at the time of this review, an iconic class like Gunslinger took a year to release, and maps are poorly laid out.

The biggest downgrade is the UI/UX. There's an extra layer of menus added both outside the game and during a match which causes gameplay to feel slower (which is another problem, stiff gameplay). Do you want to get attachments for your gun? Gotta go to your armory, click through each class and weapon to see what materials you need to farm (EIGHT DIFFERENT DROPS), THEN you're allowed to finally make a loadout. This lets you buy it ingame after navigating the new trader UI which has, you guessed it, another menu on top of the first one.

Killing Floor 3 as a whole feels both dumbed down and overdesigned to mask the poor gameplay and even poorer art direction. If you're expecting a very simple and straight to the point horde shooter, I would suggest Killing Floor 2 over this everyday till major changes happen.

review:
It's just really, incredibly mediocre.  I only need to disconnect from my first game and finish my second to tell that this just ain't it.  Something about Killing Floor 3 doesn't feel like "Killing Floor" and I can't quite put my finger on it.

Performance is honestly abysmal with little change in graphical quality while changing the settings.  The movement feels incredibly floaty and slow until you crouch-slide?  Crouch-sliding from some reason is INSTANT in its response and weirdly tight and rigid for a game that feels like you're walking on ice.  Instead of using your knife or the sprint to move the fastest, you now crouch-slide and jump everywhere.  Most weapons function exactly the same despite playing different classes with just a different element damage or just physical.  The lack of healing other players on a TEAM-BASED GAME is such a stupid design decision.  Limited syringes for self healing compared to a static cooldown is extremely harsh and forces at least one player to be Medic, instead of playing their way.  Enemies are laughably easy to fight and evade, especially thanks to the sliding.  

The only thing I think is actually really good about the game is the designs of the zeds this time around.  They all look fucking awesome.

review:
★☆☆☆☆
Fun times, staring down your ugliest developer for 30 minutes, to a 30 second loop of techno-metal, while shaders pre-compiled, just so I could test the latest entry in some mid franchise that wasn't even good decades ago

★★☆☆☆
The game itself is basically just a worse version of CoD Zombies.  That might have been acceptable as a source mod, nearly 20 years ago for KF1, but KF3 is nonsense.  


[h1]Reasons to Buy:[/h1]
- meh, I tried it on the free weekend, doesn't seem worth 40 bux, maybe 5, if they fix the shaders  

[h1]Reasons to Bail:[/h1]
- Shaders, Shaders, and more Shaders! 
- Game breaking matchmaking bugs, game breaking performance bugs, game breaking quest bugs
- KF3 is woefully under developed.  Its just the wave defense mini-game from every other modern game, with no actual game attached.  Class design is equally lacking.  

[h1]Nitpicking & Biased:[/h1]
+ Non-Reload Reload Animations
+ Looks like battle passes last forever
+ Specials have finisher animations, they should make that their actual mechanic
+ You can pick your character/specialist and bonus gun without being class locked

+- Lite parkour 
+- Rare Random Slowmo
+- Some of the shotguns are almost satisfying
+- Flashlights look so meh in modern graphics
+- You can close doors, to stall enemies for like 2 seconds...
+- Lite talent tree, which is too lite and unlocks about 2x too slow
+- You can kinda customize weapons, but you still hafta buy into them each round
+- There is a decent number of maps, but they're mostly just vanity flavor, and don't really provide different experiences
+- Classes exist (are for some reason called Perks), but are super minor, they should give the abilities 100% uptime to actually change playstyles 

- No party HUD
- Armor makes no sense
- Limited multi tool ammo
- Matchmaking is nonsense 
- Many a game breaking bug
- Boss on wave 6 instead of 5? 
- Can't join or respawn mid-match
- Pointless lobby that lets you open the menu... 
- Probably the worst attempt I've ever seen at a story 
- Froze/Crashed multiple times, while compiling shaders
- All these daily/weekly quests amount to "play the game wrong" 
- Guns don't auto reload until you manually attempt to fire when empty.  
- Game barely manages 60 FPS on low, and like half that on every other setting
- There are turrets, preset around the map, with sad CDs, and u can't put your own
- Ziplines shoot you in the wrong direction, and then have a cooldown so you can't get back 
- There are randomly waves where all enemies explode on death, so that's super viable as a Ninja

review:
[h1] Loading Floor 3 [/h1]

Tried it due to the free weekend promotion by Tripwire and after playing for roughly 45 minutes, I can understand why this game has mixed reviews on Steam and never took off the way it's predecessors did. 

[h3] The good : [/h3]

- Music is amazing. KF3 continues it's tradition of heavy metal music which fits the games fast-paced, chaos action perfectly. 
- The re-designed zed designs are good. With Killing Floor 3 taking place in the future, the cybernetically enhanced versions of classic enemies like the Fleshpound, Scrake, and Siren feel like a refreshing evolution rather than a simple redesign. The Scrake, in particular, has gained a new ability that pulls players toward it, reminiscent of Scorpion's iconic spear attack from Mortal Kombat, adding an extra layer of threat during encounters.

[h3] The bad: [/h3]

[b] - The first-time launch is atrocious.  [/b]

My first launch took nearly 20 minutes. Sure, the Fleshpound artwork on the loading screen looks great and the metal soundtrack helps pass the time, but asking players to wait that long just to start the game for the first time is simply unacceptable.

The fact that shaders will load at every launch taking a few minutes and even then the in-game lighting looks bad is just another addition to the series of issues KF3 has. 

[b] - The characters are bland. [/b]

One of the things that made Killing Floor 2 so memorable for me was its phenomenal voice acting. Every character had a distinct personality, and you could tell who they were just from the way they spoke. 

Killing Floor 3 has lost much of that personality. I played two matches as Mr. Foster and was genuinely surprised by how little he spoke. The sarcastic one-liners, terrible jokes, constant complaints, and obsession with dosh that made him such an iconic character are all gone. Instead, he's left with generic, supposedly witty dialogue that lacks the charm, humor, and personality that defined him in Killing Floor 2.

[b] - The gameplay is poorly optimized. [/b]

In the two matches I played in KF3, my game crashed the moment my character died and my match ended. I verified the integrity of the game files after each crash, adjusted my graphics settings, and tried a few troubleshooting steps, but nothing made a difference.

According to the game's Steam page, my PC meets the requirements to run Killing Floor 3 on the Low preset. Even so, the experience was borderline unplayable. The Zeds often appeared blurry, gunplay felt janky and unresponsive, and performance tanked whenever the action became even slightly intense. Every encounter with a Husk was particularly frustrating—I knew my frame rate was about to nosedive to around 30 FPS, making the screen a chaotic blur. More often than not, I'd be dead before I could even process what was happening.

[b] - The guns look rubbish.  [/b]

The weapon design in Killing Floor 3 genuinely frustrates me. It feels far too similar to the design philosophy found in many modern, microtransaction-driven games, where a single weapon exists in multiple purchasable variants that differ only superficially. 

Killing Floor 2, despite all its flaws, earned its loyal fanbase—myself included—because of how exceptional its weapon design was. Every gun had a distinct identity. A Desert Eagle felt worlds apart from an assault rifle, not just because of its damage, but because of its recoil, animations, sound design, and overall handling. Every weapon was satisfying to use, and every shot carried a sense of weight and impact. For a franchise built on brutally satisfying gunplay, that's a significant step backwards.

[h3] Conclusion.  [/h3]

I was able to try Killing Floor 3 for free, so thankfully I didn't lose any money—only the roughly two hours spent downloading, installing, adjusting settings, and troubleshooting a game that ultimately allowed me to play just two matches. However, if the question is whether this game is worth purchasing with real money, my answer is a definite no.

Killing Floor 3 is currently a hot mess. Its launch was already riddled with issues, and even after being available for over a year, many of the problems still remain. 

The characters exist, but they lack the personality, the enemies are present, and the shooting mechanics are functional, but the combat feels hollow and incomplete. The pieces are there, but they fail to come together in harmony to create the experience KF1 and KF2 did.

Unless Tripwire addresses the game's stability issues, improves performance for mid-to-low-end PCs, and brings back the personality and identity that made Killing Floor special, Killing Floor 3 will continue to feel like an unfinished product rather than a true successor.

review:
My first impressions with this game isn't great. I spent practically my first hour and a half compiling shaders, crashing twice while shaders compiled. My pc has fallen behind in modern day, greatly after UE5 became mainstream so take some of this with a grain of salt.

The shader compiling in this game immediately almost made me uninstall because of how frustrated I had felt waiting that long to compile shaders, only to have to compile shaders again the second I changed a single setting which also caused my second crash.

The gunplay is okay, I don't really like it all that much and they don't sound amazing. This does suck a lot in a horde shooter though as you'd think with such a heavy emphasis on consistent fire into hordes of enemies the guns would feel as good as shredding gore would be.

The animations in this game are REALLY fucking weird, sometimes they skip and jank, enemies will occasionally T-pose for a frame. A lot of animations just look unfinished and bad, and due to some odd game design choices they also just don't look very good for telling you what attack an enemy is doing at first glance.

This game is REALLY fucking aggressive with its projectiles and often times taking damage feels unavoidable due to almost every enemy in the game having a way to shoot a projectile that does a certain effect at you. Cysts can spit at you, husks constantly shoot projectiles and spawn a fuck ton. The husks alone are seriously really fucking annoying, shooting mortar attacks that can be impossible to see when dealing with hordes and suicide bombing you on top of just naturally shooting at you. Sirens can shoot you with projectiles that seemingly can't hit other zeds, mess with your screen, and slow you down making them REALLY fucking annoying on top of everything else. Scrakes can now straight up grab you and fleshpounds will destroy you for merely existing. Bloats are whatever, they've always been the way they are but at least have a good visual cue for when you should get out of the way.

Being able to climb ladders and mantle is a nice feature that makes the game feel fluid, but holy shit you will eat damage for just trying to run or climb. The other movement features added such as sliding and dashing is nice yet they feel jank and unreliable. Sliding feels kinda weird, would be nice if they had leg models you could see, which would give cosmetics more prominence and make sliding at least visually cooler. Dashing is nice for getting out of small attacks but sometimes I feel like its just fuckin' useless and makes you eat damage. I've had times where I SWEAR I dodged something perfectly but the enemy will do a sudden 90 degree turn and hit me anyway so I have to go fuck myself.

The difficulty in general is pretty harsh, and is really rough for someone playing during the free weekend. I feel like I can't play on any difficulty other than the beginner one due to just how hard the difficulty in the game spikes. Classes feel incredibly pathetic until you get them to a way higher level, which I don't remember being as bad in prior titles? I could be remembering things wrong though. The additions of the crafting system and upgrading not just your class, but your guns is pretty cool but holy FUCK dude the amount of grinding this game is asking of me feels crazy just so I can shoot some zombies.

I don't mind the purchasable content, it's a norm nowadays and if it at least means we can get more content in a killing floor game I can let it pass. Since the game is on sale, once I get paid I likely will still buy this game. It's not awful, but it's weird and I know its BETA period was really bad. I think in some ways it improves from KF2 but also shoots itself in the foot in comparison. The game is still worth checking out, but do not expect remotely the same experience you got in prior titles.

Its kinda fun once you get into it. But uhh...

The software is awful, running overkill anti-cheat on a game that is lucky to hit 200 concurrent players is laughable. The frame-rate cap is controlled by a slider that... dynamically changes the frame-rate? It took me 5 minutes to set my FPS to 120 because the game would stutter as it updated my frame-rate while I was still moving the slider. There's numerous small issues like this that cause the software to feel clunky and dated, even though it shouldn't be dated.

Speaking of dated, the movement feels off. The dodge has a weird delay or cast time to it, the sprint feels like I'm trudging through mud, the slide is twice the speed of my sprint for some reason, and I'm able to vault over walls twice my height faster than I'm able to sprint or slide. This is early access beta levels of slop that would normally be fixed by full release, but this game is in full release.

Then the game itself, KF3 does an extremely poor job describing their mechanics and conveying information to the player. Stumble, toxin, panic, sonic, UV. The audience can intuit the general vibe of SOME of these effects by the name, but the audience shouldn't have to. These effects and their tooltips should be easily accessible. There also needs to be a detailed log for the enemies, describing what they do, what damage types they resist, their movepool of various attacks, all of this other stuff so players can look forward to crafting their build appropriately. Right now, players are guessing or hoping someone on Reddit knows more.

Game is okay. and if it was released in Early Access today with plans to release in 2 years, then I might be more optimistic, but this is an extremely disappointing product that soils the Killing Floor name.

review:
KF3 ain't a Killing Floor game.

I really tried to like this game. I played the beta and thought it felt awful, but I gave it another shot after all the improvements, hoping it'd change my mind. Unfortunately, it still doesn't feel very good.

The biggest issue is that it just doesn't feel like Killing Floor. The Husk is completely overtuned, while Scrakes and Fleshpounds have almost no presence, blending into the horde instead of standing out as intimidating threats. The Zed AI still gets stuck on each other, guns lack impact, and the gore and ragdoll physics are a noticeable downgrade. Even loading into the game is frustrating because of the long shader compilation times.

Some of the new mechanics also hurt the overall experience. Executing Zeds breaks the flow of combat, and removing the syringe takes away the teamwork of healing your teammates. The shop feels barebones, and the damage type system is far more complicated than it needs to be without adding much depth. All maps feel very small; I'm not sure why, maybe because of the parkour system? Before the boss spawns, the game reveals which boss it is, ruining the surprise and even revealing its weaknesses.

Even after a year, the game still feels unpolished. I wanted to enjoy it, but it misses too much of what made the previous games so satisfying. It may be called Killing Floor 3, but it doesn't feel like a true Killing Floor game.

I genuinely hope the game can make a comeback, but so many of these mechanics and design choices are deeply baked into its core that it would take a massive overhaul to fix them. At that point, they might as well make another game instead of trying to change what already exists.

[h1]How far Killing Floor has fallen...[/h1]

One of my favorite titles which I've been playing since KF1 turned into a jack of all trades, master of none.

Everything in this game is a huge mess of bland MEH, and what's not a meh is plain sh*t. 

Let's break it down.

[h2]Gunplay and Shooting[/h2]

Used to be THE BEST thing about this game where it felt so smooth, so precise to shoot any gun. Now it feels like I'm trying to fight the recoil of the weapons in order to maybe put 20% of the mag into the weak spot of ZEDs. (exluding no-recoil weapons like the MP5SD)

[h2]Weapons[/h2]

Guns feel week af. Unloading a ful mag of dual Desert Eagles into a boss' face and the boss doesn't even flinch.

Almost all guns I tested in all classes have incredibly weak sounds [b]except shotguns[/b]. It's like they are all the same sounds and they just tweaked the EQ to yield different sounds for different guns, almost nothing is unique.

[h2]Movement[/h2]

All this sliding, dodging and I am still UNABLE to successfuly dodge majority of attacks from the bosses and SCs/FPs unless I seek cover behind an object. Dodging in Darktide for example is PERFECT in comparison.

Movement speed is painfully slow and constantly forces me to spam sliding and sideway-dodge like a super-excited and a little r*tarded fortnite kid.

[h2]Classes[/h2]

First and foremost, WHERE THE F IS THE DEMOLITION CLASS? It is literally one of the most fun classes of all time in Killing Floor games and you decided to not even put it in the game!?

My favorite class during the testing of KF3 was Engineer due to the shotguns and being able to use the environment to your benefit, no other class felt right.

Gunslinger was the worst of all classes I tested. How come pistols have so much recoil? Go shoot some guns in the shooting range, devs.

[h2]UI and Performance[/h2]

I am excited, I was about to be playing KF3 for the first time ever in this free weekend. I downloaded the game, I launched it and... [h3]THERE IS 40+ MINUTES OF SHADER COMPILING AND 15+ MINUTES AFTER I TURN ON ULTRA GRAPHICS.[/h3]

WHAT THE F- ?!?!?!?!?!? (BEFORE YOU ASK, YES, I HAVE THE GAME INSTALLED ON MY M.2 NVME SSD)

The game only runs smooth with high/ultra settings if I have frame generation on, otherwise I have to go medium to low to reach a comfortable FPS.

I'm not going to devote much time to type out a lengthy review of this one. It's just not worth the time and effort it would take. 

The good: I like the fact that perks have more in-depth skill trees. Guns feel nice and have good feedback. Graphics are decent. Movement feels less stiff and clunky. you can slide. Gadgets are also a neat addition.

the bad: several perks have been removed and their utilities given to everyone. Melee hit-zones feel janky AF, especially when I'm dodging directly away from a Skrake and STILL getting hit. You take fall damage in between waves now. Which is dumb. and the thing that killed it for me most, even when playing on a free weekend: I should NOT have to wait on shaders to compile literally every time I open the game or try to load into a match. Shader caches are a thing for a reason. Stat pages also need more detail. I want to see how fast my weapons will apply afflictions if it isn't just guaranteed on every shot like it used to be.

In my honest opinion, just stick with Killing Floor 2. Or play Darktide. Better horde game overall.

review:
I came in expecting Killing Floor. You know, waves of horrific monsters, over-the-top gore, and that magical feeling of barely surviving by dumping an irresponsible amount of bullets into everything that moved.

Instead, I got what feels like a committee's interpretation of what someone who'd never played Killing Floor thought Killing Floor was.

The guns somehow manage to sound both loud and disappointing. The enemies have all the personality of damp cardboard. The UI looks like it lost a fight with a mobile game, and every menu feels determined to waste just a little more of your life before you can actually play.

Performance is an exciting minigame where the true boss isn't the Fleshpound—it's your GPU wondering what crime it committed to deserve this.

The atmosphere traded gritty horror for "generic sci-fi hallway #47," and somehow the soundtrack has the energy of someone reluctantly doing overtime on a Friday afternoon.

The saddest part is that beneath the layers of questionable design decisions is a game that occasionally reminds you why you loved the series... before immediately tripping over itself again.

I'd recommend Killing Floor 3 to:

People who thought Killing Floor 2 had too much fun.
Fans of loading screens.
Anyone looking to test whether nostalgia can physically hurt.

Overall: 4/10. The only thing getting slaughtered faster than the zeds was my excitement.

I made this review using ChatGPT, which probably took more effort than the devs put into the game

review:
I played a lot of KF2 in the past, and I was optimistically excited for KF3 when it was slated to come out. Due to the messy launch, the issues it had, and the other games I had to play in my backlog, I never got around to trying it out. So with this free weekend, a whole year later, I figured I'd give it a shot and see how well they spent the last year fixing and polishing up KF3 into a fun game to experience. 

Unfortunately, the game is not very optimized. It takes 10+ minutes to compile shaders on boot up only to still chug and studder as you load onto the maps. Even the lobby hub devoid of zombies fails to run completely smoothly when you first step foot into it. You can have a perfect connection to the their servers, but the game will find a way to screech to halt with only players and a boss model on the map. you can tell it's their unoptimized code because the game suddenly runs smoothly whenever the slow motion of zed time triggers. The same amount of objects present flailing around just likely far less interactions and physics for the game to chew on. 

I remember the rough launch of KF2 and how it took them a while to iron it out and figured KF3 might also need time in the post-release oven, but it seems a year later this just isn't a fun experience. Some maps run ok, but others run like a slideshow presentation. Forget whether or not the game has made any improvements or interesting changes to the formula, Multiplayer matches just don't seem to run smoothly at the best of times and are unplayable at worst of times. It is a shame that this game feels so unfinished and rough that it is hard to judge the gameplay underneath. 

In the end, I am going to go back to playing KF2 whenever I have the urge to fight waves of zombies. Maybe in a year or 2 if they have another free weekend, I'll check back in and change my mind, but as it stands now I am fighting against the game optimization more than I am fighting the zombies.

review:
Played on the free weekend.

[h1] TLDR; [/h1]
[h3]
Just pass on the game. Nothing really changed since playtest/beta one year later. Same horrible optimized game with EMPHASIS on PAID PREMIUM CONTENT BUT MAJORITY OF BPS ADDED ARE JUST RESKINS AND CHARACTER LOCKED.

Basically they take priority on MICROTRANSACTIONS over the actual functionality or QOL of the game.

Also, I don't care about all those die hard KF fans. Not an early access title stop giving me every KF game ever came out had a horrible x year start and gets better after the 10th year.

Anyways. I'll play the free weekend but it's not a game I would purchase unless like a 90 percent discount. 
[/h3]


It's just as bad as it was in the playtest/beta.

The optimization is extremely poor. The settings don't warn you when you need to recompile shaders. Spoiler Alert. If you change any graphical setting it requires re-compiling shaders so don't do it in the middle of the mission or you can't cancel. The initial shader compilation doesn't include compiling shaders when you launch an actual mission/load into the base. 

You basically have to recompile shaders twice before getting into the game and if you make any graphical changes. Also, if this game has a major update have fun re-compiling shaders each time.

I say poor optimization because I change the settings to be on High and saw no difference in Low settings in FPS. Just way lower resolution graphics at the same FPS.

Nothing really changed. BP is a worse version of the BP from HD2 but tries to get the same success. Literally almost everything is locked behind the paywall in the BP. It just says PREMIUM PREMIUM PREMIUM. Also a lot of the skins are just reskins but character locked. Not much variation. There's no point in getting a Premium BP unless you are a die hard KF3 fan. The additional cosmetics are mediocre at best.

Uses EAC so assuming there's no offline mode. 

I basically saw no difference between playtest/beta. Overall, horrible optimization and shop works first before anything else. Yes, the shop was fully functional in the playtest/beta. Which tells you where the devs put their priority first. And you can see many people who own the game have the issue where devs can't optimize add QoL content in the case first cause not enough time. But they have all the time in the world to add more reskin cosmetics/battlepass items. 

Overall, KF franchise to me was kind of the mindless killing type of game but that's all there is too it. They didn't really add anything new to the formula. They added a different system from KF2 but the real KF fans will give you those details.

review:
I ask Tripwire Leadership: 
Please stop chasing trends and wider audiences and come back to your roots, why you are here as a company to begin with. Give us a return to origin game, a simpler, polished horde shooting experience with no super high tech over engineering dystopia, the original KF was contrast, blood on cement, metal, grime, faint fires and cinematic flares? Well stick to it, maybe set the game in the 80's and 90's with SAS and Special Forces soldiers, less gadgets, less fluff, more REAL guns and Mayhem. 

Honestly I am at a loss of words, as a long time KF fan I didn't expected the game to be this downgraded in everything from the previous two titles but here we are. I didn't thought honestly that the absence of original team members could make things this worse.
I got to know KF from the version after the mod, the standalone Killing Floor 1 release, I was excited about it, a game different from left 4 dead, a game with no pretenses, seemes just a fun and fairly original horde shooter and couldn't wait to get my hands on those guns of the trailer. 
The second game came many years later teasing us everyday with pieces of the trailer on KF1 lobbies, we were going crazy for the waiting, they promised us an upgraded experience in the technical side and they didn't disappoint, we jumped right onto it. And altough there was a bit of a loss of identity when it comes to Art Direction, there were many other factors that made the game fresh and fun.

Now when the third trailer hit I was appalled by the presence of ''glory kills'', further loss of identity straying away from a grounded KF1 ''dread and dirty'' experience even more, with crazy sci-fi pushed to 9000, still, I was excited and hopeful even tho that Fleshpound animation got me worried, he looked like he had no weight while in the air.
Trailer after trailer it got worse, culminating in ''Ultimates'' for heroes and the removal of perks, I distanced myself from the game completely.

Free weekend comes up, people say they fixed a ton of stuff, reworked a lot of things and added more grounded weapons to the mix. I launch it, try to play between constant shader compilations issues two matches and then turn it off, I try few other matches the day after and turn it off.
Honestly baffled, feels like a different, simpler game with a lot of fluff. There is a loss of physicality when it comes to bullets and interactions with zeds, almost like all weapons are raycasting isntead of having a physical bullet like the other two games (not confirmed) but it's these small unpolished things that maybe new players cannot understand but still perceive as ''unpolished unreal shooter'' that hits and decapitates this game.
For me tho the biggest turndown was the weapons, sci-fi presence everywhere and the need for everything to be high tech and overengineered for no reason.

This is a 1st person arena shooter game, of gamers versus various NPC (non-playing characters) undead thingies.

Unfortunately the game Still feels unfinished in its current state, although this is the second weekend I get to test the game. 

The graphics are weirdly not that much better, than in the previous version of the game (released in 2015), while this has been released in 2025, and yet there are some glaring mistakes; game-mechanics-wise.

The controls feel oddly off, as if the integration of the controls package from the previous game version, didn't quite cut it this time. Perhaps it is just the graphics, that is affecting the way the game feels, not quite sure, but on the whole this version doesn't feel nothing at all like the previous Killingfloor 2 game.

Well aware that in order to make a successful new version of a previous game, you Do Need to make some sweeping changes, otherwise what's the point in making a new game version. The problem I ran into was mainly that the graphics were slowing my input lag (when you press a key or move the mouse is input), and this meant that I wasn't feeling as if I was a part of the action, but just some bystander unable to contribute to the team, as I usually do in the previous version (Killingfloor2), which means I feel like a burden instead of someone a part of a team.

At least in the previous version of the game (Killingfloor2), I had absolutely No problems at all, with graphics of game-mechanics, or actually contributing (usually in the top half of team contributions) to the teamwork. So I cannot say that this game is an impruvement (how it sounds no more oo's) on the franchise, since this new release has little in common with the previous version. Sure I haven't played it enough to have any insight into how the new perks, skills, and so on actually work, simply because the hill to climb to get there, is far to steep.

If you have played Killingfloor 2, and you really want this game to be alike to the previous version, then you will be sorely disappointed, since there is extremely little left from the previous version, but if you are coming into this game without any preconceptions of what it is supposed to be like, then you might have a great time.

Input-lag, Graphics-lag, odd movement, odd enemy behaviour, I cannot say for sure what it is that I disliked the most, but I never got the chance to find out more about this game, since that was enough for me to say; No thanks, might give it a try again, if a free weekend comes around in a year or two, but as it is now...no, just no.

review:
I had hoped for a redemption arc.

Let's start with the shaders.  Before the game opens, it compiles shaders.  Then, once the game opens, it compiles shaders again.  Then you press a key to start - and it compiles shaders again.  Then, once you're in a match, it compiles shaders every time you load a new level.  I genuinely don't know what Killing Floor 3 is doing with all those shaders, but whatever it is, it isn't worth it.

The graphics, once you finally see them, are okay.  Just okay and dated.  Nothing about the presentation justifies the wait or the overhead.  The style is bland and generic.

Then there's the gameplay - the part that's supposed to make other issues tolerable.  It doesn't.  Weapons lack responsiveness.  Movement feels stiff.  Combat doesn't feel good.  I tried a variety of weapon types hoping something would click, and nothing did.  It's a horde shooter, which is a fine enough premise, but the execution has to actually be fun for that to work.  This isn't. 

The meta-game is thin based on what I experienced.  There's weapon progression and possibly other systems I didn't dig into - but nothing I encountered made me want to.  Stutters and pauses during gameplay don't help, and loading times throughout are longer than they should be, sometimes significantly so.

There are plenty of shooters that feel good to play.  Unfortunately, this one doesn't.

review:
I just tried the free trial version of [b]Killing Floor 3[/b]. As someone with over [b]2,000 hours[/b] in [b]Killing Floor 2[/b] who also ran a community server for years, I was really hoping this game would be a worthy successor. Unfortunately, after playing the trial, it felt more like a step sideways than a step forward.

The graphics are definitely an improvement, and visually the game looks good. The weapon customization system also seems solid from what I tested, and the skill system looks promising. The user interface is fine as well—nothing outstanding, but it gets the job done.

My biggest issue is the gameplay. Character movement feels heavier and less responsive than in Killing Floor 2. Running, changing direction, and overall movement don't feel as smooth, which makes combat less enjoyable.

Another thing that really surprised me is the class system. Unless I missed something, it seems you can no longer switch perks during a match. Why remove a feature that worked so well in Killing Floor 2? That change doesn't make much sense to me.

The sound design was also disappointing. The weapons don't have the same punch and satisfying impact they had in Killing Floor 2, making gunfights feel less exciting. On top of that, the atmosphere didn't grab me the way Killing Floor 2 did. The previous game felt darker, more intense, and had a stronger horror vibe, while Killing Floor 3 feels less memorable in comparison.

Another major disappointment is the lack of dedicated/community servers. As someone who ran a Killing Floor 2 community server for years, this is one of the biggest steps backwards in my opinion.

Community servers weren't just a way to play with friends—they were a huge part of what kept Killing Floor 2 alive for so long. Server owners could create unique experiences with mods, custom maps, special events, and custom server settings that gave players countless reasons to keep coming back. I personally hosted custom maps on my server, and they added hundreds of hours of replayability beyond the official content. Without dedicated servers and community-created content, I'm worried Killing Floor 3 will lose one of the biggest reasons why Killing Floor 2 remained active for so many years.

This review is based only on my experience with the free trial, so my opinion could change as the game receives updates. However, in its current state, I won't be buying it. Right now, it doesn't feel like an improvement over Killing Floor 2.

I genuinely hope the developers continue improving the game because I want Killing Floor 3 to succeed. If they make the movement feel smoother, improve the weapon feedback and sound design, bring back the ability to switch perks during a match, restore support for dedicated/community servers, and continue polishing the overall experience, I'd be happy to give it another chance in the future.

that will surely end many runs unnecessarily, but you can do it during a round, so if you train them correctly I guess it is possible. 

Weapon upgrades seem pointless, you no longer get more damage, you're just supposed to use a more expensive gun. It seems like it might be tied into customization, but that's way too deep for a KF game and reminds me of gachaSlop, just add feature after feature, item after item, its so tedious and boring. I want to shoot shit and upgrade my damage, or get a new gun thats clearly better in most ways. 

The first few games felt decent, but that was mostly a bit of excitement, and copium. ADS sens. multiplier is 50% by default for some reason, which did make the game feel much worse during the tutorial. Which is weird considering the game is meant to be played pretty fast, with its COD slide and vaulting. I also feel like maybe an FOV change would have helped, but I honestly didn't need to go into my video settings, the game played pretty darn well without any hiccups for the 3 or 4 games i played and died in. (Oh nvm it did crash right after tutorial lol)

Perk upgrade unlocks are LOL, they unlock a single tree upgrade every 2/4 levels, and it's just... lame lol. very odd choice. 

I get some people will like it, well steam charts may say otherwise, and maybe I'm getting old, but it was trying too hard. Why in my killing floor game am I choosing between 6 different ammo types? And a whole list of other weapon mods? leave that for Insurgency sandstorm / tarkov / arma. 

Also was not expecting to get a grenade launcher when the first 2 guns of engineer are shotguns. No description for the guns makes for a bad experience. You try too hard in the wrong places, and fail to get the simplest stuff right in others. Also that lvl 1 bullpup shotgun should never have that much recoil. What are we smoking? 

It's exhausting, but I'm glad y'all let me try it out for free. It unfortunately confirmed all my suspicions. 

Theres definitely some great work in here and it sucks that it all combines to make something I dont enjoy. I feel like giving the company my money won't accurately reflect my respect for some of the cool shit and the work that went into it. So I guess all I can say is thanks for trying.

review:
I'm probably gonna continue to play a bit just because I love the franchise so much, but I can't in good faith recommend this game to others, and I only got it because it was on deep sale with HumbleBundle.

First off, I actually can't get it to run on Windows, and of all things, it was actually Linux, CachyOS in particular, that was the only way I could get the game to run. Well, on Windows it [i]would[/i] run, but every time I try to join a match it would crash to desktop with the error saying it had something to do with "shaders", which sucks because this game makes you wait a long time to compile shaders, like about an hour for me almost, just for it to consistently crash due to the shaders you just waited an hour for compilation.

When people say "the performance is bad" they're not kidding. On my ryzen 2600+rx580 w 32gb ram with the game and OS installed on separate SSDs, I BARELY get 60fps at 1080p with dips sometimes to the 40's, with every single graphics setting minimumed out, AND FSR in ultra performance. If I don't use FSR, i get ~25fps with everything minimumed out completely. So it's a situation where I absolutely MUST use the FSR to even run the game at an acceptable frame rate. The problem is that the artifacting of FSR on ultra performance mode is absolutely terrible, and zeds in the distance shimmer and blend in with the pixels around them almost like MGS stealth invis camo or something. Essentially, you can't see threats well beyond ~20 meters with FSR on. I know a 580 is hardly a powerhouse in late 2026, but just logically speaking, compared to other games of this visual caliber, there should be absolutely no reason that I can't get 60 frames with settings fully minned out with no FSR. If you have a really fast rig I guess you can ignore this, but this game has objectively terrible performance compared to other titles of the same visual caliber, never in all my gaming years have I ever had to enable ultra performance mode FSR or similar with everything minned out JUST to get 60 frames. 

The combat is kind of "meh", and husks are absurdly OP to the point where they're extremely annoying. Mainly because they can fly now, and they're programmed to take the high ground, and they can do shit like just fly up on the roof of a 10 storey building and just potshot you from the high ground with exploding husk balls. Their suicide attack is now jet powered, and they just fly towards you to self destruct, so it just ends up feeling a lot more cheap with everything they do, and it really does feel like the balancing is wayyyyyyy off. Gunslinger is also way too OP. "Normal" difficulty is honestly actually a little too punishing.

There is a bug where syringe bags I left on the ground were destroyed when I used an AOE ultimate nearby them. In the menus, with all settings on minimum as aforementioned, the game has problems loading in textures and models. So like for example, you'll go to the pre-mission screen where you pick your character and your loadout and things, and the game for some reason will only load in the gun, when it's supposed to be the full character holding the gun, so you'll just see this floating gun. Or sometimes the gun and the players head will load in, but no body, so you have a floating head and a floating gun - it just honestly looks and plays so half-baked in this regard. I also have been downed and while waiting to get revived, my "bleed out state" had no gun visually, so it's like my character is laying on his back with his one hand out in last stand shooting his pistol, but the pistol isn't even there visually. Half baked.

Overall it's really rough, and I also worry it may go the route of B4B and just fall off and go into maintenance mode early. Also, Scully is too cheesy, and Foster sounds dumb. Scully is the same voice actor it sounds like, but his lines are just really cheese. Foster is a different voice actor and it's "just not Foster". Only Masterson is the only character that has that classic feel, that proper cheekiness.

Heads up, if you DO get this game, there's a chance you may have the issues I had where it wouldn't even launch a map without crashing, so be aware, you're gonna chew up your 2 hour return window waiting for the game to compile shaders. If you go into graphic settings and change things, it's going to REcompile the shaders, further eating up your 2 hour return window, just a word of warning. You might have to dual boot CachyOS just to get the damn thing to launch a map

review:
Marked as obtained for free since I'm playing during the free weekend.
tldr: It's Killing Floor, but connection issues are preventing multiplayer shenanigans

Graphics: COMPILING SHADERS. Lordy, the initial install takes several minutes after booting up the game to complete. This is, sadly, common with newer games, so it's difficult to single out KF3 specifically on this. The environments are beautiful and gory and I have no complaints with the lighting or shadows. 

Sound: I don't believe that this has been updated at all since KF2. Guns fire, bones crack, and there's the wooshing sound when zed time activates. I use a gaming headset and not a super sound system, so maybe that's related.

Characters: I haven't played many of the playable characters, but from what I can tell, they have a few voice lines for any particular situation, so an experienced player will know them by heart, no doubt. I've seen comments that they differ from the KF2 PCs. Admittedly, 7 PCs a year in is pretty mediocre.

Classes/Perks: Commando, Medic, Firebug, Gunslinger, Sharpshooter, Ninja, Engineer. This is notably lower than KF2's perk count, and the weapon options for each class are a little barren. This is mixed with the weapon modification system, which enables a decent amount of variety even though the weapon selection is a little neutered. Classes now come with an additional sidearm/gadget that recharges instead of needing ammo, so you have an option for taking out enemies if you've run out of or are rationing ammo.

I really enjoy Ninja, it's a fun time of swinging katanas, tossing shuriken, and more. Those katanas have a damage reduction, which is a little silly logically-speaking, but is well appreciated. You can block with melee weapons, which the ninja makes heavy use of.

Mechanics ---
In-Match Shopping: Clean interface, easy refill-all button. I like that armor can be bought in 25-percent increments now. This makes armor much less of an all-or-nothing deal. During a round, while shops are closed, you can still refill your ammo at any shop. Instead of using an equipment weight system, you instead have two primary weapons,  which is roughly what the old system was like anyway. Also, weapons in those slots and in the secondary slot are auto-sold when you buy any other gun/configuration. BE SURE NOT TO BUY AMMO FOR A WEAPON IF YOU PLAN TO REPLACE IT. You always get a few mags of ammo for the new weapon, so you'll probably want to refill that. Armor is the same deal: when upgraded, it's refilled to 100% durability, so definitely don't fix your armor before upgrading it.

The Multi-tool: Goodbye my beloved welding torch. It's been replaced with a computer doohickey that can hack turrets, open doors, and open containers. It's... fine. I like having turrets. You can still close doors, but there doesn't seem to be a welding mechanic to keep the zeds out. Just a few hits and a door gives out...

Crafting: Enemies and the new map destroyables drop components, which can be put into making weapon mods. These mods can be set into loadouts, which enable you to buy a specific set of modifications for your gun in the in-match shops instead of the default modifications. It sucks that you don't start the match with these weapons, but alas.

Matchmaking: Choose a map, a length, and a difficulty, and hope you find people to play with. I've seen other folks complaining about player counts, but I didn't have much issue finding other players,  probably due to the free weekend. No, the issue is in actually starting the match. I waited, readied up, for a few minutes and saw no luck starting the match. I'll try a few more times later and update with how that goes. For now, I'm a bit disappointed.

Misc notes:
- No option to upgrade your perk while you're in a lobby. If it's there, I missed it.
- Party system is broken. I was unable to connect with my wife to do multiplayer until I joined her lobby using the same search terms she did. We both have cross-play on, but are using the PC version anyhow. If it matters, she's using Linux. I'll be trying to party with other friends this weekend if they accept my invite to play the game. 
- I like the wave mutators. They're made really obvious and bring some variety to the table.

The game just feels like KF2 with a few new environments and less content. In a lot of ways, this game seems to be analogous to Payday 3. Maybe Half-Life 3 shouldn't ever come out...

review:
In an hour of gameplay, at least 75% of that was waiting for shaders to compile.

The first time I booted up a match, I thought I was going to get right into combat. Only to find myself in an awkward main hub area? And had to bumble around for 10 minutes to find the "mission control center", which was a big computer, to actually start a mission. Horrible first impression already, after the 10 minute shader compilation to boot into the menu, just to have another round of shader compilation to boot into the hub area. Where I then got hit with another round of shader compilation once I decided I actually wanted to launch a mission. Jesus christ modern gaming f*cking sucks; by this point I could've already played 2 matches of Killing Floor 1 or 2.

Game is incredibly bland, generic, and underbaked; it feels completely soulless. It's just so completely un-offensive, and toothless. Like most Triple A games there is a stronger emphasis put into paid cosmetics than the game actually having a solid gameplay loop. The game also seems to follow a live service formula of seasonal story telling; kind of like Destiny 2. And yeah I just don't even fucking care; no one has time for this shit. And if your going to do it, it better be the best in the industry. And this is not even close; which is why it has hardly garnered any attention.

The story missions / seasonal story missions follow a similar formula to COD Cold War zombies. Collect thing, NPC talks to you, says go collect another thing, you pick up an audio recording, guy screaming in pain, NPC makes comment about how his death sounded painful or something. It almost comes off as parody; but in reality it's just a complete lack of self awareness.

Speaking of COD; yeah the movement and gunplay feels like it's also riffing on that. But it feels horrible, floaty, and inconsistent. In Killing Floor 1 and 2; you didn't need hit markers to be able to feel the impact of whatever weapons you were using. In Killing Floor 3, I understand why it's enabled by default, because weapon impacts feel hollow. Ragdolls are instantaneous and because of that there is no physical momentum that is felt when you hit something.

I feel bad I even wasted my time trying this game for an hour when I knew it was going to be slop. So yeah, don't buy it, and don't waste your time trying it. Because it f*cking sucks (in my opinion).
