Yes another free weekend review, except Im not gonna be entirely negative!
Positives!
Game runs fine I suppose I can't really comment on it because of my goofy ass intel gpu and not playing this game on this system before, some maps run worse and microstutters gallore but It's probably because of my other applications (i had medal recording the game so that was probably why) 

The classes actually feel kinda cool, sure there 100% could be WAY more but they all feel unique and interesting.
The ultimate abilities or whatever they're called in this game are INSANELY fun, especially the sharpshooters ability.

The enemies I actually really enjoyed, sure it's not at ALL like the other 2 killing floor games gameplay and visual wise but they really addressed some issues with those games. Like the fact u NEVER had to move ur mouse up and down, that's now an important part of aiming with crawlers going on walls, more verticality and husks being able to fly a little as well as dodging which is SUPER enjoyable and makes the combat more tense and fast paced

The guns felt great (besides the flamethrowers but those kinda always feel worse compared to other guns) they look amazing, sound nice and have great animations, devs have always been good at that stuff.

Negatives! (oh no)
First of all the compiling shaders bs like cmon this is UE5 we shouldn't have to do this so often also it should not take NEARLY as long. (It took me 35 minutes to get into a game) Compared to STALKER 2 the compiling shaders is like 150% longer than STALKER 2 and that game not only looks way better but has more shaders in total.

My main issue though is the lack of weapons, sure modding your own is cool and all but it's not nearly as enjoyable as looking at a gun and going "wtf is this?" buying it and then going "wtf is this" and then deleting a clot and once again going "wtf is this?!" (also its really unintuitive) 
6 guns per class simply isnt enough (i dont count the dual wielded secondaries)
If this game was f2p or like 10$ I'd say its worth your time the current 20$ sale isn't horrible but this is one of those games you play for like 5-15 hours and never touch again.
I'm unsure if I want this review to be negative or positive but simply because of the existence of KF2 being like 2$ on every sale I'm gonna go with a negative review, I want the devs to continue working on this game it has potential but they're gonna need a miracle to make this as popular as kf2

review:
I wasn't interested in KF3 till free weekend and tried to approach it with open mind but so far... it's just... a soulless imitation. Someone took a look at worst aspects of KF2 (tactical leds) and thought 'hmm what if we made the entire fucking game like that? oh whatever was trending in last few years and slapped it into game'.

- CoD movement/gunplay, no KF DNA so much. Weapons do not have their identity anymore, its whatever you slap together to milk out higher stats per UNIVERSAL BIG NUMBER = GOOD cancer that was dragged from destiny. Most of them are hideous, just slapped with tactical LEDs or vents/heatsinks... why? 
- Heavy level & resource investments, you can no longer just pop into a class and try more difficult matches. Higher difficulties are effectively time gated thanks to this - if you try to play on higher diff you will actively drag your team down, simply because your gear sucks - oh and your buddies can't drop you weapons. Grind!
- Gameplay wise wise it feels like DOOM Eternal but graphically it feels like Back 4 Blood in worst its meaning; the enemies look like they were made all to be foreskin nightmares and they do not look distinct anymore. Scrakes, fleshpounds and husks are all grey flesh & metal blobs that look the same from a glance, something you had to go out of your way to fuck up with "new and improved redesign". Crawlers crawling on walls are really cool so big ups for that, however their animations/behavior is so fucked half the time they just look confused.
- Health injector no longer regens, now its a consumable item - WHY??
- Weight system, which was a cool balancing factor, with KF2 upgrades somewhat balanced, now Tripwire decided it would be too complex for MODERN AUDIENCES(tm) and you have two primary slots with secondary slots.
- Elements are a cool idea as a mechanic but in practice it sucks since you can't swap classes and some classes do not have that type of damage (got electric daily quest or weakness? "go drop traps lol" this is dumb.), using weapons on classes not intended for them feels wrong but, then again, the classes feel so detached from KF its more like a hero shooter than KF. At least I have to compliment the perks being greatly expanded for classes, but the classes feel meaningless, so uh...
- Foster no longer resembles KF1/KF2 chap, Skully thankfully untouched, Masterson is just Grandson now and the rest of characters look like they belong in Concord.
- Physics reactions make no sense most of the time - enemies etiher do not react to hits or get flung 50 feet back from a pistol.
- QA not present, developers depend on suckers-- i mean CONSUMERS to find bugs, ton of jank within tutorials and anim transitions
- battlepass that gives you free shit at first that quickly paywalls you and gives you just the stickers, lol. This is a paid game, and even on free weekend I feel like I got robbed.

End result is a parody of itself that would be more befitting to be played in a background of a movie/GTA as in-universe joke game. Maybe it wouldn't be bad as a free game. But this is something many people paid money for and I have no clue who it was made for - clearly not for fans of KF1/KF2. Despite my harsh words and criticism I don't hate developers - I know first hand both on inside and outside the current game development stage is a shitshow. A lot of effort was put by developers who worked hard on this game but ultimately was squandered due to poor leadership or investor meddling. Maybe something would clear up if one would take a look at credits for KF1, KF2 and KF3 to figure that out, but clearly that's something beyond a steam review.

Get it in few years when it's going to be less than $10. If you are new to KF series, try KF2 instead.

review:
$40 for a game where you spend almost (if not more than) half of your time compiling shaders really is a bold artistic choice.
i should preface this by saying that i am running this on linux with an rtx 3070, and nvidia is not known to have particularly great vram management in their linux drivers. i am additionally experiencing a performance degradation compared to windows in dx12 games. *however.*

running something on the lowest settings with dlss set to performance has no reason to saturate all of my vram and cause the game to drop to single digit framerates after minutes of joining a match. i have tried various commands on protondb to some amount of success, but the performance remains incredibly poor. i am consistenly getting below 60 when there is pretty much anything happening on screen. this is not acceptable.

gameplay wise, it's fine. it's a more than competent horde shooter minus the fact that you can tell this was not designed for solo play in the slightest. everything moves far too fast and you are not left with enough resources to keep yourself alive unless you are on top of everything at any given moment. for the series though, this remains the weakest of the bunch.

really the only positive thing(s) about this are the file size being shockingly small at 22gbs, and the soundtrack being decent. aside from that, what is actually the point of this game existing? killing floor 2 goes on sale for like less than 2 dollars. that game runs properly, looks fine enough, is stuffed to the brim with content you don't have to pay a dime for (minus dlc weapons in the latter half of its life), and is a generally more cohesive, engaging, and fun experience. the only major pain point is that it clocks in at almost 100gbs for a title that released in 2016.

if you have the space to spare, save yourself the money and just go buy the dramatically superior prior entry. if you don't, buy left 4 dead 2 or darktide or something. this is flat, bland, and not worth your time in its current state.

Should have been free to play from the get go.

The Bad:
The amount of guns is only 5 per class. You can't use different perks guns with whatever perk class you want to play, so it feels very limited in what guns you can use. There's no secondary guns to choose from for most perks, perks being your class. You also only get 3 uses from those tools as well.

The Good:
The maps are decent, and the zed movement makes them tricky to hit sometimes which is good. Zed redesign also looks cool. They did bring back some of the legacy movement and in that i mean when you pull out a knife you run faster, i think you also run a little faster with the pistol out vs rifle. review:
I absolutely adore the first 2 Killing Floor games, they were always a little jank, but I put hundreds of hours into each of them. Both of them were fine wines that took a bit of time before they really came into their own. KF2 in particular I remember being pretty rough on release.

So with that in mind, I had seen the reviews of KF3 and all the controversy on release and it made me a sad panda, but of course I decided to wait and hopefully given a little more time the shine would start to come through.

[b]Well friends, it's not there yet...[/b]

I installed it over the free weekend with an open mind. I'll say this up front - it loves to compile shaders. The first time you load the game on the title screen - excellent, now I'll have smooth gameplay (I am genuinely supportive of this), Then it compiles a pile more if you change graphics settings, then it compiles a ton more when you go into any loading screen for a level, and elsewhere also. It seems to happen all the time, everywhere, and sometimes it's nicely integrated and other times it makes the screen flash like a strobe for some reason. Grim.

Anyhoo, fine, lets change my resoluti... oh wait, it doesn't actually seem to support my 4k screen? Highest resolution I could pick was some awkward not quite 4k. There's some options for FSR, but it won't tell me what version it is.

Right, whatever, lets play. When it comes down to it, here's the deal. It is in some ways, fundamentally similar to the old games, and there are cool new ideas in here, but really it only took one match to have the veneer rub off.
[list]
    [*]It has mouse acceleration and smoothing by default and there's no way to turn it off without going and doing some random ini tweaks - it feels HORRIBLE
    [*]Despite the excessive shader compilation, I still get stuttering in game and animation jank at times
    [*]The guns can sound great, but the music (which was AWESOME in KF2) seems utterly generic and flat, and the general sound design of enemies etc is weird
    [*]The new loadout and shop system in-match probably just takes getting used to, but I am struggling to come around to it
    [*]The gun design isn't inspiring - for reasons I can't explain, none of the guns look or feel as cool as before
    [*]The setting is all techno-future, and honestly the further it leans into that, the more I'm turned off
    [*]No server browser? Really?
[/list]

There's more I can't fundamentally express - the game just doesn't [i]feel[/i] right, and I saw enough weird bugs to start to annoy me. I think it can be rescued, but to me, they haven't nailed the feel of the game yet, and maybe more fundamentally, I'm not feeling the art style / setting etc in the same way as previous games. Will come back in a year or two and see how it's getting on.

review:
Remember when KF2 came out and we all thought it was the worst thing to release given its clunky state, strange sci-fi departure with the original setting, but over time it's one of the more popular KF titles? 3 is kinda like that except it hasn't escaped the clunky state.

KF1 is my favorite, and I liked 2 quite a lot, I think the evolution of the setting grew on me. 3 was sort of the same: In the first playtest I wasn't thrilled about the characters locked to classes (Which they eventually fixed) or the small weapon pool (Which has grown. KF2 had the same issue). But the game ran well, the evolution of the Zeds design is legitimately cool, and I like the bosses. But then the second play test came out, and the game just ran horribly for most everyone. Confusingly, it released like that.

Fast forward [i]years[/i] later and a lot of the main gripes of KF3 are actually fixed, following a similar trajection of redemption that KF2 experienced (but I guess we all decided to forget had happened). There's just one teensy tiny ever to important detail: 

The game just doesn't run? Not well, anyways. 

It doesn't care how far you clear the Recommended settings or what your setup is, you need to tank most all graphic settings to cope with the usual UE5 slop and maybe you can hold 55-60 frames at 1080p. They've really brought it home with more classes, maps, weapons, etc etc (And naturally the Battlepass store that's worked flawlessly since Day 1 is, of course, completely fine lol) but they really seem to skip around the issue of [i]the game just not running[/i] for many, or sluggishly for most.

So ultimately it's not the former fun bandwagon hater reasons I can't recommend KF3, it's solely because it barely runs, and you can see in plenty of other comments and online threads that's the single most common denominator here. The game's legitimately fun now and they really concisely addressed a lot of feedback and improved the game, except for making it work. I'm so tired of UE5 games, man.

The dodge feels odd but I guess I don't mind it for dodging the husk shots. The visuals and lighting effects of some weapons is GPU burning bright. The sound mixing on the stalkers makes them incredibly loud compared to every other enemy.

I see what they were going for and I'm not into it. It feels like a heavy injection of the Call of Duty formula but not the COD Zombies side of it, just the pvp movement shooter stuff. Go play KF2, the servers are still up.

I knew KF3 would not be great, KF2 was already a downgrade from KF1 in anything but graphics so i was expecting the same with this game.
I was not aware how bad it truly was.

Completely different weapon feel, way more complex bullet spread paterns and recoil that you need to control.
Enemies move much faster and have special attacks some that you cant dodge, and when low will start sprinting at you.
Everything is consumables now, so you will run out of your 3 syringes quickly and cant heal. Then you have to buy new ones for next round. A completely useless and annoying micromanagement that did not need to be there and adds nothing to the game.
The game also runs horrible, even on the lowest settings with worse graphics than the second game it cant keep a stable fps. 

Everything in this game boils down to the question ''does it add to the game'' and if the answer is no, they added or changed it from the previous games.
I highly recommend not buying this slop. Would not be surprised if the entire game is made by AI.

The BAD:

-GAME IS HORRIBLE UNOPTIMIZED IT WILL KILL YOUR PC UNIRONICALLY, COMPILING SHADERS WHENEVER YOU CHANGE A SINGLE OPTION.
-Weapon customization that makes it so the gun just shoot better instead of doing anything interesting, you can even make your gun shoot better by putting on ugly scopes

-Gunplay is awful, recoil is separate from visual recoil

Turns out they made all cosmetics tied to certain characters instead of being a catch all for everyone, so if you want foster you have to unlock the exact same skins as the other characters FIRST before you can reach the Foster page. review:
I got this during the free weekend, and I got to say, not a fan of it. 

However I will get into what I like:

The sound design of the enemies is fantastic when I heard the audio of certain Zeds it did make me jump and ready to fight that Zed. The designs of the Zeds themselves look also phenomenal and were improved, especially the Siren, when their neck grew that kind of made me jump.

What was mid about it was the music, it's just generic metal music, not as iconic as Killing Floor 2, but it quickly had me turning on my own music pretty instantly after hearing it in my brief playthrough. The map designs was strange, but exploring was interesting to look around

The parts I don't like:

The gun designs. They are way too big and bulky to be believable to wield, and even then if they look like they did pack the punch then it would mean something, and the revolvers while looking cool felt like hitting anything above a common Zed with a wet noodle. 

The progression was also changed to add more passives, however it still felt as limiting as I looked through and saw how the perks were within the first hour. Killing Floor 2 did have a really basic "this or that" perk tree, but they also had a bit more customizability with you being able to rank other classes as well as the class you was playing as. While I played as the Sharpshooter I grabbed an Engineer's pistols because I liked how they shot and felt, but I saw post game I didn't gain any experience in it, which will make the game in the beginning for those classes such way more to play as when you play. The maps with ziplines with a cool down for some reason, which I think is a dumb idea because well doesn't make sense.  The woman talking to you during the game was annoying and quippy for something uninteresting. Felt more like they written what one person in the office thought was funny while everyone else groaned hearing it. 

Also the map selection is much smaller than the previous game, which is a down grade, I always believe a game should launch with either equal or greater amount of maps the previous games have, and they for some reason got rid of the survivalist and a proper melee class. Why? Why limit the ways people can play this game?

The slow down mechanic I wished was changed instead of just being the same as Killing Floor 2. It would of been cooler to be able to control when you go into slow down to make it to where you use it when you either need to line up a shot, or avoid danger. instead of just randomly in the middle of a boss fight somehow slow motion while the boss was doing the weird phase out thing (I was fighting the chimera)

Also the fact they added a battle pass to this game, which can we just abandon this? I would of preferred if they just added DLC to add the skins as bundles instead of just of a battle pass, but the fact that you have to pay for the game, and then pay for a battle pass is scummy. 

TLDR: Game is ass because it got rid of features and gave a battle pass that made Killing Floor 2 fun

review:
tl;dr Happy anniversary. The new Tripwire team is heading in the right direction. But please get a dedicated QC team. Make a good game first, then add the sprinkles.

The game is clawing it's way back from the grave, but honestly, I still think it's need more time. Please find my observed bugs and issues below.

First off, introduce a (disabled by default) mouse acceleration setting please. It's 2026, this should've been an accessibility setting and off by default.

Mantling / vaulting is awfully nauseating. That perspective snap to 0 the moment you mantle shouldn't happen so abruptly.

There are some UI scaling issues, particularly with a tinkered safe-zone, where the UI doesn't scale properly, causing things to overlap, especially during a match lobby.

Also what is up with the shader compiling? Never has a game asked me to compile this many times before. Game boot? Compile shaders. Change graphics settings? Compile shaders. Change FOV? Compile shaders. Coming back from a match? Compile shaders. What the hell man.

And aside from some technical issues and hiccups like the sometimes totally needless shader caching, occasional disconnects mid-game, the game itself is everything, and anything but a KF game. It tries to be several things like Doom Eternal at some point, but that aspect and attempt also feels like a toned-down Temu version. The whole core and base of the game just feels like inferior in every aspect compared to KFII, having said that, KFII still beats the hell out of this one, and I still find that one more visually appealing over this one, and also from a gameplay perspective as well, KFIII just feels bleak and empty. Every map, encounter, boss-fight just feel tedious and boring. The game simply lacks the soul to pull you in. While I have many-many hours in KFII, I just simply couldn't bear this longer than 88 minutes. It's just simply doesn't have that click that would keep you locked in on the game to get you keep playing more. Even though it's a free weekend, I still feel like being robbed and mugged, robbed of my time, robbed of that 88 minutes. Even the current discounted price of 17,99€ is way too much for this mess. A realistic price would be like a cd-key for like 2-5 EURs tops, and that's it, and I'd still feel robbed anyways. If anyone still wants a fun KF experience, I'd suggest picking up KFII instead if you haven't already do so, and if you don't mind the bit outdated graphics, KFI is still pretty damn fun and a solid choice alongside KFII.

review:
I wanted to love this. I've put hundreds of hours into KF1 and KF2, and I was hyped for years waiting for this. What we got barely feels like a Killing Floor game anymore.

The Zeds are still Zeds, sure, but that's about the only thing left that's recognizably "Killing Floor." The gunplay itself is the biggest letdown, it feels loose, inconsistent, and honestly kind of dull. Weapons don't have the punch and personality they used to; recoil doesn't match the feedback, some guns sound like they're firing compressed air, and the whole shooting loop feels like it was copy-pasted from a generic modern shooter and then reskinned with familiar monsters. Take away the Zeds and the setting, and you could tell me this was any other soulless co-op FPS on the market.

And here's the part that really gets me: this is 9 years after KF2, on a supposedly next-gen engine, and I honestly have a hard time telling which game looks better. The lighting feels flatter, the color palette is a wash of grey and brown, and the environments don't have the atmosphere the old maps did. Nine years of "progress" and it doesn't even clearly look like an upgrade.

And then there's the monetization. A day-one battle pass, a premium currency, and a season pass structure repeating every quarter. This isn't just a full-priced game anymore, it's a live-service shell wearing a Killing Floor skin so Tripwire can chase engagement metrics.

It's not a horde shooter with soul. It's a spreadsheet designed to maximize monetization, and greed has hollowed out a franchise that used to actually mean something to its community.

Skip it. Go replay KF2 instead.
name: Killing Floor 3

review:
Now thanks to a free weekend, I understand why this sequel was panned. Coming from Killing floor 2, graphics and levels are sterile. Gunplay feels weightless, the damage your guns do to enemies feels like there's no impact.

The gore is toned down. Bodies are less convincingly sliced and diced apart. There are fewer levels of flesh to strip away and bodies once killed cannot be interacted with and shot further. It's just sterile, that's the only word that fits. Almost as if they wanted to cater to the cellphone market but forgot to launch there.

There's no soul in the animation, the sounds, the stages. It's like coming back to an idealized version of a former lover; only to find out now that when you two meet again, the idea is worth more than what you see in front of you. I wish Killing Floor 3 would have been great and a continuation of what I loved from the 1st and 2nd, it's just not.

review:
Killing Floor 3 is quite simply a lifeless, dull shell that promises things that it knows it can't bring.

Assuming you've got the needed patience to sit through a shader compile to get into the menu, and then a 3k shader compile for each level in the game (including the HQ), what you're delving into is nothing short of miniscule in its miserableness: the arsenals contain five/six weapons on average, the character selection is limited, the upgrade system contains very few options. The leveling system is the largest one in the game when it comes to character content, and personally I think that a game that's boasted an excellent armory in past entries should not have the LEVELING system as its strongest point.

It'd comment more on the gameplay, but personally I've had to deal with five crashes in the span of an hour and a half with a computer that sits well above minimum requirements. On the sixth attempt I was blasted with a memory leak that was caused by a resolution change, and right now I'm seriously considering whether this whole ordeal is even worth it in the first place. In-game the unstable FPS count gets hit with stutters and serious drops in performance caused by the weapons' projectile system that apparently is so badly optimized that shotguns were forced into the hitscan category.

I will be entirely ruthless from this point onwards because Tripwire does not deserve a sliver of patience after having existed as a culturally significant studio for the better part of 20 years. This game is a pathetic, soulless experience that is the product of a pathetic, has-been studio that has failed to recapture the magic that made the first two games iconic so many years ago. I am quite frankly angered by the way Tripwire has shown a total inability to stand the test of time, and the fact that they chose to cave in to the bottomless void of shareholder mentality by turning Killing Floor 3 into a worse version of Doom 2016 with battle royale systems to boot is, to me, the gamedev equivalent of committing suicide. 

This shit heap of a game is only possible thanks to Tripwire becoming a shadow of its former self, and I sincerely hope that this game will bring the whole studio down into bankruptcy because you don't deserve a future as a gamedev if you think that games should trade in their cultural impact just to appeal to fleeting mass consumerism and the "green arrow go up" mentality that is strangling artistic value in its sleep. This game will fade into nothingness soon enough and Tripwire will go down along with it hopefully.

You're a dead studio walking. For those responsible for Tripwire's downfall: go fuck yourselves.

review:
To describe it in a sentence or two: it is a safe, generic, uninspired, not crossing any new lines hero horde shooter. If you just want a turn off your brain and shoot *something* game, here it is, though the older titles might offer something more appealing.

Overall 4.5-5/10

As a quick note, I only played this free weekend and the first pre-delay beta so that's my comparison on wether the game improved or not.

The gunsmith is a cool way to build upon the weapon upgrading system from KF2, though having some in-game weapon upgrading would have been more interesting besides buying the presets you really like as soon as you can afford it. Adding objects to hunt for materials that you need for the gunsmith in between waves is a fine way to spend the time while your teammates upgrade as well. 

The skill trees are also a great evolution from the skills you got every 5 levels you got in KF2 or permanent upgrades every level in KF1, however as the leveling is slow I didn't try out making full builds in the trees. I hope some balancing was made because I've seen some videos from launch months where the non-melee perks were better at melee than the ninja perk because the devs didn't limit to what guns the bonuses applied, thus the boosts were just higher than what ninja could get, making it easier to survive.

And probably the final good thing I can mention (yea that's it really) is that the level art style was greatly improved from the beta, it makes you use the flashlight for once, some may see it as a negative but to each their own, and it looks like a place run down by biological monstrosities. Though the levels can be like mazes at times.

So what was bad? To start where the game does, the HUB area is pointless. I hate HUB menus in any game besides maybe singleplayer ones, but even there it can get tedious running about. HUB areas in games and especially live service, multiplayer games, should be OPTIONAL. If I want to run around with friends or go to the gun range (that's really all the damn HUB offers actually), let me do it when I want to. It wastes time having to load into it when playing solo or in a group that doesn't care about those two available things. At least you no longer have to run to the heli to start the missions.

Then in game - the zeds. Maybe I could have improved it by tweaking settings but the sound mixing was just not as focused as KF2. Fleshpounds and scrakes spawning is barely announced and the sounds they do are quite generic besides the chainsaw (which even that isn't as menacing as the engine start up you had in KF2). The designs are seemingly not that thought out while in game. I OFTEN mixed up which zed I was looking at in game because they either blended into eachother in a group or just into the environment because the lights were really overpowering any color design they might have. Speaking of, they don't really have color design. Almost every zed is colored the same. A scrake, a clot, a crawler, all similarly colored. Even the gorefiends aren't as vibrant so if a light shines on them, hey, they all look similar. Like there was a reason the crawler was colored differently than everything else, it's so they don't blend into the crowd with the clots. It was mentioned in the KF2 dev diaries cmon.

Then the bosses. Generic, that's all I can comment on them. I didn't encounter the new boss Moorcroft which seems to be way more lively and interesting (like most bosses from the previous games besides the newer additions from KF2 like king fleshpound and the massive bloat). They have WAAAAAAAAAAY too much health. On normal solo, fighting the alpha scavanger, I dumped like 400+ bullets from the LMG and half the ammo supply of the scar before it went down. Solo. Normal difficulty. And the chimera I think just throws 4 of itself in coop lobbies. And all of them are still spongy as all hell!

Moving onto the guns - I guess they're better than the first beta? The sounds are way more punchy and animations are improved but they are still a stark downgrade from KF2s quality level. Some guns seem to OVERcompensate from the critisism in the beta, I.E. the starting engineer shotgun is now screenshake hell or some guns jiggle like they are made out of jelly. Hipfiring the guns seems...off. I can't put my finger on it but maybe this game just has a stronger hipfire spread than the last games because I kept missing shots I swear should have hit (or did hit on repeat attempts). The gunslinger akimbos ARE an improvement over what the other classes have, I'd say I don't have complaints about them BESIDES the deagles on which the recoil from the slide seems too slow. If it was faster I'd say they would work fine. The weapon roster not the biggest but has increased from the beta, there are options now. The design of the weapons, which the devs seemingly took the hint on and are moving away from, can just feel like generic sci-fi. I'm not a gun nut but sometimes I just feel like I'm holding a box and I'm not sure what I should be expecting from it. Is it a shotgun, an smg, something else entirely? You can't tell without wasting some bullets and firing it when you first pick it up. They just don't feel like guns is what I'm trying to say with that, other games did sci-fi BS stuff go type of gun design better. And I'll end of this paragraph with the crime that are engineers guns. How did they make the shotgun/demolitions perk so awful to play????? The shotguns feel mediocre and the only real good option is the quad barrel, though you'll be reloading for more than you will be shooting (comes with the type of shotgun ig) or the starting shotgun IF you can put up with screenshake, which I did not really want to. The only real explosive option feel weird, the grenade launcher fires weirdly slow and I think queues your shot so sometimes you shoot one too many times. And the last laser gun thing I can't comment on much, it's a laser gun.

Characters I don't have much to say on. Uninteresting normally? DJ skully and Masterson return with their OG voice, Foster doesn't for some reason. They either knew people loved his old design or knew the new one was mid because the microtransaction store (WHICH WAS SHOWN OFF IN THE BETA) has the original style as a purchase. The new characters are take it or leave it, subjective taste, not really to mine.

Lastly for this essay is performance. I was running with everything on medium, Lumen off (thank you slop engine 5 for this tech that is never worth turning on) with DLSS on balanced and the game ran in the 40-60FPS range. Doesn't sound *too horrible*, I could turn it down to low and crank up DLSS more but I didn't quite find the suggestion of having my screen look like I was running warzone when it starts doing that thing with the assets not loading it quickly enough appealing. Also it *may* (?) be damaging to your system because holy hell, it ran maxed out the entire time. Compiling shaders - max CPU and RAM. In game - max GPU and RAM with CPU being quite busy. I think my performance would have been better if everything inside there wasnt thermal throttling from the constant load. Those system testing apps are the only place where a system should cook like this.

Also compiling the shaders takes forever. Genuinely this game took longer to compile shaders than ANY OTHER game I have played.

Buy KF2 or 1.

review:
As a standalone game it's okay if it didn't have "Killing Floor" in the name. I'd give it a 6/10.

Since it's "Killing Floor 3" it's a huge let down when compared to KF 1 & KF 2. I'd give it a 4/10. This game doesn't feel complete. It feels "early access."

Cons:
-Soyboy forum moderators.
-Very unstable/ Lots of crashing. (Fixed for me by disabling GPU hardware acceleration.)
-Too much shader compiling loading screens.
-Disconnecting/dropped from server (Penalized for their crap servers disconnecting you by receiving no xp/currency rewards)
-Less maps.
-Maps are too small.
-Less weapons. (7 or 6 per perk)
-Less characters. (where's the grim reaper, bad santa, commando chicken)
-Ugly characters.
-No more character dance moves.
-Boss Kill Cam doesn't show characters at all.
-Ugly cosmetics.
-Less perks to choose from.
-Less game modes.
-Less specimens.
-No community made maps.
-No community made weapons.
-Not allowed to change perks when a match starts.
-No way to refund proficiency points in skill tree if invested incorrectly.
-Ugly specimen design.
-No more door welding.
-No cool voice commands.
-They removed Mr. Foster original voice.
-No Server browser matchmaking list. (You get thrown into random servers with bad ping.)
-Specimens occasionally disappear on death instead of showing bodies. (Gore system fail)
-Uglier HUD design.
-Scoreboard is more useless. (Doesn't update in real-time. You have to re-open it to see players new kill count.)
-Grindfest for new unique currency for cosmetics.
-Grindfest for new proficiency currency for skill tree upgrade.
-Grindfest for new mod currency.
-Crappy mod system. (I thought the mods would already be available at the in game trader at the end of a wave just requiring dosh. Turns out it isn't. Instead you need to grind special currencies to craft the mods before hand before you ever join a match.)
-On wave 3-4 you can already unlock the best weapon in the game.
-Mandatory mutations in the default game mode like exploding specimens isn't fun
-Hidden stamina bar.
-Having to hold left click to perform a strong melee attack becomes a chore
-Limited trader stock which is shared with allies. (Thinking of restocking your #4 tool slot? Well too bad its all sold out because your allies already used it all up.)
-Ugly blizzard storm effect in one map. What a great way to ruin a map.
-Some skill trees are completely useless.
-Limited healing syringes.
-No remastered original maps.
-No remastered original bosses.
-Dumbed down graphics.
-Parrying system is worse.
-Slowed down run speed when performing melee attacks.
-No more headshots needed. People killing everything easily with just body shots.
-Having to exit out of a match completely to invest skill tree points/change skill tree abilities is stupid.
-Can't heal allies with your own syringes anymore.
-No weight system. I liked getting a run speed buff for carrying less weight.
-Can't see your own character during a match. So what's the point of cosmetics?
-Flying husks. Penalized for playing melee or outdoors. Flying husks will deplete your hp bar if you're outside since they automatically spawn on top of buildings and get perfect visibility above you to shoot you.
-Everyone camps indoors because of flying husks. Great gameplay. 

Pros:
-Ability to climb objects.
-Dodge mechanic.
-Ability to give people dosh at the trader instantly. 
-New bosses
-New weapons
-New grenade types.
-Zip line
-Auto turrets
-New tools
-Gadget ultimate ability for perks. (Some are fun to use while others look hideous like engineer sound garbage)
-They removed the specific character requirement for perks.
-No loot boxes or key system.
-No prestige system grind.

It's sad that this is what Tripwire gave us. KF 2 came out in 2015/2016. 10 years later and this is all they were able to do? Killing Floor 3 is a sad excuse for a sequel. It's by far the worst game in the series.

I don't think this game is worth buying unless it's severely discounted. Maybe $15 or less. As is KF 2 or KF 1 are much better options. This game feels as if it wasn't even made by the same development team. That they hired a bunch of nobodies or DEI hires to save a dollar.

It needs a lot more time in the oven before it's ready. I'd give it another 2-5 years of development time before I think it's worth playing. 

This game will provide some hours of entertainment but it will be short lived since there's too little content. It gets repetitive very quick. It's always you using the same weapons because there's literally no other options to use or they suck. Ninja for example always has to use Katanas because it does the most damage and provides 25% resistance. Every other weapon is inferior even with mods. Great game design.

I'm confused as to how Tripwire made KF 3 so much worse than the originals when they already had the original content at their disposal. All they had to do was literally copy and paste it while adding on to it...

Where did all the profits go that they made off of the previous games as well as milking loyal fans for microtransactions? It feels as if they didn't even re-invest it properly for this game's development.

At the end of the day KF 3 is mediocre and I don't recommend it. If you're new to the series go play KF 2. If you're a veteran to Killing Floor then come back in a few years assuming it's not abandonware by then.

review:
I played for about 1h and out of the 1h, 30 minutes were dedicated to loading shaders and messing with the settings until it worked with my pc. The game starts full screen full blast and it takes about 10 minutes of loading shaders until I can get into the menu and lower the sound so that I can click play and load another 5 minutes of shaders then get into a useless hub. Sure my PC is between minimum and recommended specs but that doesn't mean I have to spend almost 20 minutes of loading shaders into a hub that then loads more shaders for me to play the game on a map that looks worse than what I saw on KF2. 

Is it because I'm on minimum graphics? Yes, I want to be able to run the game smooth enough so that I don't run my CPU and GPU on 100% and risk blowing 1k on new parts. 

The gameplay itself is also kind of mid. I understand that they want to add more mechanics so that it's fresh for KF2 players but this is just a poorly optimized 40k Darktide clone. I kept using spacebar to strafe dodge and instead I jumped right into a fireball. 

Hell even the daily and weekly missions are similar and the battlepass or whatever the monetization tactic is; basically the same as Darktide. The main gameplay loop consists of 5 rounds and a boss that is easily beatable by jumping over a window and shooting him while he tries to pathfind its way to you. 

The armor system is weird, the weapon system is weird, why can you only have limited tool to use the map to your advantage. I feel like this game tries too hard to be something other than Killing Floor. You always have to be running which is crazy because why do you not have an auto-run toggle for PC KB&M but only for Controllers. Weird decisions all around. 

The game tries to saturate you with as much things happening on the screen as possible instead of being able to aim your shots. I was playing on normal to see how it compared to previous KF titles on normal and it's just odd that I have to keep running. Maybe the inclusion of parkour so that you can dodge everything made the balance this way but there's too many thing happening instead of just teaming up with your buddies and having fun shooting zombies. Why is there a timer when I'm playing solo and even on the menu before starting the game, why am I forced to quickly pick a class instead of being able to check what each does with a quick list of % increase or perks. 

Having played previous titles, this is not KF, this is basically 40k Darktide with a KF reskin and worse optimization. It just needs that weird POE style skill tree split and it's basically the same game. I don't need COD parkour if it means that I need to be constantly jumping and using ziplines to dodge instead of being able to check out the map for Easter eggs.

Sure there are new takes on existing enemies, the crawlers actually go on walls which is neat, the siren looks creepier, the stalkers and gorefasts make a comeback that looks nice. But this is on top of an engine that just doesn't work with you. I wanted to be able to not get stuck on weird railing or between 2 leaves in KF2 so having some vaulting would be nice, but I still get stuck in weird areas here so there's no actual advantage. 

At least make it so that I don't waste my time loading shaders and hubs that don't matter. Just let me play the game with friends within 5 minutes.

review:
I've been following KF3 since it's announcement, and was one of the voices asking for a lengthy delay after the beta, and I took this free trial period to give it another hands on shot, hoping that the performance and visual issues I had before were improved while knowing that the art and systems changes I disliked were still present. 

Before even getting into image quality and performance concerns, there are fundamental changes from Killing Floor 2 to the aesthetics, progression and game feel. The selection of guns and characters is much much smaller than Killing Floor 2, and of the guns on offer, the majority of them are large bulbus things with arrays of tubes, pistons, and lights, with scant few real weapons. The exaggerated shuddering and jostling of mechanical parts on the mostly grounded guns of Killing Floor 2 was a massive draw to the series for me, and to see them divorce themselves of this and go into almost entirely science fantasy guns is disheartening. The weapons lack the level of punch imparted by the aggressive visual recoil in Killing Floor 2, with the majority of weapons I tried in matches and in the firing range having shockingly low recoil. The zeds are now more uniformly colored with glowing red accents, which while it does look cohesive, it makes the horde a more indistinct mass, where medium enemies like Gorefiends blend into the mass of glowing red. The hub area also feels like an extra unnecessary layer of time wasting between getting into matches, and seeing the absurd number of material currencies only fills me with dread, not interest. Part of the joy of Killing Floor 2 for me was in the ability to immediately pick a server from the server browser and drop into a lobby, where the only currency was dosh and the only meta progression was leveling your perks and building your total dosh stash passively for cosmetics. 

The games performance and image quality are also concerning. The game is heavy, despite the visuals on offer suffering from some serious artifacts. Shadows have severe aliasing at times even maxed out, and the game has an overly sharp, aliased look even with DLAA. Character outlines look pixelated and aliased, almost like macro blocking from video compression or aggressive variable rate shading, but as no settings seemed to fix this I can only assume was a deliberate effect. Particle effects like the firebugs ground fire are more sparse and indistinct than the same particles in Killing Floor 2, and and the flame thrower's projection look indistinct and almost incorrect with how it blooms into massive but low resolution alpha textures that almost look like they're following ahead of the reticle when turning, not behind. The games RTGI looks more appealing than the fallback lighting, but suffers from boiling artifacts not uncommon with Lumen, and as the game is as heavy as it is already, it feels hard to justify enabling it, and without it, the game doesn't look generationally better than it's predecessor from a decade ago.

That's not to say there's nothing to commend. The game does support proper 21:9 ultrawide aspect rations in both gameplay and menus, and it's HDR did look nice on the Husks flames. Allowing the player to scale FOV in either the Horizontal or Vertical is genuinely nice for players who have a specific FOV they're comfortable with in games to correctly dial it in without having to guess if the game is using Horizontal or Vertical FOV scaling. But these are ultimately small improvements that do little to counteract the (subjectively) less interesting weapons and (objectively) heavier performance load. I would rather that Tripwire had not made such a dramatic departure from Killing Floor 2, and I can't see myself coming back to KF3 without a total overhaul that I doubt they have any intention of doing. Killing Floor 3 makes me incredibly sad as it feels less like a successor to Killing Floor 2 and more like the death of what I loved about Killing Floor 2, moving so far away from what made KF2 so special.

review:
I think the core of this game is great. The changes to movement and gameplay ensure a more reactive combat than in kf2. dodging, sliding, getting hit is now your fault more than ever. it definitely feels harder than kf2, almost to the point going back to it makes me feel like something is missing.
but it needs a LOT of work.

first of all. it needs way, way more maps. and more variety. its missing that bleak, grimy aesthetic. it needs more grunge and dirt really badly. i like and get what they were going for, during combat the environment really does change. walls break down, debris spread about, blood splatters go on ceillings... it really did impress me. but still, at this point, even remakes of kf1 and 2 maps would be welcome. 
i dont know if its the engine lighting (another willing victim of UE5) or what, but the game just looks... made out of plastic. it looks terrible. the graphics are arguably worse.

it also needs way more guns and a rework to the base guns. Some animations just feel.. Almost finished. its a given the ones from kf2 should return, but also give us more additions, and enough futuristic weapons. those should be a minority. its a zombie killing sandbox without much sand or many toys right now.
plus the current guns need animation overhauls. more shakiness. more bounce. it feels really stiff. also, theyre too zoomed in. at the very least a viewmodel slide would help

the perks are wayyy worse and more generic than in kf2. in kf2, your skilltrees benefitted mainly your weapon class, so while you can use other weapons, youd still be at a clear disadvantage. here, its gone. the skilltrees are just blanket buffs most of the time. Like blanket buffs to "ballistic weapons." or how the engineer is confused whether he's an explosives guy or a shotguns guy. When, buffs to his class weapons would fit better. plus balancing. some classes just outperform others because of these blanket buffs.
also, there needs to be a full on rework. It doesnt make sense for Commando to reload stowed weapons and Gunslinger to have reload speed, when Gunslinger makes pistols glow, and Commando is basic gun guy lol
the identity should be the defining factor. the kf2 system had it perfected. each level is stat buffs and you get skills.

Other issue is the inventory system. It was fine before the gunslinger was added, but now that he can benefit secondaries, and all his weapons are pistols but primaries, it just feels confused. a 3 slot weapon system can work, but the kilogram system from kf2 was just leagues better.

escalation is gone. from wave 1 you have a buttload of husks, sirens, stalkers, crawlers, etc from the get go. feels like that sense of each subsequent wave throwing more at you is gone, outside of fps and scrakes, instead of starting off with bloats, cysts, stalkers and gorefasts only.
this game is also hard obsessed with spawning hordes behind you all the time. it feels like a cheap way to turn this into a movement shooter. it just feels miserable that as soon as i look away theres a horde so im always just... running and sliding and dashing and am not allowed to hold off in an area, which was the magic of kf2

voicelines. not gonna lie, the upbeat happy tone of the vendor is just... leagues worse than the one in kf2. it feels out of place. a little too marvel-y. but also what happened to the contextual voicelines? characters commenting on weather, on the guns they bought. it feels a little lifeless. 

fleshpounds can hit you through geometry and the hitbox is way bigger than the visual attack. they also just have way too much health in solo. youll be dumping half your ammo in their head to no effect. i suppose youre expected to min-max and build with the elemental weaknesses like this is a RPG except youre not gonna have the resources for those when ur a low level perk.... plus thats just... not fun????

also husks. god are they annoying. theyll snipe you across half the map. youll be handling a horde and a scrake and a fleshpound, and theyll be behind a sea of enemies, so you cant shoot them, yet theyll do a jetpack leap and just spam 3 shots that do aoe damage. their attacks need to be way less spammy and they shouldnt just leap over a horde and fire. thats silly innit 

if you thought the robots were annoying, get ready for this game, where every enemy has some ranged attack. biggest villains here are bloats. they shouldnt be shooting vomit bullets at you. what happened to each enemy serving a specific role. 

the music is pretty ok, but itd be nice if each update added at least one new song to the roster. theres a good amount of songs, but youll hear the same songs more often than not. maybe licensed songs could be cool, and theres a many great smaller bands out there that im sure would be willing to license their tracks for cheap. it also just needs more variety? get some djent, get some nu metal, get some metalcore, etc

they added this reactive system but in doing that they killed the ... soul of the music, is how id describe it. it feels very factory-made.

also, some of the effects just look... unfinished. the fire specially. the way it works is also inferior to kf2. sometimes i cant tell if a zed is burning or not. 

theres the whole improve performance thing, but you dont need me to tell you that

right now, kf3 is maybe worth it on sale with its promise of more. justifies the lack of content if you get it not full price and accept its a half baked, but fun package. if you enjoy fast paced, reactive, gory games this is it. 
now heres hoping the "release unfinished, kill your image and sales" trend from game studios doesnt mean they go bankrupt before they can put out more content lmaooo <///3 would be sad, this game has potential.

overall a 5/10 as it stands.

review:
After multiple attempts and iterations by this new so called team at Tripwire, this game looks and feels like it was made by anyone but.. the original Tripwire team. Any new change of hands, at the management or director, leads, etc. (Whomever is largely responsible, or in charge of signing off on all of this) Should stick to what they were doing before trying to continue this franchise cause they're mopping the floor and destroying what this used to be. I say this as someone who cherished the original when it was just a mod.

Game feels nothing like a killing floor experience. The guns feel lifeless and tacky.. there is no weight to them, just a supreme lack of 'feedback' from the shot. Feels like you're just clicking away, and throwing nerf bullets. The sound? Damn.. their idea of a Desert Eagle, sounds more like a hollow 9mm fart in a can, with the cheesiest echo for ambience I've heard in quite sometime. It sounds awful. The rest of the environment sound also feels almost muted..and I almost want to say the directional sound is worse than the previous titles as well, somehow. Sound ques just aren't as clean and don't really gel with the game.

Guns have awkward imposed delays on them when firing, and the reload.. is so embarrassingly slow, you could probably do algebra on the side while waiting for the mag to stumble its way back into the gun. Like if they're supposed to be specialists.. why am I reloading like farmer who's never touched a gun in their life? again, just super clunky.

New gunslinger feels... meh at best. They even screwed up the alternative fire mode.. where your pistols get to fire in unison.. like a big ol shotgun blast, yay for a sudo shitty shotgun feel I guess? Feels like garbage honestly. The zed design is mediocre. Looks like a failed B script Hollywood movie. Moorcroft? Why is every design in this game a clay- greyish zombie looking cross between almost an organism that is melting, or last nights food that you forgot to put away and left on the counter? There is zero uniqueness.. just insert 'Homogonized Blob' here, and profit. Or at least that seems to be the idea lol 

Classes feel meh, and the synergy is lacking. It gives you the impression you're on a team, but nothing is really synergizing together. The only synergy is you all somehow managed to get into the same lobby to shoot at similar things together. The past titles did a good job of making you feel as if you truly were a unique and authentic class.

The game really does scream or feel like a 'fresh devs' attempt at proving they can make a real game in the 'style of' but... just don't have the chops to do it. It's sad, I hate to see one of my favourite franchises just get shit on but.. the passion is clearly not there. This is overall a huge slap in the face to the niche fans out there who honestly deserve more. Worst part is, they had two prior titles, with a perfect blueprint showing how and what these games are, and why they were treasured, and yet still somehow managed to ruin it. Literally a cookie cut, situation, paste and apply, profit blueprint. You just had to add tweaks, and small quality of life improvements and augment the game a bit. Not tear it all down, strip away everything that was good about it, and be afraid to make a real Killing Floor title. 

What a let down.

review:
Honestly a downgrade from 2. They added a home/deploy area that is just a pain for people to start with. Maybe it would make some sense after a dozen hours or so, but its just too much and just why? 2 had added a lot of a fantasy guns. Personally I wasn't a huge fan, but we have have gone completely into fantasy with 3's loadout. I Still have not figured out how to buy new guns. In game you can buy around 3 in the shop like previous titles, but it looks like 12. However they are just the same 3 guns with extra mods. I would assume you can buy more in the home/deploy area, but I still cant find were that is. The game did not draw me in like 2, so I can't be asked to figure it out.

The game just feels 'cartoony' to me. That's the best way I can think to describe it. Controls feel clunky and movement feels slow. Firebug has no accurate options so headshots are just out the window for that class. Sure it's meant to be an area denial class, but taking away the headshots for the class really kills the ability to handle med and large zeds.

Levels have missions now with objectives rather than just pure wave survival. You also collect currency/crafting items around the map as well. Again, why? I'm sure it has something to do with crafting new weapons or something similar, but doing this encourages teams to split up and try to find these items for future games rather than focusing on winning the one they are in. The grind in the first 2 was to learn your class, learn the enemies and unlock perks. 

On the positive side the maps are a lot bigger and with climbing added they are a lot more vertical. However with movement feeling sluggish I personally don't feel it's adding that much to the game.

If you're a fan of the first 2 games I'd say pass on this one. If you're new to the franchise maybe give it a shot if you think its your thing. Real bummer IMO because I was looking forward to this game for so long. However you will find me in KF2.

review:
Tripwire struck gold with Killing Floor 1. They created a gritty co-op wave survival horror shooter that at its core was just COD Zombies but presented in a way that was so much more appealing, both in design and gameplay. While KF1 was cool, it felt dated and at times clunky and badly needed a facelift, a call which Killing Floor 2 answered. Better graphics, more fleshed out characters and lore, awesome gunplay and animations, perk progression, character customization, and SO much content added over the years that it makes triple A live service games look like frauds. KF2 was an extremely rare case of a sequel making improvements over its predecessor in almost every single aspect. And how did it do it? By honoring the previous iteration. The same characters. The same classes. The same enemies. Even some of the same maps. Just done better. So much better that the game still has a cult following of thousands of active players 10 years later. I have sunk hundreds of hours into KF2 and I don't plan to stop any time soon.

Then Killing Floor 3 was announced. A game that no one asked for. Advertising improvements to problems that didn't exist. The possibility of another huge step for this series made me excited at first, but then the trailers came out. And then the game released. It brought back none of the previous classes. None of the previous weapons. Only one of the previous characters. Most of the enemy types got scrapped. A completely different futuristic environment that lacks any of the grounded gritty feel of the first two games. From 10 playable classes down to 6, and none of them are as interesting or well balanced as any of the ones from previous games. And NO character customization to speak of. 

Who was this game made for? And an even better question, who was it made BY? The Tripwire Interactive that created and was subsequently saved from bankruptcy by Killing Floor 1 wouldn't have done this. Deluxe editions and battlepasses for a game with NO content. A game that released with half as many features as its predecessor that came out 10 years ago. Was this really just a quick cash grab? A huge middle finger to the fanbase that loved and supported this series since it started in 2009. If you're reading this, just buy Killing Floor 2. Its playerbase is still active, has a server browser, tons of content, and steam workshop support. This game is just a waste of money.

review:
Killing Floor 3 feels like playing Dying Light 2. Is it a bad game? Not really. Then, why the negative review? Because it's suprisingly and unnecessarily worse than the previous one. For starters, they reduced the number of perks (from 10 to 6) and reduced the number of weapons, a really surprising decision, considering that every class felt different from the previous one (except probably SWAT, who was just fun to play anyways, and survivalist, who was a mix of the other classes). They also replaced the weapon upgrade system, which used to be mid-run, now it's meta-progression related (not necessarily a bad thing, you just need to play more).

One of the worst downgrades in my opinion is that shooting doesn't feel as good as in KF2. One of my favorite parts of the previous game is how satisfying was to shoot, even when not aiming. Here it just doesn't feel as right, especially when enemies are too close. For whatever reason, it feels like normal enemies are too big, and they get too close to you (somehow, the only ones that feel normal size are fleshpounds and Scrakes). No matter the Field of View you use, they feel too close and shooting them feels like your bullets pass through them, which never happened in KF2.

They probably focused all of their attention in the engine and graphics "upgrade", going for Unreal Engine 5, but it just makes the game's performance worse and it doesn't really look that good. In my opinion, it looks too dark and grey and it's honestly hard to see (even with flashlight on), making my eyes hurt if I play it more than 1 hour in a row (I push them too hard to try to see better).

Not all is bad though, they added new class-related mechanics, an ultimate skill and an utility tool, which are honestly fun to use.

With that being said. Probably one of the worst aspects of the game if you are considering to buy this game is the lack of people playing the game currently. While you can easily find around 4k-5k playing KF2, you can barely find around 200-300 playing this one. Making finding people to play with really hard unless you have friends to play with. So far I have almost 13 hours in the game, always playing with matchmaking on, and I have only found 1 player... Worst part is that, for whatever reason, they removed the server browser that was available in the previous game, where you could see what maps, what regions, what mode and what difficulties were people playing. Now you just select, click on play and hope that someone else is searching also.

Oh, also, servers are terrible, which makes it worse, considering they added a new dash mechanic, with a lot of enemies having some type of charge attack that you are meant to dodge with almost perfect good timing... Well, if you play online not only you won't find anyone else to play with, but you will have to deal with the terrible lags and you getting damage when you see yourself avoiding everything. I don't even know how they messed that up, considering in KF2 I could go Berserker in other regions with no problem, here I can't even perform a dash in my own region without lagging.

So, why am I still playing KF3 instead of going back for 2? Because this one is around 20 gb to install, while KF2 is around 96gb... and I don't want to use that much space with something I just play every now and then.

As a summary, it just feels like a downgrade from the previous game, with a few extra mechanics that were added (some of them being good), but I can't recommend because performance is terrible and it's really hard to find more people currently playing for co-op matches (which is kinda the point of the game).

review:
I *really* tried to like this game. I played it with all my friends, I actually liked the gun sounds and gunplay and I think that dodging added a great element, especially for bosses and heavy enemies.

However, the game runs just so poorly and every corner feels like it was cut. review:
Overall the game feels underwhelming, I have a lot of respect for Killing Floor as a series and TripWire as a company, but Killing Floor 3 is upsettingly plain and removes a lot of features from prior games while leaving nothing to fill in the voids left.

The departure to what are effectively Heroes or Classes for each perk seemed odd to me, but I can understand wanting to emphasise the unique abilities of each perk. Unfortunately when you allow the perks to be summed up by their Ultimate abilities as opposed to their weapons of choice, you end up with very bland and underwhelming weapons; weapons which are the main part of the player's experience in Killing Floor.

I found movement needlessly frustrating (a directional dodge/dash that could have just been at the beginning of your sprint), melee slow and hardly responsive, gunplay weak and without mincing words- nothing like Killing Floor. Furthermore, the input buffer for almost every action regarding your guns, healing or equipment is incredibly frustrating. Not being able to shoot for a few seconds because I tried to dodge out of the way of a Scrake but accidentally started sprinting feels incredibly punishing for trying to make use of the game's mechanics.
The variety of guns feels thin, generic and incredibly lacking, which is probably my biggest complaint with the game. Even when I think about Killing Floor 2's launch arsenal, the variety of possible playstyles and player expression is completely lost in Killing Floor 3. After almost a year I would've hoped to see more content and variety than in the earlier Beta I played or even a glimpse I had after the game's launch, but that simply isn't the case.

I hope that some of this is improved either later in the game's life or in a reboot of the series if Tripwire so wishes.
With how it plays right now though, I feel none of the joy I felt in Killing Floor 2 whether it was hacking and slashing through hoards of enemies, setting them on fire or watching the ragdolls fly around from an explosion, and I see no reason to stick with the game and unlock later content.

tl;dr
The game feels generic, plain and tedious. Especially compared to Killing Floor 2. Clunky movement and input buffer make it frustrating to even play for an hour, making the thought of proceeding with levelling perks a daunting nightmare.

review:
Well, boys. It's bad. I gave it a long time to see if they'd fix it...Nah, they fucked 'er.
A lot of homies on here say that Killing Floor 2 is a masterpiece, glorious, and a true advancement from the original! And that Killing Floor 3 is a major surprise. It really wasn't if you guys remember KF2's release. KF2 got so much shit for shipping with barely any content. KF2 had loot boxes which was the mark of the devil that battlepasses are today, back then.

The difference: KF2 actually gritted its teeth and released new weapons and classes. KF3 dropped with way too many controversies that they knew would be problematic with the player base. No more "Welding dis doah!" It's now a silly consumable gadget instead of a welder that got benefits if you play demo or support. They released with the inability to play the characters you wanted, it was tied to class for no reason. The obvious text chat being missing fiasco. Battlepass is a Faustian pact that these companies never understand. Battlepasses usually aren't complained about if the game is good and people are willing to pay (even if it's scummy imo, but I used to buy dota passes all the time and those are by far the most scammy), but having a battlepass when your game is glaring with flaws is a death sentence. The inability to heal each other with med syringes isn't wise in a team game (I main medic so as much as it's nice to be able to earn points before the asshat heals himself in front of me, I see the issue for groups with no medic). Having only 2 weapon slots was obviously going to be a no-no. And then finally, they decided not to learn from KF2's release and drop with only a starting weapon a mid weapon and an end game weapon for each class. Also, less Zeds? Why? Why did we remove Sirens and Invisi-bitches? They added stalker back I guess, but...what was the point of getting rid of her in the first place?
So, KF2's main problem was not enough content. That was an easy fix and they could hide behind "Early Access". KF3 has a lot of problems, and they haven't done anything but add more premium cosmetics.

Ignoring that nobody likes that it's set in the future instead of a contemporary setting, the character and gun designs aren't great. The change in the Zeds ranges from, "eh...kinda cool" to "That's stupid". This is of course an opinion.

To list of what I do like: Attachment system is cool when it isn't annoying and worrying about stupid modern crafting gimmicks games like to push, the execution system is pretty metal and I think fits great, the ability to heal chunks of armor instead of healing it all or waiting for the end to use the rest of your money is a nice addition...I thought for a while but that's all I got, which isn't good. The actual gameplay is "acceptable". It's a horde shooter, kinda hard to mess that up too badly.

Now for the main killer for this game:

IT'S DEAD

The game decided that server browsers are for old people, the hip kids like matchmaking. Issue with matchmaking is you can't find anyone. This game peaks at like 300 players these days. If you had a server browser, you could connect and play with other dudes by filtering by player count. I tried to play 6 games today, matchmaking each time and was alone each time. 

So the issue is: Even if you think you'd like the game, you can't play it. The game isn't set for singleplayer play. You don't have enough ammo and everything moves too quick and swarms you so you can't hold a line or kite for a bit before shooting behind you. You won't be able to afford more than one weapon and even if you can, you're stuck with only 2.  It's not like 1 and 2 where you can play solo. So basically, you're dropping your hard earned bucks to have it sit in your library and burden your drive with 22gb(Which I actually will give them props for making it only 22 gigs. Feels like every game is 100 these days.)

I give the game a 4/10. If KF2 didn't exist, it'd be probably be a 7/10. Sad truth is, you can't just sell an inferior product than your previous and expect everything to work out. There's a reason why KF2 had such a shakey launch. 1 Still had way more guns and maps. No one cared about the soundtrack, the awesome blood and gore that was location based with pools of blood reflecting things, or the really cool firing animations of the guns (Which was so sick btw) if there's less content. Once KF2 got the updates, that's when it became King. Unfortunately, I do not foresee KF3 getting the same treatment. The matchmaking makes it impossible to play with people and there's already a pathetic amount of players. The lifeblood that would keep this game going until it has enough content, will eventually bleed out from frustration.

review:
Just don't. Go ahead and buy KF2 when it's on sale for like 2$. 

I typed out this comment below on an update page. I think it'll effectively reach more of the people that need to see it here in the reviews, along with the negative statistic it deserves. I've given the developers time to work out bugs and optimization, and I've given this game a chance, but it is beyond redemption. After nearly a year since it's 1.0 release, it is clear that there is no passion to create an enjoyable and fun to play co-op shooter, it was just a grift.

 -
The biggest issue I have with KF3 is the horrible performance, game constantly stutters and lags ALL THE TIME. Running the 7900XTX on a 5800X3D and still, absolutely horrible performing game. They butchered the level up system too.

Game released with day one battle passes and microtransaction store, yet it took the devs something like 10 months to get a text chat running. THE GAME HAD NO FUNCTIONAL TEXT CHAT FOR 10 MONTHS BUT HAD GONE THROUGH 3 SEASONS OF BATTLE PASSES WITH AN IN-GAME STORE CHOCK FULL OF ITEMS TO BUY WITH REAL MONEY.

I'm not disappointed with the art direction or the Zeds, or the 'Specialist abilities' or any of that. KF3 is a poorly optimized stuttering laggy mess of a game.

No ability to heal teammates w/o the use of medic guns, forcing you to buy the medic pistol which replaces your default pistol (only one pistol weapon slot). No weight system, can no longer carry multiple guns like you used to as with the Support perk.

The level up system is minimally transparent. No longer could you see what helps you level quicker, ie no longer could you see how many Stalkers you killed w/ the Assault perk, or if killing stalkers even does anything, because all you see at game end is a XP bar fill up with no info at all. KF1 & KF2 perk leveling felt satisfying, for whatever reason, and they killed it with KF3.

The ZED Time bonuses in KF2 were felt even in the early ranks, they are basically unnoticeable in KF3 (maybe once maxing out rank, haven't cared enough to get any perk past lvl 20).

Just all around, awful game. Not worth more than 5 dollars in it's current state. I had anticipated something better, I followed along with the high production value teaser trailers, I missed the beta and preordered the 'Nightfall Edition' of the game regardless. Regrets. I don't even want to see these games in my games list anymore, they might join the ranks of my 'hidden games' where I never have to entertain the thought of playing KF3 again.

 - 
Not only did it take 10 months to implement a freaking text chat. THEY MADE IT OUT TO BE A MAJOR UPDATE TITLED 'THE TEXT CHAT UPDATE' !!!!!!!!!!!

20.4k reviews on Steam, with only 46% of them positive.

30k all time peak players on release day.
15k a week after release day.
5 weeks after release day, concurrent player count drops below 2k.
8 weeks after release day, concurrent player count drops near 800.
Steady decline ever since, with the occasional update briefly drawing a few hundred concurrent players back.
Peak concurrent players for all of June 2026, 532 players.
Averages for the month of June 2026 show around 250 - 350 peak concurrent players.
Some hours of the recent few past days show fewer than 120 concurrent players.

Counter-Strike: Condition Zero, for example, has higher concurrent players and higher peak concurrent players than KF3. An obscure solo/coop FPS game that released in 2004 on Windows XP has more players than KF3.

review:
Decided to give this game a shot since it was on sale and man. 

I really wanted to like this game. I was willing to give it the benefit of the doubt, even in spite of the numerous negative reviews and in spite of my own experience with the second beta. 

And this game has so many problems. It doesn't feel ready for one thing - which is not a good thing when the game is so ridiculously grindy (something that you can tell even after just an hour in game). Perks feel like they level slower than in past games, which only makes the fact that skills aren't a one and done upgrade worse. 

Instead, you have to invest resources into upgrading skills in order to make them really have any value at all - meaning even when you unlock a new skill it might not really have any actual value until you've played another three to five matches in order to upgrade it and make it so you can actually get some benefit. Additionally, the new weapon modification system is also locked behind yet another grind AND features an element of randomness meaning you'll have to spend even more time grinding in order to make any progress and actually have the game feel satisfying. 

Something made worse by the fact that the game has a VERY limited pool of weapons for each perk. After only a handful of games, things already start to feel repetitive - I can't imagine how it must feel after dozens if not hundreds of hours. 

Maybe I'd enjoy it more after another dozen hours, and after the Gunslinger perk was finally added to the game - but I just don't think I'm willing to risk investing so many hours in the hope that the game might actually be enjoyable EVENTUALLY.

review:
1,000~ Hours in KF2, and KF3 is a Massive Step Backward

I want to support the devs for trying something new, I really do. But the execution just feels incredibly poor. It feels like they took elements from Deep Rock Galactic, Overwatch, and Left 4 Dead, slapped them together, and completely lost the identity of what made Killing Floor great.

The UI and matchmaking are an absolute downgrade. In KF2, everything was on one simple main menu. You could browse servers and get into a game with a 2-second button click. Now you have to click to go online, physically walk your character to a terminal, click play, hold Y to ready up, and sit through a wait of about 5 to 20 during queue. All of this takes around 15~ seconds. 5 second for walking, 10 seconds and more based on queue and matchmaking availabilty.

And the matchmaking itself is a mess.

If you want to check something else while queuing and hit ESC, it just cancels the matchmaking entirely and throws you back into the Stronghold hub, The game also plays Ping Roulette by randomly dumping you into high-ping servers. I constantly get thrown into NA servers with 150 to 300 ping. When I rarely get EU, it’s a decent 80 to 110 ping, but the game rarely prioritizes it. 

Then there is the Connection Loop from Hell. If the game fails to connect you to one of these distant servers, you get a "Lost connection" error that kicks you all the way back to the initial title menu. This loop alone is what made me write this review. Really what actually made me write this review. It is so incredibly frustrating to get booted to the title screen, have to select the Stronghold again, and do the extra walks back to the terminal just to re-queue. 

How am I even supposed to know if it's an issue on my end or if it's server-related? KF2 had server browsing, and reconnecting to another server was far easier and user-friendly. To make it worse, they brought over a notorious bug from KF2 that still hasn't been fixed(or maybe its a feature?). When other players join the lobby, the game completely freezes with massive FPS drops. I've literally been forced to downgrade all my settings to low just trying to figure out what's causing it. 


The only thing I extremely loved in KF3 is the weapon attachment customization, which was missing from KF1 and KF2. The ability to craft scopes, barrels, and magazines is all great. However the worst part is it forces you to lock your loadout in the stronghold before queuing. You cannot tweak your attachments or apply skins in the lobby. KF2 allowed for simple cosmetic skins on any weapon while in lobby..

As for the gameplay, it's a mixed feeling. I like the idea that you can use non-specialized perk weapons to gain XP, but it sucks that some of these weapons won't carry over the skill perks you've invested in(like extra pallets). Plus, the game desperately needs more weapon variety. I've put 8 hours into Engineer and Commando, and I'm already completely bored with their weapons. Combine that with weird design choices like getting instantly killed when you're hoarded or crouched something feels like left 4 dead which i am not into

The game just does not feel ready. 

If I'm bored and want to kill some ZEDs, I am booting up KF2. KF3 is just a pain. KF3 Needs to be reworked all over again.
