This game ended up being one of the most disappointing sequels I've played. It's just hot garbage.

The first problem is performance. Both my friend and I had issues just getting the game to launch. The game kept freezing and loading for so long that I ended up walking away and doing something else while I waited. A game shouldn't be fighting you this hard before you've even started playing.

The previous games were goofy, chaotic, and fun. They didn't take themselves too seriously, and that charm was a huge part of what made them memorable. It feels like the devs poured so much effort into these mission-based objectives that everything else suffered for it. The missions aren't even good! They're repetitive, boring, and feel more like window shopping than gameplay. It feels like a lot of development time was spent pushing the game in this direction, only for it to end up like a nothing burger.

The guns aren't satisfying to use, none of the classes felt fun enough to stick with, and the whole game feels like a chore. It feels like the game changed things for the sake of changing them. This game is trying to be what the series once was, but it just can't make the cut. The first two games felt fresh and full of character. This one feels like stale chips.

review:
I am a big fan of the Killing Floor series, but this game just does not deserve to bear that name. It is incredibly undercooked, boring, and just a worse version of the games that came before it. The only positive things I can say about it is that the gun customization and the class abilities genuinely add something more to the game. However, the limited amount of guns for each class, the awful performance, the extremely boring physics, and the downright unacceptable amount of maps show why this game is fundamentally dead. Barely anyone is online at any given time, and there is no server browser, so half the time you will just get plopped into a lobby by yourself, which is a big problem given the awful solo experience of trying to kill a boss that is just impossible most of the time. The performance is unacceptable, I don't have top of the line specs but I exceed the recommended specs given by Tripwire, and it still drops below 60 FPS extremely often, along with just locking itself at 1 FPS randomly during matches, requiring me to fiddle around with the settings until it returns to normal, where I will likely have just died because, you know, I couldn't play the game. The game is also full of bugs, like sometimes just not showing whether your class ability is ready or not, meaning you delve into combat expecting to use your ability, just to get bodied after it doesn't fire. 

TLDR: Do not buy this game. All you need to know is that text chat was only added in May of 2026, nearly a year after the launch of the game itself. The game was released unfinished, and is still unfinished nearly a year later. If you're looking for an entry into the series, Killing Floor 2 is the vastly superior title, with over a decade of community workshop content and custom hosted servers for you to play in.

review:
As a longtime fan of Killing Floor 1 and Killing Floor 2, I was genuinely excited for Killing Floor 3. Unfortunately, that excitement quickly turned into disappointment.

The game feels unpolished, with frequent stuttering, screen tearing, and crashes that constantly disrupt the experience. At its core, the foundation is there, but it never manages to surpass its predecessor—something you would naturally expect from a sequel.

In fact, I would argue that it does less than the games that came before it. Combat feels less impactful, whether you're using firearms or melee weapons, and the overall weapon selection feels lacking. Many of the elements that made Killing Floor satisfying and memorable seem to have lost their edge.

In short, I can't recommend this game in its current state. What should have been an evolution of the franchise feels like a shadow of what Killing Floor is supposed to be.

review:
This isn't KF2, and this especially is not KF1. I still don't understand the hate for KF2, but KF3 deserves the criticism it gets.

I run the game on medium and high graphical settings just to turn up the image sharpness to make the game look better. But I cannot get a solid 60FPS and it stutters every other minute. It's just brutal.

The most requested thing for KF2, weapon attachments, are locked away from a grinding expedition by collecting nine different parts. Or scraps. Whatever you wanna call it. Every mission there are these objects that glow red. If you destroy them by shooting or slashing it, you get these parts/scraps. Those scraps go to, you guessed it, CRAFTING YOUR WEAPON ATTACHMENT.

Not only that, but you can upgrade your attachment to three different tiers. Which requires more parts, and gets MORE expensive. But, it does make the attachment stronger which is nice.

Do yourself a favor; if you must play this game, add the attachments you want, and forget about the upgrade or crafting system for a while. Don't stress about it. Don't spend money to get more scrap. Just, ignore it. Then, after a lot of play sessions later, you'll remember "Oh I have an abundance of scrap! Time for upgrades!" But even then, it's feels soulless and cruel. I'd rather just earn the attachments via in game dosh from the trader pods.

Also, some attachments do little to improve, and some do a LOT to improve the weapon you use. Eventually I'm gonna try other classes as I only played with Commando and made it to level 21. I'll update this review in the future. But right now, I think tripwire needs to knuckle down, optimize this game as FAR as they can...... And, well, learn lessons from the other two games. Simplify the attachments. Stop chasing trends that other games are making. Because Killing Floor is in a league of it's own.

I want to like this game, PVE games are my cocaine, but this is lacking in a lot of ways. Especially for newer players and the veterans of the franchise.

review:
I had a LOT of hype coming into Killing Floor 3. 
I've been playing Killing floor since 2009, I remember waking up at or before 6am to shower before school, jump on the game and play a West London Solo Medic run with XBOW and lever action (Before the weapon nerf, the addition of medic guns, and prestige, and even then it PUMPED). All the additions of funny characters, maps, and classes felt like a genuine vibe to the game, it all fit and felt like it was a game made by gamers, for gamers.

When killing floor 2 was announced for Early Access, I had so much enthusiasm for the game, the way it looked, the way you can feel the sounds of weapons & enemies. I was NOT a fan of the lootbox system as a way of getting cosmetics, sure you can purchase them from market place and blablabla but FUCK "Buy a key and open a lootbox" either let me get what I want or make opening the loot box free. 2016 Overwatch was the reason for this craze, however, Overwatch allowed you to get these box's for FREE and open them for FREE (I had only ever spent $20 on loot box's in overwatch 1 and that was because the first summer event). Didn't matter, killing floor 2 was STILL AMAZING, all the classes, enemies, boss (Because early EA only had the doctor but was still fun to fight). Providing continuous content over the years while REMAINING in early access and not releasing until it is done was the CORE reason early access was created, showing KF2 is a product of how to use a system for the people correctly. My only complaint is years later still no crossplay, otherwise, it's an amazing game.

Killing floor 3 took everything that KF1 & 2 did, and shoved in right up their own butt. Again, I was genuinely hyped for this game even if the trailer wasn't amazing, I still had hope. I played the first BETA and I was copium HARD, I wanted to like the game because SOME things were genuinely good changes like crossplay (THANK YOU, I'VE BEEN WAITING SINCE KILLING FLOOR 2 DROPPED ON PS4 TO PLAY KILLING FLOOR WITH MY BEST FRIEND), and the addition of weapon modding allowing you to build your class specific to your playstyle, or even building team compositions V.S certain boss's where acid might be better vs using bleed.
The problem is every other system surrounding the one good thing is awful. Maps felt too claustrophobic and always seemed there was a random twig or lamp you can get caught on. Classes did not feel impactful when reaching their highest Tier weapon even WITH max character, purple mods. No I do not think 10 hitting HoE boss is fun, but like 50. cal on a sharpshooter or a grenade from a demolitionist, even if it didn't 1 shot, felt good in old iterations because it felt impactful to do the thing your class is good at.
Early game boss's were basically impossible on HoE due to multi hit moves that you can not avoid where they chunk for 90% of your HP even with max body armor and armor buffs. Doable? absolutely with a SUPER coordinated team. Frustrating? Yeah
They also removed running backwards for a backdash, why? I get "realism" but it's iconic for both games.
Where is robo chicken? And all the other fun characters I have in KF1 & 2? This just feels corporate and unfulfilling.
I tried the game a few weeks ago and for some reason I was dropping frames now more than before. I might not have the best PC but it wasn't that bad when the game launched, still bad tho.

I'm done with this game, and at this point, It's only going to be updated because they have to. Don't worry, they'll keep us up with "Big" updates being.... text chat? ya, You can see where this is going.

I wanted to like the game, and I did enjoy it for what it was, but it isn't a game I can go years playing and enjoying each time I boot it up like KF1 or 2. Avoid this at ALL COSTS and just pick up Killing for 1 & 2 on sale for like 5 bucks a pop. If you can get over the jank that is KF1, it will be a forever classic in your heart. KF2 is just amazing so just buy that on sale (As of writing this review KF2 is on sale for $2.99 base game)

Do better tripwire, please

review:
I want to like this game. I have been playing Killing Floor since the beginning when it was an Unreal Tournament 2004 mod! I have thousands of hours in this series. With 100 hours into the new game; it is time to express myself.

Bring Gibson back!
Getting into a game is a chore, load into the menu (compile thy 15,000 shaders), load into a lobby, load into multiplayer lobby - if a friend joins? Now you gotta load into ANOTHER lobby! THEN you select a mission, ready up/board the chopper. LOAD INTO ANOTHER LOBBY and play. It's ridiculous. The music is too hard for a main menu or hub, it's like RAWR RAWR RAWR RAWR DUtta RAWR!!! and you're just chillin, like relax bro. 
The characters are ok... cosmetics are 99% behind some lame paywall but there are unlockables (in 100 hours I got a digital camo skin that is ugly and I will never use) The monsters mostly look cool, shame you rarely see them because of all the magic power special ability bullshit going on all the time. Just hold down the trigger until the colors stop.
Art style: Killing Floor 1 & 2 are gritty, brutal, gory and scary. It was exciting and immersive. The weapons were real, motion captured at 200fps and they even hired a mocap performer to do all the reloads etc.
Killing Floor 3 place in the future, it feels extremely videogamey like it was made for kids, but then added all the blood. Rainbow neon everything, no immersion, wild particle effects that obscure everything on the screen.
However, any explosions, fire, etc is invisible once that shot lands more than about 50feet away. Did you hit the enemy? I guess so because I see limbs flying. C'mon, the whole reason we equip a grenade launcher is to see the explosions. The lighting in this game is garbage, (DOOM 1993 had better lighting effects). Muzzle flash from weapons does not illuminate anything, so you are often watching other players running around and wondering if they are shooting or not. No shell casings, no reciprocating bolts or slides. Often can't even hear gunshots from other players so it always feels like I'm all alone watching 5 others players run around. The fire effects are a downgrade, worse than Killing Floor 1 from 2009. 
Other games you look for the muzzle flashes and that's where the action is! This game? Look for the neon highlighted characters. Flashlight is crap. Cannot see other player flashlights. (Killing Floor 2 it was incredible, the shadows cast by the muzzle flashes and player flashlights made every dark firefight memorable and engaging)
I have a 5070ti, no matter what graphics setting I use - all explosions or special effects literally disappear after 50ft. This is my biggest complaint. The graphics are too detailed to forgive this and I assume it was done so the game would run at a decent framerate. (This game has "good" graphics, but is ugly at the same time, it's weird and feels like a counterfeit copy of Killing Floor)
I'll give this game time to cook, but with only 200-400 players active across all platforms, I am not very optimistic about the future of Killing Floor 3. If you want it, wait for it to go on sale or just play Killing Floor 2. Do better or hire me as a consultant and we can make this game good. As is it's a solid 3/10. Very disappointing.

review:
Some positives before the rant; I like the double barrel cause i can send zeds to meet God both physically and literally. The melee combat is arguably slightly better and more condensed then previous titles. A whole 2 (Perchance 3, there maybe a power attack button idk) buttons to worry about versus the dreaded 3-4. Also having a little area prior to a mission start to move around, test weapons (idk how change classes in there solo cause im dumb and the glorious forced tutorial didnt cover that), probably hang out with people in your party but i didnt feel like crashing so didnt do multiplayer yet (didnt stop it when i hit esc during the tutorial tho). Ziplines are handy as well, whenever they showed up.

Now the cons: If i were to boot this game up without knowing who made it or what it was suppose to be I would say it was a blend of Killing Floor, Doom and CoD all mixed up in a blender, somehow missing the best parts of all of those, thrown onto the baking sheet of early access. 
The game feels confused on what its suppose to be, adding in random features that make it more generic instead of KF-esk. Sliding is cool, idk why its here. Feels like a distraction to make the player look away from how clunky the movement feels at times and how slow you feel moving around while "sprinting". They changed the trader menu system, not updating it from KF2 and making it a bit easier to deal with(like how they did from 1->2); instead they chucked that system out the window and went for 'Generic shooter window', banishing the weight management system for set number of each type of weapon (primary/sec./etc) and a budget system to limit the player. 
Theres a forced tutorial that teaches you two things, how to slide and once again no one at a developer company understands that MMB is a terrible button to bind shit to, please stop. Glad the Key mapping thing worked to fix that, ngl expected it to crash the game trying.
Enemies taking damage feels about the same compared to previous entries, them doing damage tho doesnt, they hit like trucks and some of them dont even want stagger to stop their combo on ya. Feels like they designed the game around having a party of 3-6 and then as an after thought put in a solo campaign while making sure nothing scaled for it. Waves just feel off, instead of them slowly ramping up in difficulty with each one to give time to build up your arsenal they just chuck Scrakes at you round 3 on normal; not single, plural cause clearly you are set for that, just booting up the game and all. (This was out of 10 waves, i think 5 was more what it shouldve been the bosses are so damn tanky.)
Armor feels like they wanted to copy warzone even though the old system was fine, some of the time it feels like i'm wearing paper even when its round 4 and i have lvl 4 armor. 
They decided healing on a timer was dumb and stupid, and the players are wrong for liking it so robbed us of a fully functioning and likable mechanic to give us generic crap. Give me my slowly recharging infinite use med gun back, i dont want your Great Value brand Warzone Stims i can only carry 3 of at a time.
A new perk system was added, expanding upon KF2's idea of having to choose between a really good perk or a really good perk every 5 lvls is gone for.... something, they give you options(2-3, i think maybe theres 4 down the line), you choose one, then you have to upgrade it by getting currency by lvling up. How do the perks compare to each other? Who knows, from what i briefly saw seemed like one was clearly better then the other. Gone are the days on the fly adjustments to better fit the team dynamic or play style.
Berserker is gone, we got ninja now. Why? Cause they coooooool, i guess. I dont mind running around with a katana or shurikens but considering they arent generally known for being front line tanks its an odd choice to say the least. (numerous other classes are missing as well but how can we expected a game studio to deliver a finished product nowadays? Clearly Live-Service means you can get away with anything and use that as a defense for sending out something that nowhere close to done.)
Theres turrets and armor containers you can find spread about the place, shouldve been a perk or a class item for team dynamics (like how ammo pouches are). review:
I really tried to give this game a chance. On paper, each individual system they've implemented in this game is fine on its own and is well executed for what it seems they wanted to accomplish. As a whole, the direction the game was taken in and the combination of all of these systems, just isn't fun. I twas clear with the launch of Killing Floor 2 that they wanted the game to go in a very different direction than Killing Floor 1, and this launch shows they want to distance themselves even further. It really feels like the director of the game pivoted a game initially designed to be more like Overwatch to instead be more like Helldivers 2 during crunch time.

Starting with the basics: Movement is now dash/slide heavy. If you are not spamming dash or slide within your sprinting, you care at a disadvantage. Be ready for your fingers to get tired if you want to try hard. Otherwise, movement feels slow, which is fine, except for that some enemies are doing attacks that expect you to dash away from them so keep spamming those keys.

There are fewer classes (perks) than killing floor 2 and even killing floor 1 - these classes no longer gain base stats on leveling but instead gain passives and a choice of buffs that can be leveled up on certain level increments. Most passives/buffs are inconsequential but some are really powerful.
You might think this would mean there are fewer ways to play, but more on that later.

There are 5 primaries and one pistol per class which can be used by other classes as well. These weapons can be modified to increase or decrease their damage, punch-through, damage types, and reload and aim characteristics. These customizations can be set as kits and purchased mid-game, with the in-game cost increasing depending on the modifications made. These weapons are visually boring and flat, to allow for greater customization via the skins and trinkets they also offer through microtransactions.

However, where the game really falls apart is how the varied progression paths play with each other.

This game could add as many classes as it wants, it could add so many weapons, but it really doesn't need to because in the end the various progression systems push you to put all of your resources into making a singular build that you cannot easily pivot away from, so you'll end up playing the same gameplay over and over and over again to get the most out of your one build. There will be no room for experimentation or mixing things up, because you will be putting all of your crafting resources and perk points into one build initially, until that build is enough to clear all the content you want to clear - THEN you can start branching out. I think. I didn't get that far. It doesn't matter how many weapons or classes or mods this game adds, because unless you want to be stuck in the early game - you're just going to be using 1-3 weapons and one class for a loooong time.

This game is frustrating to think about. It really has the potential to be a good game, it does. There's something in here. I truly think it's salvageable, like how they found a fun game in kf2 eventually. The enemy designs are amazing, most of their animations are superb. The way they interact with the environment is great. The weapons, while there are only a few, feel great to use. This studio still has it. The graphics are... all over the place. Lighting and shaders are fancy, but is it really worth making the rest of the game's materials and audio look/sound and perform awful for those two things? I suspect it's all lighting's and UE5's defaults fault here, oh unreal engine 5.... I really hate you. 

Why did they double down on the annoying characters from 2? Why must they comment on EVERYTHING? I know it's a setting but like - who? anyone at all? who would ever enjoy them? surely the devs knew? I cant imagine nobody knew how annoying they always were in 2 and how much worse they are now? Sure, if someone gets hit, call it out. If you're enabling something for the team, call it out. These are supposed to be experts. I can't imagine anyone doing a confident quip in a fun, chipper tone after getting punched 10 feet away by a giant monster. You're not breathing at that point. How are you quipping?

In summary, this game thinks its giving you more options to play than one or two did, but in reality it's fewer in every regard. It runs poorly, it's tiring to play (movement), and it's the most repetitive the series has ever been. It's frustrating because you can tell the developers are great and everything they have has a lot of care and effort put into it, but the overall design and direction of the progression loops and the annoying monetization of this premium-priced title is just icing on the cake. KF3 devs, who made you kneecap your own game? Why did it end up like this? I really hope this game get some overhauls because like I said earlier, there is something in here.

review: KF3 kinda lost its way. KF1 and 2 were silly at times, and didn't take itself too seriously. Because of that, some of the flaws of the game were more forgiving. KF3 is rather stern and rigid, and I don't feel invested in the characters. The level up mechanisms is a clear improvement over kf1/2, and you can mod the weapons like deadspace. The DLC content is very boring and player content is player specific, unlike kf2 where say anyone could wear the sunglasses. In that manner, it feels like youre forced to earn a bunch of junk you dont want, neither can you recycle; nonsensical filler. I miss fun characters like Rae Higgins and Anton Strasser. I miss the goofy bosses. The stages feel oppressive and draconian. The game itself is very PC intensive, and you have to wait for shaders to load. The player start area is annoying, repetitive and large for no reason. There are very few stages all in all, 9 maybe? There are no ammo boxes laying around like kf1 and kf2, and your health refills dont regenerate. On the harder difficulties, when you run out of ammo or health you're just done. A lot of the cool classes have been nixed, condensed, or replaced. Weapons are all scifi-ish now vs anything recognizable. There are no random drops of anything. We DO see tweaking of classic opponents as well as some new ones which is nice. There are a lot of weapons and perks that are fun. Although you cant change player classes once youre in a game, you can still use the weapons. You can custom configure weapons before hand and buy those at the trader. A lot of neat stage items can be leveraged like auto turrets and zip lines. Theres a lot more character movements like slide and parry, charged shots and alt fire modes. But again, the game comes off as being tacti-cool, instead of a zany survive-a-zombie-apocalypse scavenger motif. Buy this game if youre loyal to the franchise. I have 125hrs in so far, once I rank everything up I'll probably move on or wait for another expansion pack.

review:
You know something is wrong with your franchise when the new release is a lot worse than your first 2005 mod.

The Worst:
First off, as a whole, this game plays poorly. Input lag exists all over, animation is terrible, and hit detection is spotty; gunplay has lost its oomf, guns feel unsatisfying to shoot, and the broken hit boxes create a fight that's more annoying than exciting. Identifying ZEDs during a chaotic wave is impossible.

The Visuals:
This game takes on an almost generic "UE5" style and loses the grittiness that was the original's style. The original atmosphere, a bleak post-apocalyptic world with dark humor from Britain, has turned into a bland, overly serious version. The personalities of characters have disappeared and feel like a serious step backwards from KF2.

Missing Features:
It's quite surprising that this game is so minimalistic. There is no text chat, no emotes, no voice lines or taunts, and really nothing else to express yourself with as a player. While emotes and player-initiated voice lines were a small detail in the last two versions, they added personality and felt alive. The absence of text-chat is clearly due to some woke nonsense.

Monetization:
Paying $15 to take off a helmet from a character is setting a bad standard. And considering there are so many missing core features, I wouldn't say it's aggressive, I would say it's outright predatory.

The Trader:
Another thing that disappointed me was the trader. In place of returning the old trader character from Killing Floor 1 or KFMod 2.5, we have to continue using the bot trader system again. All of the cool details of a trader room are just gone.

The Maps:
Probably the best part of this game. Maps are great design-wise, visually pleasing, and allow for a variety of ways to engage in combat. It shows that the team put a lot of work into designing the maps and flow.

Good Changes:
There were attempts to differentiate the gameplay of Killing Floor 3 from the previous titles in this series. I appreciate this attempt, although the implementation did not always succeed. Another thing I liked about this title is that it returns to creepy whispers from the zombies. It adds to the atmosphere somewhat and brings back some memories of the original mod. I do, however, appreciate that there are currently no loot crates (at least).

Summary:
Overall, I believe Killing Floor 3 has misunderstood what made it unique. A big part of what made the original so popular was the tone and personality it had. Satisfying gun play was another part of why people loved playing earlier versions. Those elements have been taken out of this new title and replaced with something more generic and boring. Although some of the map designs show potential, along with having some new ideas that could have worked better, there are too many problems with the core gameplay and identity of Killing Floor 3 to call this title a good addition to the franchise.

review:
2026 review:

-I played the horrible mess that was the early access beta.
-Game still feels like an early access beta, but now you can choose your character (wow)

The worst thing about the game is the performance and how the game feels when performance is low.
I get a solid 120 fps but when 6 players are on the server and shit hits the fan, the game stutters and it doesn't show on the fps meter, but it feels like playing on variable fps that's going below 60.
Not a good thing in a game where you are supposed to shoot headshots and weakpoints.

When zeds bump into you, it's like your character is rubberbanding in place. It feels awful. There might be some knockback effect that's causing it, but I'm not completely sure.

Other smaller negatives:
-Forced single player tutorial. Stupid and pointless.
-Tutorial messages and story related mission messages taking up valuable screen space. They can't be disabled. Why??
-Matchmaking put me in a 200ms server while I was the one starting the match. So the matchmaking didn't match me with a distant player, it just put me in a distant server by myself. This doesn't happen all the time but it is notable that it happened at all.
-Audio design in a nutshell: zeds can walk up right behind you without you hearing them. Directional audio is a mess. I would love to help shoot down the scrake that's enraged but I have no idea where the sound is coming from. Etc.

Gameplay:
KF 2 style map design but even more cramped. There aren't any safe areas where you can hold zeds in a chokepoint, there are always crawlers spawning from the walls, firebugs flying behind you and shooting you from the sky, and clots spawning from the tiniest holes you can imagine.
This results in very messy, spam heavy combat. It just isn't satisfying when all you are doing is spending the maximum amount of ammunition in the least amount of time. While doing 180s constantly.
The gadgets and turrets are a nice addition to watch your back.

I can't go too deep about the classes cause I can't be bothered to play any more.
The ninja is pretty fun but where the fuck is berserker my beloved?
The sharpshooter could be fun if I didn't have constant stutters.
Maybe I'll try again late this year assuming they do all the planned patches.

review:
I think I've played enough gametime to give a fair review. here's my take. bullet point form cause it feels more readable for me.

Likes:
+Since ive been playing Ninja, I like the inclusion of Dashes and Slides. its takes the ideas from Darktide to a tea. 
+Specialist characters seem to talk less and are less annoying
+Glad you are now not locked to a character when you choose a perk. Should've been there from the start.
+you dont need to hop in the Vtol anymore plus every part of the the hub can be accessed in a menu immediately
+The "Battle Pass" is actually pretty pro consumer and follows Helldivers. You'll have enough to get at least 1 premium pass for free if you keep playing the game.
+Kill shots are meaty and have nice sound effects
+Unlike other coop games, this has a solo mode so I gotta give credit
+I like the inclusion of missions and comics. gives us some access to the story

Dislikes:
-The game is poorly optimized. when there are many particles on screen (flames, explosions, freezes) forcing me to mod the games ini file. even so, it needs Frame Gen for it to work.

--The game did not introduce that Bonus abilities are RNG when you craft them and there is no info which mod can possibly get which bonus ability. This lengthens the grind of resources unnecessarily. You have the codex. you can put that info there if you insist on this RNG grind.

--Its Dedicated Servers. not Peer to Peer. making multiplayer experience horrible especially for Ninjas with builds who rely on Parries. Cant even choose servers. Even so theres no excuse when Darktide has dedicated servers yet its multiplayer remains smooth.

--lacking visual feedback such as Parries being very inconsistent and unreliable in multiplayer
 
--Cannot check Ping. have to go to options > gameplay > Crossplay 

--The Gadget Hook Ninja ability is very buggy and inconsistent. There is no targetting so you end up missing a shot and it sometimes leave you in an opening longer than usual since its so buggy, this goes worse in multiplayer. Also hook sometimes double taps.

--there are bonus abilities about bash damage but there is no info about bash damage in the game at all
--Block Stamina and Heavy attack charge level are both in the same bar. whose idea was this? its awful to look at since they're both the same bar

--Rhodes sounds annoying compared to the other Operator. just replace her with that Old lady instead.

--No Text Chat

--No Kill Feed. I would like to know if I killed the boss or the large zed. There is a feed for callouts, so use that.

--No Lobby / Server browser

--Switching from Solo to Multiplayer is awful. why not just turn matchmaking on/off from the get-go? why always go back to menu to do it?

--My Player Card keeps going back to default when there are disconnects happening (BUG)

--Sometimes in multiplayer cannot Fill up my Primary weapon in Trader (BUG)

--Levelling up is painfully slow

--Sometimes even in Solo HOE, myy healing pistol loses its healing darts. it doesnt regen anymore (BUG)

--Cannot emote in game. just callouts. this is sad. Kf2 already has this. you could even add this to fill up your supply pass rewards instead of useless weapon charms and stickers.
--Damage feedback is terrible. you just get flinched without knowing what hit you leading you to die without knowing what killed you

--Devlin and Clone Foster sound pretty annoying than the rest of the cast. Even more than Scully

--The training room is lacking. there should be Damage numbers in one of the dummy targets so that we can gauge the damage. you can be creative by making the dummy targets have the health of a HOE Large Zed like SCrake or Fleshpound. Make it have purpose so those content creators can make more informed builds using this area. (basically a Darktide Psykanium/training area)

--The game doesnt tell you that Operational budget (the initial guns you bring to the first wave) are one time use only and doesnt carry over. I only realized cause I found it out from some youtubers.

Since I have more dislikes, I still cant recommend this game. Its still lacking in a lot of areas.

review:
This game feels more like a mod or early access than a full release. The maps are very small, almost like arena-style layouts, and the gameplay quickly becomes repetitive - you’re fighting the same 3-5 enemy types over and over again. This game only offers a 5-wave or 10-wave mode, which isn’t enough to keep things interesting.

Visually, the game is underwhelming. The graphics are generic and lack any distinct or memorable art style. What’s worse is that despite not looking particularly impressive, the game has surprisingly high hardware requirements (I recommend an RTX 4070 or higher). There are noticeable FPS drops whenever new enemies spawn, which hurts the overall experience.

From a technical standpoint, it feels like the game is running on outdated engine technology. Modern engines - like those used by Saber Interactive that is called Swarm Engine, can handle hundreds of enemies smoothly, so it’s disappointing to see performance issues at this scale.

In terms of design, the game would benefit greatly from more variety. Adding multiple enemy factions or “races” would make the gameplay more engaging, similar to how other shooters diversify their encounters (e.g. Destiny 2 got like 5 different enemy races). Right now, everything feels too repetitive.

The art direction also needs a complete rethink. Many successful games don’t rely on cutting-edge graphics but instead stand out through unique and recognizable art styles (e.g. Team Frotress 2, Borderlands, Overwatch, WarCraft 3, Destiny 2 and so on). This game lacks that identity, making it feel generic and forgettable.

As it stands, the game doesn’t justify a high price. It would be more appropriate as a €20 title at most, €5 on sale, or even a free-to-play game supported by a season pass and cosmetic shop.

Overall, it feels like a generic FPS mod rather than a fully realized game. You’re not missing much if you skip it.

I recommend that the development team introduce more diverse zombie races and game modes, redesign the art direction to establish a unique visual identity, and explore licensing the Swarm Engine from Saber Interactive.

Anyone looking for a good zombie game should try John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando!

review:
After quitting this game because multiplayer had severe lag and server connection issues, I'm happy to say that after over 8 months away, the issues still persist. What a mess of a game, absolute disgrace to the series. Stick to KF1/2.

Updated review:
What a downfall for such a beloved franchise. KF1 was amazing and set the scene for wave based zombie games in a way that wasn't done before. It was so unique in the terrifying and creepy atmosphere and did so well despite limited budget. 

KF2 came along and had a slightly bumpy launch but quickly became another phenomenal game. Improved on the first in every way, gameplay, graphics, QOL, atmosphere etc. Genuinely such amazing first two games to the series.

KF3 finally launches after so much hype. I cannot begin to put into words how much of an utter disappointment this game is. It genuinely feels like the devs were trying to make some open world battle royale, realised it wouldn't work and at the 11th hour salvaged it into whatever this is. Unoptimised, clunky, soulless garbage. I'm so disappointed and it's difficult to even convey this in my review. Fans of the series have been betrayed by the devs with this release, it is such a monumental failure compared to the expectations and standards the first two games had set. It's plagued with technical issues, multiplayer lag/disconnects, frame rate drops, stutters, freezes and that's before we get into how bad the gameplay and atmosphere of the game feels. It's like someone went into ChatGPT and asked it to create a new Killing Floor and this is what it came up with. It's blatantly obvious this was meant to be some microtransaction ridden open world battle royale style game which they abandoned at the last second and created this instead. What an absolute let down. 

If you're a fan of the series, stick to the first two games.

KF3 leans to far away from what the first two brought. The new zed designs are fine and cool. I was really excited to see the zeds in trailers and media. Although they don't fit in what this game offers. I was still hopeful when the game was coming out. 

Except when the beta came around. It was clear from the start it made to be something else. The game came with an nda being the start of many red flags. Run's like shit on my old pc and my new one. It heavily un-optimized, a lot of people say there systems fail to run it with higher specs than mine with enabling dls and such. My pc is mid range compared to what they rock. As for the design of the game I still feel the Killing Floor vibes especially since I'm playing all of them for achievement grinding. review:
KF3 definitely has potential but there are some things really holding it down. For starters optimization for this game is quite literally non existent. To be fair that's on me for not checking the required specs before buying. 
The game feels rushed and still unfinished and some of the new gameplay features kind of remind me of Helldivers. Mainly the starting hub, the mission selection screen and the scavenging the maps for resources for upgrades.
Most maps are bleak and lack personality. The voice lines are buggy and a bit anti-climactic, they didn't even manage to record downed voice lines. Animations for Executing a zed and being executed by a zed are buggy and delayed. 
But looking passed all of that I still found myself really enjoying the game and wanting to keep playing apart from the constant crashes and my graphics being in the toilet. I do really enjoy the new movement mechanics since it adds a way to maneuver around enemy attacks. The Zeds now feel like a real threat compared to the Zeds in KF2. The gun gameplay is interesting because the guns feel weak but I like that. It adds a feeling of helplessness and desperation to any situation you're in.
Ultimately the price tag for this game is NOT worth it.

Please let this game f***** die so that lazy Game Devs learn to be honest with the playerbase.

It's basically Helldivers meets Call of Duty meets Killing Floor.

I don't get why Tripwire felt the need to copy another game. It's like they had zero confidence in creating another masterpiece.

Performance is still an issue. Some maps run really rough. Game is very unoptimized.

With that being said. I have enjoyed the game for what it is. I try to ignore the fact that this is a Killing Floor game.

The game is not pleasantly busy like KF2 was, but visually cluttered making the already milquetoast redesigns of classic enemies blend into the cluttered yet soulless environment design. And this is before we get into the mess of custom weapons. I do not know who this game was made for, but it sure wasn't for me.

review:
It's a fun game, but has a lot of stuff that clashes with what one might have expected to be having played the first 2 games throughout the years. It advanced in some places, but I'd say it did some bad decisions.

Good
An upgrade system (with buffs if you can max them out), ammo options (each with their own dynamics), more perks per class (perk active special skills), kept the identity of the Zeds and gave them additional features. Multiple unique bosses. Directional dodging mechanic.

Less then ideal
Default set of 6 waves + Boss of Zeds with no option for increased waves, or endless waves, it takes a long while to grind resources for weapon upgrades, weapon upgrade bonuses are random (recraft for reroll). No customization during a game, no cross-class weapon progress (they seem to do the same damage without the appropriate perk).

I don't know if the sliding mechanic is a good thing or bad thing, but it feels unnecessary. It let's me slide down stairs, but outside of that it barely does much.

TL;DR the gameplay loop has a lot of friction, and makes it a bit hard to recommend.

I'm not opposed to all the decisions, I would just like to have more familiar things return.

review:
It's unbelievable what the development studio has brought to market here. There is absolutely nothing I can say that is positive about it. The German dubbing is by far the worst I have ever experienced in my more than 30-year gaming career. 

The movement is terrible, the weapons don't feel right, the purchase menu is absolute garbage, the HUD is cluttered with annoying pop-ups and mission hints, the enemy AI is terrible, the graphics are nowhere near as good as in the trailers, and the game constantly switches between German and English dubbing on its own. If you want to switch from the solo hub to the main menu, you have to watch the entire disclaimer and loading time display again, including an explanation of it, only to then have to press a button again to load your profile data so you can finally return to the main menu. Loading the shaders when starting the game for the first time took a whopping 10 minutes, regardless of whether it was done with an RTX 3090 or an RTX 5080. In every round, there are multiple severe lag spikes that sometimes last 1-2 seconds.

With the best will in the world, I can only advise everyone not to play this garbage, let alone buy it. I agree with other reviews here and recommend playing Killing Floor 1&2 if you haven't already. 


I can't understand how anyone could turn such a good franchise into such crap. The developers and publisher should be fired and never allowed to develop or release games again.

review:
Positives: 
1. Good graphics
2. Stable Performance 

Negatives:
1. Boring.
2. Not enough content(8 maps at launch and taking nearly 4-5 months to add a single one? Laughable. Literally not even a quarter of the weapon count base Killing Floor 2 had at launch too.)
3. Generic. You've played this game if you ever played: Back 4 Blood, Left 4 Dead 2, or any CoD zombies mode. Furthermore, these games have done everything this game set out to do infinitely better.
4. Annoying/unlikable characters: The girly girl who is quirky, the tech guy/engineer who makes technology references, the doctor who makes medical puns/jokes, and the bri'ish bloke that was done better in the previous two games.
5. No community mods/servers. This makes no sense when the previous two games thrived on this...
6. Crossplay issues: this is my largest gripe, don't implement a feature that isn't to work, especially don't if you aren't going to fix it!

Overall this game is just painfully boring and generic. No individual identity in a sea of generic horde based zombie shooters. The nicest thing it has going for it is that looks good. Save your time and money and just buy anything else at this point. If you're a Killing floor veteran, I'm sorry this happened to you.

Updates: they seemed to have patched the cross play issues. Yay, the game is still painfully boring with absolutely zero charm or originality. Banking on recognizable characters from your franchise for a cheap nostalgia 'member berries is the classic sign of a studio who ran out of ideas and are desperate. 

The player count on steam even on weekends is absolutely horrendous. Just under 250 people peak? Time to throw in the towel, start over, you're done. The player count tanked in just a month from approx 16k to 3k... Ouch.

Reintroducing basic features from previous games that were available at launch is not a "major update". It's a sign your game was unfit to be sold in the state you offered it in. This game still have performance problems, although incredibly minor in scale to how it was at launch. 

While a minor mercy; the game is just bad. Do no buy this; even if it is free, just stay away.

review:
I would wait until it is cheap or until significant improvements are made before purchasing KF3. KF2 is still far more enjoyable, functional & affordable.

Pros:
-I really like the ninja class and there's a more noticeable difference between playing the classes
-Playing with the different specials are fun
-I like the slide and ziplines different tactics / styles of evasion and combat and can appreciate the effort put into the changes like the ammo/heal bags, traps etc.
-new killing floor content 

Cons:
-3/5 times the game crashes in the middle of my game and I loose my progress and game. 
-It often crashes looking for a server to join even if you pick any - and the lack of ability to choose your server - nothing like being added into the end of a groups round and then everyone leaving because...
-you cant view your needed daily/weekly tasks once victory in the game is achieved so nobody stays for a second game 9/10 times.
- no ability to text chat with teammates.
-no choice of length of game. 
-One of the fun things about kf2 was unlocking special fun gear and all the gear they want you to buy / that you can work to get for free in kf3 are all BASIC/LAME and have barely any distinction between each other to make it matter at all. 
-Overly embraced the cheat safe software it uses as a game aesthetic and it is soooooo lame, lazy, tacky and unappealing. I don't even care that it uses cheat safe but its super lame to make it such a huge deal and part of the aesthetic. 

I'm hoping that over time they will continue to better the game and make it more desirable to play or lower the price to reflect a fair gameplay to cost experience. If you get to try if for free to ahead it is fun but be ready to be stripped of control over your gameplay and probably crash out of most your games. I hope the 2000 crashes I report help fix the problem XD

Not as good as KF2. The hit detection feels off. Its lacking content on launch and feels like KF2 when it was in early access. Some may say that KF2 started barebones, but KF2 launched in early access, this game doesn't have an early access tag so will be judged as a full release.

Pros:
the class talents feel much better now. class abilities are a welcome addition. Melee feels stronger and more impactful on the ninja than it did on the Berserker in KF2. EXP is tied to playing your class and not using the class weapons so you can use any weapons you want technically. More ability to climb and ziplines make the movement around the map better. Ability to mod weapons is nice. No more loot boxes is a plus, its a battle pass, which will annoy some, but I'll take a battle pass vs a loot box anyday. 

Cons: lacking content. Hit detection feels more like KF1 than KF2. All personality has been fully sapped out of the game. KF1 felt cheeky and british and I loved it. KF2 had less, but several of the same characters returned and had the same voice actors and still felt silly. KF3 has no silly, its decades in the future so everyone is dead and mr foster returns as a "clone". The team is fully international and so are the missions. makes sense storywise and how its progressed, but it feels so distant from the charm of the original. it has battle passes, which will be a negative to many, even if its a step up from the loot boxes, for some I understand that its negative regardless (the bar is so low its on the ground). Originally the characters were tied to the classes. There are less enemy types in KF3 than KF2 had at launch, and now especially has less. I don't understand why we have to take a step back, they could have just ported over the same enemies from KF2 and added more later. I heard they have since removed that, but I haven't played it since because I'd rather play another coop shooter instead. Oh and player hosted servers are gone.

TLDR: it lacks the charm of KF2 and especially KF1. hit detection feels off. less content than KF2 had at early access launch. it feels like this is the Sims and we have to take a step back everytime a new entry launche and we have to wait years for them to add back the content from the previous entry. Just go play KF2 and get it and most of the DLC weapons on a dirt cheap sale.

review:
Honestly where do i begin with this game.... I want to love this game because i really love kf2 and when i heard this game was coming out, I was super excited! I don't understand why content they release is now considered "new" when it's already in the last game. The performance is horrible and that's why UE5 is horrible if the devs don't understand how to optimize it, I can run this game just fine but i would rather just go back to kf2 with a really high framerate so it will be way smoother to enjoy. Kf2 in my opinion has better graphics with a more vibrant look to it and again with the horrible performance, It's hard to get new players on kf3 and if they don't have the best hardware out there, Then just forget about playing kf3 and especially with the prices of PC parts lately definitely forget about it. I'm really not trying to bash this game but the negatives out weigh the positives. The weapons in kf2 are really something special and never get old using but the weapons in kf3 are like peashooters against sponges, The selection of weapons in this game is very underwhelming while the weapons in kf2 actually feel great to use. I totally understand that this game just came out and won't have as much content as the previous game but there should of been more maps, weapons and characters at launch. The last negative thing i will say is that the new characters are horrendous but i'm happy we got Foster and now Scully but the new characters need to be replaced with the ones in the previous game and then maybe add new ones. Few things i enjoy is the new movement because it's truly helpful in combat and the new system of putting attachments on weapons is really a cool thing. I would of loved if we had different attachments in kf2 but overall i'm glad they finally added that feature. I will gladly change my review from negative to positive if they fix and add better content but as of right now, I just can't recommend this game in this state, I hate that i can't recommend this game because killing floor in general is really a great franchise!

Edit 7/24/26: Played it again and i must sadly say my review remains mostly the same. Performance being one of the big ones, It's gotten better and I'm honestly happy about that even though it took a while. That's the only positive for me but it sucks for that to be the only one. If you are thinking about getting into Killing Floor then just go with KF2, It's cheap and has a lot of content with a great community! I'm not giving up on kf3 but as of right now i am. Also why is Medic so bad in this game and the limited stims is crazy to me.

review:
Updated for Season 4:

I still can't recommend this game yet but it certainly getting there. 
There is a lot of work still to do to get this feeling like a proper killing floor game and I do have hope the team can pull it off if given time. 

TLDR,  After season 4 the game is feeling better to play. Combat is more consistent, Gunslinger is feeling really nice to shoot with. Some of the classes are lagging behind. Performance, sound, anim could really do with a final oomph polish pass. 

The good: 
-Map art, zeds models all look great. 
-Gunplay is sort of getting there, but deffo needs more, oomph. Shooting in KF2 feels better on audio and anim feedback than in KF3 (Most likely due to mocap)
- Skill tree is great (they fixed the crashes!)
- Characters are no longer tied to classes which is fantastic!
- Weapon customisation is a nice addition. The grind has been reduced even more with being able to choose your T3 mod and material exchange. 
- 10 WAVES IS BACK!

The eh:
- Limited healing, and no healing team with your syringes. You have to buy the inf healing pistol. Medics main weapons will run out of charges and need to be rebought (Outside of one weapon that earns them when dealing damage)
       - I would personally like the inf syringes back on a long cooldown, but you can speed up the recharge by doing damage to zeds. Healing a team mate reduces the cooldown by half. 
- Medics weapons feel awful, Insane recoil, weak damage. With customisation there is 0 reason to take a medic weapon when you can just make another classes weapon have a healing dart on it if you want. (S4 still very much the case)
- Battlepasses are eh so far, but at least you can earn credits for the next one by playing just by completing the battlepass. (Latest battlepass is better, but its still eh)
- The Stronghold (Previously bad)  has been made pretty much redundant withe verything being available via tab, and ready up being done without going to the VTOL. This is signicantly better. Needs a way to interact with the area alone, and with teammates to make it an actual hub area. 

The Bad (Removed a lot of this list and im being way more petty now):

- Spatial audio is absolutely awful. I can barely hear a team mate firing their weapon. A full horde combat grouped together sounds like your the only one putting in any work. 
- Physics - Every single zed is going flying and not in a fun way. I hit them with a pistol and they're sent across the map
- Gore - Feels like this has regressed a bit. Firebug especially, why is my flamethrower dismembering and popping heads? Just cook em please. Charred effects barely applying. Damage  always being removal of the limb and not stripped flesh. It looks weak compared to what it was advertised to be. 
- Performance. My rig is not the problem, it's my friends i play with. They are stuttering a lot even on lowest settings. A good low end pass so low end systems can enjoy this game would be amazing.

review:
I want to start by saying that I loved Killing Floor 2, but this game feels like a step down in comparison. Yes, the graphics are better. Yes, you can now add attachments to your guns, which is a great addition. And yes, enemy behavior has changed due to the new setting. However, despite these improvements, the overall gameplay feels rather bland.

There are only a handful of maps available, most of which feel much smaller and less detailed than those in Killing Floor 2. There are also roughly half the number of classes the second game had, and the perk systems feel more complicated than they need to be. Weapon variety has taken a noticeable hit as well, with only about 25–50% of the weapon choices that Killing Floor 2 offered.

The cosmetic system is another major downgrade. In Killing Floor 2, you could at least grind for cosmetics or buy exactly what you wanted from the Community Market. In this game, you earn armory points to unlock items, which sounds good at first, until you unlock around ten items and are then required to spend real money to continue.

Overall, the few improvements are appreciated, but they don’t make up for what was lost. These changes would have worked much better as a DLC rather than a full sequel.

[b]5/10[/b]

review:
I must say that after the disaster of the game’s launch, it has improved a lot.
Overall, the game is now a decent, casual, action, zombie shooter.
It’s fun to play, but it’s nothing special. It became more casual than the previous Killing Floor games, which is where it lost fans of the more hardcore gameplay, but it also failed to be interesting enough for a broader audience.
And since the game market is very saturated, there is no room for errors at launch.
The first impression is important, and despite massive improvements compared to the release version, the player base died out. From my experience, a dead game can rarely be revived.
They’re very slow at bringing out updates and new content, and the game is now basically dead, with around 300 PC players on average. Consoles have roughly three times that number, and lobbies are almost always filled about 80% with console players. But it still feels dead.

It’s definitely not worth the full price, and even on sale for $20 I can’t really recommend it.
You can get at least 50 hours out of it while learning the game and leveling classes, but the gameplay loop becomes boring sooner or later.

review:
[Edit at 11 hours: The game does get better but core features still arent great. The main issues of the previous version down below still apply to various extents.]
Im going to be brutally honest here. The game isnt worth your time. I bought it when it was discounted to 1 euro and while I dont regret it, I really dont see myself playing it at any point in the future. The game has zero realism and thats unacceptable for a simulator. Especially one which is called ultimate fishing simulator. In my short time playing it it became abundantly clear to me that its half-assed in practically every realism aspect concerning the equipment and fish fighting mechanics.  It takes fishing planets path of higher level = stronger equipment and from what I understood it doesnt even factor the reels capacity and the fishing line thickness when it comes to how much fishing line you can put on it. Moving the rod around feels absolutely useless fighting the fish. And take 'fight' with a spoonful of salt cause 1 landed a 6.7 KG rainbow trout with probably less than a minute of resistance on a 1.5 kg monoline. On the same line I was flinging a 2kg largemouth in the air before collecting it. Aka game physics are non-existent where it matters. Hauled over a 9kg rainbow trout on a 3kg max drag reel (I wasnt even using max drag) in probably less than a minute too. I havent used the aracade mode nor the sandbox mode. Just the realism mode. The shop is half assed too. 
The graphics are awful but for the 1 euro price tag its ok I guess (Ultra preset). At least the fish are done well on that end. 
From what I understood (In realism mode) each lure is only meant to be used with one retrieval method but I might be wrong on that. And each lure can only be bought at a specific gram weight and while there are different colors I HIGHLY doubt they coded something around colors  affecting the lures effectiveness depending on the different environmental factors or the fish targeted. 

I dont know if this game was made by coders that dont know how to fish or fishermen who dont know how to code well. Regardless of which scenario it is they definitely gave up mid development. You cant possibly half-ass a game this much otherwise.

Like seriously I throw in the lure, let it drop as low as it will go before closing the reel and when a fish bites directly after the tension line appears directly on the surface of the water and suddenly the fish is at topwater. 

Stick to RF4 for realism and genuine fishing mechanics (and of course graphics). Even as a completely FtP gamer you will have a much better time in RF4. As for fishing planet, you have to make the choice of either grinding for hours in a game that is as greedy as a megacorporation but at least has accurate(ish) fishing mechanics, or getting the 1 time purchase UFS 2 which is a vastly inferior simulator game but it wont ask for any more money. If you respect your time then you would do neither and simply find a different category of game to play. 

If you want a game for a child that doesnt know about fishing I can recommend UFS 2. If you want an accurate fishing simulator then steer FAAAAAARRR away from UFS 2. 
I might not delete this game purely because I can play it offline (Unlike RF4) but beyond that there is zero worthwhile reason to play this. 
If I had bought it full price I would have felt scammed. But I can see it giving me a better experience than a packet of chewing gum (1 euro).
Might play more to see if it gets better at any point in the progression.

review:
Held together by duct tape, poor optimization and dreams of being a real Remedy game.

The concept had potential, but the user experience isn't kosher.  From the moment you launch the game, the lack of polish hits you.

My onboarding experience began with the game forcing me into a windowed mode despite selecting borderless fullscreen.  It then bypassed the main menu entirely and pushed me into gameplay without even giving me the chance to configure basic settings or keybinds.  Who designed this onboarding flow?

Once in the game, I attempted to alter the settings - and the game crashed.  Turning on ray tracing caused the game to crash while still in the options section - and then it wouldn't launch.  I had to manually hunt down a configuration file in a completely different directory and edit it just to launch the game again.  Once back in, I had no idea what to do.  If what I had been pushed into was a tutorial, it was nowhere to be found (that I saw).

[For those who need it, I found the config file here: "YOUR PATH/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/2272540/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/Local/Remedy/FBCFirebreak/renderer.ini"]

Underneath the broken settings and unstable performance is a product that feels unfinished, unpolished and poorly designed.  Optimization is a fever dream the devs never explored.  As I progressed into each session, "playing" increasingly felt like wading through mud and the display looked not unlike a slide show of still life paintings.  Lowering the settings didn't alleviate the issues.

Unfortunately, much that I've heard about Firebreak seems to be true.  While there is fun to be had, to experience it firsthand is a bit shocking, as I've enjoyed all Remedy titles to date.  Hints of Remedy are present, but they do little to improve the experience and serve only to remind me of their better games.

This game feels like a poorly implemented fan-made mod - made for a Remedy game that was never released.  I advise you not to buy this game in its current state.  It shouldn't have been released in this state (which is after, seemingly, all the updates it will receive) and given the update history (or lack thereof), its release state, the game's poor reception and sales to date, there's little reason to believe the game will meaningfully change, if at all.

I just don't understand.  There are similar games on the market to consider.  This game doesn't even possess basic features considered staples of the genre.  It's as bare-bones and slapdash as can be.  Even if this were a mode bolted onto Control, it would've needed more time in the oven - and an overhaul.

review:
[h1] The 7 Year Ordeal [/h1]

Remedy, I'm disappointed in you. This game has so much potential to be fun and it just falls flat on its face. To keep this short, the game is essentially unplayable if you want a challenge and are playing solo or with another. I shouldn't have to play with anyone to be able to complete a level, it should scale enemies and difficulty to match. However, this is not the case with Firebreak.

Enemy spawns are laughably excessive. I can't barely get through one wave before 2 more spawn. My guns feel like peashooters and enemy weapons feel like 50cal snipers. The characters are slow, and I'll even dig on the cosmetics because wtf were they thinking with 75% of the choices?

Progression on paper is good, but far too slow for how little content there actually is. There are 6 different stages to choose from with slight variations in modifiers. Admittedly, I like the concept of all 6, especially since I love the lore and world of Control so much. Sadly, when you force a player to have to constantly restock health and ammo ad nauseum then it becomes trite. I was playing with a friend on hard (not even extreme!!) and we became softlocked due to the fact we could not kill enemies fast enough and they would constantly break the machines necessary to complete the mission. We ran out of lives and game over. 30 min or more wasted. Poor design.

I would honestly steer clear of this one. Not much to offer for the frustration. I doubt they'll patch it, but if they do I'd consider revisiting.

review:
I love Control and I love Co-Op PVE games. I was excited when I heard this game was a thing and really wanted to enjoy it. I even bought it on launch, played for roughly 10 hours and came back to it.

Sadly... this game is absolutely terrible. Like genuinely one of the worst I have ever played. I don't think I can truly touch on everything this game does badly, so for the cons I think I will keep it to the big ones.

PROS:
-Hank (narrator/mission control guy) is genuinely fun
-It is visually appealing

CONS:
-Gunplay is weak and floaty, shots don't feel impactful at all
-Content is amongst the weakest I have ever seen in a full release. It isn't just that there aren't a lot of missions; the layout is always the same and the missions themselves are tiny
-No scaling based on players in-game despite having a nonexistent player base
-Difficulty is done TERRIBBLY even though they had the answer right in front of them! Corruption modifiers are fun and add interesting impacts to the game. Raising the baseline difficulty just adds genuinely endless spam. I tried doing the OSHA achievement and found it it is basically impossible to do solo unless you're willing to spend literally 2-3 hours in a mission that is supposed to take about 15 minutes just because the spawns never stop.
-No interesting progression whatsoever. Cosmetics look awful, no interesting meta progression

I am glad Remedy took a swing at making a game like this, but FBC: Firebreak is a massive miss.

review:
At first I was like, WOW, why haven't I heard of this game? A Remedy Left 4 Dead sounds amazing! Playing as FBC agents, investigating and then containing the anomalies? Count me in! Then after finishing all the maps (I think there was six, one-area maps in total) in a few hours, I got it.

There's nothing much to the game at all. Not even an interactable lobby area where you can check out the FBC building (now wouldn't that be sick if you had your own cubicle and got to see all the lore bits you collected?). No real lobby = quick, mobile game experience-feel. 

Game has special equipment called Crisis Kits. They looked wacky and were fun to use (got a certain TF2 zaniest to it), but if the goal is to extract fast, then there's no need for any of them except for the repair kit. This kit comes with a stationary turret and a melee weapon: the wrench can clear objectives faster, repair healing and ammo stations - all necessities (but I guess if everyone had to have one, the game would be even more bland). Also, even though the weapon feedback felt good, all the low-caliber guns sucked against all enemy types.

My group played multiple difficulties, still FBC: Firebreak felt the same. It's too clear on what to do in the game to get maximum efficiency on everything that it becomes repetitive, which is fine for this genre, but there are SO few maps and enemy variety that it is also boring. Repetitive AND boring = not a game.

Extraction games, when you gotta do a time crunch there's adrenaline, the music changes, for example, Back 4 Blood adds in percussion when a horde arrives, this game, no adrenaline, I'm running but I don't care, the game doesn't either. I can see why this had friend passes. FBC: Firebreak still feels like it is in EARLY ACCESS in terms of everything (except optimization, it ran perfect on my Legion GO). The one time it was fun was doing the boss fight with friends. There was only one, the rest were mini bosses that don't really do much but float around.

No offense, but not for me. Might not be for color-blinded people either, it has a really unfriendly color palette. Refunded.

review:
What's here is so, so good, and there's an incredible foundation...

...for an alpha game.  For a fully released game?  There's just...not enough here.  12 weapons, 3 "classes" to play, and 6 missions.  And an endless mode.  And while it's all very competent and immensely fun...there just isn't enough content.  After about 4 hours, you've seen everything the game has to offer, and the only reason to keep going is...to spin a hamster wheel.

Which is a huge shame, because I wanted more, desperately.  The bones here are incredible and this could have been something.  But as a fully released and definitively finished game?  There's not enough here, not by a long shot.  Even ramping up the difficulty just makes enemies swarm, the balance is a little all over the place, it's...a bit of a mess, honestly.  It's a super fun mess, and I wish I had a reason to play in it some more.  But there's not enough reason to keep going, and not enough to see or do.

Fun for an afternoon with friends, but don't expect it to have anything resembling staying power.

review:
The best way I could describe this game is disappointing.

As a huge fan of the Remedyverse I was immensely looking forward to this game, and what I ended up getting was... lacklustre, to say the least.

I genuinely don't know why they rushed the release of this game so much. The amount of content is so miniscule, the replayability is pretty much non-existent, and with the game not getting more updates there's nothing left to bring you back to it. There's essentially no lore to be explored, in the most lore heavy setting of the series, which I found to be the most saddening fact. The gunplay is [i]fine[/i] and entirely unremarkable. The concept of a Left 4 Dead clone in the Control universe is incredible, the execution is unfortunately sloppy.
It's not ALL bad - the soundtrack is nice and groovy, and the banter between the firebreakers can be amusing, but that's about it. All of the other gameplay elements have been done better elsewhere.

Never thought I'd be writing a negative review of a Remedy game, but this one isn't really worth it even at a 40% price reduction.

review:
I really want to like this game. It has a myriad of issues, so let's start with the abstract, non gameplay issues:

1) Clear Branding Fail:
Instead of naming this game Control: Firebreak, they named this FBC: Firebreak. I know, I know -- it's not a single player game, so they don't want to set the expectation that this game is a direct continuation of Control. But for most players, "FBC" means nothing. How are you supposed to know it refers to the Federal Bureau of Control? That's the fun part: you don't, unless you know about the game already. So now you're not reaching players who may know about the series.

2) And Again...:
What the hell about the series design or logo says "Game set in the control universe!" Again: nothing. The logo looks like it was written by a toddler. Nothing about the graphic design for Firebreak says "Co-op game in the Control Universe." It looks closer to a Fortnite game than a Control game in the font stylizing, and the outfits the characters wear.

Okay, Gameplay stuff....

1) Clearly balanced for three players.
God forbid you want to play with one other friend. No bots to help you if you want to play with one friend or no friends.

2) Frustrating mechanics.
Let's not explain how to swap kits, or why you may want to. Let's just recommend you jump straight into a mission.

3) Bad tutorial.
Cute tutorial, but bad. One of the first playable missions introduces the different objects that float around and make your life hell. You are told on the left hand side of the screen that you need to find a thing to disable or contain these objects. Turns out it's a gun you can find in the shelter. You only know this if you are following the prompting. You also tend to get attacked by opening shelters, so good luck noticing the prompting on the left hand side change. Oh, also -- you can't drop the gun. There is no clear indication on how to drop the gun. Good luck if you want to swap back to your melee wrench to fix something that your teammate isn't.

4) Bullet Sponge Time!
Hope you love bullet sponge bosses with mechanics that can one shot. I sure don't! Pick either bullet sponge final bosses or mechanics. Mechanics should make bosses significantly easier, instead of "I still need to do the same thing eight times to beat the boss... on normal difficulty."

5) Frustrating controls.
Hope you don't like clearly explained controls, because you'll find few in this game, which is set in the Control universe.

6) Poorly Explained Mechanics
Did you know that the shower can... I don't know, run out of soap and stop healing you? Is that a bug? Who knows. The shower animations still play, you can still charge it, and it'll still tell you to the hop in the shower. Is it supposed to work? Is it a mystery? Who fucking knows, because this game doesn't tell you.

----

CONCLUSION: I thought this game failed due to branding issues and not really labeling itself well and having confusing graphic design. No -- it's just a foray into GaaS by a company that is known for polished and intricate single player story based experiences, but is unknown for multiplayer experiences. This was honestly a fun concept with some cool ideas. I love the idea of people fighting dimensional beings that manifest as trite shit like Sticky Note Golems. But the execution is lacking, and instead of trying to go back and fix the issues that they could -- by adding bots, by changing mechanics so they last longer and have some damage in them themselves -- they have given players the ability to have their friends play  a frustrating, questionably designed game with them, and run away from fixing any of the issues the game has. A lot of multiplayer games have done incredibly well with overhauls to address gameplay issues. While they can't go back in time and call this game "Federal Bureau of Control: Firebreak" or "Bureau of Control: Firebreak" which would fix a lot of their sales and brand problems, they could have gone back and made some things better for the players they currently have.

As it stands -- and since the game is on life support, so this likely won't change -- I cannot recommend this game. Will I play it with friends? Probably; I spent money on it. But I would not recommend that you, dear reader, buy this game for the $20 discounted price of admission. I'm not sure I would recommend you buy it on sale for $10, unfortunately; there's better experiences to be had out there with friends for your money.

I figured I would try this game out after the last big update, and unfortunately I can't really recommend it. The action isn't as exciting or intense as you'd want from a horde shooter, the gunplay isn't as fun or satisfying as you'd want from an FPS, and the gameplay isn't as inventive and fluid as you'd want from a Control game. I can't even say I'd recommend this for someone who likes Control, since other than it reusing the setting (and assets) from Control, there's not really much here to chew on.

review:
As much as I enjoy this game and have had genuine fun with it. I cannot rightly recommend it unless either you're a big fan of Control or are REALLY into COOP horde shooters. Even then it's a hard recommend due to Remedy's latest update on the game as of the time of writing this review, they are ceasing major content updates for a already relatively content lacking game. 

This is likely due to the poor player counts within the past year the game has suffered due to it's poor launch.

While they lowered the game price and introduced a "Friend Pass" system to allow anyone who owns it to invite up to 2 friends to play is nice, it doesn't excuse the abandonment of the game and the fact anyone who originally purchased the game for full price (especially those poor Deluxe owners) are getting nothing for their early support which is a shame.

Again, while I do like the game, I cannot truly recommend anyone to purchase it due to it being abandoned, which is very frustrating as there was great promise for this game's future that was unfortunately squandered due to mismanagement of player expectations and trying to attempt a "live service" style format without a real concrete plan. Somewhat similar to what occurred with Halo Infinite. Though sadly Remedy isn't a studio who has a megacorp backing them such as Microsoft to continue efforts.

LOOKING FORWARD TO CONTROL RESONANT THOUGH!

Eh. Kinda just ran out of steam for me.

Sure, the concept is good, and the universe is interesting, but... The game's just lacking.
Like the individual parts of this are just done better (or at least are more fun) in other games.

And I just found the combat tedious in the long run. The frequent spawning hordes, forcing you to either drop what you're doing to deal with them, or just try to run past them. I didn't feel like the weapons did enough damage for most of the time, so running away for as long as your stamina-bar allowed always seemed the better option... When the latter [b]is[/b] an option, and you're not stuck in a strange siege-situation in one of the respawn-rooms, cause the enemies have become a relentless barrage, so you have to shoot your way out. I suspect that there's a meta when it comes to which perks, weapons, mods, and grenades you should use, but I couldn't be bothered to unlock it all. I don't think I should have to, in order to have fun.

review:
I really really really want to like this game, but I just can't. It looks incredible, and the new horde mode should be fun, but it just doesn't work, the bones are too messy at the very base of the game. Moving is omega slow and stunted, you really feel like a regular guy lugging around way too much crap. Shooting sounds great and is sometimes pretty good, but in general can feel very laggy or unresponsive and generally weak. The objectives are cool on paper but the implementation is really rough, which is why the horde mode works, you just shoot Hiss.

There is nothing in this game you can't find done better elsewhere, and it's a real shame too because of how great Remedy's games can be. Without an even more serious overhaul to how the game feels to move, shoot, and complete objectives, the good will never outweigh the bad, and there's no point in trying the unique roles or elemental combos.

Even though I played this during a free weekend, I was still sitting in matchmaking queue for a pretty long time and never got a full crew for a mission.
