review: As much as I love Alan Wake and Control, those universes are far better suited to slower, more introspective experiences. FBC Firebreak takes that setting and pushes it in a direction that just didn’t work for me. On paper it sounds fine, but in practice I couldn’t get invested. The gameplay loop feels repetitive very quickly, with missions and objectives blending together instead of building tension or atmosphere. Progression is slow and grind heavy, and without a strong narrative hook or memorable moments, it never really feels like it earns the Remedy name. I kept waiting for that sense of mystery or escalation, but it never arrived. It could have worked with more variety, stronger pacing, or a deeper focus on mood and storytelling, but as it is, it felt shallow compared to what these worlds usually offer. Maybe I’ll come back to it down the line, but at this moment I didn’t enjoy my time with this game.

review:
[h2] 4.0/10 [/h2]

Pros:
+ Interesting world setting: Returning to the Control universe gives the game a unique and intriguing vibe. Some areas look stylish, mysterious, and visually appealing.

+ (Some) creative enemy designs: Enemies like office workers floating on chairs or monsters made from yellow sticky notes are genuinely original. These designs are refreshing and exciting when you first encounter them.

Cons:
--- Poor gunplay: Shooting feels dull and unsatisfying. The sound effects lack impact, and enemies barely react when hit, making combat feel weightless. Player interactions—such as setting up tools or switching weapon modes—are slow and clunky, which drags down the pace of combat. And who thought it was a good idea to use a sequence input just to reload ammo?

-- Boring and repetitive progression: The gameplay loop is extremely repetitive: go to Zone A, defend waves, complete objectives, unlock Zone B, and repeat. Objectives are often uninteresting and sometimes awkwardly designed. For example, having to physically push a shuttle from behind during a chaotic firefight is more annoying than fun. The map layout is mostly linear with almost nothing to explore. Even the main boss fights are generic and fail to create any excitement during or after the battle.

- Lack of enemy variety: There are only about 6–7 enemy types. Aside from a few creative designs mentioned earlier, most enemies are bland and forgettable.

review:
Short version :

Dead game with no players even during free weekends, unoptimized ugly mess, generic randomly generated rooms and corridors sprinkled with waves of useless, suicidal and same-y enemies spawning out of thin air. One of the most bland, boring, confusing and mind numbing games I think I've ever played, which is a shame considering the source material and how easy it is to craft a fun co-op shooter experience.



Long version :

Now, let me tell you how my experience with the game went. If anyone at Remedy reads this, take notes.

When I launched FBC Firebreak for the first time, it asked me to configure the subtitles, then proceeded to show me an introductive puppet video WITHOUT subtitles, then made me sit for at least a full minute in front of a loading screen showing pages of text about a briefing and info in English ONLY with again no subtitles or translation. Every loading screen in the game is like that by the way, with full size pages of info dumps and exposition.

After that I was forced into a tutorial without going through a menu first, and of course since this is a modern game, it has to look at least twice as bad as most games from 2014 while running five times worse. My fps initially tanked to 15, so I set the graphics to the lowest preset, enabled FSR Performance, and got between 45 and 65 fps. It wasn't pretty, but surprisingly enough, not much worse than max graphics, which is a testament to how bad the game looks overall. 

I was still sitting in the elevator where I spawned while tweaking the settings, when for some reason, everything on my computer froze except for the game (I won't throw any accusations but my thoughts immediately went there), so I rebooted it and relaunched Firebreak. It put me in the main menu this time, but now the tutorial was nowhere to be found. The game then asked me to start a session, which I did, and waited around 20 mins or so for other players to join, but no one came. I reluctantly started the game anyway, hoping that there would be bots fighting by my side like in every good co-op shooter with some self respect, but I was alone. 

I spawned in an elevator once again, and not knowing what to do because I couldn't play the tutorial, I stepped into the corridor, only for 10 humanoid enemies with guns and melee weapons, all sharing the exact same appaerance, to spawn out of nowhere right in front of me and jump me. I killed them all in less than 10 seconds with my melee weapon (the animation freezes when you hit something, very unpleasant), completely unharmed, wondering if they were really that weak and dumb, or if I was truly the next best gamer of all time. 

Still not knowing what to do, I went a bit further, only to be harassed by the piles and piles of sticky notes lying around everywhere on the floor and walls, as they started to cover all of my screen while a voice told me to use water against them, without telling me how. I noticed the "sticky notes meter" on the top left of the screen and understood that I was there to fight those paper pests. So I started hitting and shooting them, but even if they were actually disappearing and a hitmarker was there to indicate that I was doing some sort of damage, the "sticky notes meter" wouldn't budge. 

After some time, a new wave of the exact same humanoid enemies as before spawned out of nowhere again and I took care of them even more easily, confirming that they can't aim and do almost no damage, triggering the question: what are they even here for ? After some light exploration (light because the area I was in was pretty small, just a hall with a bunch of small rooms and corridors on the sides) and some random button pressing on my keyboard to see what the keys would do, my character started attaching a litteral piggy bank on my melee weapon. Assuming that any modification to a player's weapon in a video game is probably a bonus (my years of experience as a gamer are really showing), I started hitting more sticky notes, but I was quickly interrupted by new visual and sound effects that looked like more enemies were spawning, or like I was targeted with some magic spell or something. Two seconds later, enemies were spawning next to me and I again killed them with my gun with absolutely no effort. This is when I noticed that the "sticky notes meter" had filled a little bit. But how ? What did I do, or what happened ? It turns out that the weird new visual and sound effects from earlier that looked like I was being attacked were actually the result of me hitting sticky notes with the piggy bank from my melee weapon, and only by doing that was I able to fill the meter. All of this makes total sense. 

Now understanding that the game would entirely revolve around hitting the floor and walls for 15 seconds every minute or so (because the piggy bank is on a cooldown) while being interrupted here and there by the video game equivalent of waves of mosquitos with water guns, I laughed, I cried, then left my pc as is to get something to eat (without pausing the game, not that it's possible anyways, because modern games have to be online only, even when you play solo). I came back 20 minutes later, and I kid you not, the enemies that spawned while I was AFK were still trying to kill me with absolutely no success. 

This is at this point that a random player joined me, so we pushed together through the molasses of this game and found a boss at some point. I slipped and fell into a pit and died, only to respawn not near my partner or near the boss at the end of the level, but in the elevator where I spawned when the game started. I laughed and cried some more, backtracked to the boss and killed it with no more effort than regular enemies even if it took more time (you have to make it weaker by hitting pipes with your melee weapon smh), then had to run back to the elevator AGAIN to escape the level and finally end this miserable experience.

All of this happened while I was playing during a free weekend (I didn't buy the game), on Normal difficulty, in French language, with a GTX 1080 + i7 8700k + 16G DDR4.
I also tested other game modes on the Hard difficulty where there are a few more enemies that can mass spawn in the air right in front of you and kill you in seconds, but don't worry you're invicible as long as you stand in the shower. It makes perfect sense.

review:
People need to ask less "Why did Remedy make a live service shooter?" because that has already been answered. 505 Games forced them to start a live service project in 2021 when they owned the Control IP, and after Remedy bought it, cost sunk fallacy likely kicked in and figured they may as well release something before Control: Resonant in 2026. The far more important question to ask is: Why did Remedy make this a horde shooter when it doesn't play to any of that sub-genre's strengths?

Talking about surface level stuff first, the base shooting and some of the elemental status effects going on are what I'd describe as "okay", but falters behind the competition (including Remedy's own games). Visually, the game looks decent (it's 99% reused Control 1 environments, and that game still holds up) but they completely cut the environmental destruction, so everything is more static than Static Shock. No longer can you have the joy and whimsy of blowing up toilets and bathroom stalls. 

The game has a total of six missions (about the length of 20-30 minutes tops) and you will burn through them quickly. Despite taking place in the Oldest House (an ever-shifting labyrinth), the level layouts and objective locations are identical every time you play them. Also for whatever reason, they ripped off Darktide's mission board system post-launch, so now you aren't allowed to manually select missions to play (if people not connecting to games was an issue, a quickmatch system would've gotten the job done, which they also implemented). The only other piece of content is a boring survival wave mode they're calling a "roguelike" which is a stretch to say the least (Vermintide 2: Chaos Wastes this is not).

To start focusing on the horde shooter elements, let's begin with the enemy roster. They're all recycled directly from Control 1, but enemy behavior and attacks are cut down to bare essentials. There's either Hiss with gun or Hiss crackhead who runs at you with melee weapon. The "boss fights" are bullet sponge versions of the regular enemies and just like those enemies, can be stun locked by shooting them so they're basically a non-threat. No disabler enemies, projectile focused enemies, or enemies that take advantage of the elemental system either. It is embarrassing that the deadliest enemy in a paranormal/SCP themed shooter is not anything that would fit the theme of that, but just a generic floating enemy with a gun because they're weirdly spongey + can more or less avoid almost all status effect damage with floating.

Speaking of enemies, the audio design is absolutely atrocious. Audio cues for them are non-existent other than an easy to miss one for when enemies are about to spawn. After that, it's all visual. You can have fifty or so Hiss running up behind you and you wouldn't know any better until they're piled on top of you. For that matter, music does not sound audible unless the escape mission kicks in, meaning that most of the game is hearing dead air.

The loadout system is not in a great place, in particular, the weapon roster is a mess balancing wise. Once you play above Normal, anything that isn't the semi-auto rifle feels like playing the game with a self-imposed challenge. It has good range, great damage, good RoF for a single shot, a scope, and a reload time comparable to every other gun. Nothing else can even touch it. What doesn't help this is that each weapon type have special "mods" that can be equipped and unlocked that sound unique and at the very least, could make them more interesting to use. I wouldn't know, even with the ongoing double XP weekend, it feels like it takes forever to actually unlock them.

I think the most damning thing relative to this being a horde shooter AND from Remedy, is how little character the game has. Horde shooters are incredibly well known for having memorable casts of playable characters (L4D1/2's cast, the Ubersreik Five from Vermintide, og Payday gang, the selectable personalities in Darktide, etc.) or quotes so memorable that they're endlessly spammed (ROCK AND STONE, SAY HELLO TO DEMOCRACY, etc). 

Similarly, Remedy's game stories live or die on how compelling the characters are (I couldn't care less about the interconnected "Remedyverse" stuff their fans keep pushing harder than Remedy themselves). Max Payne 1 is an incredibly straight forward revenge story, but made interesting by Max's cynical perception of the world and by the end of the game, has players rooting for him to murder a big pharmaceutical CEO. Alan Wake is a story about a guy trying to find his wife made interesting because it's fun to argue how much of a potential hack he is and how it reflects on Alan that the story being played out is something he unconsciously wrote. Jesse Faden in Control 1 is a woman who wants to save her brother made interesting by being unwillingly thrust into a position of great responsibility and having to frequently deal with a crumbling foundation.

For playable characters, they went with a voice pre-set a-la Darktide and Helldivers 2 which is fine on its own. The problem is, there's only a total of five (one of them locked to DLC) and all of them lack a really defining personality. Even if they did, characters never speak to one another, so whatever potential chemistry that could've been developed between the voices is non-existent. The only real characters of the game are Hank and Jerry. They're serviceable stereotypes, but you can only hear conversation between them IN THE MENU. Jerry is never heard in the actual missions. Hank is exclusively your voice com character in-mission and all he does is bark at the player every two minutes to do an objective you were probably already in the middle of doing.

Even if you are a "lore head" or whatever, this game will do nothing for you either. Environmental storytelling in the levels are non-existent and the only post Control 1 stuff you have are a grand total of maybe five readable documents in loading screens that you will never be able to properly read because matches load in about 10 seconds unless you take a screenshot and read it OUTSIDE of the game. Even then, I'm 100% certain this is all stuff that will be explained within Control Resonant by hour one of the game. It's as non-essential as you can get.

The worst part of all of this is that the game is barren playerbase wise. This is doubly bad because the game requires a 24/7 online only connection. This is most likely to facilitate crossplay which probably worked great to fool the shareholders within the first month of the game that people were playing it (1 million players on Gamepass who didn't stick around). Even with ongoing "free weekend" experience, my experience with FBC has been near exclusively SOLO. I did not see another player join my game sessions other than the very first mission I played on Normal. Added with the fact Remedy barely marketed the recent update, it feels like counting down to this game's inevitable shut down. No wonder people don't want to bother playing it even when it's temporarily free. Why bother getting invested in something that might not even be playable in the near future? They have not said a thing about an "End of Life" plan, so I'm not holding my breath for them to actually let it be played offline or with client specific P2P.

review:
Played during the free weekend, and 6 hours might not be enough to paint a full review, but I've done enough to conclude Firebreak flat out isn't fun to play. I love Remedy's other works, but this ain't it.
Everything feels so slow to interact, respond, and react to. From shooting to melee, using your tools, the QTEs, to even just player movement, nothing in the game responds to your actions in a timeframe that feels good or flows well for the genre it's in.
I mostly played jump kit, and there's no way to indicate how far your shock goes, or what charging it with the knockback does better. When it does connect, there's some innate delay before enemies will respond to your action (shooting has similar problems).
I don't have friends, so I was forced to solo until rank 4 when the game unlocks quickplay, and even then I'm only ever matched with 1 other player. Most the game's missions aren't tailored to solo, and those I can adjust to still request one kit over the others (paper chase and hot fix without splash kit is an awful experience).

Another problem is game and online stability. Games will always have crashes, but if you're in a genre like this you have to have some kind of host migration, or material compensation when you or another squad member crashes to desktop or loses connection, making that 20+ minute mission with a handful of materials you just played vanish from existence. "Ehh it's not that long, you can get that back in one more run", you may say, and while factually correct, having any amount of time blanked from your day like it never happened is disheartening, mentally draining, and is enough for people to drop the game until a solution is provided.

So I'm going into this game one last time, player base is dead and we're at a 60% discount and free weekend. This has not affected the game's player base at all, and above all, the game is still not fun.

I've never played a game in my life that feels like a chore. There's just a lot of busy work with uninspired levels, playing co-op where there are no one to join your squad. And guess what? If nobody joins and you start anyway there are no bots to help like in L4D2 from 17 years ago - a much better game.

Every "mission" that you do feels uninspired, like a brainstorming session from some indy high school project, or "hackaton" or similar. It doesn't feel like a Remedy product at all, but more like a way for some business major to make a quick buck using ChatGPT to design a game.

FBC Firebreak is just a horde shooter where you hold in tiny sections against the "hiss" from Control completing various chores by hitting the E and Q button. This is where the game really falters, the level design and gameplay is so terribly bad and small that it feels like a demo or an Alpha build. Everybody playing this game asks themselves the same question "where the hell is the rest of the game?"

The weapons feel very underpowered and weak, like shooting peas at the enemies. You don't feel that "meaty" feeling of mowing down enemies like in L4D2, here we just run around and fart at the enemies. It just isn't fun. I can't stress this enough, this is a game devoid of all sense of fun, it is just plane boring, and I get flashbacks to doing menial service jobs in my early 20's.

If you go into this with an unlimited weekend of time you'll have 100% this game on the first day. This game instantly died on release, and various game mods draws a fraction of loyal players back into the game - or just the curious wondering "is it good yet?".

No, no it isn't and it never will be.

review:
[h1]It pains me to say it…. This game just sucks.[/h1]
Man, talk about disappointment. In theory, I should love this game. A 1-3 person co-op shooter in the Control universe made by Remedy themselves without any of the money grubbing FOMO bullshit of other live service games? Sounds great! But damn, even when I tried my hardest to like it, I really just can’t. Even after waiting around 8 months for updates to fix things, I still find myself struggling to continue playing due to problems baked in from the start.

Let's get the biggest issue clear first: [b]the gunplay is downright atrocious.[/b] I’ve played nearly a dozen co-op shooters that have all come out in the last decade or two, and almost all of them to my memory have felt better to shoot than this one. From terrible gun audio to nonexistent feedback enemies give from your bullets outside the most trivial healthbars (which make visibility terrible), it just feels like I’m shooting airsoft guns or plastic replicas of what a firearm should be. It’s one of those nagging pillars of the gameplay loop that as much time as I tried to give it, I never got over it. It’s truly bad, and unless it’s entirely overhauled, no amount of new content is going to change my opinion sadly.

Worse however was gameplay pacing. I’m convinced that from playing this game solo, nobody who worked on this has played a co-op shooter, or has played them in enough detail to understand how they work. These games have ebb and flow from combat, to exploration/traversal, to objectives, and back again. No one segment of that flow should feel like a slog to get through, nor so short you’re repeating other parts of the cycle too often. Even then, these games understand that pacing for group and solo play is different, and accommodate enemy spawns, AI aggression, and objectives to scale accordingly. [b]NONE, I repeat, NONE of those things are present here.[/b]
 
Enemies will spawn in hordes consecutively, seconds from the last one, not even giving the time for you to find ammo. Objectives require traversal across medium to large spaces (not to mention you’re not the fastest), so you’ll often be swarmed again before you even reach the next objective. There are no mechanics to shove hordes away, even to get some breathing room to reposition, and as stated before, seemingly no scaling for player count. When you’re suffocating with endless enemies & mediocre gunplay, with very little variation to possibly make it worthwhile, it all just ends up bringing the whole experience down in the player’s mind. Mid goes from boring to unbearable.

The “crisis kit” classes seem interesting on a surface level. As an FBC grunt, you don’t have Jesse’s psychic powers to handle the Hiss, so these encumbering backpacks of junk are your only option, within the rules of the Oldest House for the guns you wield alongside. They seem sufficient, with each filling a niche in the co-op lineup that make sense: the turret engineer, the spray medic, the mobile stunner. These lead the classes to feel complimentary to each other’s playstyles, right? Sure, but it also leads to none of them feeling capable of much on their own, which drags down solo play immensely. Each kit can handle a certain objective task well, but the other ones have you repeating the same button-tapping minigame to complete any other. When your playerbase is small, and solo lobbies are likely the only way people will be playing at some point, this will only give a sub-par experience.

The status affect system also ropes into this: there are plenty of status affects that affect you and enemies in complimentary ways akin to immersive sims. Wet enemies are vulnerable to electric shocks, fire damages over time but increases enemy speed, cold will slow hordes down, etc. However, these systems can feel cumbersome to navigate when compounded with the other problems I’ve already spoken of. Not every status is made clear to the player quickly other than wash it off, and often, these effects don’t make the pacing or balancing any more bearable, just more tedium to get through.

The game’s levels are jobsites that while their layouts don’t change, some of the assets in them do. Health and ammo stations are arranged randomly, various currency collectibles are spread around, and even the objectives themselves can vary a bit from room to room. It does make me wonder if a warping Oldest House with RNG-made levels could have been that spark to make things more interesting to replay. Personally however, I think this level of variation is serviceable, but again, when compounded with the other issues, it just makes replays even more of a chore, especially when grinding materials for perks & upgrades. I won’t even speak on those mechanics, as I don’t think they change anything significant enough, early enough, to dissuade player concerns, even after being wholly reworked twice since launch. 

Finally, I don’t think this game embellishes Remedy’s core strengths: narrative and worldbuilding. There’s none of that here, even when trying to utilize the Control universe’s aesthetic fairly well. The Hiss are just there, no mention of Jesse Faden or any characters from Control, no cool FMV sequence of a new paranormal entity you have to deal with: you’re a schmuck just doing work to no end. I almost think making it a third person shooter, just so we can at least see our Firebreaker could have given it some personality (maybe even have them emote?), but it’s really just as mundane as a 9-5 job, all irony or humor ripped straight out, where you clock in, clock out, repeat for an upgrade or two or change of clothing. Not saying they had to make something so addictive you’d want to play for hours on end, but when it feels like a chore or bore to even get through 1 job, I don’t think that's successful design.

[i]I REALLY tried to give this game a fair chance, against the naysayers at launch who called it a failure. It had so much potential, for a universe I desperately loved to see again, and felt less cynically made than a lot of multiplayer spin-offs I’ve seen die in much quicker time. But, it reminded me incessantly that Remedy REALLY hasn’t made this kind of game before and would need at least another year to get this into shape, especially as a full priced $40 release. But by now, a lot of people have already dropped it  (even Remedy themselves) for better options. If the idea seems promising and you’re somewhat patient, it could be an interesting experiment to try. [b]But anyone expecting a polished co-op experience, this is NOT that. [/b][/i]

review:
The concept of the game as a whole was very appealing to me. I am very interested in co-op objective based shooters, and seeing one set in the control universe was especially exciting. Unfortunately the game falls short of the concept. For me the gunplay is the best part of the game. The environments look amazing, but I can see repeated assets from 'Control'. No issue normally, but it seems like all environments are like that. Balancing was my biggest concern, the game seemed incredibly inconsistent in enemy spawns, and health. In my first 2 hours of gameplay enemies would spawn in  set times after completing objectives and would be a variation of a few enemies. In my last few hours enemies would spawn so frequently it was hard to even do the objectives, along with far more variation of enemies that had far more max health and armor. Both of these experiences were on the same 'Normal' difficulty. The only way I could think of the crazy difficulty spike is either due to my player level (which doesn't introduce major upgrades to warrant the increase in difficulty), or s silent balancing patch. Although in game enemy encounters are incredibly inconsistent, out of game progression is also lack luster. The major way of progressing your character is to level up, thats it. you can buy perks from resources found in match, but the most they do is stat changes in game. The overall gameplay remains the same without much variety. This along with static maps, and objectives that change every now and then can get very stale, very fast. 

Overall: Ignoring the rant, I had high hopes that in the end were brought down by the (in my opinion) bad balancing of enemies, and lack luster upgrades out of match. Leading to a inconsistent and boring gameplay loop. I'm glad I got to try the game for myself, but I would not recommend this game to anyone in good consience.

Any permutations are due to difficulty, random spawns of objectives, or complicating factors. There's no alternate routes, and the boss events were somewhat janky. This is the main issue in my eyes, if every mission can be played through in 15-20 minutes apiece, there's only so much potential for entertainment, even in a co-op game. The content is there, but there's not a ton of it, so on the plus side this title won't ask a ton of your time. That's not a bad thing, quite the opposite, I wish more games would be like this as mid-budget titles. I wasn't expecting the moon here, but I don't know, it just doesn't speak to me like it does to many others I guess. Maybe I just wanted to see more of the CONTROL setting. Worth giving a go though.

MOGS RECOMMENDATION: Kinda? It's Janky tl;dr but can be fun

A lot of the negative reviews here talk about multiplayer, but let me give you a single player stance.
Darts is broken. It just physically doesn't work. Blackjack odds are completely FUBAR'd. As an actual professional blackjack player, there is zero way the dealer is hitting 21s as often as it does.

The tutorial is a straight up PITA. Going through it I was confused on quite a few areas, and as a legally blind gamer, not having proper directions or visual cues isn't a good look for accessibility. I was lost for a solid few minutes when it said "pin the recipe," like where the hell is the pin button? It doesn't tell you it's G, nothing blinks or glows, I didn't even notice the G prompt in the bottom left for a few minutes.

The cooking experience itself is actually fine, though I've had a few foods bug out even though I know for a fact I cooked them perfectly and they still score less than 90%. Food also seems to bug out and show incorrect cooking status. It'll clearly say it's done, but it's actually still 1% raw, and you get docked for it.

It isn't a bad game by any means, but this is full release? Interesting.

And speaking of full release issues, please note my listed specs. I'm getting stutters, freezing, and fps drops, which shouldn't be happening in this type of game. Please advise.
Do I recommend it? Kinda. With all the reviews about the multiplayer being super bad or flat out impossible, I'd say maybe try it. I'll keep playing because I'm easily entertained, but some others might not be as tolerant of this stuff.

review:
I've spent over one hundred hours in this game because it scratched an itch few cooking simulator games could: it was fun making the food, had ways to make things more or less challenging if needed, and best of all, the dev team was frequently putting out updates and bug fixes. However, the update in August introduced some extremely game-breaking bugs. These include:

[*]Game crashing frequently even in single player
[*]Massive desync in multiplayer
[*]Completely broken mechanics that render gameplay impossible on one of the two "maps" and difficult on the other
[*]Bugs that result in permanent incorrect fixtures that never leave your save
[*]Incorrect recipes that don't match up with their instructions, or that don't recognize the ingredients you put in, so you can never actually create them, etc.

This is in addition to other bugs that existed before the update, such as the other game modes (the cooking competition in particular) not working.

I was in the Discord server for this game, along with a lot of other players really excited about it. The Bug Report thread got bigger and bigger, with dev responses becoming increasingly rare. There are no longer any updates, or bug fixes, or developer responses. It's clear the devs have abandoned this game, and worse, they abandoned it in a state that you can't even play the original (mostly working) version of it. Instead, you're stuck with a buggy mess that will only waste your time and frustrate you.

I know I'm not the only person who understands that bugs happen, that real life happens, that slow development doesn't mean there is no development, and so on. The community really liked and supported this game and its developers. But the lack of response, while still selling this game at a whopping $18, is inconsiderate of its current and new player base.

In short: don't buy this game. It's not worth $18. It isn't even worth $5. Sucks to say that, because I was genuinely a fan and wanted to support the project.

review:
So first: the idea is great - not just a motel simulator, but also a shop/gasstation and some little sidejobs- great!
The idea with getting money through ads - super! The Phonebooths - super!

But this is it so far. I am not new to Simulators. But this here has the worst warehousemanagemantsystem and KI restockers I have ever had the pleasure working with. And I am not talking about the stuck cars - thanks for the emergency button!

If I want to restock would it be asked to much to see on ONE page - what is in the warehouse and what is in the shop? I am not even asking for a scanner to reorder in the warehouse or shop themselves.
Could it not have been possible to assign the employees by just talking to them or let them have fallback options? 
How should I keep 20 rooms clean, thre possible lanes in the gasstation, more than 1 checkouts in the shop, restockers from the Deliveryvans and into the shopshelves with just 6 extra persons? Have you ever done the maths for that? No mather how many washers / dryers I have.

Shelving system: 20% ok. tiles and paint go into them by their catogory, pillows, lamps etc by their other category. Fine so far. I can live with that.

But products in the warehouse. What a mess. You can assign certain shelfs to one specific product. NOT THE CATEGORY. So you have p.e. 20 differents styles of sunglasses you need 20 shelves for them. You cannot just throw all sunglasses into one shelf. You must have one row per shelf per style. Tiny boxes. Take ages to unload. Same with hats. Per sytle - one row in a shelf. Carsupplies - guess what. Travel supplies - guess what. Gifts - guess what. And we are talking on average 15 different styles / category. 
But we are not done. There is bakery. Then Snacks / Chips. Then baverages (soft drinks) and alcohol. Same - one row in a shelf per one kind of item.

Why even bother assignig the rows to certain productd? I can tell you: max 3 employees in the warehouse. No chance of restocking and loading from the trucks. BUT if I put 3 of my 6 employees in the warehouse, I am short with housekeeping, cleaning, shop checkouts and gasstation. 

And guess what: it is calles MOTEL SIMULATOR. That means check in and check outs. Sure. That is waht I have to do because I cannot assign this to any of my employees. And let us be fair. This is why we are actually here for. 

But with all my helping in the warehouse, there is nooooo time to design rooms. I sometimes need 6 days just to get one room ready. If you want to put more than the bare minimum in them.

And my warehouse is organized just fine. But the KIs just swag a little in front of a shelf, get the box, run to the store, restock / refill, swag a little, run back to the warehouse, swag a little, put the box back on the shelf, swag a little, go to the next shelf, swag a little, get this box out of the shelf - off to the shop AND REPEAT. 

I know that there are no updates comming and I would REALLLY love to keep playing, but I am capped by the reordermanagement, the KI restockers and the limited amount of employees to hire. There is NOOOOO WAY to run all rooms with maxed out gasstation and shop PLUS getting the busstop for more customers. Check-in and Check-Out. 

And don´t even get me started on police and robberies. Also time consuming. But this you can at least turn off. 

Sorry, I have nothing better to say. If you are happy with around 10 rooms and a few shelves in the shop, this game is for you. If you want to go all in, there is not a single chance of having full shelves in teh waehouse and the shop, clean rooms, shop and office, done housekeeping,  check-ins and chekouts, doing new rooms.

AND: You cannot play both settings at once. It is either or. 

Just taking away the employees cap would have done it. I am on day 90 with 77k and no way to spend it, because unloading orders takes longer than my money to increase and to spend opn anything like new room-furniture. 

A perfect example how a good idea gets limited by its own programming.

review:
I'd like to be able to recommend this game, but it's plainly unfinished and suffers from a wide variety of bugs, a lack of endgame content, and a profound lack of QOL features.

Here are some examples:

- Employees frequently idle for extended periods for no obvious reasons.
- Traffic AI is bad enough to cause reliable jams that you are then obliged to fix yourself.
- God help you if you order a bunch of books at once. None of them come boxed up, they can't be boxed, you can't upgrade your ability to manually hold objects, and consequently this is immensely tedious.
- Advertisement is unclear with regard to when your payouts arrive and can be collected, and this also applies to automatically paying employees.
- Price Setting is barely required or worth doing. It is barely affected by your rising rating, and while it does work as intended as far as customer failure-chance, there's absolutely no reason to ever use less than 100% chance, since you can dismiss extra customers for free, juggle them by asking them to wait, or simply accept the popularity cost, since it has no real benefit.
- Cars don't appear to function or have any purpose. I bought all three, have no idea where they went or what they're for, and attempting to leave the motel by the road causes the game to teleport me back to the play area. No idea what the cars are for, or do.
- Warehouse Shelves can be set to specific products, but there's no ability to set warehouse shelves to things like blankets, sheets, or towels. This means that your warehouse will, always and inevitably, become a cluttered nightmare mess of random boxes everywhere, and this is even more true if you have any employees working in the warehouse.
- The Store gameplay is very basic. I don't necessarily have a huge problem with this in isolation, but in the context of the game, it just becomes very clear that this is intended to be executed via employees, the same way as the Gas Station
- Employees do work as intended with regard to the Patience Timers, but what I find really strange is that they have very specific locations where they idle, and do not communicate well as far as tasks or inventory go. I can watch my housekeepers sprint back and forth from the warehouse to the various motel rooms, carrying single objects, and wonder whether they are worth the paychecks at all. Additionally, Employees stop working if their paycheck exceeds $300. This wouldn't be a catastrophic deal, except that the auto-pay system works daily, and occasionally, will not pay employee wages in time to prevent them from going to rest. Once this happens, their assignment clears, and you have to manually reset their entire behavior from your PC. This is inconvenient, annoying, and honestly just adds bloat to an otherwise remarkable framework.
- Finally, decorating is a chore. Most of the decorating in this game is broken up by extremely tedious systems that you need to interact with to accomplish any kind of decoration. As previously mentioned, you have a very limited carrying capacity, and the carts are a chore to use except for items you need to deploy in bulk, like paints, floors, and ceilings. Many items which can become a box within the warehouse,  expand to full size on a cart, resulting in an impossible task of loading too many refridgerators onto a cart that is too small for them, but simultaneously allowing you to carry five of them in your hands. These systems make the highlight of the endgame feel tedious and inconvenient, and not worth participating in, which is a shame, because the mechanics surrounding decorating the rooms (as far as they relate to customer pleasure) is actually kinda cool and interesting. For me, this is the critical failure of Motel Manager Simulator.

Conclusion: This game showed promise, but instead of being a labor of love, it was clearly abandoned a year ago, and has received no attention despite a plethora of bugs, some serious QOL issues, and some balancing problems. I can't recommend it in good conscience unless the developer shows some initiative in getting the game to a more playable state.

With that said, I am still a sucker for games like this, and it'll probably take me some time to fully disentangle myself from this disappointment.

Also you can't customize the stairs or the buildings' roofs. Tragic.

review:
[h1]Sengoku Dynasty — Great Potential, but Still Feels Like a Beta[/h1]

[h2]DISCLAIMER[/h2]

I love this game, its setting, and its style, but I can't recommend it in its current state.

I'm the kind of player who checks every corner, looks closely at every detail, and tends to be a perfectionist. So you'll find issues here that you might not have noticed yourself or simply wouldn't care about.

I came back to the game after some time away, and I couldn't help but notice how many things still need attention.

🎨[h2]VISUALS & GRAPHICS[/h2]

• [b]Textures:[/b] Even with graphics settings maxed out, some textures look like they're straight out of the PS1 era.

• [b]Water:[/b] This is probably the worst offender. You can walk through water as if it were solid ground. There's no swimming, and the water doesn't react to your character at all. The visual effect is noticeable in shallow water and sometimes even on the beach itself.

• [b]Map:[/b] The map could use a higher resolution. I don't think replacing a static image with a better-quality one would have a significant impact on performance.

• [b]Lighting:[/b] Lighting is inconsistent. Some caves are so bright they feel like open spaces, while others are properly dark.

• [b]Building details:[/b] I like the building customization system and the ability to change materials. However, building prefabs often feel too empty and could use more detail. I understand that some of this might be intentional to give us more freedom when customizing our buildings.

🌿[h2]WORLD & IMMERSION[/h2]

• [b]The world feels dead:[/b] There are animals, a few random camps or tents with recruitable villagers or bandits, but no travelers or ambient events to make the world feel alive.

• [b]Cities and NPCs:[/b] Cities look plastic, and NPCs mostly walk around without doing much else. They feel shallow, often look alike, and have very little personality. The same problem applies to villagers.

• [b]Dialogue:[/b] NPCs have only basic dialogue lines. They don't reference the conversations you have with them, and they lack facial expressions.

• [b]Idle animations:[/b] There seems to be very little variety in idle poses, if any at all.

• [b]Points of interest:[/b] They often feel repetitive. Most seem to be variations of camps, tents, altars or cities that look as if they were built by players.

• [b]World interaction:[/b] The environment feels static. Plants don't bend when you walk through them, there are no footprints, and footsteps sound basic rather than crisp and satisfying. During rain, almost every surface sounds the same, even indoors. There are no leaves drifting through the woods, just a few tiny particles falling quickly and almost straight down beneath the trees.

• [b]Weather:[/b] The weather system feels very basic. There's sunshine, rain, and winter, but not much else to make the world feel dynamic.

• [b]Plants and animal resources:[/b] Almost all animals provide the same meat, fur, and other materials, with only a few exceptions. Some plants also share the same materials. It's pretty disappointing.

🧍[h2]ANIMATIONS & CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION[/h2]

• [b]Movement:[/b] Animations often feel clunky. On hills, character feet don't align properly with the terrain, sometimes sinking ankle-deep into the ground. You can also point in one direction while your character moves in another.

• [b]Character creation:[/b] Customization options are very limited, often offering only a handful of choices for each feature. The same limitation applies to NPCs.

• [b]Villager clothing:[/b] We still can't change villagers' clothes ourselves, either directly or through a suitable workstation or building type.

⚔️[h2]GAMEPLAY, BALANCE & PROGRESSION[/h2]

• [b]Balance:[/b] It barely exists. Weapons feel too similar, durability is far too low, and raids make little sense. They're random and don't scale with the player's level.

• [b]Economy:[/b] Item prices make little sense across different categories. At the start of the game, hunting alone can make you rich enough to buy almost everything instead of having to work your way towards it.

• [b]Skills:[/b] The skill tree is very basic. I actually like keeping things simple, but there could be more variety.

• [b]Sandbox options:[/b] I like the available sandbox settings, but I think we need more options.

• [b]Village management:[/b] This system still needs a lot of work. Other reviews have explained issues with filters, lists, and general management much better than I can here.

• [b]Villager assignments:[/b] Personally, it's easier for me to do everything myself than to rely on villagers. If you assign villagers to a project, their jobs aren't remembered properly, so you have to assign everything again, one task at a time.

• [b]Building variety:[/b] I'd love to see more building types, such as a dedicated stone warehouse for storing stone, ores, and ingots.

• [b]Tree stumps:[/b] Digging out tree stumps should require a shovel. I accidentally chop down trees far too often when I actually want to remove the stump, preventing the tree from growing back.

🐛[h2]BUGS & TECHNICAL ISSUES[/h2]

• [b]Getting stuck:[/b] Looking inside a warehouse chest once left me completely stuck. There was no unstuck option, so I had to kill my character and lose some of my progress.

• [b]Animal sounds:[/b] Animals sometimes continue making sounds after they die.

• [b]Surfaces:[/b] Under rain even floor inside of buildings is wet.

• [b]Items stacks:[/b] Once weapons are stacked in storage and then taken out, they take durability of the worse one.

• [b]Other issues:[/b] These are just a couple of examples. There are more bugs that still need attention.

🚀[h2]PERFORMANCE[/h2]

Performance is another problem. Even on a good PC, a large village can kill your FPS. Sometimes even a simple rain is enough to make things run like crap.

🎵[h2]MUSIC & AUDIO[/h2]

I love the music. It helps with my depression and calms me down, which is something I genuinely appreciate about this game. That said, even the soundtrack could benefit from more variety.

🛠️[h2]MODDING SUPPORT[/h2]

Please add Steam Workshop support. If the developers don't have the time or resources to address every issue themselves, at least the modding community could help take care of some of these things.

✅[h2]WHAT I LIKE[/h2]

• [b]Village building:[/b] This is where the game really shines. Building and customizing your own village is satisfying.

• [b]Building customization:[/b] Being able to change building materials is a great feature.

• [b]Sandbox settings:[/b] I appreciate having some control over how the game plays.

• [b]Music and atmosphere:[/b] The setting, style, and soundtrack are a big part of what makes this game great.

• [b]New item sets:[/b] They're cool additions, but I believe the focus should be elsewhere for now.

[h2]FINAL THOUGHTS[/h2]

These are just some of the things I've noticed. There are more issues, of course, but there are also good things that make players come back and stay for a while — emphasis on [i]a while[/i].

I really like this game, but it still feels like a beta, or perhaps an Early Access title. The village-building aspect feels good, while much of the rest of the game feels abandoned.

Many of the issues I've mentioned seem like things that should be relatively straightforward to address, yet we're still dealing with them years after release.

The developers seem nice, and they sometimes respond to comments under updates, which I appreciate. However, adding new sets of items is not what the game needs most right now. New item sets are cool, but the devs should focus on other things first.

I really like this game and want it to be better.

[b]I want to recommend this game someday. In its current state, I just can't.[/b]

review:
This game is just a clunky, ugly, buggy mess. It misses so many user friendly features that are taken for granted in games like this. For example, building: do you have a birdseye perspective? No. Well, at least the building you're placing is transparent so you can see behind it, right? Lmao, no. Placing a building is a guessing game, and you never know why you can't place it when it glows red. Basic quality of life features are completely missing; like renaming fast travel posts. Get ready to keep an actual list for all your 'Travel Post 1–20'. You can't even build anything pretty. There are only two different room/hourse types for the player with a meager choice of decoration, and no wall dividers. Which is ironic, considering those assets exist in other NPC villages, but you just can't build them yourself.

Managing a village is equally horrendous. Since you can't set an input list for each season, have fun manually changing their schedule every four days. On top of that, your villagers eat everything by default instead of prioritizing higher tier food. You might have a dedicated cook preparing meals for everyone, but apparently raw rice is just too delicious to resist. Admittedly, there is a priority list where you can toggle food preferences... but only for the host of the lobby. :^)
Also, fun fact: according to the game's logic, simple wood produces more heat than charcoal.

And the bugs, everything is buggy. There are UI bugs where your HP or stamina bar is displayed incorrectly; sometimes you're stuck at 1 HP, and other times you somehow have double your maximum HP. Enemies don't react when their buddies are killed right next to them, enemies get stuck, you get stuck on random props.

This game is just frustrating. It isn't really a survival game, because hunger and cold are non issue (just wear a straw jacket). It's not really a city builder either, because everything is clunky and your villagers barely have any needs. I think there are about seven, and even if you ignore them, villagers won't die of hunger or sickness, they just leave eventually. And to actually reach that point, I honestly don't know what you'd have to do wrong. Combat is also... meh? I mean, it technically works, but it gets repetitive fast. The core gameplay loop is just unfun: go to a region -> clear a bandit camp -> build something -> repeat. There are no livestock, no horses, no matchlock guns, and so on, I could keep yapping forever.

All in all, it's a poor representation of the era. At a certain point, I got so frustrated with everything that I just dropped it and never touched it again.

review:
Do not buy this game.

Group of friends bought it planning for COOP sessions back on release.  We've attempted multiple runs over the years without any progression because the network code for this game is terrible.  Lag makes the game unplayable multiplayer, especially because of how combat is so fast paced.  This is still not fixed.

I ended up playing a full solo campaign because I bought the game and wanted to experience it, and was let down incredibly. 

Village Management and UI:
Do you like scrolling down lists?  This game is for you.  Once villager count, village count, and workstation count reaches more than one screens worth of list items, you are forced to scroll endlessly through the menu to manage your village.  All of the dynasty tabs (population, jobs, priorities) list every single possible entity.  To manage the needs of your village you will need to scroll every item just to find a missing tool, unemployed villager, or that workstation you want to find.  Filters provided in the game are useless and do not correlate to anything you ever need to filter on.  I've spent so much time scrolling lists in this game because I cannot pinpoint a specific workstation or person I know I need to find.

Additionally, your villagers level each season and can produce more at whatever station you work at. However none of the work gets updated to the villager's level.  Each time a villager levels up you need to manually increase the amount of production they produce.  This led to me to each season clicking on every single workstation and ticking up their products a few ticks to ensure they were producing the max they could.

The map is terrible, all the icons are just icons.  No popup describing what the icons are and no way to filter icons out.  Traveler posts (player placed fast travel) cannot be renamed.  At the end of my run I have ~30 different traveler posts and had to remember where each of them went by their default number generated when they were created.  Note that villages can be renamed, and you can even assign a new icon for them.  Why they didn't include the traveler's posts in that system is beyond frustrating. 

Raids and Enemy AI:
This game has a large curve for stats at the beginning. Copper -> bronze -> iron is a significant step.  Raids however are incredibly broken.  I enjoy a challenge and enjoy a steep stat curve, but I have had multiple instances of raids on my villages where the enemy spawned was a Samurai(steel)/Ashigaru(iron) when I still had bronze weapons.  The only way to deal with these enemies was to zerg rush until they died.  And the amount of waves ensure I lost a ton of items and failed the raids. Walls had no effect, enemy AI attacks the closest wall when you are in range so you cannot even funnel them into a choke point or plan for a good defense with your militia.

Additional problem is that once you get iron tier armor, the game is very easy.  Enemy AI is stupid and predictable and the aggro system is flawed.  Attack patterns are the same for the same weapons.  If you fight one, you've fought them all.  Also if you shoot an arrow, all enemies in the vicinity aggro, where if you slowly walk up you can aggro one guy at a time.  This made all the enemy camps very easy to clear.

Major Bugs:
I didn't see these bugs in single player until roughly half way through my run.  However there were many instances of my equipped weapon unusable once I blocked a few attacks.  This would actually lock out my entire hot bar.   Also I've gotten stuck many times after building a workstation in a place where my character could not exit.

Leveling System:
The perks for all of the trees are either boring or useless. 50% of the monk tree just increases your base stats for stam/HP/resolve. The entire first tier is to boost XP gain in this tree or other skill trees.  There is a skill that takes two points to reduce the MASSIVE/s cost of fast travel (10g).  Complete waste of time.  The craftsman tree just increase speed of harvesting or durability of tools. The leadership tree is split between reducing villager needs by a % or unlocking new structures.  The warrior tree actually allows you to unlock new attack moves and has impactful skill allocations.  However four achievements for this game are tied to maxing out three of the trees.  Through this solo run, where I've wiped out all of the major bandit camps, plus significant hunting/minor camp replacement, I still need 36 warrior skill points to max it out.  I currently have 39 lvls in this tree.  So at the end of the game, when I've completed 36/40 achievements, I need to gather a similar amount of XP in warrior just to finish off this achievement when the only enemies left on the map are animals and random spawns of minor camps. Its crazy

Mansions, Walls, and Decorations:
The mansion system is broken.  Interior walls snap to the ground level and since they clip the structure of the mansion you cannot place them.  Mansion walkways do not snap to the actual mansion structure.  End game tier wall connector pieces do not have all their snap points.  A cross section only has two of the four snap points coded, L sections only have one snap point, and the T section only has two.  The "end cap" wall has zero snap points.  This is such a basic function I cannot believe this game is two years after release with these issues still in it.

Decorations are silly.  Do you want to place a weapon rack?  Ok, next you need to build one of a very few selection of the weapons in the game and then place it in the rack. BUT this weapon cannot be pulled from the rack, its only there for decoration.  Minecraft added picture frames ten years ago where you could put and remove any item into a decoration. 

Production Systems:
Late game production systems are stupidly balanced.  Paper, a late game luxury resource, requires 6 different stations to process. Where the final tier of metal requires two.  Paper sells for pennies and any tool/weapon made of the final tier of metal sells for hundreds of gold.  Medicine is incredibly vague and useless on the most part.  There are about 15 recipes for different types of medicine, but none of them actually effect your character at all and all provide roughly the same amount of need for your village. There are probably ~20 different types of food that all equate to the same villager need satisfaction.  The problem is there is no variance to the recipes that you can produce compared to where you actually build a village.  You can get the same food resources anywhere.  This leads to a huge amount of recipes that are completely useless and a bore to navigate through.  

Legendary Weapons and Island Expansion:
They added four sets of legendary weapons to the game.  Only problem is that all of the weapons from the same type have the exact same stats.  Why did you add three legendary katanas that are identical except for their icon and skins?  Such a wasted opportunity for a bit of variety.  Additionally the legendary weapons have such a small increase in power from their masterwork counterparts but require a huge amount of increased resources to make.  Legendary weapons should be unique, not a slightly better version of the previous tier. 

The new islands they added are a complete waste of time.  They replicated the same progression system as the main land  (bronze -> iron -> steel).  It looks like the goal was to make a new way to start the game? But once you complete either the mainland or the islands, the other remaining regions are ridiculously easy and just a time sink to clear.  New content was basic at best, very disappointing.

This game needs a lot of work and with the path its on, I don't see myself ever changing my recommendation of:

DO NOT BUY

I really like this game, I do. It has so much potential!
BUT, there's issues that just make the game hard to play. 

Even on the lowest graphics settings, it is laggy as heck. I often have long lag spikes, and it only gets worse the longer I play. It has kinda forced me to play on the lowest difficulty, cause it makes combat impossible. My PC can run other games similar to this just fine, like lag is not a problem in ex Medieval Dynasty.

There's also several minor things that just bothers me - you can't set jobs to season based, like crops and forgeables, so every season you have to go and manually change them.

Changing between tools take too long, so if you want to swap from ranged to melee combat, you have to start running or you'll get hit.

You can have a child, but you don't know it's gender and you can't name it, at least not in it's first 2 seasons (haven't gotten further, so I don't know if it will eventually be an option)

There is a somewhat frustrating sidequest in Iwasaki. The purpose is learning about mining and smithing I guess, but it pushes you to talk to the villagers and their dialogue is all about the slavery as the village is run on slavery. It feels like it’s leading you to be able to take a stand and help the slaves or change thing, but nope. You can help one guy and then that’s it. Apart from that, you have no impact on the village.

And then there’s just a bunch of smaller things that all add up: 

- When you go to a workstation you can craft one item (or multiple of the same items) and then the menu closes, so if you need to craft multiple different items, you have to enter the workstation after each item crafted
- Items that your villagers forage, craft, gather, etc aren’t slowly put into the general storage throughout the workday, but is all put in at once at the end of the day, which is bothersome when you need a bunch of something in the middle of the day, so you either have to get it yourself or wait until the workday is over
- There are several bugged plants that can’t be harvested and doesn’t disappear when you build something on top of it, so I’ll just have a house with a bush coming up trough the floor
- There are several things that have better alternatives that’s you’ll get access to with higher levels or more money, but you can’t upgrade the existing item. So you might have created dirt road throughout your village and want to upgrade them to cobblestone roads, well you can’t. You either have to go erase all the dirt roads, or put cobblestone roads on top of the dirt road and hope you line it up perfectly. It’s the same with shrines/temples and wells. You can’t upgrade them. You’ll just have to take them down and build the new version.

It really sucks, cause there is so much potential, and between the issues and the severe lag, I have had fun. I love the rural Japan setting, even with low graphics I can tell it’s a pretty game, I like the music, The maps is big and full of different places to see. I really think if the devs did some more polishing and working on the lag spikes, which I can see others struggle with too, they could have such a banger of a game.

review:
Japanese theme for Medieval Dynasty (MD). Personally find it worse than MD in enough ways that overall I think it is not a good game

Disclaimer: Yes I should probably have more hours into the game before making a review, but also it didnt hook me as much and had more frustrating experience with the amount I did play that I likely will not

Pros: 
Personally like the theme

Much much MUCH more options for raw materials, craftable items, and differences of settings than MD

Having more of an "objective" to go for in certain sections before having villagers be able to extract resources from said area is an interesting concept and makes each areas resources and unlocks feel more impactful.

More customization options

More options of weaponry to use in combat, albeit with somewhat meh differences, they are noticeable enough that I can see preferences of certain weapon types over others

The meh:

Combat; you'll either love it, or hate it. Its very... clunky? Parrying feels unreliable, dodging attacks is almost always guaranteed even if you dodge INTO the swing (sure you get no ability to counter attack but you dont lose hp).

The camera having only 3 fixed 3rd person and 1 first person perspectives can be quite limiting. Want to be in third but like only over the shoulder? Nope. The next closest third person camera is like 1.5-2 feet back. That still to close? The final one is like +-5 feet detached from your character.

Many simple inclines force you into the climb animation. This just makes exploring clunky, can get you tripped up in combat, and locks you out of building occasionally.

The raids are more of a nuisance than an issue. Guards dont really make a difference, the only goal is to stop them from hitting you village bell (the main "hub" that signals your village as a village), with the aforementioned camera and combat issues its just a group of 3-4 enemies in 3 waves and thats it. Not exactly special but also something that can get improved

The bad: 
I have had many trees fall through the floor :(

There isnt a safe place to store gold, it feels punishing to die mapping out the world and losing +-10% of my net worth.

Controls. This is likely a personal issue but until remapping parry to RMB, combat was literally so unenjoyable. L-alt parry felt so unnatural when I would assume its RMB to block, but instead of holding block, I time it. By default RMB is power attack and once you are in the animation, good luck! Hope you dont get hit.

Vllages/merchants are so sparse that ultimately the main goal is to become 100% self-sufficient without specializing in a trade/skill you enjoy early. Yes most of these sandbox games end up being a never using the NPC towns except to sell your goods but once you have an idea of what you want to do, you can buy things from activities you dont want to do, or at least not yet.

Building is annoying without being able to move how far away you are building from yourself. You have to manually place and move each building over and over until its finally where you want it. Unfortunately since you only really able to build slightly close to you since moving your mouse y axis positive or negative moves it; it doesnt give you more than +-.75 sec worth of walking distance between you and the building

review:
This is a tough review.  I thoroughly enjoyed my 60 hours of playtime but I have to stop playing due to extreme lag near late game - I've literally decided to stop playing and write this review.   This is disappointing enough to discourage ppl from buying it at this point since you may not be able to comfortably reach end game with current performance issues.

That said, here's my general overview:

Pros: 
- If you like Medieval Dynasty you’ll like this as well - there is a lot of gameplay to be had here.
- There is always something to do and planning what to do based on seasons helps you find focus.
- The mechanic of needing to liberate regions and each having unique specialties is a really nice touch and upgrade from MD.
- The importance of combat and need to deal with enemies, and actual incoming enemy raids, adds yet another interactive layer.  Some players don't like the combat but honestly I got the hang of it and enjoy it just fine now.
- There is usually more than 1 way to attain things you need, be it from choosing different regions, crafting vs buying, or recipes with different options for the same result.
- You can be as immersive as you want when it comes to customizing your village with décor and looks.
- If you like hunting and gathering, this game will scratch that itch.  You can manually find and harvest all the mats and it can be satisfying finding new favorite areas for particular resources.
- Hunting with a bow/arrow is much easier in this than in Medieval Dynasty. On max draw your arrow goes where your cursor is so you don’t have to fuss with falling trajectory. 
- Most jobs can be automated but its up to your discretion as to how you utilize this feature. You can manually craft things and often it is best to pick and choose.
- The setting is quite pretty - from the music, village layouts, and scenery.
- You can expand on the number of villagers than can work a single building by adding more workstations via the furniture options IE you have a lot of control over editing your builds to suit your needs and maximize your space.
- Dynasty Legend panel is pretty robust in terms of buffing various stats or abilities.



Neutral:
-Combat is a tad wonky, but realistically it does make sense that you can’t interrupt a swing mid-action to block or parry. From my personal experience, the combat isn’t as bad as a lot of reviews have suggested.  Perhaps this might be due to weapon preference as some weapons just feel better to use than others - heavy weapons feel way too clunky to me. I prefer the Naginata due to its long/wide reach.

Cons:
- The Biggest one is the late game lag. Once you get to 4+ villages and 70+ villagers, it starts to creep up from sporadic to consistent, to downright unplayable with it hanging up every few seconds.
- You cannot remove villagers from your village if you want to optimize which specialties you need in the later game.
- There is no label or easy distinction between multiple villages when viewing Villagers and jobs (yes you can sort but that is still overwhelming and you only have a general idea), making it a bit tedious to switch them around.
Inventory space cannot be expanded making it tedious to clear large camps where multiple trips are required to bring back all the loot.
- Items can only be repaired when they are fully broken.
- When stacking in storage, items will take on the HP of the stack they sort into. Earlier on I didn’t realize this, and spent a lot of time using items until they broke, repaired them, and then dumped them in storage only to realize they reset to a 20% health. Now I simply abuse the mechanic by making sure the base stack is full health and dumped all the looted low health items in after. I wouldn’t mind if this were fixed so long as it was possible to repair partially damaged items, so I don’t have to use every single one till it breaks just to repair it so I can sell it or have my villagers get more use out of it.
- Sometimes arrows cannot be retrieved and disappear after hitting their target.
- Randomness of worker specialty when recruiting refugees. I rarely find what I actually need when I need it. Also finding new refugees in terms of location is really random.

Features I’d like to see:
- Improved Performance at late game.
- Production limits and notification when limits are reached so you can move villagers around.
- More Clarity on where villagers and buildings are location EG which village.
- A filter box so you can type what you are looking for.
- Change name for Traveler’s Outposts
- Track more than one quest at a time.

review:
I want to like and recommend this game but I cannot in its current state.

- It is not sufficiently optimized - I have played Bellwright, Medieval Dynasty, and other similar sim titles and this is the worst I've played in terms of freezes, stuttering, crashes. I cannot stream the game to Discord or Twitch without crashing my system's memory and corrupting my drive.
- I want to like the combat system but the AI and systems are quite poor for both the enemy and your villagers. You do not have much control over your own people in combat, the guard/security system is extremely barebones, and so the raids can be incredibly brutal to the point of being unrealistic and unengaging. The guards really don't do much and I don't blame them, I can't give them anything. The game's going onto 3 years and this seems a wildly lacking part of the game.
- There's just straight up errors on the UI (the tooltip hotkeys are often inverted or just incorrect so you have to press all your keys to find out how to actually interact with things) and sometimes the UI just disappears (e.g. if you move buildings/plans, the resource requirements disappear).

I really really want to like this game, the memory hogging has messed with my PC but I still tried to plow through. However, I just can't keep failing to load the game, it crashes once or twice, and then I have to repair my drive. I'm hoping for more improvements in terms of system depth and stability but I have to put this down which is a shame because I was enjoying the larger game narrative, base building systems, and the themes.

Devs, please fix your game.. It's hard to enjoy this game in cooperative in current state. 
We like the game setting, the graphics and progression. Game gives nice vibe and is very relaxing. But in needs to be fixed :(

Here you are some of the problems:
• Co-op ONLY for 4 players. We cant play as 5 because this restriction.
• Animals and enemies in co-op are very often stuck, and looks like if there is 2 people on server - they behave normally. If there is 3-4 players animals and bandits stand still and dont move at all. Very cheating gameplay.
• Co-Op desync. A lot of lags, freezes, pings. Very unfunny to het hit because ping lags.
• Game can at random moments start lagging and give you 15-30 fps drops for quite a long period of time, all of a sudden, while normally you were comfortably playing 70-90fps. Yeah, I know I'm playing on laptop, but its happening not only to me, so not my issue. 
• Can't rename our traveller's avanpost. Its hard to remmember which avanpost number stands for which location.
• You better disallow players opportnnity to change villagers count in game settings. Friend of mine who hosted the save ramped up villagers count to 128 people and we didnt even left first Sosogi location. I dont think this is heaalthy to give polayer such an opportunity to break game progression in any game mode except of  "Creative" or "Chillout". Because of this I distanced myself from argueing about breaking game progression and just stated that I will not touch village infrastructure ever and will only hunt, gather resources and explore the world from now on.

Last two of them are kinda minor, but beleive me, I'm not downplaying about performance and coop unstability issues. 

I hope devs read this comments and will work on them.

EDIT:
Combat in co-op is broken. Rubber banding just kills any possible pleasure from fair battle. You jest running around, making hits while holding Shift, and hope that game will register your hit and you will manage to press ctrl and dash away just to repeat. Just can't parry at all, because from server perspective NPC already have hit you before you saw or didnt managed to hit you at all. So do You, your hits can just not register, and instead of enemy being in small stagger, enough for you to dash away or prepare your block or parry he simply hits you instead. 
Also, random enemy NPC camps with wooden cages, sometimes cage can be invisible and may kill you by teleporting you below the ground. Instant death. 
Any NPC or animal can just stuck and stand still. You can kill them with anything you want, they won't mind. At first I limited myself from killing such helpless poor fellows, but after some time it's too annoying when there are 80% being inactve, 15% give you a fight where they are teleporting around, rubberbanding, ignore your hits, and only maybe 5% are a relatively good and fair fight. 

Also, you should do something about your economy. Trader monk just leave any trader with no money and literally no goods at the same time. And I dont see a reasoning why would some traders buy specific stuff. Why farmer should buy seeds or croops? Why tavern seller buys food or weapons? Why woodman buys wood? Etc. Even if you are not monk just running around and killing animals and harvesting their corpses you can make EVERY trader bancrupt by selling them fur, teeth, claws and fat.


Well, TL:DR 
• For singleplyer - you may take it. Game has some vibes, despite sincerely weak combat mechanics and cheap animations. 
• Want to co-op with friends you will struggle. Netcode is complete garbage. 
• You possibly have more than 3 friends to co-op with - just pass by, this game is 4 players max.

review:
as much as I enjoy this game, there's a few things that make the experience a bit less enjoyable

1 - health regens too slow (I have to sit and wait between enemies and work on something else while my health returns.) if health items didn't expire, this wouldn't be too bad.

2 - combat is a little clunky at times (the best experience I have had with a weapon is the naginata) some weapons just don't work how you think they would and the block/parry mechanic just doesn't really work.

3 - seasons by default are incredibly short, 7 days would be a nice default but 4 days is a bit too fast (especially with how frequent bandit attacks can get even with small settlements)

4 - the compass bar at the top is a tad bit useless when everything is cluttered together and all the same colors

5 - the ui for each village should be separate instead of everything being all together. I haven't seen a way to set the screen to show one village at a time to let me properly organize it. (I do appreciate that the materials are shared across each village that is a really nice feature)

6 - certain menus / mechanics are a bit finicky to figure out (fast travel requiring specific levels and need to happen AT those places rather than across the map, the hammer ui is a tiny bit cluttered and the block / parrying is clunky to figure out)

7 - personal taste but the game would be awesome if ai art wasn't used (I can't 100% confirm but when I looked into it, people have noted that it more than likely is which is a shame as the actual scenery in the game is lovely)

the game in general is honestly a really nice way to pass time, I'm enjoying the story and the mechanics are fairly nice as well. the game scratches an itch I've had that other games haven't gotten close to and overall it's not a terrible game to pick up especially on sale. I do look forward to seeing how the game progresses and hope that some of these things are fixed in the future <3

At around 30 villagers I start hitting constant stuttering as the game waits for a single thread to constantly calculate villager pathing. This happens regardless of where you are on the map and isn't even based on PC limitations (my CPU is at 14%, GPU at 14%, RAM at 45%). These stutters get so bad it even causes the hostile AI mobs you fight to stop pathing properly or even freezing in place. If they optimize the game further I'll change my review, but as for now, stick to Medieval Dynasty if you want a survival village builder game along these lines.

review:
This game is... a lot of things.
Perhaps those things that it tries to do, ultimately makes it fade into the background rather than define itself as unique unto itself.
Combat is still pretty clunky. It's unnecessarily hard sometimes, and while a little bit of planning can certainly go a long way towards successful encounters, it doesn't feel fluid.
Also, what is the point of having all these villagers if you can't make some of them companions that help you in combat? Is this game so reliant on Co-op, that you cannot play alone?

Another aspect of the game that just bugs the crap out of me is the lack of an overworld or local grid system. It's not like it's particularly easy to organically grow your village either. Different buildings have different sizes and dimensions. You can totally lock yourself into have to rebuild sections of your village, and it's just frustrating.

Resource management is another area of problems. Why are my villagers consuming RAW RICE? Why is there no way to restrict what meals they can and cannot eat?

Then there is the fact this game released into v1.0, but it still feels like an Early Access game.

I don't know I can't RECOMMEND this game, especially having played similar games of the genre. It needs to go back into the oven and bake for a year or two.
