I will be specific here in that I checked no for if I would recommend the game, not for if I enjoy it. Something about the building system and basic mechanics tickles my brain. But I'd never recommend this to anyone, mostly due to the horrendous lack of directions I know most people need, even I struggled to justify some of the stuff this game pulls with the quests.

The way the quests are handled in this for something like "Mine Iron", are way off from anything else that's remotely smart about how it guides players. That's one of the first things it asks you to do once it's done showing you how to build your settlement (which is also a stretch to say it does that), but it ignores that you need to have bronze to do that, and that you need tin before you can get bronze, which needs a copper pickaxe...you're getting the idea right? A good quest progression would tell you to 'Mine Copper', then next quest is 'Mine Tin' and so on.

I'm all for a hands off approach, but when it's also gating progression HARD when doing this, it's just bad design. If you can get past that issue though, very chill game. I'd just recommend Bellwright instead, different theme, same concept, done better in every way.

review:
Grind beyond grind. Various familiar mechanics (fatigue, resource requirements, tool durability, to name a few) are punishingly difficult. In order to progress, you need to complete quests, but it feels like every time you take a quest, you're signing up for a dozen sub-quests, most of which must be inferred, even in the tutorial. To use metal, you need a forge, for a forge, you need a workshop, for a workshop, you need people to run it, to get people, you need to recruit them, to recruit them, you need a litany of other things... The last straw for me was: I was quested to mine iron, so I needed bronze, to make bronze you need tin, to mine tin, you need a copper pickaxe, to make a copper pickaxe, you must unlock the recipe by "liberating" an area of the map... alone, with a wooden spear... I turned it off and uninstalled that very minute. Most of these prerequisites (while a bit tedious) at least make sense to me, but then you add the "recipe unlock" feature, which is an overt "The devs say that you should be doing something else right now" from the game engine. I agreed, so I turned off the game and did something else.

I think that a tutorial should EITHER hold my hand until I understand the basics, OR naturally encourage me to build in at least a partially-correct order. Preferably, they should do some of both, with frequent rewards for doing so, (you know, like a quest system is designed to do) but this game lets you off the tutorial leash before they let you out of the natural progression kennel, so you're still trapped. Eventually you'll back-trace (or blunder into) a door that'll let you through, but you're gonna find another room of locked doors on the other side. It really feels like the tutorial should be more involved if THIS much of the game is gonna be locked down until I pass through their initial maze of mirrors.

I really wanted to like it. A shame.

review:
[h1]2/10[/h1]

[b]Pros:[/b]
+Visually appealing
+Combination of survival, city building and RPG
[b]Cons:[/b]
+Construction system is a bit shallow
+Poor optimisation
+Shallow NPC system
+World feels lifeless
+Combat is a bit stiff

In general, the idea of the game is interesting: combining coop survival with city building and RPG elements. However, the realisation is not the best. The game is overly grindy, which is acceptable for survival games, but the world does not feel satisfying to explore, fight the enemies and grind those resources. One of the main features are city building and NPC interaction systems with the possibility of building your own village, assigning different roles for its residents and automating their work, so you can focus more on other things. The building mechanic consists basically of choosing something from the proposed structures, introducing minor changes into its exterior, and dropping resources into the construction site. The NPC interaction part is also quite shallow. A little bit disappointing.

review:
Even though I really love this game - the audiovisual content implements a true japanese atmosphere, the vibes and setting are just great and really to the life from the historic sengoku period, there are even some quests etc - but I cannot wholeheartedly recommend it in its current state. There are way too many thing underdeveloped that really hinders the player's ability to enjoy the content... though maybe I'm way too critic to the things I like, idk, but imho these issues need to be addressed before wasting time with "lol now u can fish" updates;

 - Even though the gameplay heavily focuses on managing your village, the UI to do so is so garbage that it has not even got any filters or sorting implemented, you have to recognize workstations by names like "Guard Station 6" and you cannot rename them (but you can rename the building they are placed in, but that is not helping as building name does not show up lol). We need really these and they already exist in the player's inventory, so implementing it to other windows should not be really difficult. 
 - Raid strength and frequency needs to be aligned more to the actual power of the dynasty. Like I did a lot of exploration and built many decorations, so I'm still at wooden/copper stage, but I have a second village and the game thinks it needs to send me several waves of armored ashigaru equipped with swords. Those bad guys literally 2-shot my guards and 3-shot my (iron armored?!!!) main character. How in the hell was this calculated? This whole 1.1 update raid thing would need a revisal, in its current state it feels like an amateur mod instead of an official update. 
 - Villagers you assign to jobs are not differentiated by any skill whatsoever, you can literally reassign someone and replace them with a random homeless from the forest and they'll have the very same efficiency. Villagers need to have at least some amount of preference or skills, otherwise I don't really understand why even bother having different names for different villagers. This is really not difficult to implement, since it is only affecting the calculations, no fancy animations or props needed.
 - The economy needs some love as well. On hardcore, the value you sell is reduced to 10% of original value, which makes getting Monk XP really hard and also makes the Monk perks giving increased selling prices kinda worthless. Also, the visiting beggars tend to have multiple times my money in their pocket. This is not hardcore, this is bullshit. Also it would be really nice if e.g. a food vendor would be interested in food items to purchase, not every last stick I've found on the streets. It would be really nice to see regional prices as well; if a region does well, it should have more purchasing power and more stuff available with merchants. Not to mention what exciting thing would be to have trade routes.

Most of my pain points above could be easily solved, but until that I cannot and I won't recommend the game. Looking forward to return to this game once these are solved, as I really enjoyed playing it, and this game would deserve a more content and these corrections!

review:
Let's get this straight: this is not Sniper Elite 6, and it barely feels like a proper DLC to Sniper Elite 5.

I have played every Sniper Elite game, and the modern ones in co-op with a friend. Resistance feels like someone took the Sniper Elite 5 engine exactly as it was, kept all its old bugs, and gave it to a much less experienced gameplay and level design team. That is probably why it is not called Sniper Elite 6.

The biggest problem is the AI. It feels like a considerable regression from Sniper Elite 4 and 5, and it makes the game way too easy.

Enemies never use the alarms. There are alarm systems everywhere for you to disable, but what is the point if nobody ever triggers them? There are basically no reinforcements either, apart from maybe one or two scripted events where a truck arrives with four to six soldiers, and even that is not threatening.

You can just start shooting loudly and enemies often come one by one through the same path until they are all dead. Nobody surrounds you, no serious counterattack develops, and there is almost no feeling that the enemy is reacting intelligently to your presence.

In Sniper Elite 3 to 5, I felt under constant threat. I wanted to stay hidden, break lights, avoid alarms, move bodies, set traps and plan for failure.

That planning mattered because resources and inventory space were limited. Choosing one more mine instead of a bandage mattered. Spending a talent point to carry more equipment mattered.

Here it does not.

There are barely any roaming vehicles, no meaningful reinforcements, and almost no reason to mine a road. At the same time, explosives are everywhere. After looting only a few soldiers or rooms, my inventory is already full of ammo, mines, medical supplies and almost everything else, even on the hardest difficulty. I could practically mine every road on the map, but for what?

The same problem applies to traps. I used to enjoy rigging bodies or preparing an ambush in case a patrol found them later. Here, once the nearby soldiers are dead, almost nobody is coming.

Even VIP targets behave stupidly. Instead of fleeing the map or hiding somewhere secure, which gave you a real reason to remain stealthy in previous games, I have seen scientists grab a gun and come outside to hunt me after I already killed dozens of guards.

So the game gives you more tools than ever while removing most of the situations where those tools were useful. Nothing feels scarce, preparation barely matters, and very little feels rewarding.

Talents have the same problem. You can revive yourself, shoot while downed, carry plenty of supplies and replenish almost everything constantly. Most upgrades simply do not feel important.

Weapons also lack personality. I noticed surprisingly little difference between rifles, ammunition types or many weapon modifications. Even the sniping itself somehow feels less rewarding and more arcade-like than before.

Then there is the HUD, which keeps one of my biggest problems with Sniper Elite 5.

The game offers a million difficulty and realism options, yet there is no sensible middle ground for the HUD. Either I get too much arcade information, including indicators showing when enemies are spotting me and text literally explaining what the AI is doing, or I disable so much that I also lose basic information like my health and remaining ammunition.

And no, "just play without the HUD" does not solve this.

In real life I know how many magazines, grenades and other items I have on my belt or in my backpack. Hiding that information is not realism, especially when the game has no proper tactical inventory screen where I can simply check what I am carrying.

I just want to know my health, ammo and equipment without the game also telling me what every enemy around me is thinking.

Sniping has a similar problem. Even with my sniping settings pushed toward maximum realism, the game still gives too much assistance and too much indication of where the shot should go. Combined with the weak AI and lack of danger, it feels more like an arcade mechanic than something I really had to judge and earn.

Then there are the bugs. Many Sniper Elite 5 bugs are still present, with new ones added. Traps attached to electrical panels sometimes simply do not explode, for example.

The world also feels lifeless. There is little interesting dialogue to overhear, little environmental storytelling, and almost nobody except soldiers waiting to be killed.

The two things I still appreciate are that the campaign can be played entirely in co-op with a friend, and that you can save almost anywhere instantly. Unfortunately, when the game provides so little resistance, even the excellent save system becomes much less important.

I am genuinely disappointed because Sniper Elite is a great series and the basic engine is still very good. But Resistance removes much of what made the previous games interesting: tension, stealth, preparation, scarcity, meaningful loadouts, intelligent enemy reactions and rewarding sniping.

I cannot recommend it, even on sale. I would rather wait and hope Rebellion comes back with a proper Sniper Elite 6.

review:
A Game That Feels Stuck in the Past

Visuals
The game is ugly — noticeably so, and in my opinion far beyond what we saw in Sniper Elite 3 and Sniper Elite 4. It feels visually dated rather than intentionally stylised, which makes it difficult to overlook how little the series appears to have progressed.

Gameplay & Innovation
The biggest problem is how rehashed and tired the experience feels. There is very little here that feels genuinely new, and I haven't seen any meaningful improvements or innovation that justify this feeling like a new entry rather than a retread of what came before.

AI & Immersion
The AI constantly pulls me out of the experience. Enemies will make completely nonsensical decisions — for example, remaining completely unalerted while everyone around them is screaming, scrambling for cover, and engaging in a firefight. Moments like this make it impossible to stay immersed because the game repeatedly reminds you that you're fighting against a collection of scripted behaviours rather than believable enemies.

Music & Atmosphere
The music also feels like it was carried over from the previous game rather than designed around this one. It doesn't fit the environments particularly well and often feels disconnected from the atmosphere the game is trying to create.

Bugs
I'm actually writing this review because I've encountered a game-breaking bug where my weapon has become stuck in an infinite reload loop and can no longer be used. It's an especially frustrating way to be reminded of how rough around the edges the game feels.

Overall
Overall, this feels like a great game from 2009 that somehow never got the memo that it's now 2026. The core concept is still enjoyable, but the dated visuals, lack of meaningful innovation, questionable AI, mismatched music, and game-breaking bugs make it feel like the series has failed to keep up with the times.

review:
I got this on a -70% sale, keep this in mind.

I hadn't played a Sniper Elite game since two or three if I remember correctly, and this is a fairly formulaic release. The arcade-y sniping mechanics are still quite visceral and fun to witness, the third person combat is uninspired and quite poor honestly, the stealth mechanics aren't anything interesting, you crouch around bushes and shoot lamps out and walk up behind people and most of the levels are about navigating around the patrol routes. The AI is nothing impressive. There are vehicles and such which can be an interesting encounter and add life to levels.

The progression is locked primarily to finding a single collectible per level, which is fine, I wish there was more to unlock without having to search through every level.

The survival mode can be quite intense, the invasion mode is definitely a highlight (spawning in others' campaigns to try hunt them down) although it's very clearly poorly thought through with how common things come down to camping, or the existence of players who empty out levels of AI and set traps.

Overall, I wouldn't recommend this purely because of the price outside of sale. It's fairly formulaic, you don't actually do a lot of sniping and the campaign primarily consists of crouching around and navigating through a very very generic stealth level with all the tools you'd normally expect (so generic I won't even name them as you can expect decoys etc.) I'll definitely play it to completion because I have low standards.

review:
I know I checked "Not recommended", but it's really a "It's mid" - at least for Solo play. 

tl:dr - If you have played  Sniper Elite 4 & 5, this one feels really bland. It's beyond bland. It's mediocre in every sense of the word. Maybe don't buy if you expect something on the same level, as I don't think it is as good.
It's not bad per se, it's just the blandest Sniper Elite I have played (I have played 3, 4 and 5 I think 1 year ago).

Everything is mid. This game, the way its formula is applied, just exists.
Just like the game "went through the motions", I just went through it all the same.
I feel nothing having finished this game, and I am left with nothing.

It might be blander than steam-cooked chicken breast, no seasoning.
Do with that information what you will.

--- Wall of text below ---

Of course, all of this is only my opinion. Mine. I only play solo, so I did not test Invastion or whatever. Please take this into consideration.

As I mentioned in intro, I know I checked "Not recommended", but it's more like really "It's mid".
There is no standout good feature. There is nothing astonishingly bad. I have played other Sniper Elite, I was more entertained while played those than this one. It just never clicks for me.

Let's start with performance. It's doing great. I don't think you will have any issue with any decent PC (I rank decent starting at 1070 - that's what I played 3-4-5 with, and it did wonders).
Graphics wise, there is nothing better than 5 in my opinion.

Gameplay wise, it's Sniper Elite. I do not know what to say.
It is exactly the same.
It's fine, it works, no need to break what works. There is no refinement of what was present before.

Difficulty is funny. I played in the Sniper Elite difficulty (second to highest I believe), I honestly do not think it's difficult at all. Maybe I should have played the hardest one. Enemies are dumb. You will be fine whatever you choose.

The maps are...ok. I felt 3-4 times that I may have played that map before. It's a weird feeling.
No standout maps either. The maps are not bad, you can do the objectives multiple ways, that's nice. But I don't think you will feel like "oh wow, that's ground breaking level design".
For a game set in France, it did not feel that French. It's weird.

The weapons are ok. Gewehr DLC? That's garbage policy. But I don't really care.
I don't think you will be frustrated by the feeling or handling of the guns, it's good.

The story is ok, I think. I could not care at all. Another new superweapon to destroy with its architect as the last boss. It was not memorable.
It's something along the lines of 11hours of gameplay for the main story.
You have additional challenges to unlock everything, so you can have fun this way if you feel like it.

The MC. The way he speaks feels...off. The dialogue is not great. I do not know what happened during conception. It's the low point of this game, but this is not enough to prevent you from buying the game if you don't mind the deep mediocrity of this game.

review:
This game is simply sauceless. I explicitly avoided buying it when it released because it looked like a massively overpriced DLC to Sniper Elite 5, and only decided to give it a try with a -60% sale.

Even at -60% I still feel robbed. I was wrong to think it was an overpriced DLC to SE5. That would imply it'd at least be of the same quality as SE5. But it's not, it's worse, and SE5 wasn't great in the first place! I finished the game only because I had a friend to suffer through it with, I would have dropped it 2 missions in otherwise.

[h1]Plot[/h1]

Not even worth addressing. It's bad, and it's badly executed. SE isn't known for its plot, it only needs to clear the minimum bar of justifying the missions and what happens in them, but it fails even at that. Hell, I don't think the main nazi you're chasing the entire campaign even has a single voice line. He just appears in an absurdly nonsensical cutscene on the last mission, smiles, and then you just shoot him while he runs away on a motorcycle (that he stole from two german soldiers after shooting them because uhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh who knows)

[h1]Gun play/customization[/h1]

It's the exact same as SE5. Except with less guns than SE5. Don't ask me why.

[h1]Campaign[/h1]

It's bad in so many ways... I'll try to be as concise as possible: 
[h2]Boring and predictable[/h2]
Every mission follows the same template. You have a main objective, optional objectives, and one target to kill (in a specific manner if you want to unlock a new weapon). Half the time the objectives are completely redundant, go blow up something but the RAF comes to bomb it all anyway when you leave. 
[h2]Kill targets[/h2]

Each mission demands a different method to kill the mission's specific kill target. But while it's often interesting, there is no kill cam ever for these, even though half happen off-screen (poison, manipulation, sabotage... all stealth methods where you can't just stay to observe). It's incredibly disappointing to go through the effort of setting up a trap and not see it when it springs in action.

[h2]Resource attrition, or the lack thereof[/h2]

There is NO resource attrition in the game. You are a lone sniper behind enemy lines with minimal french résistance help, yet every mission gives you everything you could possibly need. The first few missions shower you with anti-tank rifles and rocket launchers, but there is not a single armored target you could possibly use them on! Need to breach a safe or a door? No problem! Here's 5 satchel charges! In fact, breaching a door with a satchel charge will sometimes immediately reward you with 2-3 satchel charges! 

You want to use a key instead to avoid making noise, or maybe the game is daring today and actually requires you to use a key? Have no fear, the key will without failure be within 50 meters of where it needs to be used! Don't bother trying to look for anything you might need, everything will naturally fall in your hands. I played the entire campaign on hard difficulty and regularly finished with 10+ satchel charges, and having found more AT rifles and rocket launchers than enemies on the map!

[h3]Yet, half of the abundant resources are useless![/h3]

As I mentioned earlier, missions with [i]not a single armored target[/i] will shower you with rocket launchers and anti-tank rifles. But even for the missions where there [i]is[/i] a tank, all those rarely ever come in use! Why? Because you can't actually carry them with you! Every weapon you find on the map that isn't part of your loadout isn't a weapon you can actually equip, it's just a limited-use weapon that takes your active weapon slot and that you immediately drop when you switch weapon.

The way for you to make use of the rocket launcher you found 5 minutes before encountering a tank is to backtrack to where you found it, painfully navigate through the enemies between you and the tank as you have to drop the rocket launcher on the ground every time you need to use any of your weapons, all that so you can make use of the SINGLE SHOT rocket launcher against the tank that requires 3 to 4 shots. 

So of course, what you end up doing is the much more efficient strategy of just going behind the tank, loading armor-piercing rounds, and shooting it's rear until it blows up. It shouldn't work, but not only it does, it's the most efficient strategy by far. 

[h2]No vehicles. No threats. No nothing.[/h2]

I said earlier some of the missions don't have a single armored target, so what are the big threats you have to worry about then? None. It's just going to be your regular old sniper, or with a bit of luck maybe a machine-gun emplacement, but even these barely count as a threat you need to keep track of... 

Even the few missions that do have armored targets, it's one of two things: Either the damn King Tiger from SE5, or a static armored train car with... a King Tiger turret on top of it (how original!!). And I cannot overstate how boring the King Tiger is! You either throw explosives at it until it blows up, or you shoot armor-piercing rounds in its rear until it blows up. SE4 had different armored vehicles with different capabilities, and you actually could take out the crew members inside with well-placed shots through the visors! You know? Precision shots?? In the sniper elite game??? Why did you remove that???? 

[h2]Bugs that softlock you :)[/h2]

Mind you this wouldn't have been acceptable on release either, but it is even less [b][i]a year and a half later[/i][/b]. If you knock an enemy unconscious and that enemy is relevant to an objective, and you hit a checkpoint after that, and for whatever reason you have to reload from that checkpoint, there's a good chance that enemy will become invisible and intangible, essentially soft-locking you out of that objective until you restart the mission from zero! Cool!

Similarly, the enemy's AI will just... get stuck. They'll sometimes stay permanently locked in a state of alert and you have to restart to do any objective that would require them to [i]not[/i] be in a state of alert. 

[h2]Speaking of, wow, the enemy AI is bad[/h2]

Not that it was super smart in SE5 either. But boi. I've seen them get distracted by a single rigged generator for 10 minutes, the whistle mechanic to lead them to you is useless because they seem completely deaf and can only hear you whistling if you're right in front of them, they'll favorize waking up their unconscious allies (or even picking them up and carrying them!) even if that means getting out of cover and right in your gunsight in the middle of a firefight, and of course, as I've mentioned before, sometimes they'll just get stuck in a perpetual state of alert...

[h2]The kill cams don't even try to be smart either![/h2]

Literally a signature feature of the game! The kill cam! By default it is way too frequent, and the only thing you can adjust is just that: [i]the frequency[/i]. So if you reduce the frequency, the game will just randomly jumpscare you with a kill cam for a 50 meters shot you did in the middle of a firefight, but [i]won't[/i] do a killcam for a 500 meters shot across the map. You might as well remove the feature if it fails at making the cool shots look cool and instead focuses on the bad shots lmao

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

I genuinely hard recommend against it. Even on sale. It is just SE5, but worse. It brings absolutely *nothing* new of value.

review:
Sniper Elite: Resistance feels more like a large expansion for Sniper Elite 5 than a standalone game. 
The campaign puts players in the role of Harry Hawker and, honestly, I hope Rebellion never lets whoever wrote some of his dialogue do it again. Hawker is one of the blandest protagonists in the series, and very little about him makes him memorable. 

Unfortunately, Resistance inherits almost all of the problems that plagued Sniper Elite 5. The AI remains weak, the sniping mechanics are still oversimplified, and many of the design decisions that disappointed fans of earlier entries are still present. 

The one area where I think the developers listened to player feedback is map design. The maps generally offer more opportunities for long-range engagements and provide better sniper positions than many of the locations in Sniper Elite 5. For a game called Sniper Elite, that is a welcome improvement. 
Sadly, that is where most of the positives end. At its core, Resistance is the same game as Sniper Elite 5. It reuses the same mechanics, the same formula, and many of the same flaws while charging a price that is difficult to justify.

If you were disappointed by Sniper Elite 5, Resistance is unlikely to change your mind. If you enjoyed Sniper Elite 5, you may find some value here, but I would still recommend waiting for a significant discount.

In my opinion, Resistance should have been a DLC rather than a standalone release.

review:
I bought this a few hours ago since it was on sale, and the recent reviews seemed positive. I heard it was buggy at release, but reviews were vague about what state it remained in now. 

I like to play Sniper Elite fresh, on the hardest difficulty, and see how far I can get without dying. 

I just finished the first mission, and it doesn't bode well for the other 9 missions; to be fair to it it did seem to be a tutorial mission, which would explain the linear route towards extraction and the lack of any Invasion throughout.

The 1st Mission features a lot of fast-flowing water to mask your shots in part, but it also masks all your lures from the enemy. If I smash a bottle on the concrete behind you, reasonably, you should notice it. If I whistle behind you, no amount of rainfall is gonna mask it.

Once I blew up all the Local AA and cracked some holes in the dam at the same time, I found the enemy ran about for a few minutes but then quickly lost interest and went back to tired patrols. Not the great end battle I expected.

I did notice that on some surfaces, you leave a trail of footprints far behind you, which I assume an Invader could see and follow. That seems new.

Otherwise, it's just Sniper Elite 5, with slightly worse graphics. 

It didn't seem janky in cutscenes, and the frame rate stayed consistent throughout.
But I did already notice a few invisible walls I couldn't throw bodies through, and I had an awkward time with trying to peek or cling to corners.

I enjoyed it because I got what I expected, but If you haven't played Sniper Elite before, or are looking for a polished title, I would just go back to SE5. SE:R runs well, but it's not been tested well enough.
If you want a better stealth experience, I hear earlier titles are better, but SE5 Invasions help to keep a sense of urgency to the missions not seen before, and they did a better job with the atmosphere.

The accent of first resistance contact seems like a British person talking French, rather then a true citizen. Weak.

review:
I play these games on authentic mode only. I didn't start there with this title. My first playthrough was on normal.

It isn't that I think the games are easy. On authentic, they are... more of a challenge. But if you play a lot (I do), and have better than average game sense and skills (I do), authentic is, simply, the ONLY way to play. That is my first critique of this series where it is now. I am slam up against the ceiling of what this game offers, and the truth is the game still isn't either as difficult as it could easily be, or authentic in any sense.

Normal difficulty is a fantasy setting. An arcade version of WW2 ghost fighting. NOT REAL. But, here is the BAD part: On the settings called AUTHENTIC PLUS, the maxed out, most difficult preset the game offers, almost every enemy NPC in the game takes THREE headshots to kill. A targeted boss NPC can require FOUR. Blood and brains splattering on every single shot, and the bastard is still shooting back at you. In addition, even on the max preset, you still have to go into custom settings and tell the game to account for bullet drop, wind, enemy fire interfering with your concentration, etc.

I set both MY health, AND the Nazi health setting to the lowest possible value. That way, one good clean head or body shot to to either myself or any enemy NPC is an instant kill. The Player will still survive many single shot wounds, but you can accept this as "grazing fire", requiring bandaging, but not enough to kill.

On any game that even pretends to behalf-way serious, with mechanics as thoughtfully honed over no less than four games (SE3, SE4, SE5 and SE: Resistance), for it to still be necessary to do this, and to have to do a deep dive into the game menu to find it at all (both the result of deliberate choices by the designers) is inexcusable. And it has happened now FOUR TIMES IN A ROW.

I don't want to write a novel, but it is also necessary to point out that on ANY difficulty settings, there is a white marker indicating how to compensate for both wind (horizontal) and bullet drop (vertical) that CHANGES to compensate for ANY RIFLE chosen. And you CAN'T TURN IT OFF. I can describe how you go about determining these elements of a shot without those markers. Well, one way, at least. Here it is.

You pick a point in your scope at the same distance as your potential target. You make sure the point of the reticle is on that fixed point, and fire. You mark the place the bullet lands. It may be, for example, up a few inches (on a say, 200 meter shot), and a few inches to the left. You can then move directly to your actual target and place your reticle a few inches DOWN, and TO THE RIGHT. Bang.

Which, as you can imagine, makes 1900 meter shots virtually a unicorn in real life, especially with WW2  level equipment and a one man operation. Such shots in all of the titles I listed are routine.

I never trained to be a sniper. So if I know how to adjust for those factors without a crutch, it means LOTS of players do. The game refuses to allow ANY player to do so. Even after it does this, which makes it impossible to miss ANY scoped shot once you know the system of the game, it STILL places visible tracer lines showing the arc and vector of every shot you take over a certain distance, which basically conforms to the distance at which the arc would become noticeable to the eye. ANOTHER CRUTCH.

Lastly, these are very good games. The solo campaigns are rich and interesting, and the look of the game is heartbreakingly beautiful. This is a gorgeous game, visually. And, despite the catering to low skill players, the games are fun and challenging the first time you play.

But Rebellion's support? ABYSMAL. All four titles listed above have multiplayer. All have been overrun and RUINED by cheaters and lobby mobs.

Rebellion talks a good game about support and fair, honest play, and makes several pretty websites and portals where you can report cheaters, but then does NOTHING AT ALL ABOUT IT.

In closing, two real, positive comments: The solo campaigns in these games are worth the price if you play a LOT of games. I am 64. review:
Sniper Elite: Resistance feels like the point where the series finally collapses under its own weight. I’ve played every SE (except the first), so I’ve seen the progression - the rough but distinctive second game, the excellent third, the solid fourth, and the already tiring fifth. But this one? This feels like a complete misfire.

Sooooo - Resistance just isn’t a good game.

The AI is probably the most frustrating part. Enemies can hit you from absurd distances with almost any weapon, with a level of precision that feels completely unfair. This was already an issue in earlier games, but instead of improving it, they somehow made it worse. You can get killed by a random soldier from a distance where it’s hard for you to hit anything even with a sniper rifle.

The system for accessing certain areas is another questionable design choice. Items like explosives or crowbars spawn in inconsistent, often inconvenient locations. Sometimes they’re nearby, other times they’re scattered across the map or carried by a random enemy. It gets to the point where restarting from a checkpoint can actually be a more efficient strategy than continuing, which says a lot about how poorly this is handled.

Mission design doesn’t help either. Objectives quickly become repetitive, and there’s very little sense of progression or payoff. The campaign is boring, and the main character... well, he has no personality.

The story is also a garbage. It clearly shows Nazis as the enemies, which is expected - I mean, Nazis being bad isn’t exactly a big revelation. But here it almost becomes ridiculous. There are no Germans as such, just “NAZIS” everywhere, like everything has been reduced to that one word. It feels like the game is afraid to say directly that this was Nazi Germany. Because of that, there’s no real depth or context behind it. Everything feels very simple, without really exploring the historical background it’s based on. For a game set so strongly in World War II, it ends up feeling strangely disconnected from that setting, almost like it’s trying to avoid fully acknowledging it.

What’s most disappointing is that there’s nothing here that really stands out in a positive way. Previous SE always had something going for them — atmosphere, level design, or the satisfying feel of sniping. Resistance, on the other hand, feels empty.

Overall, it’s the weakest game in the series — a frustrating and underwhelming experience.

[spoiler]This game is fucking garbage.[/spoiler]

review:
Look, I normally really like the Sniper Elite franchise, ok? Like, I've spent literal days on individual maps trying to optimize my route, get achievements, find collectibles, and things like that in past SE games.

Sniper Elite Resistance is pretty bad.

It feels like an afterthought, as if the developers were like, "Hey, we have some European assets lying around, let's shove them onto some maps with half-assed buildings, missing polygons, and objects you should be able to move through or over but can't because reasons. Then we'll sprinkle a few bad guys here & there, create a new main character with annoying & repetitive lines, add a big bad with zero story (and a stupid death), invent another 'superweapon' threat with zero urgency (and a stupid name) and call it a day."

It's only worth buying if it's been *steeply* discounted, including the DLC, and even then only if you're really into the franchise.

Otherwise you're buying a game that is buggy as hell, has some ridiculously small maps, and doesn't have nearly enough enemies. The campaign only has eight maps unless you buy the DLC, and whatever story there is isn't engaging at all. I got enough skill points after half the game to fill all the useful skills. The healing skills were almost never used, because the enemy AI is dumb as hell!

On top of all that, it's STILL a pain in the neck to check your "service record" to see which collectibles you've gotten.

Rebellion, it's pretty clear you're just phoning it in at this point. Either quit the franchise and make something else, or put some real effort into your next Sniper Elite game.

Please.

review:
I personally am struggling to decide if I should recommend the game or not - I think that says a lot, I would've not hesitated to recommend Sniper Elite 5 (SE5). In fact I did many times and bought two separate gifts for friends.

I'd say if it's on a HEAVY discount then potentially purchase it, however if you have other games on your wishlist look elsewhere, there are 100% funer games to be played. I paid £20 and I'd say that's to much... If you've never played Sniper Elite 5, then don't hesitate go buy that now. If you can get it for a good price then yeah absolutely enjoy it but don't expect to even get 100 hours of fun out of this game.

The graphics are very good however without HDR enabled or turning the brightness up far to high the map is FAR to dark.

The movement is slightly clunkier than SE5, which causes all sorts of weirdness normally at the worst times.

The map design is pretty cool to during the campaign but is a bit mental without a friend present, and the absolutely insane map design makes Axis Invasion (which I'd argue is a fan favourite) an absolute nightmare, more on this later.

The campaign is ambitious, but I found myself not as invested into the story line as SE5, it just didn't feel right. However I did enjoy playing through it, but I believe that's mainly because I had a friend with me.

The lack of features such as DLSS, FSR, Frame generation, is absolutely unacceptable for a modern game - the previous game had FSR (all be it FSR is terrible). This makes it less accessible to lower end systems, this isn't an issue for me but it's worth noting.

Axis Invasion my favourite game-mode is an absolute hell hole, due to the games insane map design with more angles at variety of different heights the game is an absolute camping hell hole. I'd consider myself fairly decent at Axis Invasion but the constant mines placed, insane peak angles, and instant death if you don't check for mines at your spawn point. Axis invasion is borderline unplayable a majority of games. It's genuinely no fun compared to SE5. Yes SE5 had this "issue" but due to the map design it was far more obvious to find as there where only a few good camping spots not 500 a map. The AVARAGE player will NOT enjoy Axis Invasion, end of story.

Level design is probably the worst I've ever seen. Each map has been covered by previous entries that did it so much better. Resistance feels like it is trying to cover everything and ends up hitting absolutely no marks. Enemy placement, problem-solving, stealth, sniping, item placement; everything is quite awful.

For a sniping game, it forces you into so many CQC situations. I don't believe there is enough concrete in Germany to cover all the "secret" underground Nazi bunkers that house the endless machinations of destruction. The only way you could remember it's a sniping game is that occasionally you're given a clear opportunity, like the game remembered what the title was. And hell, that's not even covering the bugs and broken mechanics....

All in all, one of the worst entries in the franchise. It brings me back to the olden days of Sniper Warrior....

review:
Was a fantastic game to start with with some much needed additions to make the day to day parts of your car dealership tasks more automated. However, the updates just keep coming and they don't stop coming. Bugs from updates take weeks to fix all while we keep getting more and more and more things nobody is asking for. While I get that it is supposed to be a "simulator", it shouldn't be aiming for realism over being fun. 

Devs added in liquids for the vehicles like oil. Sure, fine. But only you can buy them and the empty containers go into your warehouse where only you can destroy them. Devs added in soap for the car wash, and sandpaper for the body shop. More consumables that only you can buy and destroy. The automation platform needs you to park cars in a specific spot and tell it what to do to them, not very 'automated'. If you put cars in your garage you need to go through like a 30 second animation to get them back out before you can drive them to the parking spot for the automation platform and tell it what to do. The settings for the platform are not saved, you have to tell it exactly what to do every single time beyond fill up the gas and tires and give it a wash. All of this in a game where you are the owner of a car dealership full of employees and you are literally the only person that can sale the cars. 

If you fell in love with this game watching certain youtubers play it, just know.. that game is dead. This is the shell of what was a great little game. The devs need to stop trying to expand beyond their scope and focus on returning the fun to the game. If you want consumables in your game, fine, give us an employee to handle that. Give us employees to sale the cars so we can leave the lot during business hours. Make the automation platform have a default set of tasks to perform and claim vehicles straight from our underground warehouse.  And most importantly. Code the current employees on how to use a freaking trash can.

I can't recommend this game at full price, not with how buggy the damn thing is. The deal breaker for me is repeated save file corruption. More often then not, 8 or 9 time out of 10, when loading a save file it fails and resets to the starting state, loss of all upgrades, vehicles, and cash. Get the bug on all saves and autosaves and you have to just start over again after hours of progress. A third to half of the 68 hrs of game time I have at time of review was mostly spent sitting in the pause menu to avoid this issue.

It also has a issue where the longer you play a save it starts freezing for several seconds during autosaves, with the length of the freeze getting worse the longer you play, and restarting the game does not fix this issue.

If you want to give this game a try, wait for a sale and get it when it's around $10 USD, it's not worth full price in it's current state and quite frankly the quality of the game feels too cheap for a $20 game.

review:
[h1]I played 23+ hours before realizing this is more of a tycoon than a proper Car Dealer Simulator[/h1]

Unfortunately, it took me a while to figure it out because I noticed it little by little!

After 23+ hours, I’m leaving a negative review because I think the game has a fundamental design problem.

It is called Car Dealer Simulator, so I expected the dealership, sales and business management side to be the core of the experience.

Instead, a huge part of the game is spent repairing and restoring cars in the workshop, while the actual selling process is extremely limited, repetitive and shallow.

[h2]You can sell a car to an NPC with so many flashing red warning lights like a Christmas tree and it won't affect its sale value or reputation at all!!![/h2]

That would be less of a problem if the workshop mechanics had a strong impact on sales, but many of them barely matter. Several maintenance actions feel important at first, yet have little or no meaningful effect on how NPCs value or buy the car. 

[h3]Do you guys realize that you don't even need to tighten the screws on the parts and it makes no difference! The game considers it as a correctly installed part[/h3]

Ironically, the part I enjoyed most was the tycoon loop: buying cheap, making profit and expanding the business.

But the actual “dealer” side is not where the game shines, and in my opinion, it absolutely should be.

After 23+ hours, it feels like the game spends too much effort simulating workshop tasks that often do not matter enough, while the dealership systems that should define the game remain underdeveloped.

That mismatch is the main reason I cannot recommend it!

review:
As so many others, on this game or otherwise, have stated - God I wish I could give it neither thumbs up nor thumbs down.

tldr: It's a game with a good base but which fails to (yet) capitalize on what it has. Its systems are complete, but shallow; the world is small and barren; it is stable and well-running game with random technical bugs, plagued with random QoL annoyances that detract from the play but only just. Ultimately, it feels like an early access game yet isn't. As it is, it's a 6/10 game (with 5 being an actual average and not 7.5). But the team behind it seems to be continuing to work on it so it has a chance to be in the future a better game. Right now it just needs more time to cook. I can see what this game could be and I hope it gets there one day. But that day isn't today.

Long review:

This is a game which has such a solid base. It could be a mixture of Gas Station Simulator and Car Mechanic all wrapped up in one with a sprinkling of Big Ambitions thrown in for good measure. Right now it just isn't that. I will at least add the caveat of 'yet' because the team seems to be actively working on it. It isn't abandoned. But 'yet' isn't a guarantee.

Finding and restoring vehicles to sell is legitimately fun. It's a decent gameplay loop. Everything works. the game is stable. They've even modeled the interiors of all the existing cars so you can drive from behind the wheel. It's cool seeing the inside of a 70s Oldsmobile with the grandma tach or that of an ultramodern Porsche. But the longer you play, the more cracks you see as the house is being renovated. 

You can feel the team's dedication. The fact they made custom music for the radio, that they did very professional voice recordings, that they try to make everything work before adding it in. But then you'll look at what's there and say 'not yet.'

I had a longer review, but maybe it's better to do a list for prospective buyers and in case the team sees and (I'm assuming they already know, but still) reads it.

The good:
* The core gameplay loop is fun and engaging.
* The vehicles are cool, unique, and enjoyable to work with.
* Growing your business feels  REALLY good, as does renovating the building and seeing a lot full of vehicles you restored from the ground up.
* Everything works, and I mean it. The game is stable and runs well.
* You're generally never trapped if you make a bad bet and there's always a lifeline if things get real tight, though you likely won't ever need them.
* I always appreciate custom music in-game as that's a lot of work. More of it would be welcome.

The Meh:
* Not enough vehicles in general (I realize they're making more, but I'm still putting it here for completeness sake), and the lack of models during mechanical restorations is... frustrating, but understandable. Those vehicles also just need a bit more to them. Interior lighting when you're behind the wheel would be cool and make reading the dials easier.

* I find it hilarious that instead of doing a minigame to restore parts, you just put them in a magic dryer for 6 minutes. This isn't bad, but it feels... well, you could do better. If it's a stop-gap, I get it, no problem. If not, uhh...

* The mechanical restoration feels undercooked in general, too. Complete, and understandable, but you could copy Car Mechanic's homework on that and it would make sense. I'm talking things like the rest of the suspension, carriage, and smaller things. It's hilarious the engine is just one blob instead of multiple parts. But I understand why, of course. It's not an accusation, just an observation.

* The physics can be hilariously bad at times and it's common to get your truck/trailer stuck in strange places and have to use another car to push it off. Or, worse, have to reload and hope the last save wasn't TOO long ago.

* The driving is... not great. But this isn't a racing game (at least, the base game isn't) so I'll excuse it. It definitely doesn't handle like the kind of game where driving is a core feature. Cars are floaty, don't turn well, don't break sensibly and... well, you get my point.

* The traffic is equally hilarious. Traffic will back up constantly, and they only make right turns or go straight. Apparently, like Derek Zoolander, they're not ambiturners. (I realize you can reset the traffic in the menu, but it needs listed anyways).

* The setting is very tongue-in-cheek, a pastiche of American Southwest where all the industry has vanished and died, but it depicts a very bleak interpretation of it at the same time that it can become somewhat uncomfortable. Because it's bleak. It's Pennsylvania-town-where-steel-was-traded-for-drug-trailers bleak and when you as a player are growing and succeeding and the world around you stays that way, it feels crappy. I realize this is a weird complaint, but there you go.

* It's both weird and cute to see them promote other games in this game.

* Man, I wish there was an auction house like Car Mec Sim. And I wish the junkyard worked more like they did in CMS2021.

* The car models when cleaning and doing bodywork can be frustrating when there are sharp, concealed, or hidden surfaces that you can't really reach easy. Otherwise it works well and doing a 'once you get 95% it completes' compensates well, but I felt it was worth saying.

* Dropping cars using the trailer and immediately having the game complain that you can't attach it with the ramps up is annoying. Bruh, let me at least pull away first.

* I've gotten my character model stuck on such weird things because they're fixed points. Like traffic cones or other things I feel should be easily knocked over.

* So many other little things to list. There's a lot of annoyances (besides the one below that really grinded my gears) and weirdness and screw-ups and just... it really takes it out of me.


The Bad:
* The sales of cars is very shallow. The negotiation process makes no sense and generally comes down to guessing. I just make every car 'non-negotiable' now, set prices at 98% market value, and wait a little longer to sell. It's easier and less annoying. Beyond staging, photographs, and waiting, there's not much to do. This is not me advocating for, like, financing and paperwork, god no. But I wish there was more to do on this side rather than just wait for a sale.

* The car purchasing is shallow, too, but this is more forgivable since it's private sales, not dealership-to-dealership. Since Winston Springs (the setting) is so small, it's funny buying a car from a house directly beside the dealership just to screw with the odometer, fix it up, and sell it for 2-3x what you paid for it in direct view of the previous owner.

* Once you're financially stable, you quickly realize that the world feels shallow and empty. Winston Spring isn't big, and it isn't deep. I know they just added a bar and pawnshop, so there's SOME things to do, but that's it at this point. There's so much potential here, however. I realize some of it was sectioned off behind the Up 2 U dlc, which is kinda uncool, so I'm only reviewing based on what's in the base game.

* The hitbox for screws and the timing using both the ratchet and drill are frustrating to no end. It makes me not want to do that kind of work specifically not to deal with it. I wish it were closer to Car Mech Sim. Also, it's funny and weird that an electric drill is kept behind a reputation bar and then costs $6k to purchase. By the time I bought it, that amount of money was nothing, but, man...

* The control layout when interacting with a lot of menus is very sluggish and sometimes confusing. Especially when working on the mechanical aspect of the cars. Using right mouse button to move the camera around and also back out is a bad idea for example.

* The car painting feels really shallow.

* Moving cars around the lot that aren't drivable is miserable. (Note: I realize car movers are coming in an update soon, but I'm still putting this down here.)

review:
This game is so buggy. There are fast and frequent updates, but I believe this is the problem. There isn't any quality testing happening to ensure that the game still works. 

Overall, it's an ok way to kill time, it could be a great game, but the problems with it are so difficult to overlook.

Frequent freezing and crashing, employees getting stuck, updates that break core functionality, updates that no one wants or asked for, existing bugs aren't being fixed.  Instead of making the game better, the studio is instead focused on a shared universe with their other games, neat idea on paper, terrible in practice.  If you can't even get one game working properly, why would I buy your other game at full price, that's really just acting as a DLC?

The recent update with the vehicle wholesaler is broken, and double charges you.  Updates to the staff has rendered the office employee useless, and what is with a manager position that just stands there?  It's supposed to increase speed, but it doesn't do anything, there is no difference before versus after hiring them, and $300 an hour?  Seriously?  

Automation is borked to hell.  Frequently gets stuck trying to move a vehicle.  If the path gets blocked, it won't always continue on once cleared, meaning you have to reset the automation, and then reenter everything that you had set.  New cars bought on dealer contracts can't be automated, which means you'll need to collect them, photograph them, park them, list them, and all the while try to sell other vehicles.  It doesn't sound like much, but it is a serious time sink.  At higher reputations, you can't actually keep up with the sales because you'll be spending most of your time collecting vehicles from the garage.

Another recent update, the "I need a car ASAP" emails are also massively borked.  The emails say that they'll pay a premium on the car if you deliver it.  You go through the hassle of getting a car to the specs that they ask for, deliver it, and they significantly low ball you.  If you sell it to them anyway, they don't actually take the car, it just sits where you parked it, but can't be moved because it's listed as currently for sale.

All of these issues have been reported through various channels, including directly through their Discord, and as of yet, these serious game breaking issues haven't been fixed.  They have made it clear that they don't care about fixing this game, only expanding on the shared map with their other games.  

Skip it, there are better sim games out there.

I wanted to love this game. And sure I do. A little of a love-hate relationship. But oh boy, I haven't seen such a poor optimisation for a long time. The game stutters no matter what my in-game settings are (tried all the way from epic to low, various setups including DLSS). 
Let's start with positives. I had fun. I genuinely had fun. That was the reason why I was tryin' to force myself into bitin' my teeth with just accepting the stutters. Cleaning and fixin' the bodywork really felt satisfying.  The map looks okay, even the graphics do have some charisma and charm.  
Now the mediocre stuff - the handling model. Just felt average at best. Cars felt overresponsive and, quite frankly, not even remotely close to characteristics of an automobile. Probably the reason why I'd skip the racing DLC altogether unless it goes for a really really cheap price (50+% off the regular price bein' a minimum).  
Now you probably know there's a skeleton in a closet of this game - the optimisation. Stutters no matter what you do with in-game settings. I wouldn't complain if my setup was a pile of junk. But again - there's a difference in stuttering in a large scale game and this one. This game has no rights to be so poorly optimised. Outta the time I had spent in the game most of it was tryin' to figure out how to make it run with as less tedium as possible...
Well, you probably know how this one turned out to be - in fact it is one of very few games I've submitted for a refund.

I love simulation games, I play all kinds of trash, you name it. This game has very obvious bugs that should have been fixed well a year into release that are essentially game breaking. 

My tow dolly is stuck in front of the garage. I went to move it away with my truck, it caused my truck to glitch airborne, and fly around. I ran inside, reset the truck, and the truck safely moved. That's great and fine, exactly what the reset button is for.

Yet the dolly remains. That's fine, let me wait out the timer (no  idea why there's a timer on reset) and reset the dolly. Timer runs out, reset, and... dolly is still there. That's odd. Let me check out the support channel and see what's going on.

I see a post from February of this year describing my exact issue. No developer response, just kind players trying to help, except.. there is no help. The player uninstalled the game, reinstalled it, and the save file is screwed for that exact reason.

That's incredibly bad. That's wild. That's a bare mininum expectation for a simulator with wonky physics, just to have a functioning reset, and it doesn't work to such an extent that it essentially creates an unplayable game. Convenient for the dev that this is after the refund window. 

Another note, you can sell your cars online starting at level 10, bur you can't actually respond to people trying to buy your cars until apparently level 18, leaving you with a notification of someone trying to buy your car online that you can't respond to! Yet Garage Monkeys seems more interested in selling mixed review DLCs than literally making a functioning base game!

Edit: tried to get a refund, didn't happen for obvious reasons (past the two hour marker). Just incredibly unfortunate that I didn't experience a game breaking bug til hour four.

review:
Amazing Premise, Still needs work.

Genuinely a fun idea. I love games like this, where you buy, restore, and sell something. Houses, cars, gadgets, etcc. I've played several. And every aspect of this game is pretty darn perfect. My issue is with the sand, putty, sand, paint, process.

In the tutorial the game has you pick up a scanner, and calls it a "tool." Simple enough right? Fast forward a few tutorial steps later, and it tells you to "use the scanner tool" to identify rust spots. Nifty, it doesn't work. You actually have to pick up the SANDPAPER and then you can just push X to highlight the rust. No actual scanner, just a shortcut while holding the actual tool for the job, not the scanner the game called a tool just minutes ago. Very fun to spend 45 minutes figuring this out.

Once I had figured that out, I thought I was in the clear. Okay, my fault. I'm over reacting and I'm clearly dumb. I'll eat it and enjoy the game. Well, the rust removal is progression based, as in you need to complete one tool, to move on to the next of 4 tools. Metal sandpaper, putty knife, finishing sandpaper, and paint. Each of these steps involves clearing roughly 97% of the affected surface. Once you hit 97% it auto completes. On cars with very little rust, say 8% of the body, it can be extremely, insanely difficult to locate all of the rust, even when highlighted, as there are microscopic bits along every panel edge of the car, in crevasses of bumpers, and even on the bottom edge of the wheel wells where you cannot possibly sand it. Meaning if you hit the ratio, and I have now twice in 5 hours of playing, you'll essentially be stuck doing all four steps to every single inch of the car, from every angle until you catch JUST enough to pass the threshold. This has been over an hour of my gameplay. One bug.

Save OFTEN, before every appointment to buy a car, so when you go to do body work, and its glitched, you can reload and not waste your time.

If you don't mind that, enjoy the game. I will come back once they've adjusted that bodywork system. I will be uninstalling, but hopeful.

review:
The basic gameplay loop does not change and is as follows: Set up meeting to buy car on PC; drive to location and "haggle" for the car (the npcs you haggle with will never let you win); tow/drive car back to lot; wash car; do bodywork on car; repair exhaust/suspension/brakes/engine. Eventually you will unlock the ability to have most of these parts done automatically via hired npcs. And finally you list car for sale where you can either haggle for a larger price or set a smaller buyout price. 

 If you're hoping for in depth car repair mechanics, you should look elsewhere. If you've done one car, you've done every car. They are exactly the same in the repair minigame, which essentially comes down to clicking 2-10 bolts per part and waiting for them to screw/unscrew. And you will be doing A LOT of this, as nearly every single car you purchase or find needs nearly every single piece replaced/repaired. 

 Occasionally you will get an email of an abandoned car you can pick up for free, these are always the absolute worst condition possible.

 The game gets very grindy and repetitive thanks to the "reputation" system which requires you to raise it to unlock new features and upgrades, and since before getting npc upgrades you have to do everything yourself you can only do 1-2 cars at a time, each car sold gives you a small amount of reputation.

 It is full of bugs, such as softlocks during the tutorial often requiring a new game and UI flickering issues along with bad physics, terrible driving mechanics and awful performance, especially at night. The entire game world looks like ass, with some kind of brown/dirt filter over everything.

In conclusion: I had high hopes going into this, I was hoping for CMS repair mechanics with an actual decent car dealer simulation attached, but alas this is not it.

HBP out~

review:
I got this game shortly after it came out and honestly I enjoyed what it was at the time, giving it passes on some minor stuff as it was a small team and by and large it was minor inconvienences.
Well it's been about a year and my views on the game and devs have changed quite a bit.
I no longer will recommend this game.
This game is primary about cars, you would think it had passable driving for that reason. Nope, it feels like the person who did the programing never drove before and only had the vague concept explained to them. The turning radius of the cars is not good and horrible if you get over 20km/h (about 15mph) to the point where you would need 6 lanes of traffic just to hope you could pull a u turn.
Breaking is more of a suggestion than an action.
At the start of the game it really does not feel bad as you are only dealing with a few cars and generally have plenty of time betwen. Late game it becomes unbearable due to how may you are moving around and the extra time it takes becomes compounded by the number of cars your trying to deal with.
Late game is honestly demoralizing. You get to hire a bunch of people to do stuff but your so involved in every facet you have no time to breath.
I only sell cars two times a week because of how poorly designed the late game is. Finally got a feature to not negotiate prices (implementation was a complete mess) yet even maxing out the price where they will sell I will end up selling 30 cars in a single day which is good I guess.
But to replenish my stock I spend so much time running around what feels like micromanaging I get no time to enjoy what there is.
You can make trophies out of cars in game and have different levels to them, But it's implementation feels like an after thought with no actual consideration to the players time, the number of cards for each trophy you have to crush is absurd.
Then there is the unashamed self marketing shoved down your throat for their other stuff when you are playing. It's so over done it's sickening.
Personally I am never buying another game from this deveoper / publisher again as I view them no better than the AAA studios and their ill concieved practices.

review:
I want to like this game more than I do.  What it does right: it's got some game-like features and an open-y world.  What it does wrong: look, at this point I think we all know making games is hard.  But let's not beat around the bush, just because it's hard doesn't mean any effort is good.  And here we have a game with some effort, but it looks like any other low-effort asset flip and it plays like it was cobbled together out of Unreal templates.  To that I can't give it a thumbs up.

Not because it didn't do better, but because I don't think it *can* do better.  I think it's very likely that this is the peak of what the person or people making it can produce: a distraction.  There's no depth to the gameplay.  If you've done any of the tasks in this game once, you've done them as many times as you need to.  There isn't any evolution, there's no progression and importantly the open world kind of works against it because if you let me go out there and see things, you need to put some effort into what I find.  Which, of course, there wasn't any so it's a dead world on top of a lifeless game.  Fitting I suppose, but not good.

Part of me wants to be kinder, because I was born in the eighties and I go, maybe my standards are too high.  I mean, I've played literally tens of thousands of games and it would be unfair to judge this one against all of them.  But I remember a game like this would've sucked on the BBS Micro let alone a modern PC because the gameplay loop is a line between when you started and when you quit.  I won't begrudge anyone who likes it, but I definitely wouldn't recommend that anyone try to.

DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. The developer is engaging in an asset flip, offering bare minimum gameplay, and then releasing it for profit. 

A few "placeholder" items that I have noticed between this game and various other "sim" games they've developed. As well as just terrible gameplay elements such as:

- The "buying a vehicle" stage: Same animation for EVERY PERSON who sells you a vehicle. You purchase a vehicle from a random NPC in town, and you do a little haggling. The dialogue is just... rough and doesn't flow well. It just feels very generic, and no thought was put into it. Then, once a deal is made, they ALL do a little "happy dance" like a waifu anime girl and magically disappear (No im not exageratting its a LITERAL WAIFU ANIME GIRL DANCE). 

- NPCs: The NPCs in here are the same placeholder NPCs in their other games down to the EXACT same face, body, clothes, hair, and even HAIR COLOR. They were so lazy, they literally just COPY AND PASTED their NPCs from one game to the other. Theres a tall bald guy too that i believe is the default NPC devs get with their asset packs anyway.... 

- Animations: NPC animations are lacking - and what is there is extremely small variety. When someone wants to "buy" a car that you have for sale on your lot, the customers magically appear out of thin air - walk a straight line - then do 1 of 3 or 4 animations that dont fit well. (Like a odd jumping up and down with their heads waving above their head). It all looks generic placeholder and unrefined. Note, ALL BUYERS appear in the SAME spot, follow the SAME pathfinding to the car, and then all dissapear the same way. It makes it feel so... robotic and lifeless. 

I can go on - but please until the devs show us respect please dont buy anything from them. 

The CORE gameplay loop is fun. There is potential, but i would 100% call this alpha stage.

When I saw this game, it was love at first sight but now I'm split.

[b]PROS[/b]
[list]
[*]Its graphics, and ambiance as a whole, gave me a rush of nostalgia ; 
[*]I love the  concept of the game (AI and its abuse) ;

[/list]

[b]PROBLEM[/b]
[list]
[*][b]No manual save nor frequent autosave ![/b]
[/list]
No manual save would not be a huge problem had a frequent autosave been implemented. Saves only occur when you reach specific levels. I read that there was a way to create manual saves later in the game but it seems it costs money and its costs increase with every use. As a consequence, progressing in the game is in itself a source of stress as you never know if you will reach another save and may have to continue playing to reach it even if you want to stop because you don't want to lose your progress.
If you can accept that "risk", though, the game is interesting.

review:
This game focuses more on [b]aesthetics[/b] rather than [b]gameplay[/b].

You're basically doing captcha's of faces at the start, then you automate it, and then game adds management genre into the loop, since upgrading your automation will put stress on your PC components which will need upgrading. And to upgrade them you'll need to [b]W A I T[/b] for your money to accumulate, up to 3 times (for 3 different components). 

Then there's this mechanic, [b]harvest[/b]. Instead of buying the captcha sets from the shop with varying levels of "purity" (something you'll need "auto accuracy upgrade" for), it will generate its own sets, with no wrong tiles (100% pure) and you wont have to pay for them. Instead what you will pay with is your PC components capacity, cuz the cameras this mechanic needs are using up your everything, which makes progression EVEN LONGER due to you needing to wait for better components to handle it. You can ignore this thing completely [spoiler]THERE'S EVEN A FUCKING ACHIEVEMENT FOR THAT[/spoiler] and have a faster completion. 

In essence: progression is more on the idle side, unless you just commit to just upgrading auto speed, then game gets better. And when to achieve that you have to avoid the mechanics dev has made, is... dissapointing.

Things that are less important: [b]achievements[/b] are quite varied, but require several playthroughs, wether to do a perfect run, another difficulty run, endless run to reach unreachable-in-normal-playthrough milestone, etc. Win95/98 [b]aesthetics + OST[/b] are pretty neat, helping me to get through the drag that was the "harvest". Didnt care for [b]story[/b], you're a  [spoiler]simulation being tested on your efficiency to burn down the world, AI foreshadowing[/spoiler] .
[hr][/hr]

Captcha'd a cat, burned/flooded the world for social credits AI monitoring (thrice), BSOD'd 5.27$ worth of equipment, [b]6/10[/b]

review:
I adored the aesthetics and music, but man, the gameplay felt really weak and the writing didn't land for me. I get the message and agree with it, but the game doesn't feel like it's saying or doing anything profound with it. 

Game-play is, unfortunately, the generic clicker/idle experience: Number go up, buy resources to make number bigger, rinse and repeat. There are no gameplay elements that Faceminer brings to the table that are unique. Sure, the UI and the reasons for the numbers getting bigger are interesting, but they don't really lend to the overall game experience at all. I wish there was more to do with the components and upgrades you bought as some of them provide a new application on the desktop, but this is mainly for viewing data at a glance. If there was some kind of interactivity that required the player's attention within those screens we had to balance with the other elements in the game it would have made for a richer gameplay experience.

The moral at the end of the story is "[i]AI is bad for us and the environment. These corporations are doing everything to enable AI and, inevitably, doom us.[/i]" and while I do agree with most of this (to a degree), it's just a reverberation of what I consistently see on Reddit, BlueSky, etc. I'm left wishing there was more substance to the message here. I was hoping to get more out of this experience, but I finished it feeling disappointed.

review:
Just go read about CAPTCHA, data privacy, and surveillance, then skim through a gallery of eerie liminal creepypasta images, and go play an idle game that actually lets you idle. It's astounding this was in a bundle with Horripilant.

You ever wanted a clicker game to be an uphill battle to keep any progress? Faceminer wipes your save file repeatedly, but barely seems to autosave backups. Just couldn't get a foothold, the game kept failing and wiping the save for a bunch of reasons. Spend your earnings on an upgrade like every other clicker game, wipe. Leave the game in the background when you think you have enough accuracy upgrades to at least break even, wipe. Try to read the accumulating emails for a minute or so, wipe.

The automated function is terrible enough that it needs to be constantly micromanaged to avoid one of several fail states, when it picks up the pace you can't click along with it any more or you'll wipe again, and even on the quick game mode the upgrades are slow & uninteresting enough that this game feels like nothing. Like a chore. Doesn't help that it's purposely trying to emulate office PC work.

Faceminer gave me verification fatigue.

review:
Sounds important (but isn't), has nostalgia. Yeah that's it.

The game is fun for the first hour as the Win95 esthetic very much drags you in if you have nostalgia for that late-mid-90's technology theme. The visuals and music are incredibly thematic and build a fun atmosphere but gameplay drags it down really quick. The initial 15 minutes or so is a logic game when you need to click on pictures. Then, it's an upgrade simulator. And not even a complex, robust one with lots of strategy. Once you play it for the first 30-60 minutes you realize oh f*** that's the entire game isn't it?
 
To add insult to injury, the story is honestly painfully predictable considering the premise of the game i spelled out instantly, even advertised. It's incredibly simplistic "AI datacenters bad, corpo bad, world go boom" commentary  which is a valid message sure but you're not experiencing it in any meaningful way here. It's just generic videos and some ok e-mail messages of the environment going more and more to heck the more you play. Not even a significant number of those. And gameplay isn't really fun as I mentioned. I play a lot of games which are rather repetitive in nature but this here feels like a browser based Flash game I'd play years ago. And not a very good one I'm afraid. Maybe it's a low key attention span test in the sense if you can't play for long then you're "brainrotten". Yeah thanks I'd rather read a book or Wikipedia at this point. One more annoyance to the collection is that in order to manual save you have to pay with in-game money that you also use to upgrade everything it's a "unique" feature but just a nuisance. Auto-saves take place not more than 30 minutes though at least based on my progress so it's not a complete disaster.

I do want to again point out the esthetics of the game are incredibly thematic and if you love that mid-90's and like upgrade simulator-style games then buy this one at least 50% discount to get those vibes. Other than that, due to it's gameplay and "story", even at its price point, skippable.

review:
Although the Operator has a good premise, there were a few things that stopped me from really enjoying it. First, the game is set in 1992 yet all the characters seemed to have cellphones. My entire family didn't even have a computer between us in 1992, let alone a cellphone. There doesn't seem to be any reason to set it in 1992, so a later setting would have worked just as well. The Operator felt short and only half finished. Just as things are really getting interesting the game ended in such a way you can tell that it will be continued. 

Finally, there aren't any chapters, yet there is one big event that is easily failed. Once I finished the game, I wanted to go back and try again. That meant I needed to play the game from the beginning. After getting to that point, I failed yet again. As far as I can tell, I would have to start over to retry that portion of the game.

I really enjoyed the idea of having access to pretty much all information and having the ability to do face and image scans from videos and photographs. However, it became a little less enjoyable as the actual storyline for the game kicked in pretty much full force when you meet the main character. You're then just forced to  jump through whatever hoops the game holds out in front of you whether you want or not. The investigation then becomes annoyingly predictable and the game becomes less fun. The way the trailer looked it seemed like you would be pretty busy and very involved in your workload, but you get maybe 2 work days of fun investigating. I'm honestly not sure if I would recommend this game at full price. I got it on sale for about $8 and would probably say it's worth about that if not less. This wouldve been so much cooler if there were more caseloads that didn't have anything to do with the story's 'hidden' agenda or just not as obvious about it. Even better if it had an completely separate option of play that was a set number of cases to try and solve just for fun. In the end, no, I don't think this is a good enough for $14. This level of inevitability is expected for story mode games like GTA, COD, GOW etc. and I probably would've rated this higher if it shared a similar format. But the choices that weren't really choices is what threw me off. It felt like none of my efforts as a player were rewarded or even mattered at all. Because quite frankly, they didn't. If this game had the option for multiple endings I think it would've been great.
